body.title: Marine Fossil Skeletons and Giant Squid (Eng/Esp)
body.body:
> With this post, I conclude my tour of the Museum of the Sea. I went through all the exhibition areas and saved the one with the skeletal remains for last. There, I was able to examine the underside of a baba’s (cayman) skull, which is rough and has alveolar textures. In this part of the country, “baba” is the name given to small caimans that typically live in streams. I noticed large cavities around the eyes, while on the underside of the “V”-shaped lower jaw, rows of sharp teeth were visible. It’s the best example to illustrate how this animal catches and tears apart its prey after biting it.
![1000123812.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvgJ3vwGY6aJmAz9VM8MBAtV4aETqiFgemFxyD1TMQhYkEFzbeAConL4vVSZKX3ZuCw.jpg)
There are also some bone fragments from the head of the labiated peccary, also known as a wild boar. The collection is divided into three parts: two of them are skull structures (lateral and dorsal views). The first shows the elongated shape of the head and the row of upper molars, while the second displays the eye sockets and the pointed shape of the snout. The third structure is the lower jaw, viewed from above, where other sharp teeth can be seen. A morrocoy shell and a turtle shell are also part of the exhibit. Other skulls are on display, including that of a lapa—a rodent of considerable size that is highly prized in Venezuela for the flavor and texture of its meat.
![1000123804.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvY8FvwbGoNTyQsWQPgSmygraZsbvqw6tSh2gJ743V5aA4UKZw7zooY58zzJfTcdNn1.png)
![1000123805.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23uExBMovZeuVKnaDFwLiH8SRzTkN3Nbx2dPt2163rFhW54dmKJT4XRfYgb93G5DBZ9o5.png)
![1000123806.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tm9Fn8ghd1gceyUssqR9bHG5qAXY5E5wx2cuL6QjNyYi7Y5Fo9SoUPEpECQ1nPmwEPs.png)
Then I came across another display case featuring the jaws and skeletons of marine fossils. The most impressive was the head of a sawfish—a long, flattened structure with teeth along its sides. I also noticed shark jaws, which displayed rows of sharp, terrifying teeth. I was amazed by the jagged arrangement—whatever it bites into is pierced and torn apart. It’s impossible to escape unscathed from a shark attack, even though only a few species of sharks are aggressive.
![1000123807.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23xVAi1bdFkbQnkK31ttoQJp7GToDbyG7w27s4MrqobNUUkRTRTrupgiuNzMkS12fUbfW.png)
![1000123809.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23ywis5ra2iQJ5tczGMoQfN7R24k9biSkixzYrnCYschumMoA8ZDEcwMfmDznxEph9M45.png)
The last place we visited was a glass jar filled with preservative liquid (formalin) that preserves the body of a giant squid; its elongated mantle, head, and tentacles are truly fantastic. It reminds me of the one Jules Verne described in his *20,000 Leagues Under the Sea*, although that specimen was as huge as the Nautilus.
![1000123811.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23uEz3tsZ9vJdeKv4GjsLsdmus85f1JWCBTxuJNwaae6XF89n91riE12JCUB5Ez9GvzUY.jpg)
![1000123810.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvc8ysUcMNFGfNRvtPf8CjdDuuKSbtvteZdAhvnyR9V9QYy2icmJ5FXqAKY7rGc9fut.jpg)
Here in Cumana, squid is a highly sought-after marine species due to its versatility in the kitchen and its delicious flavor. Whether battered, served with vinaigrette, in a salad, or stuffed into an arepa, squid will always be a star ingredient. Thinking about food and movie sharks, that’s how my visit to the Museum of the Sea came to an end—a wonderful and educational experience that left me feeling very satisfied. *** ***
## Versión en Español

>\n\nCon esta publicación termino mi recorrido por el Museo del mar, pasé por todas las áreas de exposición y dejé para el final la de los restos óseos. Acá pude apreciar la parte inferior del cráneo de una baba (caimán), la cual es rugosa y con texturas alveolares. En esta parte del país se le denomina baba a los caimanes pequeños que por lo regular viven en los caños. Noté grandes cavidades en la zona de los ojos, en tanto en la parte inferior de la mandíbula, que tiene forma de \

, se podían apreciar las hileras de filosos dientes. Es el mejor ejemplo para explicar cómo este animal atrapa y desgarra a sus presas tras aplicarle una mordida.


<center>
![1000123812.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvgJ3vwGY6aJmAz9VM8MBAtV4aETqiFgemFxyD1TMQhYkEFzbeAConL4vVSZKX3ZuCw.jpg)
</center>

También se observan algunas piezas óseas de la cabeza del Pecarí labiado, también conocido como jabalí o cerdo salvaje. El conjunto está desglosado en tres partes: dos de ellas son estructuras del cráneo (Vista lateral y dorsal). En la primera se muestra la forma alargada de la cabeza y la hilera de dientes molares superiores y en la segunda se exhiben las cuencas de los ojos y la forma puntiaguda que representa el hocico. La tercera estructura es la mandíbula inferior expuesta desde arriba, allí se aprecian otros dientes filosos. 

Un caparazón de morrocoy y otro de tortuga son otros elementos de la exhibición. Otros cráneos se muestra en exhibición, esta vez el de unas lapas, roedor de tamaño considerable que en Venezuela es muy codiciado por el sabor y la textura de su carne. 

<center>
![1000123804.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvY8FvwbGoNTyQsWQPgSmygraZsbvqw6tSh2gJ743V5aA4UKZw7zooY58zzJfTcdNn1.png)
</center>


<center>
![1000123805.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23uExBMovZeuVKnaDFwLiH8SRzTkN3Nbx2dPt2163rFhW54dmKJT4XRfYgb93G5DBZ9o5.png)
</center>


<center>
![1000123806.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tm9Fn8ghd1gceyUssqR9bHG5qAXY5E5wx2cuL6QjNyYi7Y5Fo9SoUPEpECQ1nPmwEPs.png)
</center>

Luego encontré otra vitrina que tenía en exhibición mandíbulas y osamentas de fósiles marinos. La más impresionante corresponde al rostro de un Pez Sierra, una estructura larga y aplanada con dientes a los lados. También noté mandíbulas de Tiburón, acá se muestran hileras de dientes afilados y aterradores. Me pareció asombrosa la disposición desalineada, lo que muerde lo atraviesa y destroza, imposible escapar ileso de un ataque de un tiburón, aunque son pocas las variedades de escualos que son agresivas.


<center>
![1000123807.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23xVAi1bdFkbQnkK31ttoQJp7GToDbyG7w27s4MrqobNUUkRTRTrupgiuNzMkS12fUbfW.png)
</center>


<center>
![1000123809.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23ywis5ra2iQJ5tczGMoQfN7R24k9biSkixzYrnCYschumMoA8ZDEcwMfmDznxEph9M45.png)
</center>


El último lugar visitado fue una urna de vidrio con líquido preservante (formol) que conserva el cuerpo de un calamar gigante, su manto alargado, su cabeza y tentáculos son realmente fantásticos, me recuerda al que describió Julio Verne es sus \

, aunque aquel espécimen era tan gigante como el Nautilus.
![1000123811.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23uEz3tsZ9vJdeKv4GjsLsdmus85f1JWCBTxuJNwaae6XF89n91riE12JCUB5Ez9GvzUY.jpg)
![1000123810.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ramisey/23tvc8ysUcMNFGfNRvtPf8CjdDuuKSbtvteZdAhvnyR9V9QYy2icmJ5FXqAKY7rGc9fut.jpg)
Acá en Cumaná el calamar es una especie marina muy buscada por su versatilidad en la cocina y lo delicioso de su sabor. Rebozados, a la vinagreta, en ensalada o rellenando una arepa, el calamar siempre será un ingrediente estelar. Pensando en comida y en tiburones de películas, así culminó mi visita al Museo del Mar, una experiencia maravillosa y didáctica que me llenó de satisfacción. *** *** ✓Photos from my personal gallery, edited with Fotocollage. ✓Text translated with DeepL.

body.title: Celebrating Love, Family, and our Mother's 58th Birthday at Avenue Plaza Hotel!🎂
body.body:
***A Pleasant and Beautiful Day to everyone!***🤗🌺

***Hello to all of my friends here and of course to all my dear fellow hivers in this lovely @hiveph community!***😍

***How are you all today? I hope everyone is doing well and happy right now. This is me again @lj1728 and I am happy to share in this community my simple life story with you all.***💕

![July 2026 Blogs.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/242YP44J3p2egnJGfGB5tjWS9EFWFAvEfmyNrZTN9RBELoYmhLNLN2H65xJum1vB8Xr3z.png)

***Last June 22, we celebrated the 58th birthday of our dear mother, and it turned out to be a wonderful day filled with love, laughter, and delicious food.*** My brother and I came up with the idea of treating our mother and the whole family to a fine dining dinner instead of celebrating at home. ***We all loved the idea because it was a nice way to make her birthday feel extra special.***

![IMG_9347.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wX9Zchyw4ewYAeCYXaLHmKCgJ3SahVS1Sth6p6Cwx5dapGwfFdQRqRfYAbV8aoBtCVy.jpeg)

![IMG_9350.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wCJ2P4J6FqSoubGcHkvnTD6Q5Fd7wug5eECkvBXowXsG8Ru4xNFRAxJFf4JQfXSCiBZ.jpeg)

![IMG_9349.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23uR2pQu2tuzsLEC37Jwy1ZxSjnmsLsiEAG8TLiF7oHZC1XAq4TPbyprYmBDoPoqJmyXS.jpeg)

![IMG_9361.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/EpNqpCdqQjUUJupNDWhrBkNfNrp2y8FEFmYYCdShPQbW6kkfKzz5Gk78uqqUDyThb5a.jpeg)

***He suggested that we have dinner at Avenue Plaza Hotel, so we all headed there in the evening. The restaurant had a cozy and elegant atmosphere that made the celebration even more memorable.*** As soon as we were seated, we took our time looking through the menu before deciding on dishes that everyone could enjoy.

![IMG_9360.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/Eos3krabw9YUgmv7jB1s7VnV4yeRJj1665zEx2Ptnpo2TJUwM3usG3mK6yHHRhCZBi4.jpeg)

![IMG_9362.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/EpJb1pAt2B7irp33oV9iLC8i6hb5QAjrGPjHYWFpaSfJfc1MxxoehA4aDTG12hN8d7c.jpeg)

![IMG_9358.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/EpNqFZRqF5HHRn7upVAs1EzQafmngGTdmFQMrX59rVCMZeLs4ikRt4DyZrfePphFd1S.jpeg)

![IMG_9357.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/EowKSESvrDRudmwAdWRvxdrsfWnay2r9htwqcN91Zu1L8yT939MrxwQcDKVYGFixj63.jpeg)

***We ordered several meals that were perfect for sharing, including a steaming bowl of bulalo, crispy lechon kawali, flavorful buttered chicken, and everyone's favorite lumpiang shanghai.*** Every dish was served fresh and tasted amazing. We spent the evening talking, laughing, and enjoying each other's company while sharing the delicious food.

![IMG_9356.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/EpVDziD3zqV4A9RPDNnWihNMMxFuQuP3V4wZr13oP11rUsYYJvEzTDNLXYFXgWgqE3R.jpeg)

![IMG_9363.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23vi8FSusP2F8xiezi8D7AZgLDgrVkcBdnSCfz5z7oRxY5m3Yyoo3ZQ674voiuAhzayBS.jpeg)

![IMG_9364.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23tvpc8DCY9TNi8CihvAoXaXeCP4NvvegY4cJTb9j3ysem81tqanumT9S8YXDWi7sgFj4.jpeg)

![IMG_9365.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23vsb3khsx4DkwTxiEjQJ6ASoMj6Nh4pbGNjVD6MTV2y9qd6VkZod1az12rUn911RHCyg.jpeg)

![IMG_9368.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23w2ynyjXeJc4ZPkBy8tyTc45VULun9SvVSsznKuSr8kXFpC46dEM8p2NBzSw5UQRonw7.jpeg)

***Just before we finished eating, we surprised our mother with a slice of carrot cake. The waiter carefully brought it to our table while one of the hotel's singers performed the traditional \

song. It was such a sweet and heartwarming surprise! Our mother smiled from ear to ear, and you could see how happy and touched she was.*** We all sang along, clapped, and captured the moment with plenty of photos and videos to remember the occasion.

![93f58d61b371e7ad80726ae6be2d5e8c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23uR5FY53xjUwLt5HPMLr1EtkEe2rVoL9i7yRQpzPG7igwW3m4CEYsG4RhN9oizdFcCvE.jpeg)

![141a1b7448b62056e6cf8005a0967a62.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23wCNSuwrJvttWTxtzL15v6fNeT2mWeVcvRA6D5howVgs6ZuztDoRHUZ41ZA8iR7RUWU8.jpeg)

***Seeing our mother so genuinely happy made the entire celebration even more meaningful. She truly deserved to fell loved and appreciated on her special day after everything she has done for our family over the years.*** I am grateful that we were all able to celebrate together, creating another beautiful memory that we will cherish for years to come.

![71a06396a6ba9cca872570d0f5fcbca9.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lj1728/23uR32V2V6NrcmGD7MmF1w5V24TkgPwK2i693wTmMLUxp3aoFzXQqy1UdgovjdR5BEPc7.jpeg)

***And that's it for today's blog! Thank you so much for dropping by and taking the time to read my simple life story. This means a lot to me! I hope you enjoyed it and see you on my next one. Have a nice day ahead to all of us.***😍

***These photos were mine and taken with my iphone13pro and the lead image was edited through Canva.***✍️👩‍💻

**Lots of love,
LJ**💗

body.title: Homegrown Goodness Picking and Enjoying Super Sweet Sugar Apples From Our Own Tree
body.body:
![1000036627.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/piyaanggtiu/AK2FLNeK58Ffhab6X4VvLhgrb2ewTekGyFMyewKpCGdeKAam48pVhT3T5DpjpGu.png)

right outside our house stands our own sugar apple tree which we also call atis. it has been growing there for years standin strong under the sun and rain. we did not do anything special to it just let it grow naturally in its own place. now it has become a big healthy tree that gives us plenty of fruit every season.
 

![1000036629.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/piyaanggtiu/AKuupVhi2wkS9Yiwot6DrgLJMT6DzzxAWG9DNGDqZTC3crb4HZUw2MWMdr2zgEq.png)

this time around it is really heavy with fruit. So many have grown that the branches look like they are bending low just to hold them all. it feels wonderful to see it hitik  loaded from top to bottom. you can tell just by looking that it is going to be a good harvest for us this year.
 

![1000036630.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/piyaanggtiu/AKF9SVu8jDarvcuW41LTUNs2TeuHDEwhRciAD4rEjy9HsEoaAT5ur98Ybx8Ziu8.png)

yesterday we went out to pick some. we chose the ones that felt soft and had turned a little yellow‑green. it was easy to twist them off the stem. bringing them inside felt like bringing home a nice gift from our own garden no need to spend money buying from the market.
 

![1000036631.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/piyaanggtiu/AL7Q3SeecNgcM76LfK2rm6pr8Bp8TefW6rBb53qmH3NXJJUhVWdeBw3pAZas6ze.png)

the skin is bumpy and scaly but gentle to hold once ready. when you open itthe inside is pure white soft and creamy. it looks just like what you see in the picture clean and plump ready to eat. the black seeds are easy to spot and remove.
 

![1000036632.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/piyaanggtiu/AKPmFPPtwGBH8ssK8CgXhuCeEUqF6q18yQTZjfH41YfyiXCSTDgioYvn1iqXznq.png)

the best part is the flavor. it is very sweet almost like sugar mixed with soft custard. it melts right in your mouth and feels cool and refreshing perfect for our warm weather. every bite makes you want to take another one because it tastes so good.
 

![1000036628.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/piyaanggtiu/AKtUYMknft4eS7rvRBbnJoQQaRkCNRnBTiZpxadg4prw3LKcDk236eVvW5k2W9y.png)

this tree does not ask for much. it only needs sunlight and a little water when it gets too dry. it grows well here in our place without fancy fertilizers or extra work. it is the kind of plant that gives back more than what you give it.
 

![1000036633.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/piyaanggtiu/AKYNbPpDhXDJ7PM33oWzixLHSHdpiLT2ELguJ8DfpQX7R1ro24XwB9zQNj49wAg.png)

having this tree is a real joy. we eat as much as we want and we also share with neighbors and family. it feels great to have something natural and sweet right at our doorstep. this sugar apple tree is truly a precious part of our home.

body.title: A family lunch featuring delicious chicken and rice, mortadella, and fried plantains—an ideal combination of flavors.
body.body:
>
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmQPg5pseaweqWrBuiG77fTWDQHVqUcFvtWRC98HGFKkCp/1001827804.jpg
Feliz martes para mis respetados amigos lectores y seguidores amantes de la buena comida para todos ustedes mi saludo y con respeto! Una vez más aprovecho y le comparto una nueva receta ideal para un almuerzo familiar, delicioso arroz con pollo y mortadelas ideal combinación de sabores. >Happy Tuesday to my respected reader friends and followers who love good food—warm greetings to you all! Once again, I am sharing a new recipe that is perfect for a family lunch: delicious chicken and mortadella rice—a wonderful combination of flavors. Ingredientes: 1 kilo de muslos de pollo, 200 g de mortadela de pollo, 1/2 kilo de arroz, 1 cebolla, 1 pimentón, 2 tomates, 1/4 de ají dulces, 1 cabeza de ajo pequeña, aceite, orégano, color, cubito y sal. >Ingredients: 1 kg chicken thighs, 200 g chicken mortadella, 1/2 kg rice, 1 onion, 1 bell pepper, 2 tomatoes, 1/4 kg sweet peppers (*ají dulce*), 1 small head of garlic, oil, oregano, food coloring, bouillon cube, and salt. Preparación: Picar y lavar los muslos en piezas medianas, seguidamente lavar pelar y picar en cuadritos pequeños los aliños como cebolla, pimentón, ají dulces, tomates y también triturar los ajos luego colocar las piezas de pollo y los aliños en un caldero al fuego y precalentar.
![1001827409.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cielitorojo/AKF8qnxihpve5wwhenD4jJAzJXhuauwTTNjCu9BWK5WsTKUd19b2KdDfXtX5Qcp.jpg)
>Preparation: Cut the chicken thighs into medium-sized pieces and wash them. Next, wash, peel, and finely dice the aromatics—onion, bell pepper, sweet peppers, and tomatoes—and crush the garlic. Place the chicken pieces and the aromatics into a heavy-bottomed pot (*caldero*) over the heat. Para continuar con las recetas se le debe agregar cierta cantidad de aceite también color, orégano, un cubito y sal al gusto proceder a revolver y dejar en cocción. Se debe lavar el arroz para quitar el almidón e incorporar al guisado de pollo también se le agrega las tazas de agua, en lo particular a la familia nos gusta que quede blandito el arroz luego revolver por unos minutos y por último le incorporamos la mortadela picaditas en cubitos y una pizca de sal proceder a revolver y dejar en cocción para sellar los sabores.
![1001827412.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cielitorojo/AJoJdgD52dQuabdzVzLgkD3cgpt8yfjyKZ1kQ2Aeg12P54vTdmy4AQxdt6Shbub.jpg)
![1001827413.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/cielitorojo/AKGa3anQRnkFTcuB6Gn3VmAZvqTRv9LdMehPQzpuZx8HEzmz9TLK5fDzy4SHvdi.jpg)
>To continue the recipe, add some oil, food coloring, oregano, a bouillon cube, and salt to taste; stir the mixture and let it cook. Wash the rice to remove the starch and add it to the chicken stew, along with the water. (Personally, my family prefers the rice to be soft.) Stir for a few minutes, then finally add the mortadella—cut into small cubes—and a pinch of salt; stir again and let it cook to allow the flavors to meld. Gracias por acompañarme aquí y hasta otra oportunidad. Gracias por leerme y su valioso apoyo. >Thank you for joining me here and see you another time. Thanks for reading me and your valuable support. body.title: John The Baptist: True Greatness in the Eyes of God
body.body:
The sixth expository work of Rev. Sang Ho Bae on the gospel of Matthew is focused on the personality of John the Baptist.


<center>![TrueGreatness.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/arcelcalvin9/48PvpMYGZr8XRXVZdDjdDuE7aAiWR8UxUmZui2TJdv6apVKWY6KvcJukMSvkRoUHRj.png)</center>


<center>[Source](https://chatgpt.com/c/6a4258fe-6408-83ec-bbc7-8c574426316c)</center>

John the Baptist was the one who came beforehand, like a person who goes ahead of the king’s procession to prepare the way, just before Jesus officially appeared at the age of thirty as the King of the Kingdom of God. His mission was simple, yet great. He proclaimed:

> Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near (Matt. 3:2).

He cried out that people should prepare to welcome the King of Heaven who was about to come. Here, “the kingdom of heaven” is not merely a place but refers to Jesus Himself, the Lord of the kingdom. The statement “the kingdom of heaven is near” means that the Messiah is coming, so turn your heart. 

John urged repentance and gave baptism as the sign of repentance; therefore, he is called “John the Baptist” to distinguish him from other Johns. He was one specially chosen. He was conceived through the announcement of an angel and was filled with the Holy Spirit from his mother’s womb. Although he was born into a priestly family and could have enjoyed a comfortable life, he laid everything down for his mission. His possessions were only a camel-hair garment and a leather belt, and his food was locusts and wild honey. This was the food of the poor in those days. John chose a thoroughly austere life so that his message would not become a stumbling block.

John knew his position exactly. Fearing that people might misunderstand him as the Christ, he clearly said, “I am not the Christ.” He also confessed, “I am not worthy to carry His sandals” (Matt. 3:11), making it clear that he was only the herald who announced the coming of the Lord. 

John is the last prophet standing at the boundary between the Old Testament and the New Testament. Just as the law of the Old Testament makes one aware of sin and leads to Christ, he knocked on the hearts of the people so that they might realize their need for the Messiah. He warned that judgment would come if they did not repent. 

> The axe is already laid at the root of the trees; therefore every tree that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire (Matt. 3:10). 

> He who comes after me has His winnowing fork in His hand, and He will thoroughly clear His threshing floor, gathering His wheat into the barn, but burning up the chaff with unquenchable fire (Matt. 3:12). 

John proclaimed the judgment and urged people to bear fruit in keeping with repentance. 

Today, Christians also have a mission like John. The Lord came two thousand years ago, but in the last days He will come again. At that time He will not come as the Redeemer who saves sinners but as the Judge who judges those who reject the gospel and as the One who will take with Him the saints washed by the blood of Christ. As John proclaimed ‘Repent’ before the first coming of Jesus, so also must we, before His second coming, lead people to repent and believe the gospel. 

John’s public ministry lasted only about six months, yet he accomplished a great work. Jesus said of him:

> Among those born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptist (Matt. 11:11). 

Scripture says that a person’s greatness is not determined by his achievements but by his relationship with the Lord. John became a great one not because of poverty, justice, humility, or martyrdom, but because he testified of the most exalted Lord more closely than anyone else. The prophet Micah said that although Bethlehem was a small town, it was not insignificant because the Messiah would come from there. At that time Bethlehem was not a city but a small rural village, a humble place where shepherds tended their sheep in the fields. But it became honored because Jesus was born there. This shows that a person or even a small town that is related to the Lord one way or another becomes honorable regardless of social status. Scripture says that believers will receive crowns in the future; receiving a crown means becoming a person of honor. 

Christians must judge who is truly blessed not by the world’s perspective but by the perspective of Scripture. From a human viewpoint, John the Baptist appears to be the most pitiful person—living on locusts and wild honey, crying out in the wilderness, and being beheaded only six months after beginning his ministry. But the Lord called him “a great one.” Believers who are insulted, beaten, imprisoned, and even killed for their faith may look unfortunate from the world’s perspective, but from the biblical perspective it is the opposite. John the Baptist lived a short life, yet he lived the most valuable life. A blessed life does not lie in longevity or status. He suffered the tragic fate of having his head brought on a platter, yet before God he lived a truly blessed life. A blessed person is not one who is recognized by the world, but one who, like John, is approved by the Lord.

> Hola, amigos de **Hive** espero se encuentren muy bien. El día de hoy nos tocó el tema de la semana: **Encuentro de Talentos: El proceso**, en donde vamos a explorar un tema variado que nos haga sentir diferente, es por eso que este tema es muy bueno, espero les guste. Todo ser humano en la vida ha sufrido procesos, los cuales los han llevado a ser mejores personas, o en otros casos no les ha ido bien, pero es parte del desarrollo de la persona. Estos procesos nos llevan a entender de una manera más natural la vida y las consecuencias a donde nos llevan cada una de esas decisiones que tomamos, y por ende nos reflejamos en ella. Todo proceso conlleva una enseñanza, un ideal y un principio de donde parte todo, es decir, que para iniciar el proceso hace falta la idea principal; esto va a aplicar a todos los aspectos de nuestra vida, ya sea personal o material. Durante mi vida he pasado por muchos procesos, tanto dolorosos como de alegría, los cuales me han enseñado a ser fuerte; además, me han dado satisfacción algunos de ellos, como por ejemplo el proceso de mi vida como tal, ya que considero que he llevado un proceso bastante rígido y a su vez de poder propio, porque he pasado por muchas batallas, las cuales he sabido superar con bastante atención. En el proceso de mi vida profesional también ha sido un sube y baja, pero me ha dado un aprendizaje exacto, el cual se basa en la tranquilidad de haber alcanzado las metas que me he propuesto, porque soy una persona que alcanza las metas que se propone y eso me lleva a tener un proceso ideal de lo que quiero. En pocas palabras, podemos decir que mi vida ha servido de ejemplo a otros por lo resiliente que soy en la vida. En los procesos emocionales que he tenido, puedo decir que anteriormente era bastante fuerte mantener y llevar un proceso bueno de la gestión de mis emociones, ya que tenía otra perspectiva de lo que eso significa, pero con el paso del tiempo y las diferentes experiencias de mi vida, he sabido trabajar muchas de ellas. De hecho, estos procesos me han enseñado lo fuerte que puedo llegar a ser ante la vida, porque de verdad que he llevado batallas que he sabido manejar, y más ahora que me siento más fortalecida y llena de sabiduría. En cuanto a los procesos amorosos, también he llevado una vida pausada, sin prisa, aunque en oportunidades me he tropezado; siento que he ido al ritmo que deseo y el que el proceso me permite, ya que todo va a depender del momento y la persona, pero hasta el momento de hoy he llevado un proceso estructurado de mis sentimientos y emociones a nivel de relación sentimental. Un proceso personal es un camino continuo de introspección y acción. No es lineal; tiene avances, pausas y reajustes, pero al final obtenemos lo que deseamos con cariño y amor; además, nos sirve de lección para continuar nuestra vida con cautela. Espero le haya gustado. Nos vemos en otra oportunidad con un nuevo tema. También agradecida por esta columna a Angélica, la que nos pone a reflexionar y llevar la vida en orden debido a sus múltiples temas para este día. Nos vemos.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nathyortiz/23tvY7nHkcGMWLiCwA5e11pEYTcMhkv6gzj2dW5426zxHXWWAUp3odgvvo4QSKm7Xz97u.png)

> **Gracias a todos por leerme, por permitir dar a conocer perspectiva ante el tema mencionado, espero les sirva de algo, un abrazo a todos.**
---

body.title: Social Media : Maintaining A Balance Through Creativity And Self Control.
body.body:
SOCIAL MEDIA AND ITS IMPACT ON DAILY LIFE
Hello #scifimultiverse, happy new week. There is a saying that everything that has an advantage also has a disadvantage. Social media has been a very wonderful tool. It has impacted and continues to impact lives positively and negatively. In the early 90’s, it was mainly seen and known tools to chat and socialise. Some even took it as a tool to while away time, ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNbx42FDz8DaWqqtC3PYU2UWq622z1a7x9Bzw3TTmTEZ7/1782871543682.jpg) [Geralt](https://pixabay.com/images/download/geralt-social-media-1233873_1920.jpg) However, in recent times, social media has transformed to a powerful tool to engage, socialize, advertise, make money and even do a lot of data algorithms. For example, a company can use it to carry out a marketing campaign, survey, and data sample collection through anonymous voting. Secondly, many organisations use social media as their major platform for meetings and information sharing. Applications such as WhatsApp, Google Team App, and Zoom have become useful meeting apps. While the Canva Photoshops and Capcuts are presently important tools for editing and graphics design. Furthermore, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, now known as X, Snapchat, TikTok, and WeChat, to name a few, have become very useful apps in our daily lives. We obtain live updates on happenings around the world from these apps. We also make a reasonable income from them for those of us who monetize their social media handles. Conversely, many people have weaponized social media. They use it as a tool to bully, spread false narratives, intimidate, and body shame others. They also scam and hack into the accounts of unsuspecting individuals and sometimes take over such accounts and use them to scam others. My sister once lost her phone, and before she could block her accounts, they hacked into her Instagram and WhatsApp accounts and scammed people. Personally, I have been impacted significantly by the social media apps I use, especially WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, X, and others. They have made life easier for me and reduced my cost of communication . I communicate with my friends and family at will, individually and collectively. I also engage very well in my professional forums through social media. Additionally, in my church, social media is a helpful tool through which the teachers, fathers, and tens of people execute their activities. The importance of social media can't be overemphasised. Time will fail me to put down all it's benefits. However, there should be self-control as to how people use it. Some are now obsessed with the usage, leaving other things unattended. Some show audio and fake life on the social media, hence putting others to pressure and even depression. I once put a hold on visiting some social media spaces because of the kind of fake life and extreme luxurious lifestyle I was seeing all over my space, putting me under unnecessary pressure. To maintain my sanity, I quietly slipped off the space, worked on myself and came back balanced to handle things better. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeAPwBNv3SXiTzAfD4H4bYS8fPfJbPVnkEPNvSSwdcqhH/1782871781187.png) [WebTechExperts](https://pixabay.com/images/download/webtechexperts-social-media-5187243_1920.png) In conclusion, social media is a beehive of intentional tools per excellence. Our ability to apply ourselves consciously and positively while using it will give the desired result without hurting a fly. Feel free to join [here](https://ecency.com/@scifimultiverse/scifi-multiverse-prompt-week-74-edition-1-or-social-media-and-its-impact-in-daily-life) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbU2hSgaX1Af4R4dWfwNG3TcPhZMquzbJbmqGKqd7BpTd/1782871991446.gif)

body.title: Tech Interface Updates.
body.body:
I have been juggling many tasks and household repairs on top of what I have been writing about here. Still, I do have a few updates as to new sensations, pain and apparitions.

For the most part, things have been calm with no real images or motion pictures going on behind my eyelids. There has been something visual, something new that I will get into in a bit.

As I commented in my last post, I have being killing all power to any wireless devices within range of where I sleep. It has been very infrequent that I feel any kind of buzzing or vibration under the skin while falling asleep or during waking up since having taken those precautions.

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRCQCXB1wfkSHRpAPZRuYZQHqUdavKNXeV4pKMcm8sdrg/image.png)
</center>

The cloth that I used to cover myself in order to protect from those kinds of things did not work at first,  and I'm not sure if it's working now because of how infrequent those sensations have been lately.

I still do keep the cloth on my bed so that I can pull it over myself if I do feel something. When it starts, it is weak, then as time goes on, it builds in strength. Buzzing sensations under the skin usually pulse for a few seconds and the stop.  Then they come back after 7 to 12 seconds.  I still get them from time to time when I have any wireless devices near me.  

I had eliminated all wireless devices for about a month.  I was using an old wired mouse and a ps2 keyboard which made my work a lot slower. 
I recently changed back to those same wireless devices  and I am getting the vibrations under my skin in various places on my limbs and face.  and only during the day.  *Nights, I turn them off*

#### New visual strangeness
One of the new symptoms that I have been seeing or feeling is something to do with the LED monitors, the OLED screens on phones, and with LED lighting.  When it happens, I feel really strange.  It is so annoying that I get up and go to another room or outside.   That completely stops it. 



Imagine if you were looking at a computer monitor through the camera on your tablet.  When you snap a shot, the photo goes mostly transparent and now you have two images in view, one is what is on the monitor, and the other is the mostly transparent photo of what was on the monitor.  Now imaging that those photos are being snapped automatically, beyond your control and that it is not the tablet, it is your eyes.  No device needed.  That is what I am experiencing. 

 That's kind of the sensation that I get when I look at either the LED monitor or at my phone when I'm concentrating on reading something. It is so disturbing that I don't even want to keep reading or working - I have to get up  and look at natural lighting. I hate to say it like this, but it does seem like I'm seeing two dimensions at the same time.

This is one of the strangest feelings I have gotten, although it's not uncomfortable like the buzzing under the skin.

And the last update that I want to bring you is something related to what seems to be a long-term effect or damage from something that happened about two or three months ago.

Back then I would try to fall asleep and I could feel something just below my ankle to the left on my left foot and it was as if something about the size of a silver dollar was under my skin vibrating and buzzing and pulsing at certain intervals..

I tried to shield from it to protect it. Nothing worked, not even the   Faraday cloth that I purchased.   My only recourse in order to get to sleep on those nights was sleeping pills.  It was impossible to fall asleep with that strong sensation on the top side of your foot.

And now, for the last couple of weeks, I notice when I wake up in the morning and I stand up and go to walk, that accepts the same spot where I had felt the vibration feels like the muscles are damaged.

<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTBEJWhWPDhEJPhi2JKgSuszceZDzZbpV79xe9Coto4Qp/image.png)</center>


It feels as though someone was hammering on the top side of my foot. I do not feel it when I wake up.  I feel it when I start to walk or put weight on my foot.    It also hurts if I press on it as if I had a bruise under the skin. There is no visible bruise and the pain goes away within 30 minutes or so.  I am able to go walking on it the rest of the day and it seems normal. But every morning it's back to hurting as if it had been damaged overnight again.

Two of my closest family members know about what has been happening to me, but they are both very skeptical about it being real. A couple of times I did call them in here to feel the spot where the vibrations were happening and it was palpable, but very weak.  They  seem to want to ignore that it is happening.  Believe me, I tried to ignore all of this when it started too.  

I stopped talking about it some time ago so that they are not freaked out.  Bun I have to lot these things somewhere and this is the best place I could think of to do it. 

<center>Everything I write is my own work unless otherwise noted and referenced</center>

body.title: 😝International Asteroid Day! / ¡Día Internacional de los Asteroides! 😎
body.body: > International Asteroid Day is a global event celebrated annually on the anniversary of the Tunguska asteroid impact, which occurred on **June 30,1908.** It is a day that encourages people not only to enjoy everything related to asteroids but also to raise awareness about them and how to protect Earth from future impacts. > El Día Internacional del Asteroide es un evento mundial que se celebra cada año en el aniversario del impacto del asteroide Tunguska, ocurrido el **30 de junio de 1908.** Es un día festivo en el que se anima a la gente no solo a disfrutar de todo lo relacionado con los asteroides, sino también a concienciar sobre ellos y sobre cómo proteger la Tierra de futuros impactos. This observance was established by ***Stephen Hawking, B612 Foundation President Danica Remy, Rusty Schweickart, filmmaker Grigorij Richters, and Queen guitarist Brian May.*** The declaration for this UN observance was also signed by a wide range of celebrities, astronauts, engineers, scientists, technicians, and artists. It was officially inaugurated on December 3, 2014, but was subsequently moved to June 30. > Esta festividad fue creada por ***Stephen Hawking, la presidenta de la Fundación B612, Danica Remy, Rusty Schweickart, el cineasta Grigorij Richters y el guitarrista de Queen, Brian May.*** La declaración para esta conmemoración de la ONU también fue firmada por una amplia gama de celebridades, astronautas , ingenieros, científicos, técnicos y artistas. El 3 de diciembre de 2014 se inauguró oficialmente, pero posteriormente se trasladó al 30 de junio . Let's take a look and learn more about these impressive chunks of rock and metal. Although there are many different types of asteroids, most can be classified as **carbonaceous, siliceous, or metallic asteroids.** - Asteroids can also have smaller particles orbiting them, like tiny moons. - In 2000, NASA's NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft landed on the surface of the asteroid Eros—which is 34 kilometers long—even though it hadn't been designed to do so. - Asteroids are too small to have an atmosphere. It is believed that an asteroid impact wiped out the dinosaurs. - Asteroids are classified based on their chemical composition and the amount of light they reflect. - Asteroids can vary in size, ranging from the size of a pebble to hundreds of kilometers in diameter. - German astronomer Johann E. Bode discovered the first asteroid in 1772; it was named Ceres. - The asteroid belt contains between 1.1 and 1.9 million asteroids larger than half a mile in diameter. It is a great day to look up at the sky or get together with friends and watch one of the many movies about an asteroid apocalypse. > Echemos un vistazo y aprendamos más sobre estos impresionantes fragmentos de roca y metal. Aunque existen muchos tipos diferentes de asteroides, la mayoría de ellos se pueden clasificar en **asteroides carbonáceos, asteroides silíceos y asteroides metálicos.** -Los asteroides también pueden tener partículas más pequeñas orbitando a su alrededor, como pequeñas lunas. -La nave espacial NEAR Shoemaker de la NASA aterrizó en la superficie del asteroide Eros, de 34 kilómetros de longitud, a pesar de no haber sido diseñada para ello, en el año 2000. -Los asteroides son demasiado pequeños para tener atmósfera. -Se cree que el impacto de un asteroide acabó con los dinosaurios. -Los asteroides se clasifican según su composición química y la cantidad de luz que reflejan. -Los asteroides pueden variar en tamaño, desde el de un guijarro hasta tener cientos de kilómetros de diámetro. -El astrónomo alemán Johann E. Bode descubrió el primer asteroide en 1772. Fue bautizado como Ceres. -El cinturón de asteroides contiene entre 1,1 y 1,9 millones de asteroides de más de media milla de diámetro. Es un buen día para mirar al cielo o reunirse con amigos y ver alguna de las muchas películas sobre el apocalipsis de los asteroides. https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/thealliance/SszMQ6lq-thealliance20new20pagebreak.png ## Family Time!

body.title: A Tour of Vargas Square (Eng/Esp)
body.body:
> Walking along the banks of the Manzanares River toward the Gomez Rubio Bridge, I came upon Jose Maria Vargas Square, named after a distinguished Venezuelan who went down in history as the first civilian to serve as president of Venezuela, at a time when the military was vying for power. This square features several massive trees, so large that their roots have lifted the concrete pavement.
![1000123834.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23uFU4pfwDc8Q1gG864YQr9KgDwgNRXyKDuxozpt74D5y9qtW6Gim7k7PfJ5jL6CeUhG6.jpg)
![1000123235.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpLeyGQ2wGKyT18179tiNv8xoBq1MvS8CiBCnKEQm8jY1kmXs2CzKEozDsKDCTeurgF.jpg)
![1000123229.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23tvegZxXSCMsRf1Ck63C5XT1cipKKpEdsAYC6szR3jUHH3ovRnDqzta1bH2XmCZnFxq9.jpg)
From here, you can see the river from a more peaceful vantage point than the one offered by the city center. The square used to have a bust of Dr. Vargas, but it was vandalized, leaving only the pedestal. From this spot, you can head in several directions: in addition to the city center, you can go to Gomez Rubio Avenue, on the way to the barracks, as well as toward the Historic District and the road to Cantarrana.
![1000123234.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EnYRKodCNF8fur2rxwdvCoZKStR2NY1Gq6XD4DKTpuhGvush3PQpyaSgetcxgGVR8wC.jpg)
![1000123233.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqUctQk2PerTUozqJuoLeEs3dMExQs7Y3YaS1vZdpMhN4QqG3VtVtHaMRHF4rpJ9fnx.jpg)
![1000123232.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EnWHTrM19ivHURMtSXC7aDiqCJQUHtUPJTL3Ch2jAauYecBgS7EgCTAPXv7gfCmmbPW.jpg)
![1000123231.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EoChaGri9aUsNtMTDnMQ9xpXvbxotQVDSx8tuMnEZ5dHMVhKGzYWMxN7CedduKsgnZk.jpg)
In this small square, I realize what historical figures mean to the places that were founded in their honor. For us here in Cumana, Jose Maria Vargas doesn’t hold as much significance as Antonio Jose of Sucre, but in the former Vargas state, the image and legacy of this distinguished physician are very important; Vargas Square is very large and is located near the governor’s office.
![1000123225.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EqHyyFcQ68WuzSsTprjkNGhPsjH9VMuEQBUnpLkescU6zFSTbjBMG8SCFZ19XFKisoe.jpg)
![1000123222.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/243q8cXiiMWUMegfGcyqPAD1LTqgQSrfZjb3JNBZ7vDJrwLhCQ5fJLWCB2dAiZ3vqcVrN.jpg)
![1000123219.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23xp6UzP8RByEGwqsK72s9z7CsvK666rh8xC3Gu5y3LTKT9dAsr8DTkwwPrXUWMZD7RNG.jpg)
![1000123218.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpnCo1EXrWWJF6iYfuRu4dCHtNtDJVngoTnu3vr6VAxH7VbhfkrjCEiGBDyxqqZtFfn.jpg)
![1000123220.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EpxpNJGTftBeDLiyA2BMzJPw7a3PDQqHid4xrnGn6CLmeTNuDRhrvUQtMsPcLAztRsN.jpg)
The name Jose Maria Vargas is also used to designate institutions—the largest and most important ones, such as the hospital, a high school, and the sports complex. There is also a Vargas Hospital in Caracas, which is one of the largest in the capital. In Sucre State, on the other hand, the memory of military figures and battles is honored more, pushing into the background the humanists who clearly contributed greatly to the consolidation of the Republic and the advancement of civilization. *** ***
## Versión en Español

> Caminando por las riberas del río Manzanares, en dirección hacia el puente Gómez Rubio, me encontré con la plaza José María Vargas, insigne venezolano que pasó a la posteridad por ser el primer civil que ejerció la presidencia de Venezuela, en una época donde el militarismo pugnaba por el poder. Esta plaza posee algunos árboles de gran magnitud, tanto que las raíces han levantado el piso de concreto.
![1000123834.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/23uFU4pfwDc8Q1gG864YQr9KgDwgNRXyKDuxozpt74D5y9qtW6Gim7k7PfJ5jL6CeUhG6.jpg)

Desde acá se aprecia el río desde una perspectiva más tranquila con respecto a la que se tiene desde el centro de la ciudad. La plaza tenía un busto del doctor Vargas, pero fue vandalizado, dejando solamente el pedestal. Desde este lugar se pueden tomar varias direcciones, además del centro, se puede ir a la avenida Gómez Rubio, camino al cuartel, también hacia el Casco Histórico y la vía a Cantarrana.
![1000123234.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/saavedraa/EnYRKodCNF8fur2rxwdvCoZKStR2NY1Gq6XD4DKTpuhGvush3PQpyaSgetcxgGVR8wC.jpg)

Para nosotros acá en Cumaná, José María Vargas no posee tanto significado como Antonio José de Sucre, pero en el antiguo estado Vargas, la imagen y lo que representa el insigne médico es muy importante, la plaza Vargas es muy grande y está ubicada cerca de la gobernación.

body.title: Historia: El vestido perfecto.(Esp/Eng)
body.body:
# Español

# Saludos amigos💁☀️

¡Feliz día para todos!

Hoy amigos, he querido despedir este mes de Junio, con un pequeño relato esperando que les guste y genere pequeños escalofríos. Disfrútenlo y salud por un Julio de abundantes vibras positivas.

# ✨El vestido perfecto✨
#
<center>
![1782771351636.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23wfquZAbbi5Q8VNAQJJQiJLrARyKiZJdPVwbjvWMFRPFRRQ3sCcLW1KESaAYCq7TvEYv.png)
</center>
#
Caterine llevaba semanas buscando un vestido para la gran fiesta del pueblo, pero el dinero apenas le alcanzaba para los gastos de la casa. Justo cuando estaba a punto de rendirse, una amiga le habló de una pequeña tienda de ropa usada donde, según decía, siempre aparecían verdaderas joyas.

Al entrar, sintió un extraño silencio. El lugar era antiguo, con estantes llenos de prendas olvidadas. Mientras recorría la tienda, un vestido llamó su atención. Era hermoso, elegante y juvenil. En cuanto se lo probó, sintió que le quedaba perfecto, como si hubiera sido hecho especialmente para ella. Sin pensarlo dos veces, lo compró.

La noche de la fiesta todos la admiraban. Nunca se había sentido tan bonita. Pero al día siguiente despertó agotada. Pensó que era el cansancio de haber bailado toda la noche. Sin embargo, los días pasaban y cada mañana tenía menos fuerzas. Subir unos pocos escalones la dejaban sin aliento, y hasta su rostro parecía perder el brillo.

Lo más extraño era que muchas personas que la saludaban todos los días comenzaron a mirarla con duda, como si les costara reconocerla.

Asustada, decidió devolver el vestido.Entró a la tienda y lo dejó en el mostrador.

-Por favor quisiera regresarlo.

La dependienta levantó la vista y la observó durante unos segundos. Luego sonrió con amabilidad y preguntó:

-Disculpe...¿ese vestido se lo llevó usted?

-Sí...vine hace apenas unos días.

La mujer frunció ligeramente el ceño y soltó una pequeña risa.

-Perdone... pensé que era la abuela de la muchacha que se llevó ese vestido.

Caterine sintió que el corazón se le detenía.

-¿Qué...?Soy la misma persona.

Confundida, giró lentamente la cabeza hacia el viejo espejo que estaba junto a la puerta.Y el aire desapareció de sus pulmones. Frente a ella no había una joven. Había una anciana de cabello completamente blanco, el rostro cubierto de profundas arrugas y las manos temblorosas... vistiendo el mismo hermoso vestido juvenil que había comprado para la fiesta.

Llevó las manos hasta su cara. La anciana del espejo hizo lo mismo. Pero cuando Caterine las bajó, la anciana no. Siguió acariciándose el rostro lentamente y sonriendo.

Hasta pronto amigos. ¡Abrazos!💁☀️

Relatos propios de Mary de Luz👻

Imagen resultada en Gemini.
*** 
# English
# Story: The perfect dress.

# Greetings friends💁☀️

Happy day to everyone!

Today friends, I wanted to say goodbye to this month of June, with a little story hoping that you like it and generate little chills. Enjoy it and cheers to a July of abundant positive vibes.

# ✨The perfect dress✨
#
<center>
![1782771351636.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marydeluz/23wfquZAbbi5Q8VNAQJJQiJLrARyKiZJdPVwbjvWMFRPFRRQ3sCcLW1KESaAYCq7TvEYv.png)
</center>
#
Caterine had been looking for a dress for the big village party for weeks, but the money was barely enough for the household expenses. Just when she was about to give up, a friend told her about a small used clothing store where, she said, real jewelry always appeared.

As he entered, he felt a strange silence. The place was old, with shelves full of forgotten clothes. As she was walking around the store, a dress caught her eye. He was beautiful, elegant and youthful. As soon as she tried it on, she felt that it fit perfectly, as if it had been made especially for her. Without thinking twice, he bought it.

The night of the party everyone was admiring her. She had never felt so beautiful. But the next day she woke up exhausted. He thought it was the tiredness of having danced all night. However, the days passed and every morning I had less strength. Climbing a few steps took her breath away, and even her face seemed to lose its brightness.

The strangest thing was that many people who greeted her every day began to look at her with doubt, as if they had a hard time recognizing her.

Scared, she decided to return the dress.He walked into the store and left it on the counter.

-Please I would like to return it.

The shop assistant looked up and watched her for a few seconds. Then he smiled kindly and asked:

-Excuse me...did you take that dress with you?

-Yes...I came just a few days ago.

The woman frowned slightly and let out a small laugh.

-Excuse me... I thought she was the grandmother of the girl who took that dress.

Caterine felt her heart stop.

-What...?I'm the same person.

Confused, she slowly turned her head towards the old mirror by the door.And the air disappeared from his lungs. There was no young woman in front of her. There was an old woman with completely white hair, her face covered with deep wrinkles and trembling hands... wearing the same beautiful youthful dress she had bought for the party.

He brought his hands up to his face. The old woman in the mirror did the same. But when Caterine took them down, the old lady didn't. He kept stroking his face slowly and smiling.

See you soon friends. Hugs!💁☀️

Mary de Luz's own stories👻

|     Genus Ricania      |      Jun 30, 2026      |       Vodrochol, Ullapara, Bangladesh      | 

Hello my dear all friends. Today I am going to share a picture of an insect, I took this picture of an insect quite by accident. I was out for a walk with a friend yesterday afternoon when I was walking along the roadside when my eyes suddenly caught sight of this insect. I stopped to take a picture but my friend had already left me and started walking. I sat near the insect and took several pictures of it.

During observation, I saw this insect sitting quietly at the end of a broken branch. The insect almost blended in with nature, although we suddenly caught sight of the insect. The body structure and color of the insect looked really great. Its beauty was brought out by doing macro photography. It was a sight to enjoy when I saw the insect, it seemed like it had drawn a perfect design in the green nature. Such extraordinary beauty of nature fascinates me.

Now I am sharing some moments of this insect with everyone below, I hope everyone likes it and everyone enjoys it.

body.title: Jugo de papaya remolacha y mango
body.body:
> Feliz miércoles #drinklovers un cordial saludo a todos, espero esten excelente y saludables, animada de estar aquí nuevamente esta comunidad de #Amazingdrinks Hoy preparé un jugo de **Papaya, remolacha y mango** es una bebida Saludable y excelente para subir las defensas. > Happy Wednesday, #drinklovers! Warm greetings to everyone—I hope you’re all doing great and staying healthy. I’m excited to be back here with this #Amazingdrinks community. Today I made a juice with **papaya, beet, and mango**—it’s a healthy drink that’s great for boosting your immune system.
![1001793108.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23xepG7qYXF9JdkX5vN66oJbKDeFHWSTfyumwF9kXWGGHrtdBodkP6WigBywe6LoSMENU.jpg)

>
Este jugo de papaya combinado con Mango y remolacha brinda un sabor delicioso, refrescante y saludable, beneficioso para la salud. Esta combinación tropical es muy rica en vitamina A y C, fibra , hierro, potacio y papaina, enzimas que benefician directamente al organismo. > This papaya juice, combined with mango and beets, offers a delicious, refreshing, and healthy flavor that is beneficial to your health. This tropical combination is very rich in vitamins A and C, fiber, iron, potassium, and papain—enzymes that directly benefit the body.
![1001785856.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23vsNmNc6Dyhkz1TWQfY6MMqx6tS3pnhcBCZkdJZajUg2YAhzJ7n9THUsbRrwMmMZqCHz.jpg)
> * 1 Papaya * 1 Remolacha * 2 Mangos manzanos * azúcar al gusto * Agua * Hielo

> * 1 papaya * 1 beet * 2 apple mangoes * sugar to taste * Water * Ice
![1001785653.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23uQvwe3D7QipTJRkSia6jAtwBGBEcajBSkGngDHoYPzVSdP3xwqJAUPXkqfgvgwh3LD6.jpg)

>

Paso a paso| Step by step.

> 1.- Primero, cortamos por la mitad la Papaya, extraemos las semillas, pelamos y corta,mos en cubos. > First, cut the papaya in half, remove the seeds, peel it, and cut it into cubes.
![1001785654.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/EoK8CvtzmFsqBwddzygiagBS9VGEWBtowyurFNUsTuw4kgzWQ68t4UxfNLkdLztER6U.jpg) ![1001785658.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23wX38vmJPHPoExnFkxw3YqzTKo1ut83qqiTAXBNJjytNj3THwavcuCb1EnB59xy5dyWX.jpg) ![1001785662.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23wX7nMxBT3x6yVuCnfPTULHhgEwycA6yKAC9teqJFXuhcRLuE5B4WzbfjgjAyEyMqjwD.jpg)

>
2.- Seguidamente picamos el mango y remolacha en trozos pequeños, agregamos el agua en el licuadora. > Next, chop the mango and beet into small pieces, add the water and the fruit to the blender.

> ![1001785659.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/EpCBR6wXtK8YJRcPMsuaWEU9dTzCuRLeq5jptFaMh9G3bgH2K9qENmWQhvzPgrFaXCU.jpg) ![1001785660.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/Ep3gCvSzemr4Y4pVjtxtSDRSHHsSdsSDkx4ascKhJfuWFigiPVB4sB85YnDMpzYwMH1.jpg)

3 -Seguidamente, añadimos las frutas troceadas a la licuadora y comenzamos a licuar, agregamos el azúcar y colamos. > Next, add the chopped fruit to the blender and start blending; add the sugar and strain the mixture.

> Servimos con hielo y a disfrutar esta JUGO, tan delicioso como refrescante **ÁNIMATE A PREPARARLO**. Hasta pronto mis Aventureros. >Serve over ice and enjoy this juice, as delicious as it . **GO AHEAD AND TRY IT**. See you soon, my Adventurers.
![1001785849.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/EpEJCuMcmwrigi4jMg94NPdrZE57zJ5qDGxjpSnJhHXEBagc1pHqiSahZUuBvWGdLHf.jpg) ![1001785855.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23xerYGsTfZyaHt6daUvy55XzRzS76r5a9VJyTx1M12YV7Yr65uTnsSjH4cn7Cr6RtcgQ.jpg) ![1001785854.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/23vsYyi7ijzVj8Cqb8RT1AsL7DTGtxT7Z7JSZaaK4RqSrGA8Sbz1wNMfq47hThVpdnmBN.jpg) ![1001785848.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/EoyRPThm94R6MPVr5vwx7NDCyGmuj77bvzaYAtyFMRaVZjRkCeMzR4eMYSChSkPNKDj.jpg) _**Fotos de mi propiedad tomada del celular marca Redmi Note 12// Texto traducido por DeepL**_ >_**Photos of my property taken from the Redmi Note 12/// Text translated by DeepL**_ ![nXPdZ5gM.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/wendyth16/243gG34BgqeoQHKUNUy2zF7avcKpREfBvcQc2uogAk4asyG31MsjUvNDHCLhUynEgzQQC.gif)

body.title: Three Tune Tuesday - Tres canciones de Brendan Perry
body.body:
Mi país, Venezuela, está atravesando uno de sus más duros y dolorosos momentos de su historia contemporánea. Por si fuera poco todo lo sufrido por casi tres décadas, dos terribles terremotos ocurridos el pasado 24 de junio han generado una catástrofe humana, que a estas horas llega a casi 2.000 fallecidos, 10.571 heridos e innumerables desaparecidos. No es nada fácil elaborar posts en estos momentos cuando nuestra atención está puesta en lo que sucede, y menos sobre música, a menos que sea el “Réquiem” de Mozart o Brahms, o un [“Miserere”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wm593SYT-_E) (“Ten piedad”), que, como dice Unamuno: “Un Miserere, cantado en común por una muchedumbre azotada por el Destino, vale tanto como una filosofía”. Noté que hoy es la fecha de nacimiento (30 de junio de 1959) de uno de los músicos británicos que más aprecio: [Brendan Perry](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Perry), que ha hecho una música muy vinculada a lo espiritual, al sentimiento universal, incluso a lo melancólico. Así que me pareció que podía ser un buen motivo para compartir con ustedes tres de sus canciones, de las cuales dejo reproducciones y letras.
![Brandan Perry.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josemalavem/23uFHASUjs15NHBFsAKJWP2NjRjBqhim1sSAaJN9TmkB63hCo83zXqJMjNh6VYBh1WNCx.jpg)
Brendan Perry - [Fuente](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brendan_Perry#/media/Archivo:Brendan_Perry.jpg) - [Licencia](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0)

Lo escuché por primera vez hacia finales de la década del 80 en grabaciones del grupo [Dead Can Dance](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead_Can_Dance), que había fundado junto con la australiana [Lisa Gerrard](https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Gerrard), a quien espero dedicar un post más adelante. Dead Can Dance es, para mí, un grupo musical extraordinario, que cultivó lo que se conoce como Worl Music, tendencia musical que se nutrió de la tradición occidental medieval y de la música no occidental (africana, oriental), con fusiones del rock y el pop. De la producción de este grupo una de las piezas que más me gusta, donde observamos la actuación de Brendan Perry y Lisa Gerrard.
Rakim https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-qHiaoz9su0 https://www.letras.com/dead-can-dance/213270/traduccion.html
Luego de que, lamentablemente, Dead Can Dance se disolviera en 1998, Brendan Perry siguió componiendo y grabando. De su álbum de 1999, Eye Of The Hunter, les comparto dos baladas en las que puede apreciarse la fuerza vocal de Perry, su tonalidad cercana a la interioridad, y el canto al amor y la ausencia.
I Must Have Been Blind https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MtrMGkSxx14 https://www.letras.com/brendan-perry/384089/traduccion.html
Alone / American Dreaming https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h6udpdpV9mE https://www.letras.com/brendan-perry/1664913/traduccion.html

body.title: Genocidal Corruption
body.body: >When I raised this topic about modern sins on Queercoin, I had cyberbullying, cyberscams, etc., in mind. But the truth is, with the recent double earthquake that struck my country (Venezuela), I decided to refocus on something that has never been evaluated as a crime against humanity, though it should be. I am talking about government corruption that, in an emergency situation, contributes to increasing the death toll.

>If a sin currently exists that cannot be redeemed, and that warrants capital punishment, it is precisely what my government has done to my people for 27 years. Before the earthquake, the Venezuelan government had stolen public funds meant for hospitals, leaving many in a state of massive vulnerability during the floods that affected us every 4 or 5 years. They also fired many of the specialized rescue workers and firefighters we currently need, just to keep that money for themselves.

>They have also stolen the humanitarian aid sent by numerous NGOs over three decades, the funds to rebuild La Guaira (after the 1999 floods), the fund for the maintenance of roads and bridges (which are only occasionally repaired before an election campaign and whose maintenance is abandoned after it ends), as well as nearly every damn cent of the oil revenues that have been key to sustaining the country's economy.

>The mass emigration of 7 or 8 million Venezuelans to different parts of Latin America, and the mass deaths in the Darién Gap, are the result of this genocidal corruption. If we add to that the complicity of a corrupt police force and national guard, which extorts street vendors and, in the middle of a disaster, was getting ready to loot the properties of the earthquake victims, we have the complete X-ray of a nation ruled by thieves and murderers.

>I am not the only one saying this. I have seen people in line at the bakery saying that a mother lost her baby because the hospital didn't have the supplies to care for him as they should have. People who have died from diabetes, heart conditions, or strokes because they had no insurance or medicine to treat their health problems. I myself was sick for weeks when everyone was in lockdown due to COVID, suffering from severe stomach pains possibly caused by the contaminated water coming through the pipes of my aunt's apartment. And I wasn't the only one; several residents were in a similar situation. And that was before the earthquake.

>Now it is worse. Every piece of infrastructure that wasn't repaired a year, two, or a decade ago is now a death trap for the rescue workers trying to pull out survivors and the deceased. Every road and bridge that wasn't repaired can collapse at any moment due to the tremors. Every hospital that was left undersupplied now has to send patients to another hospital because they cannot properly help the wounded when they are needed most.

>And that hurts. It hurts to see so much suffering, the product of the greed and immorality of a corrupt elite without the slightest sense of humanity. It hurts to see how the efforts of an entire nation that has crossed one hell after another for three decades are sabotaged by the government.
>I hope that one day we can recover from this tragedy, created not only by the earthquake, but by the monsters who rule us.

>Here is the link to the videos of Sabrina Tortora, a Venezuelan journalist who knows the nightmare of our people.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kh\_ipmP2J-E https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FJYXb3m2hAY Note 1. body.title: Freewill.
body.body: ![ffw.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdfR5VZQZSHZsRx7douBVUhPYAkHeRxfkXzyJRAN9cNVn/ffw.png) I absolutely love the way God works.... So I had this big ol' blog post planned for today. Ideas written down, notes ready to go. But then I saw a notice from @meno where he asked me if I had checked out the new version of @snapie for iOS. I immediately downloaded it, started poking around and then....Came across [his blog that he just wrote today](https://snapie.io/@meno/where-choice-ends-and-belief-begins-972404). I'm so glad I did.... Because he brought up a topic that is of serious discussion within Christianity. The question is simple...**Do we have a choice?** This thing called 'freewill' is always up for debate, even within secular circles. So please note, while Meno's post was addressing both religious beliefs and non-religious beliefs, all I can ever talk about it my experience... ### Freewill. This goes against a popular doctrine within Christianity called 'predestination'. Now if you open up your Strong's Concordance and find the word, you will see it appears 4 to 6 times...And always by the apostle Paul. Now while I admit, there is other places in scripture that seem to bring up this idea that God has predestined the elect only, it's always something that never sat well with me. Before people get the pitchforks...I do not consider this doctrine salvational. Meaning you can believe it, or not...Christ is still what matters for salvation. But I digress... The reason I have a massive issue with this doctrine comes simply for the general theme of the bible... Choose this day whom you will serve. From Genesis to Revelation the entire narrative is God's fallen race, choosing to worship Him instead of anything (or anyone) else. This is...1 John 4:8...God is love. You cannot get love if there is no choice. Think about this logically...God is love, so does He want automatons worshipping Him? How is that love? Now someone will argue, we don't get to define love, God does... AMEN! God....IS...Love. Love is not mindless forced worship. It simply cannot be. As for the word predestined, remember who wrote that word in the NT...And for that, 2 Peter 3:15-16....You might wanna look that up ;) Again, when push comes to shive I truly believe this is not a salvational issue. However it does speak about the character of God. And the reason there are so many non-believers out there is perhaps because, God's character has been under attack since the garden of Eden. Random thoughts from hanging out in the new Snapie app, and sitting in my hotel room. I hope it stirs some conversation and thought :) ---
