body.title: Three Tune Tuesday ~ The Human League ~ Adrian Wright ~ Birthday Boy #97
body.body:
#### Good evening, everyone! ##### Welcome to my #TTT #ThreeTuneTuesday entry! The day is almost over, but I’m not about to let another Tuesday go by without posting something here in this community! How’s your week going so far? Is everything going well? A lot is happening around here when it comes to weather events… Europe is going through a very difficult period with extreme temperatures across many latitudes in various European countries. Some countries and cities have already broken all-time high temperature records since temperature records began. Here in Portugal, even though we went through a heat wave just a little less than three weeks ago, maximum temperatures are expected to hover around 40 degrees in some cities across the country over the next few days, through Friday. But the problem won’t be so much the maximum temperatures as the narrow temperature range, which will mean we’ll spend our nights with temperatures above 20°C. In other words, we’re in for some truly tropical nights. But let’s move on to the topic of today’s post. Today, singer Philip Adrian Wright turns 70. In 1978, he was invited to join the avant-garde band “The Human League.” At that time, Wright was brought on as visual director to produce the entire lighting design for the shows that “The Human League” was set to perform. When the group split in 1980 to form two bands, “The Human League” and “Heaven 17,” Wright found himself forced to become a musician, teaching himself to play keyboards. He ended up co-producing many of the songs with Oakey, including the one I’m sharing here today—a track well known to everyone: “Don’t You Want Me.” Wright remained with the group until 1986, by which time he was one of the band’s key members. He then moved into the film industry and later into design. In 1982, he won a Brit Award as a member of “The Human League” for Best British Breakthrough Act of the Year. I hope you enjoy the selection of songs I’ve chosen today. I invite you to take a trip down memory lane with the three tracks I’m sharing here. I hope you enjoyed this latest post. Take care, and see you soon! ### Bem Hajam🍀 https://youtu.be/QqqBs6kkzHE https://youtu.be/v-Oq3ORqAC0 https://youtu.be/uPudE8nDog0

The post goes for Three Tune Tuesday challenge run by @ablaze. body.title: Watches that accompany my days
body.body:
>

![photo_5053075822167657533_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/24246PqH7uFKhVAFGXJ1xvwj6ustTaz1cTNxJo8GhbEa4CC9DDTieygmMNUto8sMLoG7D.jpg)

Among the oldest timekeeping devices used by humanity were sundials and hourglasses. But today, I am starting my post with something different: a sugar timer.

Hello to the wonderful **Hive Collector** community. As June draws to a close, I wanted to contribute to the monthly theme proposed by our dear @mipiano.

That’s right, friends: instead of sand, this timer contains very fine sugar. It takes three minutes for the contents to flow from top to bottom when flipped. This promotional item has sat on the wooden living room table since I was a child.

It draws the eye, yet it has been handled so much—and dropped on the floor so often—that the resulting dings on its corners are visible in my photo.

![photo_5053075822167657532_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23zSBzBiz7ZDnG64QG4pL99aDZmmy3wm7swez5SLceDptnbReqTXhFnwGi3jtJCk5Ag5B.jpg)

## Dive Watches

For everyday wear, I like a watch with a rugged build—one that won't break from a minor bump or impact and is water-resistant.
On a daily basis, I usually wear a vintage digital **Casio**: the DW-5600E, a well-known, all-terrain model.

![photo_5053075822167657544_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23qrNAzgAktCi5bLaBQvLCmWFoczG5ERnPBWNu2XxonsaCfCiTXPnZUrSRSH8EmPTdy5U.jpg)

When I go to the pool or the beach, or go snorkeling, I like to wear the **Lucien Piccard** watch—which is water-resistant to 200 meters—or the **Seiko Kinetic**.

![Lucien Piccard.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23ynSfDC8KeXtS6Va4746vvoMqzRGCBFq9xQQSzyQnmN4EWeD4mw2VytqBGZArLaVMouy.jpg)

![photo_5053075822167657534_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23z7NJWiFzsyTskPr2QxxDMC1GrBvc19N4HVwsN1ZnQq52YNDx6fDjCrHVCKy59rRemZE.jpg)

For scuba diving, I switch to a watch capable of withstanding higher pressure—one that also features a rotating bezel to help track dive time. 
I can use either of these two watches: the **Casio \

(model 6309)** or the 200-meter **SteelDive**; both are automatic models. When diving with compressed air tanks—for instance, at a depth of 20 meters—our bodies and our watches (including the dive computer) are subjected to a pressure of 3 ATA (atmospheres absolute). This is because the two atmospheres of hydrostatic pressure are added to the atmospheric pressure exerted on the sea's surface. ![photo_5053075822167657531_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23xe5smeaoJvdqfFJFjnR9HjWcpaR4eiGXT79MVjow55vHqEE4juPMr4xfBBLccaqtHAH.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657538_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23uQJLeCMj4e9vJVmpdwp8AUiugLfmcqEHPZFnzVE2tTTtE1xJwUVnohaWNzWae3Q7YRC.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657539_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23wqEWdrKvuGfxiuKHaDqg8BRxUjjM6XUCuhhqc3VZc8zMat9B3cv7fcWKjGUg3Tix19i.jpg) This **Citizen** watch, designed for diving, was a gift from a Polish man—a professional diver and a friend of my mother. It served me well for several years and comes with an interface that connects to a computer to display dive data. ![photo_5053075822167657552_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23wgUWuLFTJEXFfthAj5ETb8xz9v4oAtEnLRy3V8emp2vRv9D5apTcmAncAV7LShHGuNz.jpg) ## Swiss Watches Throughout history, Swiss watchmaking has stood at the global pinnacle thanks to the quality of materials used, as well as the design and precision of the movements. Brands such as **Patek Philippe, Rolex, Omega**, and **Cartier**, among others, are at the forefront of the industry and are the most renowned. ![photo_5053075822167657540_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23wC3R4jdSE7hV6BWRk9ym4vZx8AEX8tW8AHFPsYXBA6YvmgRoaw4MLwjinKCvekfGPkA.jpg) ## My Father's Watches My father wore several watches throughout his life. Some were Russian models sold in **Cuba**, such as this **Poljot** and another—a **Vostok**—that I still have. My father also wore this **Michele** watch. ![photo_5053075822167657618_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23vhqH6wgGDWUadDKnyozMQVn9i6H7giXNFcPnvbrePPnNsetRAUnJNXxn26zJmoQqXNG.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657619_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23u5xWup9iT39ZzbA9X7XDHojQTkRuc9QeRfau8XboWpzs3PfZW635YWvVC8UPL7JafYY.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657620_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23u5xwNuPBAsYBVm9fK1yJFMHahMpVmB3dMsGBcgZvx8zzJ5oJxtCMpZ7zhtEC3FCoikJ.jpg) But of them all, the one that holds the most sentimental value for me is this Swiss watch from **Baume & Mercier**—a prestigious watchmaker founded in 1830 and renowned for its craftsmanship, lending its products an air of great luxury and elegance. Today, they are highly sought after by collectors. My grandfather gave this automatic watch to my father to wear at his medical practice. He had a solid 18K gold bracelet custom-made, featuring his initials. This maintained the golden harmony of the watch case, which was gold-plated in the same karat. ![photo_5053075822167657541_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23y8wfSG6yvtsKprNnRata1ECaff6Hsd7veTmYg8EHUXkhJfbq6RTpkVKMcPV5xWi2Lzu.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657542_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23x1B2cmAHCwEN8nTFfPELSJCCQazMa8hEvqvDoF2bErXB7LYmNe4Kk4E7SyYVgmZPbtt.jpg) ## Women's Citizen Watches ![photo_5053075822167657546_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23xevnAPPDz9XnM8Ba8N2HhBkx6CwZ4MCm1DwTVHxiHmoQ3k4JsuZCMr52uc5uuDaUXPy.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657548_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23xVCnT1S4r728WN5RQ4gW8vBcmVNcsGvDrVHp9uVNrrkGCGtN1b8xcCjdGHMyken76JC.jpg) ## My Mother's Watches: This watch is from the brand Vernier (**United States**), known for fashion watches with attractive designs that aim to follow European trends. I really like its appearance, especially the silver-colored metal bracelet that opens and closes with a snap-lock mechanism. ![photo_5053075822167657556_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/242Y9vS6CcbU7PMhXmeWsCL6g7PCZ4a4tGMyB5SyFrs41GZscRsr6TR2cWYkoENhY6Bnd.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657554_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23ydEbSZP5Wh2Hx9J7CdMgkM4zHNNZgFiCj11zqQ1V8NAkktbLdRyiFw5xDUvLUkttaUk.jpg) I will never forget how happy she was when I gave her this Japanese **Q&Q** watch. She wore it for many years, and it still works. ![photo_5053075822167657537_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23xL2wtPujV2Tm9ownipB671PoSjEssFo1JjSHuo9BnNF4eFeVKjWo8o8jQ5yMhX1JZBz.jpg) ## Dress watches I really like this American watch from the brand **Michele**. Its case and luxurious bracelet were crafted from top-quality steel. ![photo_5053075822167657536_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23yTsjifHsMFLZ8sAW3bXPGoVj4zMjptFCsi8uKj5DKBsFBqqYALY5QegyEtGpbw1f6DW.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657535_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23x1MvcazgNzKYujUjQyTorZVViMgQDGCmuwXvLh5QUnrPAjtxLogQfb4dV2VTjKXutnQ.jpg) This watch from the Italian brand **Emporio Armani** features a rectangular case and a white dial, creating a beautiful contrast with its black leather strap. ![photo_5053075822167657586_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23wqq5SuXGsdDhAMVHKnVBnWL2s61XsSPkyqhBrtKdfVntsM9Bm6ywTE2nDvVNZShq12C.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657587_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23wgS3rzQ91MaaJV7JUYDPwSftCHbXcxjZryMbMCTtGpuu91hKp7p95rgZUVJ7XK5eExX.jpg) This **Guess** watch is truly beautiful, featuring high-quality steel and a captivating design. The movements for these watches are imported from **Switzerland**. ![Guess.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23xekFtqbRi262oDRouCmgJJbj6Ei3Zs9hks9WZmCAjXuzPvMu46BuNPp59FTWYFmcxQE.jpg) ## Cuervo y Sobrinos Watch The **Cuervo y Sobrinos** brand has been active since 1882, when **Ramón Fernández Río-Cuervo** established a family business in Havana. They imported movements from **Switzerland** and customized the watches at their jewelry store in **Cuba**, thereby building a brand identity that garnered worldwide acclaim. This **Roskopf** model is a pocket watch that has been adapted for use as a wristwatch. It is a manual-wind timepiece; its bone-colored dial, Roman numerals, and distinctive hand design give it a highly attractive look. ![photo_5053075822167657557_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23wC9MCBDvq3Ceu4YRavrR8Ui5DRJxRXg4FmTPesHjg3A18vVwFtvG91RTAHPGfNoqxJT.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657558_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/242hWRxvhaPAoJ27wqk8qWoP5QQszF83GsJro98TuyUA8zG9kTqWu3yvJLHxmW8KzeS4j.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657559_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/242ruTZsCdcELrR56Rnh8bF9WFRZPJ3DAYAFQXMmvrUNBF9rVqtbo1wkdM6Qj9ndREBj5.jpg) ![photo_5053075822167657560_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23zS7YiucArXAzLEtpwkzXacEME5W8MVoRiD7Qkce7VjUxnT5pYUWFkBegLm5ZjmM7fSs.jpg) ## Other watches: I gave this **Q&Q** to my wife, and it’s still keeping time, too. They are battery-operated watches, but they perform very well as long as the battery has sufficient voltage to run. ![photo_5053075822167657545_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/243qAkkmoZBfuq5cw5oCkmuQgh1qnGf7bkmNULEBryyHERPV3NcigDTV8X9DJVU6VMBQ9.jpg) This all-blue **Movado** watch features a metal strap with a magnetic clasp. ![photo_5053075822167657551_y.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/242NueSP5tFVf6UnyBhiwfmufyJJtxxXMVRXc6o6C5NrHEVkr4hmNJw3PnzPdtmAkTLpu.jpg) ## Wall Clocks Wall clocks simply had to be included in this post. They have graced the walls of my home for years. They all still run, and their wooden bodies—along with the sounds they produce—transport our minds back to the past, to the days when my parents were young. There are American, German, and Russian models, among others from various countries. Each one holds stories that I have already shared in previous posts. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/EokezQfTzebdjTUfsF4xSXHTYwV2krdAMzaXiKF6RqdTggK52Rd1vJGBHR3rLbVAXs1.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/48XfDARsz9365AE4pKF3KfeErYZ65hqmi1XTWwJdxJPP5HsjU9of5cDRJPHvL7JszW.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23zkyDWhSWJ7Ams5rNxdWMDXfsn4bkxrp3dYavkSmzM1E3MPCkwXV6JWNE3LX8Y7efmSR.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23zS7UREDXMjhRv7NHLjKvXgvqkJya3uFqQoefpxAXKMJQuZQ5cNpcxdKgXS4uqxDSo44.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23x19AfRezhuzVCW8xzD1CqgrUGr9jxKdSaTzFbEeCkF7kizsv7e9eQNeNoCXzbrgJBwB.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23xAY7pGeUP8DYunzLxB39Ze5ELLM8CuZjRpJnq2i9iXYAe1rHdgttcn3qLDfvAghFy7k.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/23ydA1wpyKwxALNwdR4Kn3rNa3XtRyi1xRaqGeqmiio2SijuHZaNc1BBSwVAxGtSv41HT.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/EoyQ2GE9xgUDp9LWbgM8ERyuZreyJtNk37gdQHDfCxM87G3TBdy7AduBEbQXChRS4WF.png) ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/abrunet/48UHXfRXs3heeCegYaE9vRk84w7QQMLU5Gsr7dXeeQxz1n3W7byu8JzdaoSndGGD12.png) Well, thanks to those who read my posts and for the chance to make a small contribution to the month's theme, which wraps up today. body.title: “Silver Adventures”- Captain Joshua Slane – 30JN26- 'We Come In Peace!'
body.body:
)...Continued...

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZHtxYf3JhtK9bqyejMpSegrXT7VuRthmozc6DwvgRSYR/image.png)

*[Last time...]*

There, on the bank of the river, Chief Minetoh stood with a tall staff, surrounded by forty or fifty warriors armed with bows. Their gaze was northward, downstream. In the distance, a tiny craft was rowing its way up the eastern bank, five crewmen on-board were clearly visible.

“So…the white devils come!” (Translated) The Chief muttered as he watched their approach.

Closest to his side was the warrior Running Fox who scowled and spat on the ground. Beside him was the small boy, Little Grey Wolf who couldn’t help but smile slightly in excitement...

*(See: https://hive.blog/leofinance/@joshuaslane/silver-adventures-captain-joshua-slane-29jn26-memorandum-of-understanding )*

〰️⛵〰️ ⛵〰️ ⛵ 〰️⛵〰️

![aaaa.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma2iBt1QohAbfr4RLi4kbm4e6TjaXUgVAdFqWQTcoa5M6/aaaa.jpg)
![river.5.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZYH5VuqDwRFhHwRFKkvHuEWGuHJH6FGhHvcYEX2EZGRd/river.5.jpg)
*[On the River Niagara…]*

By the time the dinghy made its way upstream towards the main Seneca Village, the crowd of warriors standing about Chief Minetoh had grown to several hundred.  They were angry, they were bitter and all of them had blood in their eyes!  They stomped their feet in a steady rhythm that echoed across the river in an ominous rumble! If it were not for the strength and wisdom of their Chief, they would have surely rushed into the river and killed the brave crew of the Silverton!
![crowd.angry.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWcDwEvq99LAkUo1ye7UKH3FhhJq8UjnV3n75kzh7uJT9/crowd.angry.jpg)
But Minetoh knew that any such action, however satisfying to his people, would bring disaster down on the entire tribe. He feared the great ‘fire-sticks’ on the ship and had no inclination to test them again.
![cannons.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbEDBjVKm62X3GW35VtYk5xznFvRipAswYhPovhSxsri4/cannons.jpg)
As the dinghy finally drew near its final destination, Commander Kerrislravenhill sitting in the bow held her pistol pointed upward, at shoulder level…
![pistol.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZARSJukp5SS95eUHqEGbztKVUYhTBy7QAWaV2kFkvUmJ/pistol.jpg)
*“Here we are.....at the site of previous encounter!”* Lieutenant Bleujay whispered to Warrant Officer Lupega, *“If those squaws get a hold of me.....I am dead! There is nothing that quite matches up to the fury of women in battle! Thank goodness we are armed to the teeth!”*

![Bleujay.11..jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYLLPRga885GioJu1KrPxQQqT2ULKDmYikGVEzEGkrrtz/Bleujay.11..jpg)

“I've had some problems here, and I'm stubborn. I admit I'm not very pleasant when I'm difficult, so here I am, and I'll stay here!” Lupega whispered back.

![Lupega.10..jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNdxqgy2pHSRRuJrzSByYdRKaSRJKgy3f5z6KtTR1pwd1/Lupega.10..jpg)

*“Cut the small talk men! Get ready to throw a line!”* 
![Galligan-19.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma7Z1CqwHyH6qxJuHnbioBWogo3c4oUt93WQjzRrrMtyD/Galligan-19.jpg)
Commander Galligan ordered as he steered the small boat in towards shore not twenty feet from where the Chief was standing.

The bow turned quickly as the strong current moved against it and in a moment the bow-keel ran-up on the gravelly shoreline. Kerrislravenhill threw a line ashore with one hand while still holding her pistol with the other. The warriors glanced down at the rope momentarily, marveling at its tight weave before one finally picked up the loose end and pulled the dinghy up higher onto dry ground.

Galligan was the first man out, jumping the side-rail and wading through the shallows, heading directly towards the Chief. A quick blocking maneuver by four warriors was dismissed with a wave of Minetoh’s hand and Galligan stepped up to greet him. A hand-elbow-hand shake brought a slow quiet to the press of warriors as their leader accepted the visit of the strangers.

Kerrislravenhill, Bleujay, Lupega and Trumpman climbed out of the boat and walked over behind Galligan. 

Quickly recognizing Bleujay, the warrior Running fox lunged forward and uttered an unknown insult. Kerrislravenhill cocked her pistol and pointed it directly at his forehead! 
![Running-fox.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbBcJM9bh7oPv6U9WZyCNrWGVvSEnTWttdWvzByP86Gyc/Running-fox.jpg)
![kerrislravenhill-4.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVQWn9ghyfDdkDZT3Bbt7nXkpgyatrZ6ky5m3adX57EbY/kerrislravenhill-4.jpg)

**“No!”** *(Translated)* 
![Chief Minetoh.4.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmScxW7Jc6C5MJXk8eoN4nJjPf3w5YJfEu8ewdWXmEhiVZ/Chief%20Minetoh.4.jpg)
The Chief quickly rebuffed and gave Running Fox a hard look that sent him stepping back and pursing his lower lip in frustration.

Bleujay’s heart pounded and for a brief moment, a flash of fear from her past experience flitted through her mind, but then slowly began to fade as Galligan released the Chief’s embrace and held both hands up high in the air…

***”We come in peace!”***
![Anchor-epilog.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZBrzRNzCK8GohnVKkT77B6MtydmLYNuvDuWSaEFa1shm/Anchor-epilog.jpg)

body.title: Mensaje diario de 5  minutos: no refleja la realidad / 5 Minute Freewrite: not representative of the facts
body.body:
>



# Ilusión

​

#


En ocasiones las personas experimentan situaciones desafortunadas que no pueden predecir; es evidente que ninguno quiere sufrir, sentir dolor o tristeza, pero la vida está llena de sorpresas que sin razón aparente llegan y golpean fuerte. Los seres humanos a pesar de todo han demostrado que pueden caer en el hoyo y tener la capacidad de salir de allí, incluso fortalecidos; siendo entre muchas una de las tantas cualidades que los caracterizan y si necesitan llorar, gritar, quejarse eso está bien, sin embargo, muchas veces lo ocultan muy dentro de sí para no afectar a otros sobre todo si son sus seres queridos.

Cuantas veces no le ha tocado a una mamá fingir felicidad frente a sus hijos para no transmitirles tristeza o decir que no tiene hambre solamente para que ellos tengan su pan aunque eso **no refleja la realidad** hay verdades tan duras que no son necesario decirles y menos a un niño y sobre todo si es tu hijo. Ante esto quizás surjan cuestionamiento sobre mentir cuando y como porque hay que decir siempre la verdad, pero una madre sabe todo lo que ella es capaz de aguantar y hacer por sus hijos. En medio de una devastadora tragedia te ves sola en medio de la nada sin techo, sin comida y en lo único que piensas es en proteger y arropar a los que amas.

Les dices aunque suene a una ilusión que todo estará bien y que esa tormenta pronto pasara, es tanta la Fe y la esperanza puesta en esas palabras que logras que en medio de tanta dificultad vean más el vaso medio lleno que vació. Hay realidades que de momento es mejor disfrazarlas hasta poder cambiarlas, que tan malo puede ser buscar darle una sonrisa a un pequeño niño en medio de tanta tristeza, así que sé la luz y la ilusión para todo aquel que esté en oscuridad hoy.
​

​<center>![WhatsApp Image 2022-05-12 at 3.28.50 PM.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeucn6MeLy6DkeFM7A2nU8vB9xADUBt8Yr6bzbsja2DRK/WhatsApp%20Image%202022-05-12%20at%203.28.50%20PM.jpeg)</center>



# Excitement



#
Sometimes people find themselves in unfortunate situations they cannot predict; clearly, nobody wants to suffer, feel pain or sadness, but life is full of surprises that come out of the blue and hit hard. Despite everything, human beings have shown that they can fall into a dark place and still have the ability to climb out of it, even emerging stronger; this is just one of the many qualities that characterise them. And if they need to cry, shout or complain, that’s fine; however, they often hide these feelings deep inside so as not to upset others, especially if those others are their loved ones.
​
How many times has a mother had to pretend to be happy in front of her children so as not to convey her sadness, or say she isn’t hungry just so they can have their bread – even though that **doesn’t reflect reality**? There are truths so harsh that it isn’t necessary to tell them, especially to a child – and all the more so if it’s your own child. Faced with this, questions may arise about lying – when and how – because we’re always told to tell the truth, but a mother knows exactly what she is capable of enduring and doing for her children. In the midst of a devastating tragedy, you find yourself alone in the middle of nowhere, without a roof over your head or food, and the only thing on your mind is protecting and caring for those you love.
​
You tell them – even if it sounds like wishful thinking – that everything will be alright and that this storm will soon pass; there is so much faith and hope in those words that, in the midst of such difficulty, you help them to see the glass as half full rather than half empty. There are realities that, for the time being, are best disguised until we can change them. What’s so wrong with trying to bring a smile to a little child’s face amidst so much sadness? So be the light and the hope for everyone who is in darkness today.
​

#

body.title: My BusyBees & SlothlySavers Weekly Update - 2026 Week 26
body.body:
The #SaturdaySavers programme run with huge dedication and commitment by @shanibeer came to an end with the close of 2025. 

But there are a couple of initiatives to keep the motivation going !

I've decided to post them in the BusyBees Community. This is a community set up to support @zakludick's tireless work in encouraging and teaching newer Hive users. Additionally, I'm adding the #SlothlySavers tag and linking my updates in their weekly update post, because that's another place where former #SaturdaySavers are gravitating to.


![Busybees2.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/EppLbzgN3V6scyZCA4g2e4EXmenmK4hGjT5PWLkJ3TgrcC5UMmHQZ3AGpQRKTXqV8xb.jpg)

Image by [Rebekka D](https://pixabay.com/users/castleguard-2970404/?utm_source=link-attribution&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=image&utm_content=1537694) from [Pixabay](https://pixabay.com//?utm_source=link-attribution&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=image&utm_content=1537694)


![Hive Divider3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/243C5mWFmzYKkxg4arJr6HtnfHGJpnth33F4sSek1XxEQS3vHpdjcuokqyKGz3jFHfMZf.jpg)


Here's a screenshot of last week's progress;


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/EpVGMDVngLDbyUrceZ4HV1UuraNDsDHZcpBxZ2gtHapy7w6t7kTkVykQiivRNTmXHF9.png)




![Hive Divider3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/243C5mWFmzYKkxg4arJr6HtnfHGJpnth33F4sSek1XxEQS3vHpdjcuokqyKGz3jFHfMZf.jpg)

### How Did The Week Go ? ###

Well I'm a couple of days late posting this update, as expected. This last weekend I was away at a re-enactment event. It's actually a wonderful feeling to totally step away from modern technology and the crazy hustle of 21st century life for a couple of days. I only touched my phone once, to take a couple of photos, and I didn't even have to put my glasses on for a whole 48 hours 😁

The only slight downside is that I came home absolutely exhausted and with a huge amount of kit cleaning and repairs to do. I spent yesterday evening doing the urgent stuff, like cleaning the musket so nothing had the chance to corrode. Then slept. Lots. So now I feel relatively human again, and actually quite energised.

In Hive terms, there's not a huge amount to report, because although I did a couple of posts, most of last week's spare time was taken up trying to get ahead with work and pulling everything together for the event. But putting some effort in the previous week certainly paid dividends, with my stack of HIVE and HP increasing by 168 (compared to 68 the week before).

It's also exactly halfway through the year. Most of my goals are on track, with two notable e3xceptions. Posting is a bit below where it needs to be. More effort required ! Additionally, HBD is a complete failure, but that's because the picture has totally changed since the start of the year and I've turned most of my HBD stack into HIVE. I'd say the two cancel out and if I hadn't done that both would be on track instead of one massively down but the other massively up.

Also, I'm so late posting this that.... tomorrow is HPUD day ! 😁



![Hive Divider3.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/alonicus/243C5mWFmzYKkxg4arJr6HtnfHGJpnth33F4sSek1XxEQS3vHpdjcuokqyKGz3jFHfMZf.jpg)

body.title: FreeBeings DAO is live, and built in the open
body.body:
You're looking at FreeBeings DAO. FreeBeings.io is building it in the open, on the platform it creates, and this project is that work made public. Watch the DAO take shape, and help steer it.

![freebeings-dao-cover](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNvq4Z82CqgQ12typvkiRAMvmQ5FTfdh2doxJKduLzPPE/freebeings-dao-cover-art-preview.png)

It started as FreeSpace, a dApp begun before things stalled. It's back under its real name. The working title is gone, and the DAO is what it was always becoming.

What it is: the working home of the FreeBeings community, where ideas for positive change find the people who'll build them. You join with your Hive account, then start or join projects, discuss, vote, and post updates. It runs on Hive, under your own account, open and yours to keep.

How it's built: in the open. The roadmap is public, polls show where the community stands, and the conversation happens in the discussion room. We say what we decide and why. As the platform matures, FreeBeings governance will run through here too.

So this is where you watch and shape what FreeBeings DAO becomes.

Join the discussion, at [dao.freebeings.io](https://dao.freebeings.io).

*Live and let live, freely.*

body.title: Politically Weaponised 30th June March
body.body:
/></center>

**This is Johannesburg today and red is not a good color because it normally depicts danger. If i had seen this earlier I would not have driven through Katlehong which I did this afternoon and saw what was happening on the ground.**





Today was the 30th June and we saw the March and March anti migrant protests taking place in the streets across South Africa. I never intended to be part of this and avoid bumping into any of the marches. 

This morning we had a group of around 5000 armed wielding marchers move past our one warehouse premises with no incident. We were asked to visit the magistrates court this afternoon to collect some papers for our legal case and had no idea the court was in Kathlehong and a hot spot for trouble. During the drive we were ushered through by police whilst passing by a large group of people marching holding various primitive weapons which included pangas. This would be very intimidating for any foreigners in close proximity and why most have left or are in hiding. A peaceful march whilst carrying items that can kill you is a mixed signal.

The court was open, but the staff had left at 10 am this morning so nothing was open due to the threat of possible trouble. The organisers of the March to March protest stated that this would be peaceful and was more about highlighting the numbers of illegal migrants within the borders of South Africa. During the march they would like to point out crime hot spots and drug dens to the police in order to make their community more safer. This is not an unreasonable demand and I do think the intentions were good, but this was hijacked by various smaller political parties and the government.

The government on the one hand says peaceful marches with no deadlines yet they are the ones who have been upping their spot checks on illegal migrants which they had never done prior to this. Once the 30th June was the date for the marches it became the date to remove illegals across the country under the pretense of their safety.

The government had to be seen as pro active with the illegal undocumented migrants because the people of South Africa are not happy. This was a powder keg that was going to explode at some point which would leave the police useless as they could not contain the country wide uprising. The difference between here and Europe is this is not far right or far left or racist as it is Africans showing their grievances on something that is clearly wrong in how this has been handled.

The problem is not South Africa but more the countries where these millions of migrants have come from that needs to be addressed. South Africa can not handle an influx of people on this magnitude and any realist will see that this was never going to end well.

I know there are millions of migrants here documented or not documented which makes no difference with the locals on their feelings. Nigeria thinks there are 5 million Nigerians in South Africa which is a scary thought because the SA government thought they only had or they reported that there were only 5-6 million migrants in South Africa. Nigeria is middle Africa so logic tells you the neighboring countries numbers are going to be that much higher. Zimbabwe would have to be much more than 10 million, Mozambique in their millions along with Malawi and Zambia so what is the real number as this is far bigger than anyone really thought. Over 20 million is realistic which represents 1/3rd of the total legal population in SA so no wonder there is problems and the crime rate is so high along with a high unemployment rate.

The 30th June addresses the issues, but does not fix the problem and now is the time to use this opportunity to remove undocumented people on mass as soon as possible. The people know how bad this is and one can see why they are that upset. Imagine your country having 30% extra people who have no right to be there and why there are service failures due to the extra people as the systems are not capable of processing these numbers.

links.title: ¡Deja Salir tus Emociones!
links.body:
> 
	
*Hola amigos, espero se encuentren bien. En lo que concierne a mí, estoy en un momento que no basta solo con llorar, gritar o sencillamente orar. Nuestro país vive algo tan extraño que solo Dios sabrá por qué tanto sufrimiento.*

***Terremotos,*** que el solo hecho de escribir esa palabra genera en mí tanta angustia. No vivo en la ciudad capital donde sucedieron los hechos, ni cerca; digamos que a unas 12 horas, pero las noticias han generado en mí un vaivén de emociones que no sé cómo explicarlas; es un duelo, un duelo que no se superará tan pronto.

He querido desahogarme un poco viendo esta actividad interactiva que nos permite dejar salir un poco lo que llevamos dentro a través de una imagen.

**Nos han propuesto cuatro imágenes, pero he escogido solo una.**


![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXFrr4r2SLDMjXCdVQwoJ57LYsjXMpCEGmaGSVn6wrDmj/image.png)

 [IMAGEN 4 de Pixabay-Steve_a_johnson](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/basura-reciclaje-frustraci%C3%B3n-3259455/)

He escogido esta imagen siguiendo el hilo de lo que les he comentado sobre la situación de nuestro país. Venezuela es un país que por muchos años ha sufrido y ha surgido de esos sufrimientos. Han sido de todo tipo: económico, social, político, de todo, pero jamás pensé que este desastre natural traería consigo tantas muertes de personas de todas las edades y esto es lo más asombroso para todos.

Esta herida profunda que nos sacude a todos, mucho más allá del movimiento de la tierra. Es una tragedia que nos deja sin palabras, viendo cómo la vida, en un segundo, se desmorona. Y es allí donde entra lo que siento con esta imagen, estos acontecimientos: es como una pequeña libreta que puede arrugar y arrancar páginas enteras de un libro que apenas se estaba escribiendo.



Mirar esa libreta abierta, rodeada de hojas rasgadas y arrugadas, toma en mí un significado. Es como ver escrituras y fragmentos de la vida de quienes yacen en el suelo, un sueño que fue arrebatado, las historias de quienes ya no están para seguir escribiendo.

Cada una de estas personas que partieron en estos días tenía su libreta de vida abierta sobre la mesa. Con escritura de planes para mañana, metas para el mes que viene y sueños con sus familias; terminar un proyecto, iniciar un negocio o simplemente una lista de compras para llenar la despensa.

Estas páginas llenas de letras han sido arrebatadas con la fuerza de la naturaleza; la naturaleza es ciega e implacable. Esas hojas arrugadas nos demuestran que cada día debemos agradecer por ese respiro.


Por otro lado, tenemos nuestras hojas, las que aún siguen ajustada al espiral de la libreta dispuesta a ser usadas, que sé que nosotros podemos darles ese sentido de seguir, que algunas quizás se rasguen por sentirnos abrumados y no querer seguir con la idea de esa escritura.

Sé que a veces la situación económica que vivimos nos hace sentir que el esfuerzo es inútil. Miramos lo que queríamos lograr y, al ver que los propósitos que queremos no los podemos alcanzar al plazo que queremos, preferimos arrugar la idea y lanzarla al montón del olvido. \

, nos decimos, y el papel suena seco cuando lo arrancamos con resignación. >Mi mensaje para todas esas personas que lograron sobrevivir quisiera decirles que Dios les dio una nueva libreta en blanco, aunque la naturaleza les quito un llena de varias páginas escritas, no les ha quitado el derecho de seguir escribiendo, ha sido un milagro, ha sido Dios y su misericordia. **Espero muchos de ustedes puedan escribir en esta [iniciativa](https://hive.blog/hive-131951/@emiliorios/deja-salir-tus-emociones-que-sientes-ante-esta-imagen-actividad-interactiva-en-domingo-de-7mo-dia-esen) del amigo @emiliorios los invito a participar. Saludos**

links.title: My participation in the Phone Photography Contest! - #119: The Arboretum of the School of Physics [Eng/Esp]
links.body:
> A big hello to the [Feel Good](https://ecency.com/created/hive-190931) community! I've been a bit disconnected these past few days because I've had two teaching loads this semester: teaching the theory class and, on the same day, preparing and teaching the lab session! And as if all of this weren't enough, there was the double earthquake last Wednesday, a true tragedy. It's been almost a week since this sad event, and while rescue efforts continue in the coastal state, we here at the University have organized ourselves to turn the schools and faculties that suffered minor damage into collection centers for supplies and medicine. But this time, I had to go to my Faculty for a Faculty Council meeting. In this meeting, we were going to decide on a timeline for the gradual resumption of teaching activities, of course, once the engineers had inspected all the structures and determined which buildings could be used for teaching and which should be closed due to severe damage. What I didn't like was that this meeting was to be in person, and I wasn't keen on leaving my house knowing that we were still experiencing aftershocks between 4 and 5.1 magnitude! The building where the meeting was to be held was the physics school, which suffered practically no damage. It had been several years since I'd been to this part of the faculty, where there's a mini-arboretum that almost no one knows about, and I wanted to photograph it with my phone to share it with you in this Phone Photography [round #119](https://ecency.com/@untilwelearn/phone-photography-contest-119).
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTCqgX2uPT6K8aW5cL5DARc1xj3tKNuJ81Ev7jT1hfRjB/photo_6_2026_06_30_13_16_27.jpg)|![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdGitFAP7rNqCL8PDZhiRK5uMixSahh7QcnUEmWzD81Yg/photo_3_2026_06_30_13_16_27.jpg) --|--

> Each of my contributions to this contest always has a long story behind it, and this one is no exception! In the first semesters of the program, you're required to take math, physics, and chemistry—just those three subjects. It might seem like a small amount, but the level of difficulty is quite high, and for me, physics was the most challenging, not so much because of the math involved, but because of the logic applied in classical mechanics. I struggled to visualize the problems and how to solve them. That's why I came here constantly, to the physics department, where I had long consultations with my professors until I finally understood them! But one of the things I enjoyed most about coming to this place was the small arboretum in this building. Actually, this building shares the same space as the Zoology and Tropical Ecology building, so the presence of a small botanical collection between the two buildings was natural. When I arrived, it was drizzling, so since I was early, I had a coffee and a meat pastry and went straight to the meeting, but not before photographing the large royal palms that adorn the entrance to the physics department—they are simply magnificent. Nearby stand other equally imposing trees, one of them a mango tree. Although mango season is over, last month it was still laden with mangoes, and you could simply take as many as you wanted completely free! This place definitely seems frozen in time; it looks just as it did when I used to come here for consultations during my first semesters of university. Only now I'm a professor and share the same responsibilities as the professors who taught me. It's like watching the same movie but from a different perspective!
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ28SLsQ8Je7EBjBF7NcjxZK9fBjTd3jsXcmSuB9iJzD5/photo_2_2026_06_30_13_16_27.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/Eo6HzX715sc8y3UTEx29EJRiWo2Dc9jAKUZDHy1aYFb1TV3gnBo5kVKXXA3kcRAZ6yn.png)

> The meeting ended as I expected, without any clear conclusions. That is to say, they will most likely extend the suspension of activities until we have complete certainty about which buildings are suitable for working. Although, yes, I was annoyed because, obviously, to reach these conclusions, the meeting could have been held virtually. But at least I was able to leave my house after so many days, breathe some fresh air, and take the opportunity to photograph these wonderful trees that adorn the physics school. See you in the next #phonography, friends!
*** # Versión Español ***
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVi4Q6iXyB1pRxiLmotVjdZJsrH4z5DmCaK4yYAhdJkjQ/photo_1_2026_06_30_13_16_27.jpg)

> Un gran saludo comunidad de [Feel Good](https://ecency.com/created/hive-190931)! He estado un poco desconectado estos días y es que estas semanas se juntaron mis 2 cargas docentes de este semestre: dar la clase de teoría y el mismo día también preparar y dar la práctica de laboratorio! Y por si no fuera poco a todo esto se ha juntado el doble terremoto del miércoles pasado, una verdadera tragedia. Ya va a ser 1 semana de este triste evento y mientras continúan las labores de rescate en el estado costero del país, nosotros aquí en la Universidad, nos hemos organizado para convertir las escuelas y facultades que sufrieron daños leves, en centros de acopio de suministros y medicinas. Pero en esta ocasión tuve que ir a mi Facultad para una reunión del Consejo de Facultad. En esta reunión íbamos a decidir un cronograma para la reincorporación gradual de las actividades docentes, por supuesto, una vez que los ingenieros hubieran revisado todas las estructuras y dictaminasen cuales edificios podían ser utilizados para las actividades docentes y cuales debían ser restringidos por daños severos. Lo que no me gustó es que esta reunión sería presencial y no me entusiasmaba salir de mi casa sabiendo que todavía estábamos teniendo réplicas de entre 4 y 5.1 grados! El edificio donde sería la reunión fue en la escuela de física que prácticamente no sufrió ningún daño, tenía ya varios años que no pasaba por este espacio de la facultad donde se encuentra un mini arboretum que por lo general casi nadie conoce y quise fotografiarlo con mi móvil para compartirlo con ustedes en este Phone Photography [round #119](https://ecency.com/@untilwelearn/phone-photography-contest-119).
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTCqgX2uPT6K8aW5cL5DARc1xj3tKNuJ81Ev7jT1hfRjB/photo_6_2026_06_30_13_16_27.jpg)|![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdGitFAP7rNqCL8PDZhiRK5uMixSahh7QcnUEmWzD81Yg/photo_3_2026_06_30_13_16_27.jpg) --|--

> Cada uno de mis aportes a este concurso siempre tiene una larga historia detrás, y esta no es la excepción! Los primeros semestres de la carrera debes obligatoriamente ver matemáticas, física y química, esas tres únicamente, parece poco pero el nivel de exigencia es bastante alto y para mi el más complicado era física no tanto por las matemáticas que se utilizaban sino por la lógica aplicada en la mecánica clásica, me costaba imaginarme los problemas y como resolverlos. Por eso venía constantemente aquí, a la escuela de física donde tenía largas consultas con mis profesores hasta que finalmente los entendía! Pero una de las cosas que más disfrutaba de venir a estos espacios era del pequeño arboretum que tenía este edificio. En realidad este edificio comparte el mismo espacio que el de Zoología y Ecología Tropical por lo que era natural la presencia de una pequeña colección botánica entre estos 2 edificios. Al momento en que llegué estaba lloviendo ligeramente, así que como había llegado temprano, me tomé un café con un pastelito de carne y me fui directo a la reunión, no sin antes fotografiar las grandes palmas reales que adornan la entrada de la escuela de física, son simplemente imponentes. Al lado se encuentran otros arboles igualmente imponentes, uno de ellos es un árbol de mangos y aunque ya pasó la temporada de mangos el mes pasado estaba bastante cargado de mangos y simplemente podías tomar los que quisieras completamente gratis! En definitiva este lugar parece detenido en el tiempo, luce igual como cuando venía de consultas los primeros semestres de la carrera, solo que ahora soy profesor y comparto ahora las mismas responsabilidad que los profesores que me dieron clases, es como ver la misma película pero desde una perspectiva diferente!
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQ28SLsQ8Je7EBjBF7NcjxZK9fBjTd3jsXcmSuB9iJzD5/photo_2_2026_06_30_13_16_27.jpg)
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/Eo6HzX715sc8y3UTEx29EJRiWo2Dc9jAKUZDHy1aYFb1TV3gnBo5kVKXXA3kcRAZ6yn.png)

> La reunión terminó como lo esperaba sin ninguna conclusión clara, es decir, lo más probable es que extiendan la suspensión de actividades hasta que no tengamos la completa certeza de cuales edificios son aptos para trabajar. Aunque si, estaba molesto porque obviamente, para estas conclusiones, la reunión podía hacerse virtual pero no bueno es que pude salir de mi casa después de tantos días, respirar otro ambiente y aprovechar de fotografiar estos maravillosos árboles que adornan la escuela de física. Nos vemos en un próximo #phonography amigos!
![ecency_spring_banner2025_6.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/243fzw92qU1TYGxoTAtzTQ2BAwNmSPvZhpG2EXsZmzEA3t3KtSL88hxURV3sy74U2iX9R.gif) ![ecency_spring_banner2025_10 II.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bulkathos/245TSwLsaP8B4DpGdfKu1AnCcDxAEpYqNkHS7CjSaz767Qfd9utXB3W5uvaPhkJgcjhys.gif)

> The images for the reviews were taken from my Redmi 9c cell phone. The translation was done with the [Deepl](https://www.deepl.com/es/translator) translate. > Las imágenes para este post fueron tomadas en mi móvil Redmi 9c. La traducción fue realizada con [Deepl](https://www.deepl.com/es/translator) translate.

Great article on a topic I think about and watch videos on.

For me, coming from an Engineering background, I see most things as a probability. I am 99% sure I am typing this comment, but I could be in a simulation and someone/something else is controlling this particular avatar/character in an elaborate game/simulation.

If we're raised in a belief community, we tend to believe what they believe. The people who feed and protect us tell us things and we tend to believe they are true things. Even when we're adults, it's hard to choose to look into other ways of thinking. It's easier to just read and do what we're told.

For me, I heard all the stories and claims as a kid, but even then they seemed like just stories. Unifying stories that keep a group together and give them identity. I'm still that way. I feel that the available data shows most things my tribe believes are highly probably just stories in my opinion, shaped to ensure group cohesion.

But there is a chance they are \

.  I like my tribe, and I like being a member. So I choose to believe some things in it which I assign a low probability of actually being factual.  And I make no secret of it.  I'll discuss multiple sides of the same topic and I'm always happy to hear new points of view.  This is interesting to me, so I engage with people on it when I feel like doing so, if they are also agreeable.

I appreciate this article! These were my spontaneous thoughts, tangentially related to the topic.  Thanks for the mental stimulation.

Have a great week!

by The Free Thought Project on The Free Thought Project Podcast 
View my bio on Vigilante.TV: https://vigilante.tv/c/thefreethoughtproject [![Guest: Catherine Fitts - Stargate & Surveillance: How Taxpayers Finance The Data Center Matrix](https://vigilante.tv/lazy-static/previews/11e4d2f6-2dce-4fc7-998f-f2de406d9f0a.jpg)](https://vigilante.tv/w/gqZXu7GddrcMQpfcMGmc1R) 
 
 Matt Agorist and Don Via, Jr. sat down with the relentless Catherine Austin Fitts for an incredibly vital status report on the global fight for financial freedom. A former Wall Street powerhouse and former Assistant Secretary of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) under the Bush Senior administration, Catherine is the publisher of The Solari Report and one of the liberty movement’s most brilliant economic minds. After famously looking inside the belly of the beast and blowing the whistle on the missing trillions of dollars leaking out of the federal budget decades ago, she has dedicated her life to exposing state overreach and the encroaching digital panopticon. Fresh off a massive interview with Tucker Carlson and a major speaking appearance at the John Birch Society Conference in Salt Lake City, Catherine joins the show in the midst of a grueling multi-city tour to break down how everyday people can bypass the uni-party trap and construct an unbroken, parallel world.

The core of the discussion dismantles the insidious architecture of the \
and the mechanism of what Catherine defines as the \

. The conversation exposes how recent political theater—such as a temporary ban on retail Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs)—serves as a massive bait-and-switch, masking a back-door corporate-government hydra built on private stablecoins through legislative frameworks like the GENIUS Act. This programmable ledger system aims to transition traditional bank deposits, stocks, and bonds into a machine-driven surveillance apparatus that can instantly freeze, block, or condition transactions from above the institutional level, entirely bypassing human legal accountability. The dialogue maps out the immense physical scale of this grid, detailing how the United States has become the global hardware hub by housing more data centers than the top 14 countries combined. Crucially, the breakdown reveals how everyday citizens are being manipulated into financing their own digital cages through local taxpayer subsidies and heavily concentrated 401(k) and IRA retirement portfolios that pour billions into tech monopolies. Finally, the geopolitical lens is turned onto the deceptive \

narrative, revealing that central planners across both the BRICS nations and Western alliances remain uniformly loyal to the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) digital ID model, reframing the current global tension as a mere turf war over who secures \
data rights.\n\nShifting gears entirely to actionable resistance and \

the episode maps out a comprehensive tactical manual for individual and community empowerment. The path forward demands an active financial decoupling—urging listeners to defund the surveillance panopticon by auditing their wealth, pulling retirement funds out of Wall Street's concentrated index funds, and shifting capital toward localized, tangible assets. True systemic pushback relies on a dual-layered approach: aggressively utilizing physical cash through localized \

campaigns to build community resilience and starve data center resource consumption, while simultaneously adopting decentralized, protocol-level digital privacy networks like Monero or Zano to secure long-distance commerce outside the matrix. Catherine highlights the Coming Clean blueprint—a downloadable guide packed with practical steps to systematically stop feeding energy to the state and start financing your own family. Ultimately, building a free civilization relies on a node-to-node system anchored entirely in real-world human relationships of trust. The show closes with an inspiring spiritual framework drawn from The NeverEnding Story, reminding the audience that the ultimate defense against the technocratic \

is to aggressively protect personal joy, foster community connection, and maintain an unshakeable state of amusement. (Length: 56:12)

links.title: Forgiveness & Reconciliation.
links.body:
There is a powerful myth, depending on if you believe it or not, that forgiveness is not a waiver of justice and it does not endorse wrongdoing. It is just a choice to stop carrying on grief or injury of the past. Forgiveness is not an approver, it doesn't give you freedom, it doesn't mean you have to do it over and over again to that person, to anger the person or hurt the person.

The fact that I forgive you does not give you the levity and the freedom to do something bad again. I forgive means that I don't want to carry the hurt and at the same time I can take chances into my hand to make sure that I stay away from you so that you don't do such a thing again to me. Most of us grew up with a narrow, moralized view of forgiveness.

To forgive is to say the offense was acceptable, to lower the standard of right and wrong or to let someone off the hook. That misunderstanding keeps people chained to a wrong thing they have endured in the past. When someone hurts you, two things happen at that point in time, there are two burdens that is conjoined together, first is the original wound and the second is the ongoing work of carrying it all around, it can even increase whenever you see that person.

Anger and resentment becomes every object you hold in your hand, though at first they may feel righteous because if the person hurts you and your anger or your resentment is genuine, after all they confirm the injustice you experience but over time they bend your posture, they make you exhaust your energy on things that you shouldn't and shape how you relate to the world. Forgiveness removes the extra load without declaring the harm meaningless, so you have to choose your peace over every punishment. Forgiveness does not erase consequence, accountability, justice and boundary setting.

Though all these things should still matter, whenever you forgive someone and you let that person know what he or she has done, it doesn't mean you have to stay in an harmful relationship and keep on doing that kind of a bad thing. Forget what happened, block legal and practical recourse, instead forgiveness is an internal transaction you trade the hard currency of resentment for. While you cannot always control whether the person who hurts you changes or pays a price, you can control whether you remain defined by the harm.

Forgiveness is also very hard, it takes emotional courage, a lot of emotional courage to handle forgiveness and it requires naming the hurt properly and perfectly right, don't add emotions to it, you have to acknowledge any desire of revenge and you have to examine it compassionately, then you must be willing to set boundaries so that such a thing does not happen, you don't get hurt over and over again and stay in a toxic relationship because you want to forgive. Then you have to accept that forgiveness is your own welfare, it's not your offender's welfare. People often mix forgiveness and reconciliation together and it's a two different thing.

Reconciliation involves rebuilding trust, this always comes after a big fight or an injury that was so severe, in some big cases it can also mean war. Reconciliation involves that forgiveness is unilateral and internal. Reconciliation deals with acquiring or requiring changes on the part of the offenders and to make retribution.

There are so many practical approaches that you can take to choose peace. If you want to move forward, forgiveness without your experience, you can try to recognize and validate the hurt, reframe the forgiveness, take a symbolic step and reinforce the choice. Holding on to resentment cannot help you and it will help you to shadow the truth, also you won't be able to even forgive easily.

It prolongs suffering without changing the past. Choosing forgiveness is the best thing you can ever do for yourself. Though forgiveness does not guarantee immediate relief, I know it is sometimes a long process with setback, but every time you are choosing to stop carrying that weight, you become very light and you can carry on in life as fast as you can with that.

links.title: The Quiet Hunt.
links.body:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=torrisi/nzowd0h1

<center>logo_from_wikimedia & font_from_resourceboy</center>

Using tracking instincts, I silently choked out mine guards and used a sharpened knife for a brutal takedown. After carefully clearing the remaining perimeter guards to reach my horse, an abrupt cinematic cutscene triggered where Merlo intercepted and forcefully captured Enzo at the gate.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRJNFp1rWrZKP7LE3thaUF4DHUFFX6nFLyE9pd6iKCpNY/screenshot_1_.png)

I had to take down a mine guard who was looking for me at the ground floor of the farmstead. And I had to avoid detection while I got this option to detect enemies using instinct.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRXbyTUyRd4bv3P5avsQRxEBPFS5y1rhdBLPiXtiuZPip/screenshot_2_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVA1wq82Q41N8V4QHFWnVw8cyyzvr1GEVDV9yYd5vB43o/screenshot_3_.png)

After getting close to that guard who was trying to open up a door, I went for him silently, and I grabbed him while he was unaware. And I choked him to death until he completely stopped moving.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSLGRaGYeQmXa9RzW1HiMnyJcekfa4X8msTsBdqSsstWX/screenshot_4_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRTYvd1xoeca79ZtXLjjaEnR4dNA1Z5dMcNkdSxskatfx/screenshot_5_.png)

I found a whetstone from the body that I could use to sharpen my knife. And then I used my knife to open that door that the guard was trying to open up, sliding the thin blade into the lock until it clicked open.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYA99NYSz4CnLbSE9CnFcrSd1eXSyBFwbFTKKyzzc8rB8/screenshot_6_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU8Enf2YgFfii5fHkrLrB2os2qq7T5AbL1r3eX1X5VyzQ/screenshot_7_.png)

That door led me out of that farmhouse, and now I had to leave the barn, getting to my horse. But there were more guards on my way, so I had to stay low to map out their patrol patterns.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX5ji8zq7rnegkCbbZTgaczNoyZbz9bwvdPddqjJWJxX3/screenshot_8_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTzbJR1H8oqB7ojvZjawb2kaU4sGSScQnAL8ZkwLrZwkd/screenshot_9_.png)

Fortunately, this guard was also faced to the other side, so I could take him down easily by choking him to death. And then I used the whetstone to sharpen my knife for future use.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPfc7VRCFzMiXkfprDKNNNMV3RYWq5PWErXmKtYsiBPFZ/screenshot_10_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYbtovCPiu9rv5mHGPYqFvQ23MgNWL2fNTfV4zCEKd8R3/screenshot_11_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSp6FPz2Lm1N3Kpz4fgk9DfES8wG4roRtqHJFzkVAeXXh/screenshot_12_.png)

I found another guard on my way, and as I sharpened my knife already, I could try faster takedowns using my knife. And that guard faced a brutal finishing as I caught him off-guard from the shadows with a swift, lethal strike.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUabmVb9UGA9ZuQv2VETJJAytfW91mJJxm2RVwV5ghZRz/screenshot_13_.png)

Right when I was about to leave that place and move ahead, I noticed there came two more guards who were going to find me if I had jumped out there. So I just waited for them to get separated.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmagxFbSMei2wPWMTtY5TD6BRvHqaBBjDTZm64PhEzsuDT/screenshot_14_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUa66XpUTTRYHPUQVLp8NSzRbFoGRAxdL5byGgkbinSqy/screenshot_15_.png)

I found them separated as they kept looking for me around, or they were just guarding the perimeter, so I wouldn't be able to leave this barn. And I took them both down one by one, by choking them to death without wasting any whetstone for faster takedowns.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPezYKgPV2ywtpzxDRi7EdaqoeVxeCQU2JjFGRF2xJMhQ/screenshot_16_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdK2NxBJXmPg53d9TFi8TJZZN8MdKvHFAAfsjgJ3uzcYz/screenshot_17_.png)

Then I reached another gate where a cinematic moment started, and it looked like Enzo found his horse was being guarded by another mine guard.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSmSPh3XQm9ZXvBK1Qaw8J9CZhyxt1xqBHyHo9gWPcWUX/screenshot_18_.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQCFHTMcDNcYm9PDEBBPtP39nEb7heEtiszYKqCPg29Wv/screenshot_19_.png)

Right when Enzo was about to get out of that shade and maybe get to his horse, there came Merlo, who kicked Enzo out of the door. And yeah, after trying my best to avoid detection, Enzo was caught.

To be continued.

links.title: Verse of the Day | Tuesday, June 30th
links.body:
Deuteronomy 6:6-7***

Today's verse reminds us that the Word of God is not meant to stay confined to a church building or a Sunday morning — it is meant to flow naturally through every moment of daily life. The home, the road, the morning, and the night are all spaces where faith is lived, taught, and passed on to the next generation.

That is why transmitting faith to our children and those around us is not a task reserved for pastors or teachers — it is the responsibility of every believer in every ordinary moment. The most powerful discipleship does not happen in classrooms, but in the daily conversations, habits, and decisions of a life lived intentionally in God's Word.

## Versículo del Día | Martes 30 de Junio

Deuteronomio 6:6-7***

El versículo del día nos recuerda que la Palabra de Dios no está destinada a permanecer confinada en un templo o en una mañana de domingo — está diseñada para fluir naturalmente a través de cada momento de la vida cotidiana. El hogar, el camino, la mañana y la noche son todos espacios donde la fe se vive, se enseña y se transmite a la siguiente generación.

Es por eso que transmitir la fe a nuestros hijos y a quienes nos rodean no es una tarea reservada para pastores o maestros — es la responsabilidad de cada creyente en cada momento ordinario. El discipulado más poderoso no ocurre en salones de clase, sino en las conversaciones cotidianas, los hábitos y las decisiones de una vida vivida intencionalmente en la Palabra de Dios.

links.title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly Side of Social Media
links.body:
> *Social media has become an important part of our everyday lives, and it comes with both advantages and disadvantages.*
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT56vif3k9wThygWyrGTUsxnkuErRcGdC2SteA5Evkav8/image.png)
[source](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/social-social-media-communication-3064515/) *Some people regret the day they joined social media, while for others, it has been one of the greatest blessings of their lives.* *There was a lady who met a man on Facebook. Their conversations eventually turned into a relationship, and she decided to visit him.* *Unknown to her, the man was allegedly an organ harvester. Sadly, she lost her life after visiting him. It was her body, with some organs missing, that was discovered when the police eventually raided the man’s house.* *On the other hand, many people have met the love of their lives online. Others have discovered life-changing business opportunities through social media, and their lives have never been the same. For them, it has been one testimony after another.* *Now, let us put people aside and talk about the information we consume on social media.* *Every day, I come across a huge amount of information, some useful, some completely meaningless. There is hardly a day that goes by without me using one social media platform or another.* *Without leaving my apartment, I can know what is happening in my neighborhood, across Nigeria, and around the world.* *Yesterday, I saw posts about drivers charging 4,000 Naira from Oshodi to Tollgate for a trip that normally costs around 700 Naira. The reason was the heavy rainfall, which caused severe flooding and massive traffic.*
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeJaevN5fR9cKf1Z2WaoHMz997H54VWhJEUStuEhYq9y3/image.png)
[source](https://pixabay.com/photos/media-social-media-apps-998990/) *Just by seeing those posts, I knew it wasn’t the right time to travel because transport fares had skyrocketed. That is one of the many benefits of social media.* *I also watched a viral video of a flooded street where a man was helping carry children out of a house that had been filled with water. The video spread rapidly, and hopefully, it reached the people who could assist them. That is another powerful side of social media: it can bring attention to situations that need urgent help.* *However, while I am learning about what is happening around the world, I also find myself wasting time consuming content that adds little or no value to my life, mindlessly scrolling through entertainment, watching random videos, or spending time on content that doesn’t help me grow.* *The good part is that whenever I am consuming meaningful content, I rarely do it passively. I usually multitask, listening, reading, or learning while working or grinding on something productive. That way, social media becomes a tool that supports my goals instead of simply stealing my time.* *At the end of the day, social media is neither good nor bad on its own. It all depends on how we use it. It can open doors, save lives, create opportunities, spread awareness, and connect people across the world. At the same time, it can waste our time, expose us to danger, and fill our minds with things that don’t truly matter.* *The choice is ours. We should strive to consume more content that helps us grow and be intentional about how we spend our time online.*

links.title: Back on Hive — and FreeBeings DAO is live
links.body:
It's been a while. My last real posts here were in early 2023, and before that I spent years building and writing on this chain — HAF Plug & Play, the Global Notification System, Hive DEX, and a lot of thinking out loud about attention value, communities, and what this blockchain makes possible.

Then I went quiet. The short version: the funding for what I was building didn't come through, and I stepped back to regroup. The longer version is that I never stopped working on the ideas — I just stopped posting about them.

I'm back, and I'm bringing the work with me.

### What I've been building

The ideas I used to write about here — that freedom depends on systems that can't be quietly corrupted, that [attention is a real economy](https://hive.blog/hive-133333/@imwatsi/thoughts-on-proof-of-brain), that [communities with their own economies](https://hive.blog/utopian-io/@imwatsi/steem-a-story-bigger-than-itself-os-insights-1) are how change actually happens — have grown into a vision: **FreeBeings.io** ([freebeings.io](https://freebeings.io)).

FreeBeings.io is a research lab and community incubator. We use AI to surface the truths that matter — and we build blockchain-based communities where those truths can land and become fertile grounds for change. Hive is our Layer 1: accounts and content live here. A FreeBeings Layer 2 is planned for community tokens and governance — and if you remember Hive Attention Tokens, you already know the lineage. The L2 is HAT, matured.

On AI: we use it as a research instrument and a building tool. It's how a small team does research at a depth that used to require an institution, and how I ship software faster than I ever could alone. The thinking, the convictions, and the direction are mine — same as they've always been on this account.

### FreeBeings DAO (you may have known it as FreeSpace)

Some of you might remember **FreeSpace**, the dApp I was building as a portal to the FreeBeings DAO before things stalled. It's finished, and it's live — under its real name: **FreeBeings DAO**, at [dao.freebeings.io](https://dao.freebeings.io).


![post-comeback.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcGkSZj9v7oEuAfCo5xLKuCbfijH95Kjescz2HguNBRyG/post-comeback.png)


Why the rename? FreeSpace was always the working title. More to the point, the DAO is what it was always becoming. The name now just says what it is.

It's where the FreeBeings community lives: a space for projects that aim at positive change, built on Hive's primitives — posts, comments, votes, HBD/HIVE earnings — with discussion rooms, polls, and project updates on top. You join with your Hive account, and joining is joining the DAO.

It's also our testbed. The features we prove there will shape the communities infrastructure we build next.

It's live now — go in with your Hive account and look around. There are projects already running (including FreeBeings DAO building itself, in the open). A fuller walkthrough — what it does, how it works, how to start — follows as the next post.

### Why come back here

Because this is where these ideas started. I joined in 2016, lived through the Steem era, and watched this chain survive things that would have killed a centralized platform. Everything FreeBeings.io is building on — sound infrastructure, voluntary participation, communities with their own economies — I learned and argued for here first.

We publish in the open: writing on Hive, and our Hive tools open source on [GitHub](https://github.com/FreeBeings-io). The @freebeings account will carry the project and research posts; this account stays what it's always been — me, thinking out loud.

Good to be back. More soon.

*Live and let live, freely.*

It just goes to show you how interdependent species really are on this planet. Kill off one major food source through deforestation and you kill off another species as a consequence. We've seen it time after time sadly. At least now in the more developed countries we strive to save these creatures.

 The Fiat Money Maestro

Former Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan passed away last week at the age of 100. Greenspan chaired the Fed from 1987 through 2006.

Despite being a lifelong Republican, Greenspan refused to lower interest rates, though doing so may have helped George H.W. Bush’s 1992 reelection campaign. However, he did tailor monetary policy to support President Clinton’s 1993 budget, as well as the 1997 bipartisan budget deal.

Greenspan’s handling of monetary policy was widely credited as responsible for the 1990s strong economy. As a result, the cult of the Federal Reserve chairman reached new heights under Greenspan. During Greenspan’s tenure it became so common for the Fed to act to help bail out large financial firms that experienced financial difficulty that many began referring to the “Greenspan put.” Greenspan was even the subject of a bestselling biography by Bob Woodward titled Maestro. New Republic reporter Stephen Glass wrote about Wall Street professionals maintaining a shrine to Greenspan. While the story was later revealed to be one of many fabrications created by Glass, at the time it seemed believable that Wall Street offices would contain shrines to Greenspan.

links.title: The World Cup of equals [EN/PT]
links.body:
>


The Brazilian national team showed what they came for in this 2026 World Cup, and that became very clear in the match against Japan. I already mentioned in a previous post that this World Cup is different from the others, not only because of the new format or the increased number of teams, but because there are no longer any \

national teams. Maybe this really is a consequence of globalization and the way strategies have become increasingly balanced across the world. Sure, some teams have generations of players who are less talented than countries like Brazil, France, and Germany, but the gap is nowhere near as large as it used to be in previous editions.

The proof of that was the match between Japan and Brazil, which, in my opinion, was a very balanced game. And Japan, to me, is the strongest Japanese team of all time, more mature and more aware of itself than any other version I have followed. I have to admit that when the first goal was scored, for a brief moment I thought Brazil would not win this match. But, as I said, Brazil showed what they came for in this World Cup and managed to turn the game around with goals from Casemiro and Martinelli, two names I definitely did not expect to stand out in this match. Casemiro did not have a good first half, but he redeemed himself with that surprise goal, and Martinelli, whom I personally consider a very weak player for the Brazilian national team, scored as well and proved me wrong.

My bet is still on Vinicius Junior, who came incredibly close to scoring an unforgettable goal with a first-time shot through his own legs, beautiful and precise. It was a masterclass inside the penalty area, making the Japanese defenders dance awkwardly around him, and by a cruel twist of fate, the ball hit the post. It would have been a goal remembered for years and would have drawn comparisons to that legendary Maradona goal. Well, not this time. It is also worth mentioning that the assist came from my favorite player on the national team, Rayan, who came through the youth academy of my beloved club. He is the youngest player on the squad and has enormous potential, if not for this World Cup, then certainly for the next ones.

And today, well, Brazil's next opponent in the Round of 16 has been decided: Norway, the Vikings. Coincidentally, they are one of the teams I have been rooting for in this World Cup besides Brazil, but obviously my support will be with those wearing the yellow jersey. Norway has a good team, and Haaland can decide a match at any moment. Once again, he scored today, adding another goal to his World Cup tally, and I hope that by next Sunday they will have their ships prepared and fully supplied, because I have faith (not in Odin) that they will be leaving the tournament. See you in Valhalla?

And I could not finish this post without talking a little about Germany's elimination, which, for me, was sweet. My apologies to the Germans, but after the 7-1, Germany became my biggest rival after Argentina, of course. Morocco also proved their worth and sent the Netherlands packing for home. And well, while I am writing this post, I am also watching the France vs. Sweden match and cheering for Sweden, of course. I want the easiest path possible for Brazil to win its sixth World Cup title. Let's go, Braza!

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeHEZQu2hofpKLZmSd5uVHKpwk4mNXMKMan26XHFaSeeb/image.png)

<center>[Source](https://fotografia.folha.uol.com.br/galerias/1869355913164352-veja-lances-do-segundo-tempo-de-brasil-x-japao)</center>

A seleção brasileira mostrou a que veio para essa Copa de 2026, e isso ficou bem explícito no jogo contra o Japão. Eu já mencionei aqui em um post anterior que essa Copa é diferente das outras, não somente pelo novo formato ou número maior de seleções, mas porque não existe mais seleção \

. Talvez isso se deva mesmo ao fato da globalização e como as estratégias estão cada vez mais niveladas. Tudo bem, algumas seleções possuem levas de jogadores menos talentosos do que seleções como Brasil, França e Alemanha, mas a disparidade não é tanta quanto nas edições anteriores. A prova disso foi a partida entre Japão e Brasil, que, na minha opinião, foi uma partida muito equilibrada, e logo o Japão, que para mim é a seleção mais forte de todos os tempos, mais madura e mais consciente do que qualquer outra que acompanhei. Confesso que, quando saiu o primeiro gol, achei por um breve momento que o Brasil não venceria essa partida. Mas, como disse, o Brasil mostrou a que veio a essa Copa e conseguiu virar com gols de Casemiro e Martinelli, dois nomes bem inesperados para mim nesse jogo. Casemiro não fez um bom primeiro tempo, mas se redimiu com esse gol surpresa, e Martinelli, que particularmente acho um jogador muito fraco para estar na seleção brasileira, deixou o seu também e calou minha boca. Minha aposta é no Vinicius Junior, que por pouco não faz um gol antológico com uma bola no meio das pernas, de primeira, linda, certeira. Um baile dentro da grande área, colocando os japoneses para dançar de forma desengonçada e, por um capricho do destino, a bola parou na trave, um gol que não seria esquecido por um bom tempo e que remeteria àquele gol antológico do Maradona. Bem, não foi dessa vez. Ainda vale lembrar que esse passe veio do meu jogador preferido da seleção, Rayan, que é um jogador que veio das categorias de base do meu time do coração, o mais novo da seleção e com um grande potencial, se não para essa Copa, com certeza para as próximas. E hoje, bem, está definido o próximo adversário do Brasil nas oitavas de final: Noruega, os vikings, logo uma das seleções para a qual estava torcendo nessa Copa sem ser a seleção brasileira, mas minha torcida é óbvia que será para os que vestem a camisa amarela. A Noruega tem um bom time e o Haaland pode desequilibrar uma partida a qualquer momento, como hoje, mais um gol registrado na Copa, e espero que no próximo domingo eles estejam com seus navios preparados e abastecidos, pois eu tenho fé (não em Odin) que eles deixarão a Copa. Nos vemos em Valhalla? E eu não poderia deixar de finalizar esse post falando um pouco da eliminação da Alemanha, que para mim foi doce. Me desculpem os alemães, mas depois dos 7x1, a Alemanha será a minha maior rival, depois da Argentina, claro. Marrocos também mostrou seu valor e deixou a Holanda com as malas prontas para voltar para casa. E bem, enquanto estou aqui escrevendo este post, também estou vendo o jogo da França e Suécia, e torcendo pela Suécia, claro, quero o caminho mais fácil possível para o Brasil conquistar o hexa. Vai, Brasa!

links.title: My Actifit Report Card: June 30 2026
links.body:
Hello Actifit community and fitness family! ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/1b31c94f-60cb-4e0d-ac58-7ace7265a569.jpg) ​Happy Tuesday! Today is June 30, 2026, and we are officially wrapping up the month of June on an absolute high note. After spotting those elegant white hydrangeas during my neighborhood walk yesterday evening, I decided to celebrate the end of the month by heading back out to the wide-open spaces of Richmond Park. The refreshing evening breeze and expansive green fields provided the ultimate fuel to open up my stride and push my boundaries. ​I am absolutely thrilled to share that tonight was a massive victory, finishing the day with an incredible total of 14,058 steps! ​A Flawless Finish The 31 Day Streak is Complete! ​Slamming past the 14k mark feels amazing, but the ultimate reward is looking back at a full month of dedication. Checking my Actifit app dashboard, tonight's big walk officially seals my magnificent 31 day streak without a single missed day! ​Seeing that perfect row of green checkmarks sweep from last Wednesday straight through to tonight (Tuesday) is the most satisfying visual proof of daily discipline. While syncing up my data this evening, I also noticed a new community interaction post highlighted on the home feed from @actifit fitness captioned First Comment. I'll go first. It's always fun to see the platform keeping the community connected while we keep our physical momentum soaring! ​Peaceful Green Horizons ​The absolute highlight of my evening trek was completely immersing myself in the quiet, untouched landscapes of the park to clear my mind after a busy day. ​As captured in my photo, the parklands looked beautifully lush and serene as the day wound down. My route took me along a quiet, winding paved path surrounded by rolling green grass and heavy, mature summer trees under a soft, overcast evening sky. Escaping the noise of town traffic and pacing your miles out in the open makes achieving a big step goal feel completely effortless. ​Ready to Charge Into July ​Logging over 14,000 steps to finish June leaves me feeling balanced, energized, and completely ready to carry this powerful momentum straight into July tomorrow. Committing to this daily movement has proven that staying fit isn't about finding a perfect gym it's simply about choosing to step outside and appreciate the beautiful spaces right on our doorstep. If you are looking for an extra spark to hit your targets tonight, find a local trail path or a wide open park. Let nature set your rhythm, and your goals will effortlessly fall into place!
