body.title: My Actifit Report Card: June 30 2026
body.body:
> Nie chcę się powtarzać z opisami, w jakiej czarnej i głębokiej D jestem, dlatego opowiem Wam co mnie niezmiernie denerwuje - robot koszący dreame a2 2000, czy tam może bardziej prawidłowa nazwa to byłoby gówno koszące. Serio. Na zdjęciu macie trawnik, który przerasta możliwości tego robota. Te pojedyncze kwiaty potrafią wyrosnąć w ciągu nocy przy odpowiednich warunkach i to wystarczy, żeby robot już nie był w stanie skosić. Na drugim zdjęciu możecie zobaczyć dziury w koszeniu. Na trzecim kompletny zapis dzisiejszej trasy, zarazem dowód miejsc, których w ogóle nie zaliczył. A na koniec dodam, że robot nie wrócił do stacji z niewiadomych powodów. Kiedy po ręcznym wymuszeniu powrotu, poradził sobie bez problemu.  Przemyślenia mam takie, że jako sprzęt do podkaszania trawy - żeby potem móc szybciej skosić samodzielnie - jest ok. Ale za tę cenę, tj. 5450 PLN to nie. Nie polecam... I don’t want to keep repeating descriptions of what a deep, dark mess I’m in, so instead I’ll tell you what is currently driving me absolutely mad: the Dreame A2 2000 robotic mower — or maybe the more accurate name would be “robotic piece of crap mower.” Seriously. In the photo you can see a lawn that is apparently beyond this robot’s capabilities. Those single little flowers can grow overnight in the right conditions, and that is already enough for the robot to fail at mowing them. In the second photo, you can see the gaps in the mowing. In the third one, you can see the complete record of today’s route — also proof of the areas it did not cover at all. And to top it all off, the robot did not return to the station for unknown reasons. When I manually forced it to return, it managed without any problem. My conclusion is this: as a device for trimming the grass a bit so that I can mow it myself more quickly later — fine. But for this price, i.e. PLN 5,450? No way. I do not recommend it.  
_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@sk1920/actifit-sk1920-20260630t204321084z)_

body.title: 실손24 체험
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZCggoRpZ4idm6F8WivMwQC2C1cbF4i4dk3DYERTYhJoD/image.png)

몇일전에 아내의 실비보험 청구를 도와주게 됐는데
저는 그동안 병원에서  진료비 영수증과 진료비 세부내역서를 받아서 
스캔을 해서 보험회사 홈페이지를 통해서 했었다.

내 실비 청구건도 있고해서 이번에는 앱을 통해하고자 KB손해보험 앱을 설치했다.
그리고 예전에 실손24에 대해 들은 적이 있어서 실손24도 설치해 보았다.
병원이 실손24가입이되어 있다면 편리하게 실비청구를 할 수 있다고 했다.

실손 24 앱을 설치하고 가입했다. 다행히 진료받은 병원이 실손24에 가입이 돼있었다.  예전 기록을 조회하여 청구할 대상을 선택하고 신청만 하면 끝났다. 

편리했던 것은 그동안 청구 못한 내역도 조회해서 한꺼번에 청구할 수 있어 좋았다. 병원과 약국 모두 청구했다.

집사람에게도 실손24, 삼성 청구앱(모니모)을 설치하게 했다.
실손24로 튼튼병원에서 진료받을 것을 청구를 해보았는데 삼성화재는 청구하자마자 입금이 되었다.
정형외과는 실손 24가입이 안 되어 있어서  실비청구는 삼성화재 앱(모니모)를 통해서 했다. 

실비청구가 확실히 편해졌다.

body.title: Abstract hexagonal background
body.body:
Heksagonalni oblici se često javljaju u prirodi i inženjerstvu. Uvek su izazovni, nezavisno od materijala.

Koje su vam prve asocijacije kada pogledate fotografije?
Evo odgovora ako pokušate da ih pretražite na internetu.

![20260629_143013.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmax9isLPpiKebcK9u6XycewavViMVVJ5USiBnR5maYjxH/20260629_143013.jpg)

- Ova slika prikazuje teksturu industrijske metalne mrežaste rešetke sa šestougaonim uzorkom.
- Materijal može biti aluminijum ili crni čelik, a često se koristi za ventilaciju ili zaštitu opreme.
- Slične strukture se koriste u automobilskoj industriji kao zaštita hladnjaka. 

![20260629_143128.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQHtw4DSVgntThFiJq5wR93nrr5Ftw9seKRLDP54FhHrz/20260629_143128.jpg)

- Ovaj materijal podseća na rešetkastu strukturu sa heksagonalnim otvorima.
- Slični proizvodi se često izrađuju od metala (kao što je nerđajući čelik ili aluminijum) ili plastike.
- Ovakve mreže se koriste u razne svrhe, uključujući zaštitu zvučnika, ventilacione otvore, industrijske primene i dekorativne panele. 

![20260629_142617.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbAukA8YfC288VVuQFVTMiTyfRHuyiHdTAu7SMzh4TcSZ/20260629_142617.jpg)

 - Ovaj materijal je mrežasta tkanina sa heksagonalnim uzorkom, koja se često koristi za obloge u automobilima ili presvlake za nameštaj.
- Takođe, može biti perforirani čelični lim koji se koristi u industrijskoj proizvodnji i modernom oblikovanju metala. 

![20260629_142958.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRBEL5rfnxMZRw3vSGXnV8DrhyDJpysZCpP5hxmLnMTnb/20260629_142958.jpg)

- Tehnička mrežica: Ova slika prikazuje heksagonalnu metalnu mrežicu, često korišćenu za ventilaciju ili zaštitu u industrijskim i tehnološkim aplikacijama. 
- Akustična primena: Slične teksture se koriste kao prednje rešetke za zvučnike kako bi zaštitile komponente dok propuštaju zvuk. 
- Strukturni dizajn: Dizajn u obliku saća (honeycomb) nudi moderan estetski izgled i koristi se u raznim inženjerskim rešenjima, uključujući lakše konstrukcije u vazduhoplovstvu. 

![20260629_143159.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdyEQpzrYxeUu53EjJh5t1MqKNqT5vuMUUGfoiFTNKbK5/20260629_143159.jpg)

Nema tačnog odgovora.
Ne, ovo nisu mreže na golovima aktuelnog Svetskog prvenstva u fudbalu.

![20260630_091204_bw.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXNaJUZcgQ5asW5S36dkNTxLY66QkGhL1ddAejDjKDAjZ/20260630_091204_bw.jpg)

*30. jun 2026.*

Sada je sve jasno. Ovaj insekt zove se **jabukin staklokrilac**, (*Synanthedon myopaeformis*), i stoji na takozvanoj mrežici protiv insekata.

Hvala vam na vremenu koje ste posvetili mojim postovima.
Želim vam lep dan!

<center>**Srećni bili!**</center>

body.title: Could American Statutory-Rape Laws Get Any More Ridiculous?
body.body: ![Jozefm84 is the creator of this image/Source: Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2025/07/03/17/06/ice-cream-9694818_1280.png) Did any of you ever see the 1960 version of the movie titled *The Time Machine*? The late Australian actor Rod Taylor was 29 years old, and the late Yvette Mimieux was only 17 years old when the movie began filming the year before. There were romantic scenes in the movie between the two actors. However, I can be certain that the late Mr. Taylor was never a pedophile; and he wouldn't have been, because the late Ms. Mimieux wasn't a prepubescent child back then and she was even married at the age of 17. Nevertheless, there are always going to be little minds that are going to believe the worst about such scenarios from way back when. The United States has become flooded with semi-illiterate social justice warriors that cannot get the definition of pedophilia right and who believe that the statutory age of consent should be raised to 25 years old everywhere in the world, if not 35 years old. I've made it no secret in other articles of mine that I am no fan of American statutory-rape laws. Well, there is this one incident out of Tennessee that really takes the cake when it comes our criminal justice system pursuing frivolous and malicious sex cases involving teenage minors and adults that are fewer than 10 years apart in age difference. The news clip below describes the entire story. Police Arrested A 25-Year-Old Woman For Having A Harmless Consensual Tryst With A 16-Year-Old Boy https://youtu.be/NAPa1ZsbZIk?si=qKIqYOR_4nJTi8hw The name of the suspect is Tuesday Dodson. The press and the media took absolutely no time in sensationalizing this entire story into something that it is not. The facts are that a 16-year-old boy willingly made love to a 25-year-old woman in his car, went to a hotel room with her, and had sexual intercourse with her on his own free will. Now, I get what some of you are going to say. You're going to highlight the fact that she made threats against him not to tell anyone that they had sex. However, even though I do not wish to speculate on anything, I have an intuition that this punk probably was planning to brag about it to all his friends; and this woman wanted him to use discretion and keep the entire tryst under wraps. That's perfectly understandable. Why would anyone need to know? It's not as though the police are going to do anyone any favors. In any event, this young boy was not groomed, manipulated, or sexually molested; and he definitely was not raped. Do not let the criminal charge of \

against Ms. Dodson fool you.

In reading the posts in the comments section to the news clip above, way too many YouTubers appeared to have Pedophile-Panic Derangement Syndrome.  I don't have the faintest idea where any of them got this belief that Ms. Dodson was once a schoolteacher, because I couldn't find anything anywhere on the Internet that had information to that same effect.

The news media didn't help the situation at all by showing a drawing of what looked like a 10-year-old boy next to the picture of Ms. Dodson.  Oh, brother!  They absolutely love to infantilize teenage hedonists, especially a horny teenage boy looking for a good time on the town.

Why is it that the people that view the late Joseph Rosenbaum to be a murder victim and a martyr despite that he sodomized a 9-year-old boy back when he was a young adult are the very same people that will demonize Ms. Dodson for engaging in sexual relations with a teenage boy who wanted to have sex with her?  It's like a very bizarre double standard that cannot produce any logical explanation.

In case any of you don't know who the late Joseph Rosenbaum was, he was that 30-something-year-old man who threatened a 17-year-old boy's life and that same young boy (Kyle Rittenhouse) shot him dead in self-defense.  It wouldn't surprise me in the least if that Dawn Harper, who is the Chief-Executive-Officer of the Nashville Children's Alliance, is a major fan of the late Mr. Rosenbaum.  Her kind usually reek of hypocrisy.

The statistics that Ms. Harper and the news reporters in the news clip cited for how many underage boys fall victim to sexual assault are likely bloated and over-reported, because many of these boys suffered no harm at the hands of a cougar that they likely sought out for their own personal gratification.

Ms. Harper runs her mouth about how the law is the law, but somehow that law never seems to be anywhere to be found whenever an underage boy or girl gets locked up in an adult correctional facility somewhere here in the United States and gets gang-raped by career criminals.  Also, unlike forcible rape, \

is merely a legal construct that criminalizes even some of the most benign and consensual of age-gap sexual relationships between adults and teenagers.

If Ms. Harper really wanted to do something constructive for victims of actual child abuse, she could campaign to change the inheritance laws in her state jurisdiction so that no abusive parent would be allowed to cut their own children out of their will.  Of course, she's not going to do so, because there's nothing in it for her.

This \

case merits a good reason for it to be acquitted on jury nullification, because I cannot see what intelligent jury would convict Ms. Dodson for doing something that another woman in her place would have done with this 16-year-old boy if he had not come into contact with her.  I suppose that the prosecutor will search for the stupidest jurors that he or she can find.

Would you believe that so many years ago in Tennessee's neighboring state, Virginia, the police arrested a 16-year-old boy for seducing a 21-year-old woman?  I know how hard that is for any of you to wrap your brain around in light of the fact that if a 21-year-old woman were to have sexual intercourse with a 16-year-old boy today in that same state jurisdiction, she'd be the one experiencing the full wrath of the law instead.

The statutory-rape laws in our nation have never made sense.  They've always been more about societal morality than actually about the public safety.

![Jozefm84 is the creator of this image/Source:  Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2021/04/21/08/35/face-6195768_1280.png)

How much dumber is our nation going to get before we all are perforce to wake up and smell the coffee?  I do not deny that toxic sexual relationships between adults and teenagers can and do exist.  I'm also not ruling out that teenage boys can be victims of sex crimes.

Way too many teenage boys get raped in penal facilities throughout our nation.  Also, it bewilders me what people like Dawn Harper exist, whereas nobody seems to take sexual harassment seriously whenever it is a young girl that does so against a male middle-school or high-school student.

Nevertheless, none of these same above-described things mean that each and every one of us is obligated to throw a pity party for teenage hedonists who choose to manipulate our criminal justice system for their own satisfaction of one kind or another.  A sexually active high-school boy who willingly has sex in a car with a 25-year-old woman and then checks into a hotel room with her to engage in sexual intercourse with her a second time around is hardly what I call a victim.

Don't trust all the propaganda there is out there that misleads us to believe that all age-gap trysts between teenage minors and adults are exploitative and wrong.  You're doing worse than buying oceanfront property in Montana that doesn't even exist.

body.title: Content Without Consent
body.body: > Something I've come to realise with many people with regard to the digital and online space is that we're well present but have little knowledge of some of the tenets that guide the space. This is especially with my part of the world. At least I can say that in particular with a level of certainty because I've seen the ignorance in this regard, and whether to blame the people or not remains another discourse. But then, this isn't an exclusive case. People tend to be ignorant of many things when it comes to content and consent, and also the use of copyright materials. Though we seem to escape the issue, it would be painful to be unfortunate. So while people are hungry for content and content creators are equally eager to create content steadily to feed their hunger, the issue of consent and copyright shouldn't be overlooked. Of course, this isn't taken seriously in many places, and so the ignorance persists. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbifjvV5QkJUBKSETFGKVyTmou9RbQp1Nyi2jyHCAFkYs/file_00000000ea5871f4bb339ece0e590d12.png) These content creators go about creating content in public spaces, and by implication, others get to appear in the content. Not many appreciate it, while it could mean nothing to others, as long as it doesn't harm them. People have the right to take pictures and make videos in places they want as long as it's a public space, not private. The concern however is when this content is solely capturing someone without their consent. That's why I said that people need to understand and simultaneously not overlook the issue of consent and copyright, as the case may be. I wouldn't appreciate being solely and intentionally captured in content, be it picture or video without my consent. The lack of consent is a breach of my will and privacy. If it was unintentional, without actually meaning to capture me then that's a different discussion, which I won't have much concern about. People should be able to decide what content they appear in or not. Being randomly captured isn't something many might still take, but not as much as being captured intentionally, with perhaps the person being the focus. Some people just want to live a life with little to no media visibility. They just want to have a private life both on and off social media, and so, capturing such people with an intentional effort is a breach of that life they chose and desire. If you've noticed, I've been precisely using the word “intentional” because that's where the issue comes from. If you're in a public space, you can be certain that a certain content creator creating content might end up randomly capturing you as well. With the rise of content creation and content creators in our world today, it's a strong possibility. It crosses the line when that action is intentional and certainly an effort to capture someone without their consent. So then, should there be a law against such an act? If there's a clearly stated out law against that and public enough for everyone to know, it could apply. Even if not that, it should be common knowledge that capturing someone without their permission isn't right. But then, this isn't mostly a serious concern. Consequently, this could affect content creators and the need for originality, but mostly those who choose to solely use others without their consent. --- *Image is AI generated.* --- ###### Thank you for reading!

body.title: SOCIAL MEDIA AND ITS IMPACT IN DAILY LIFE
body.body:
Social media has become a big part of our daily lives. Almost everyone uses platforms like Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, or WhatsApp to communicate, learn new things, or simply relax. Whether we are chatting with friends, watching entertaining videos, or reading the latest news, social media has changed the way we connect with the world. In my opinion, social media has had a positive impact on my daily life, but I also believe it is important to use it in moderation.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPF4xXsgLEWeFtNyLJ9XShvJ86THRqzXUQbNjZpBRP6DJ/1000237049.png 


[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/ai-generated-social-media-impact-8484741/)

One of the biggest advantages of social media is that it helps me stay connected with family and friends, especially those who live far away. A simple message, video call, or shared photo can make us feel close even when we are in different places. It also makes it easy to celebrate birthdays, share important moments, and keep up with each other's lives without having to travel.

Another reason I appreciate social media is that it gives me access to so much useful information. Whenever I want to learn something new, I can find tutorials, educational videos, or articles within minutes. From cooking recipes and fitness tips to study advice and career guidance, there is always something valuable to discover. I have learned many practical skills through social media that I now use in my everyday life, even fashion designing can be learnt easily on social media.

But the thing is I know that social media is not perfect. Spending too much time scrolling through posts can become a bad habit. Sometimes people compare themselves to others without realizing that many photos and videos only show the best moments of someone's life. This can make people feel unhappy or pressured to live up to unrealistic expectations. Social media can also become a distraction from school, work, or spending quality time with the people around us.

For this reason, I believe it is important to find a healthy balance. One way to do this is by setting limits on how much time we spend online each day. Instead of checking our phones every few minutes, we can focus on activities like exercising or spending time with family, or enjoying our hobbies. Taking short breaks from social media can also help us feel more relaxed and present in our daily lives.

It is equally important to be responsible while using social media. We should think before posting, treat others with kindness, and avoid sharing false information. Choosing to follow positive, educational, and inspiring content can make our online experience much healthier and more enjoyable.

Social media is a powerful tool that has made communication, learning, and self-expression easier than ever before. It has helped me stay connected with people I care about, discover new ideas, and develop new interests. At the same time, I understand that using it responsibly is essential. When we balance our time online with meaningful real-life experiences, social media can become something that improves our lives instead of taking control of them.



**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

body.title: Lo que hoy le hacen a ellas nos lo pueden hacer a todas |
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme1C33H4LefNNwWBtpipagA8UmKEFFmcZzhCeACybgGnf/1782851111965.jpg)
Foto de portada: Elin Tabitha en [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/es/@elintabitha)

Llevo ocho años estudiando la mente humana y ninguno de esos años me ha preparado para entender cómo se sostiene, día tras día, un sistema diseñado para borrar a la mitad de una población. Hablo de Afganistán. Hablo de las mujeres afganas, que hoy, en 2026, no tienen derecho a pisar una oficina de Naciones Unidas, no tienen derecho a estudiar medicina, no tienen derecho a salir de su casa sin un hombre que las autorice, no tienen derecho, según un decreto reciente, ni siquiera a separarse de un marido sin que él pueda anular esa decisión con su sola palabra.

No es retórica. No es exageración para generar indignación fácil. Es ley. Desde que los talibanes retomaron el poder en agosto de 2021, han emitido más de 150 edictos que regulan, restringen y vigilan cada movimiento de una mujer. Naciones Unidas lo ha llamado, sin rodeos, apartheid de género: un sistema institucionalizado que decide a dónde puede ir una mujer, si puede hablar, trabajar, aprender, recibir atención médica, o simplemente existir en público. En enero de este año se les comunicó a las funcionarias civiles que llevaban desde 2021 cobrando un salario reducido por quedarse en casa, que ya ni siquiera recibirían ese pago. Sin explicación. Sin proceso. Sin nada.

Desde septiembre de 2025 los soldados talibanes impiden físicamente que las mujeres, incluidas trabajadoras de la ONU, entren a las sedes de Naciones Unidas en el país. Imagínate eso: hombres armados parados en una puerta decidiendo quién tiene derecho a trabajar por su género. Y mientras tanto, las niñas siguen sin poder pisar un aula después de sexto grado, las mujeres siguen sin poder graduarse de medicina —ya van dos años consecutivos de exámenes de graduación médica sin una sola mujer presente—, y un nuevo código penal aprobado este año solo reconoce la violencia doméstica como delito si deja huesos rotos o heridas visibles. Lo demás, lo que no deja marca, no cuenta. Ese mismo código castiga con tres meses de cárcel a una mujer que visite a su familia sin permiso de su esposo y se niegue a volver a casa cuando un tribunal se lo ordene. Y en mayo se publicó un decreto que facilita el matrimonio infantil, deshaciendo protecciones legales que existían antes de 2021.

Yo soy mujer. Soy psicóloga. Soy feminista. Y necesito decir algo que a veces la gente no entiende bien cuando una mujer dice esa palabra: ser feminista no es odiar a los hombres. Es rebelarse contra un sistema, el patriarcado, que decide que mi cuerpo, mi voz, mi educación y mi libertad de movimiento le pertenecen a otro. Ese sistema no es exclusivo de Afganistán. Tiene allí su forma más extrema, más legalizada, más brutal, pero las raíces están en todas partes, incluida mi consulta, donde escucho semana tras semana a mujeres que cargan con miedo, con culpa, con la sensación de que ocupar espacio es un acto de transgresión.

Sé que en web3 casi nadie habla de esto. Aquí hablamos de tokens, de DeFi, de cripto, de contenido ligero y monetizable. Y está bien, yo también escribo sobre eso. Pero hoy elijo usar este espacio, que es mío, que está construido sobre la idea de que cualquiera puede tener una voz sin que un algoritmo o un gobierno la silencie, para gritar por las que no pueden gritar. Porque ellas no tienen voz oficial. Se la quitaron por decreto. Y si el mundo deja de mirar, ese silencio se vuelve permanente.

No escribo esto solo por compasión hacia un país lejano. Lo escribo porque cada derecho que perdemos en un lugar del mundo legitima que se intente quitar en otro. Lo que le pasa a una mujer afgana hoy es una advertencia de lo que el patriarcado, cuando tiene el poder absoluto, está dispuesto a hacer. Defender sus derechos no es un gesto simbólico lejano: es parte de la misma lucha que sostenemos aquí, en Cuba, en Latinoamérica, en cualquier país donde a una mujer se le diga que su lugar es callado y en casa.

No tengo una solución desde mi blog. No voy a fingir que un post en Hive cambia una ley talibán. Pero sí puedo negarme al silencio cómodo. Puedo nombrar lo que está pasando con la claridad que merece, sin suavizarlo, sin convertirlo en una nota más que se desliza en el scroll. Y puedo recordarte, quien sea que estés leyendo esto, que los derechos que hoy das por sentados —estudiar, trabajar, divorciarte, salir sola a la calle— son exactamente los que a ellas les arrebataron uno por uno, con la misma excusa de siempre: orden, tradición, virtud. Lo que se les hizo a ellas se le puede hacer a cualquiera si dejamos de pelear.

Hoy mi voz es por ellas. Mañana, espero, sea una voz más entre muchas.

---


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQme1C33H4LefNNwWBtpipagA8UmKEFFmcZzhCeACybgGnf/1782851239661.jpg)

I have spent five years studying the human mind, and none of those years prepared me to understand how a system designed to erase half a population sustains itself, day after day. I'm talking about Afghanistan. I'm talking about Afghan women, who today, in 2026, have no right to step into a United Nations office, no right to study medicine, no right to leave their homes without a man's authorization, no right, according to a recent decree, to even separate from a husband without him being able to override that decision with his word alone.

This isn't rhetoric. It isn't exaggeration meant to provoke easy outrage. It is law. Since the Taliban retook power in August 2021, they have issued more than 150 edicts regulating, restricting, and surveilling every movement a woman makes. The United Nations has called it, plainly, gender apartheid: an institutionalized system that dictates where a woman can go, whether she can speak, work, learn, or receive medical care, or simply exist in public. This past January, female civil servants who had been staying home since 2021 on a reduced salary were told that payment would stop entirely. No explanation. No process. Nothing.

Since September 2025, Taliban soldiers have physically prevented women, including UN staff, from entering UN premises in the country. Picture that: armed men at a gate deciding who has the right to work based on gender. Meanwhile, girls still cannot attend school past sixth grade, women still cannot graduate from medical school — two consecutive years now of medical graduation exams held without a single woman present — and a new criminal code passed this year only recognizes domestic violence as a crime if it leaves broken bones or visible injuries. Anything that doesn't leave a mark doesn't count. That same code sentences a woman to three months in prison for visiting her family without her husband's permission and refusing a court order to return home. And in May, a decree was published that makes child marriage easier, undoing legal protections that existed before 2021.

I am a woman. I am a psychologist. I am a feminist. And I need to say something people sometimes misunderstand when a woman uses that word: being a feminist doesn't mean hating men. It means rebelling against a system, patriarchy, that decides my body, my voice, my education, and my freedom of movement belong to someone else. That system isn't exclusive to Afghanistan. There it takes its most extreme, most legalized, most brutal form, but its roots are everywhere, including in my own practice, where week after week I listen to women carrying fear, guilt, the sense that simply taking up space is an act of transgression.

I know almost no one talks about this in web3. Here we talk about tokens, DeFi, crypto, light and monetizable content. And that's fine, I write about that too. But today I choose to use this space, which is mine, built on the idea that anyone can have a voice without an algorithm or a government silencing it, to scream for those who can't scream for themselves. Because they have no official voice. It was taken from them by decree. And if the world stops looking, that silence becomes permanent.

I'm not writing this only out of compassion for a distant country. I'm writing it because every right lost in one part of the world legitimizes the attempt to take it away somewhere else. What is happening to an Afghan woman today is a warning of what patriarchy, when given absolute power, is willing to do. Defending her rights isn't a distant symbolic gesture: it's part of the same fight we carry here, in Cuba, in Latin America, in any country where a woman is told her place is quiet and at home.

I don't have a solution from my blog. I won't pretend a post on Hive changes a Taliban law. But I can refuse comfortable silence. I can name what is happening with the clarity it deserves, without softening it, without letting it become just another note sliding past in the scroll. And I can remind you, whoever you are reading this, that the rights you take for granted today — studying, working, divorcing, walking alone outside — are exactly the ones taken from them one by one, with the same old excuse: order, tradition, virtue. What was done to them can be done to anyone if we stop fighting.

Today my voice is for them. Tomorrow, I hope, it's one voice among many.

---

body.title: Day 9 - Government Camp, OR (USA)
body.body:
*(original date June 24, 2026. Almost all caught up. This backlog is taking up all of my Resource Credits, so I’m excited to get up to date so I can start Hive’ing fr (smiley face))*

Tucked off of Highway 26, right at the bottom of the Timberline access road of Mount Hood, lies a roughly one mile “loop” that hosts an unincorporated community called Government Camp. With a population of 179, the tiny town known as “Govy” is home to many of the year round Timberline employees and some deep pocket second homes. On any given day you’ll likely find the tourists and campers strongly outnumber the locals.










![IMG_1286.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdSMNJHwjR6YXy2Tr1Wv7ZAFx4s6GpHKM4Bq8HMz31MEq/IMG_1286.jpeg)








If you’ve never lived in a mountain town or another location similar in terms of it’s economic survival relying on tourism, the lack of housing, second home buyers, and low wages create rather unique living situations for the local employees. I lived in a similar town back on the east coast. In that scenario, due to extreme weather conditions and stricter DMV regulations, car living is less popular for the workers- although by no means unheard of. Instead, it wouldn’t be uncommon to find 8-10 people living in a 3-bedroom place; with people sleeping in the living room being a common occurrence. In Govy’s case, on the other hand, car/camper/rig living is much more common. 





![IMG_1284.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbjDA4vnGa72ndb6JvCMk1rjFioXrpwTNg1R27p9RfeGh/IMG_1284.jpeg)
*the local Chevron welcomes visitors at the top of the loop. It is known as the “Bev’ron” by locals, for obvious reasons*

Resources are hard to come by in this area. There is a general store in Govy. It is a great little store but the prices definitely reflect the tourism and if you’re stuck relying on it for groceries… well, you’re cooked. The next “town” is down a substantial hill about 8 miles away, which used to have a store. Said store has closed within the last year, however, so all you’ll find there is a dispensary, a coffee shop, a pizza place, a Dairy Queen(never understood this one), and a small motel. Continue down a little farther, and you’ll find a shopping center with the Thriftway grocery store. Unless you want to burn a bunch of gas to continue down the road to Sandy, this is where you’ll be buying groceries. And it ain’t cheap, either.





![IMG_1288.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbALsNWj7rzNN9nZvHjfUadSd3Dv95DviKxgoiiWnuD2w/IMG_1288.jpeg)


There’s no real point to all of this. I’m just trying to provide a general feel for the area. Because it really is quite unique. Given that most of my day was spent similar to yesterday- doing boring stuff on my phone in the electricity hub, I decided to make a little post about this tiny mountain town that I have spent oh so much time in. 









![IMG_1292.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX1dzj4z3j9VtdhSjHc5Q71cuE333hFQksSC6VCWzP6Sz/IMG_1292.jpeg)





The summers bring on the campers and training athletes. The town becomes filled with everyone from little kids getting sent to summer skiing/snowboarding camp to hundreds of seasonal transplants from all over the northern hemisphere to seasoned Olympic athletes and professional company teams. You’ll see someone you recognize from a Wheatie’s box buying coffee from Fernie’s right before almost getting run over by a mob of 12 year olds from the Midwest on bikes. 





![IMG_1287.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPXcy3rC55Sr6MDL5k7dCeiAPbXxAXpVrTBw8VwCmHYAT/IMG_1287.jpeg)



It also creates a surprisingly lively night life for such a small remote place. Music sets ranging all the way from country to rap to punk will occasionally happen in Charlie’s, the local’s choice dive bar that has everything from pub fare to a horseshoe pit to a cigarette vending machine. Or there could be a metal show across the street at the Ratskellar, a cool little basement bar that hosts a large outdoor seating area and two levels of arcade. 






![IMG_1289.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmerQUNeHsJtTRs6cRthpDKjCVxaykj2PNUHVd1iRKQvS9/IMG_1289.jpeg)
*the outside of the Ratskellar, or simply the Rat, attached to an amazing cafe that unfortunately has shut down since the last time I was here. RIP to the best breakfast sandwiches in the area*

About halfway down the loop you’ll find a bridge across highway 26 to a small neighborhood and Govy’s other local ski area, Ski Bowl. In the summer they have an outdoor adventure park, including go karts, bungee jumping, mini golf, alpine slides, etc. I wanted to go check it out for myself because it had been years since I’ve seen it but they weren’t open yet when I walked over and they don’t take kindly to people walking around over there that aren’t customers. I tried to go for a hike one evening a few years ago and I got chased down by security. It’s the only time I think I’ve ever been told i cant hike on a ski resort in the summer.





![IMG_1290.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdR5kTQFXULpnQJbmPbqZ1ZyGnm7v7xP1ks6oZEEv3AbB/IMG_1290.jpeg)


This whole area has a direct historical tie to the Oregon trail and the odd town name comes from an event in the 19th century when militia carts and supplies were found abandoned here by travelers of the Barlow trail. You can walk much of the trail around here and although I have only ever gone a couple miles on various stretches it would be really cool to take a long haul. The road I was previously camping on exists because of said trail, and there’s some very cool abandoned stretches of road from prior to the construction of the highway at the end of it.




![IMG_1291.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcvTqfbDUTvmLGzCrAS6JJG7R7FdnKtxJT4DsEnmw218y/IMG_1291.jpeg)


I think I’ll probably spend a few days van camping up here in town. The forest road has been a little isolating so it’s nice being around some folk and also having unlimited access to water, etc. The water is thanks to the rest area at the top, right next to the Bev’ron. Rarely a day goes by I don’t visit this rest area while I’m out here 😂 Right from the parking lot of the rest stop is yet another small ski area, that lies on the run out from Mt Hood. During years where there is more snow you can ski/ride all the way to town up until some time in May. It’s a really fun thing to do at the end of the day, and I would frequently leave my car in the loop and take the bus up to the mountain just for the ride down.






![IMG_1282.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUj5VFDphSRkMsoRjq1LkmJncb7rJQb8qEGALXAzyzQb8/IMG_1282.jpeg)



Hope this finds everyone well and that you are finding some way today to enjoy yourself, even if it’s the smallest thing. Keep on thriving and keep on keeping on. The world’s a mess and all we can do is try :)





![IMG_1293.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc76W8uf7HvtzaEcGHmqnRC3Xo6beKbid14s5HdPqS3iT/IMG_1293.jpeg)

body.title: [ENG-SPN] Where the Muse Was Born / Donde Nació la Musa
body.body:
![P1040028.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EpGQf4H1yLprQ9Fkxb2ayUXqJWtUWCeu6ENyWVntj21n5wPMqu8u6B2EBLjMrqcEd4p.JPG)

On June 12, 1894, Leonor Izquierdo was born in this castle. A woman who may go unnoticed by many, but who, for lovers of Literature and Poetry, will always represent the Alpha and Omega of that poet who, like the sailor in one of his most famous poems, also created a garden by the sea and became a gardener: Antonio Machado.

![P1040018.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/2432Hq52bf9Ji9ftYacMmshGb3daHHCTstgLPFKE6QWk7jrKhPffjsf57vjKcNvmHm3P3.JPG)

We are in Almenar, and at the time of the birth of Machado's Muse and first wife, this medieval castle, whose walls, even after restoration, had witnessed the wild grandeur of medieval times, was a Civil Guard barracks, where Sergeant Ceferino Izquierdo Caballero served.

![P1040023.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EpviLqWXJHXhb9EtevkZXBABxfZKYWdenkJ21Z3c7WgTcv3saaynmfpw7k66RREmoM9.JPG)

We are in another of those magical places in Soria, located just a few meters from one of its most important sanctuaries, that of the Virgin of La Llana, and that mysterious branch of the Soria-Aragonese road, which, a few kilometers further on, also cast another long shadow: that of the Templars from the neighboring town of Peroniel.

![P1040025.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/2432KytLs3DCswfF2AjDxmZ6vojitZHDYkiVKRiVP5wRYdH4YBHLHX8UkMb65pGoXCJLQ.JPG)

Un 12 de junio de 1894 nació en este castillo Leonor Izquierdo, una mujer que para muchos pasará desapercibida, pero que para los amantes de la Literatura y de la Poesía, significará siempre el Alfa y el Omega de aquel poeta, que, como el marinero de uno de sus poemas más conocidos, hizo también un jardín junto al mar y se metió a jardinero: Antonio Machado.

![P1040026.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/EpVB89SHj5wU8852v2NwT6nhcwAQjhrCyN8VHo4J3gSB2fXEHhhceQPi9qMFi65zGoc.JPG)

Estamos en Almenar y por la época del nacimiento de la Musa y primera esposa de Machado, este castillo medieval, cuyos muros, incluso restaurados habían conocido la salvaje grandeza de los tiempos medievales, era un cuartel de la Guardia Civil, donde prestaba servicio el sargento Ceferino Izquierdo Caballero.

![P1040039.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/23rAZr7CQ1hkASw6dFTNoNfU2p6MBqEDYmoEJ9AeHdV2SwQFn5WWXwk6XbWAMz3aQp1zK.JPG)

Estamos en otro de esos lugares de la Soria Magica, situado a escasos metros de uno de los santuarios más relevantes, como es el de la Virgen de la Llana y ese misterioso ramal del camino soriano-aragonés, que, además, contó, algunos kilómetros más adelante, con otra sombra alargada: la de los templarios del vecino pueblo de Peroniel.

![P1040046.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/juancar347/244xuFJorGK4ZGzKrxUYBwr5STdMxNyjgvWq3WoDV39xtDwmfrVK2yr1YbWp4ga3S8bHd.JPG)

body.title: Television Review: Hands and Knees (Mad Men, S4x10, 2010)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/iTQGuow9dlkeJYC39AqTTjIC5pk.jpg)


**Hands and Knees (S4x10)**

Airdate: 26 September 2010

Written by: Jonathan Abrahams & Matthew Weiner
Directed by: Lynn Shelton

Running Time: 48 minutes



Television series frequently rely on the dramatic convenience of cramming multiple narrative threads into a single episode, a technique that can often feel contrived or artificial. However, when that convergence of events is driven by the cold, unyielding grip of Murphy’s Law—the cynical axiom that anything that can go wrong will go wrong—such conveniences cease to feel manufactured and become deeply resonant. This is precisely the territory explored in *Hands and Knees*, the tenth episode of the fourth season of Mad Men. Here, SCDP and its staff experience a relentless barrage of personal and professional disasters within the span of mere days, validating the viewer’s own experiences of chaos.

The episode is firmly anchored to the historical calendar of Sunday, 15 August 1965, a date most famously etched into pop culture immortality by the Beatles' performance at Shea Stadium in New York. This momentous occasion provides the backdrop for Don Draper’s brief, flickering moment of domestic bliss. Having somehow managed to procure two tickets to see the Fab Four, Don intends to take Sally, who is an ardent admirer of the group. It is a charming, if fleeting, gesture of paternal affection that stands in stark contrast to the storm gathering around him.

Meanwhile, the personal life of Joan Holloway takes a dark, desperate turn. Her brief, illicit tryst with Roger Sterling in an alleyway has resulted in a pregnancy. The stakes are incredibly high because her husband, Greg, is currently deployed in Vietnam. If she were to give birth, the timing would inevitably reveal that the child is not his, shattering the foundation of her marriage. After agonising over the dilemma, Joan opts for the sensible, albeit heart-wrenching, path. She accepts Roger’s offer of $400 to terminate the pregnancy. It is a transactional solution born of desperation, stripping away the glamour of her position and reducing her to a woman facing a life-altering choice without the support of her husband.

Roger’s own world is crumbling just as surely as Joan’s personal turmoil. Following a dinner with Lee Garner, Jr., the head of Lucky Strike, Roger receives the devastating news that the company is closing its account. As the inheritor of this account from his father, Lucky Strike serves as the financial backbone of SCDP. Upon realising that he cannot sway the executives of British American Tobacco, Roger manages to extract only a thirty-day reprieve. This window is the only opportunity he has to “put his affairs in order” and discover how to plug the sudden, gaping financial black hole that now threatens to consume the agency.

The financial pressure is compounded by personal humiliation for Lane Pryce. He had hoped to meet his son, Nigel, but is instead summoned by his father, Robert (W. Morgan Sheppard). Robert arrives to issue a blunt ultimatum: Lane must return to England and “put his family in order.” Lane’s response is a defiant, almost desperate attempt to assert his independence. He invites his father to the Playboy Club, intending to introduce him to Toni Charles (Naturi Naughton), a Black woman who is also his girlfriend. The scene is meant to shock and impress, showcasing Lane’s life in America. However, when they are alone, Robert’s veneer of politeness cracks. The former salesman, using a cane, beats Lane with brutal efficiency, physically brings him to his knees, and forces him to capitulate to his father’s will. The next day, Lane informs his partners that he will be taking a few weeks off, effectively retreating from the battlefield.

Perhaps the most intense pressure is placed on Don Draper himself. The episode throws a curveball in the form of two officials from the US Defense Department who arrive at Betty’s door. This forces a security check on Don, ostensibly because SCDP has been running ads for North American Aviation. The irony is bitter; Don signed the necessary forms without even understanding what they were for. The investigation poses a terrifying risk: even if Don has no Communist ties, the probe could potentially expose him as the impostor and deserter he is, landing him in jail. This prospect plunges Don into a state of paranoid delirium, manifesting as actual physical sickness. He confesses his fears to Faye, who tends to him with a mix of professional detachment and genuine concern. Just as Don awaits his fate, Pete Campbell intervenes. Pete, who knows the truth about Don’s identity, leverages his connections in the Defense Department to vouch for him. He informs Don that he is not a suspect—at least not yet—but Don, unwilling to gamble with his life, decides to drop the NAA account entirely. This decision sacrifices a valuable client for the sake of security. It is a moment of profound personal humiliation for Pete, who accepts the loss for the team. Later, at the partners’ meeting, Roger scolds Pete for ruining the account, hypocritically hiding the news of the impending loss of Lucky Strike.

Under the direction of Lynn Shelton, a filmmaker best known for her work in the American mumblecore movement, *Hands and Knees* functions as one of the stronger episodes of Season 4. The script, co-written by Jonathan Abrahams and Matthew Weiner, handles these disparate storylines with impressive efficiency. The writers cleverly employ ironic juxtaposition, contrasting the innocence of the Beatles' music with the industrial grit of corporate betrayal. Jon Hamm delivers another great display of subtle acting in this episode. His character, Don Draper, is in a state of advanced psychological distress; his paranoia, guilt, and despair have progressed beyond mere emotion into actual physical sickness. Hamm captures this deterioration with chilling precision, making the viewer feel the weight of Don’s existential dread.

The episode concludes with a bittersweet note. Don clutches the tickets for the Beatles concert, the promise of a moment of joy, yet he gazes longingly at Megan, his new secretary. It is a look that suggests he is already moving on, or perhaps drifting away from the domestic life he tried to salvage. *Hands and Knees* is a masterclass in misfortune, where the characters are battered by forces beyond their control. It validates the viewer’s own experiences of Murphy’s Law, turning the convenience of television plotting into a visceral commentary on the fragility of life.


RATING: 7/10 (+++)

body.title: 1964 Lancia Flavia Coupé — Elegance by Pininfarina
body.body:
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQhoeTr9Ypd8XueERKxup6mG1sF9gMeZEdheZMw5XGore/b6105106b4a8a0a4.jpg)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdWTrCYCt2m37CnuEagay6dtmSULnF3Xc37UDFx1D1ete/2fa123840a1de16b.jpg)</center>

---

### 1964 Lancia Flavia Coupé — Elegance by Pininfarina

The **Lancia Flavia Coupé** is one of the most elegant Italian cars of the 1960s, yet it remains surprisingly underrated. Produced from 1962 to 1970, the Flavia was Lancia’s mid-range model, positioned above the compact Fulvia and below the flagship Flaminia. But while the Fulvia and Flaminia get most of the glory, the Flavia Coupé — especially the version bodied by **Pininfarina** — is a masterpiece of restrained Italian design.

The Flavia was launched as a saloon in 1960, but the car you see here is the Coupé version, introduced in 1962 with bodywork by Pininfarina. It featured clean, flowing lines with a delicate grille, elegant proportions, and just enough chrome to catch the light without being flashy. It is Italian design at its most sophisticated.

<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTuA3y3KSFU3VniN8et4XtmnPgZK1wWPLt992CGGhmWT1/52c1c9143e9cb549.jpg)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNfQvUzBXwX9HDdRBSi8bttZrEhmwdazexB22J8XTFVjm/9b96f5901e5d1e38.jpg)</center>

### Under the Bonnet

The Flavia was ahead of its time in one significant way: it was one of the first Italian cars to feature **front-wheel drive**, designed by the legendary Antonio Fessia.

| Spec | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Engine | 1.8L flat-four (boxer) |
| Power | **92 hp** at 5,200 rpm |
| Torque | **102 lb-ft** at 3,500 rpm |
| Top Speed | ~170 km/h (106 mph) |
| 0–100 km/h | ~12 seconds |
| Transmission | 4-speed manual |
| Drive | Front-wheel drive |
| Designer | Pininfarina |

The flat-four boxer engine gave the Flavia a low centre of gravity — a key advantage for handling — and the front-wheel-drive layout provided excellent traction. The engine was smooth and refined, pushing the car to a respectable 170 km/h.

The Coupé also featured disc brakes on all four wheels and independent suspension, giving it handling that was well above average for its class.

<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXaYBedwNrBedJHo4r29Cn7xGHkutiWAhTVoKwpwcns3g/eb36e602b1968787.webp)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNoQgAvTvJeDUTp4NoRJCVPwwqcYwNPiYSsJ9q9xp2xHu/fa2e58b43254015a.webp)</center>

### Pininfarina’s Touch

The Flavia Coupé was designed and built by **Pininfarina** at their Grugliasco plant near Turin. The collaboration between Lancia and Pininfarina produced some of the most beautiful cars of the era, and the Flavia Coupé is a prime example.

The styling is subtle compared to some of its contemporaries. There are no dramatic tailfins or aggressive lines. Instead, the Flavia Coupé relies on perfect proportions, a delicate chrome grille, and a gracefully sloping roofline. The rear three-quarter view is particularly lovely, with a gentle Kamm tail and clean surfaces.

Inside, the cabin was typically Lancia: beautifully appointed with high-quality materials, a wood-rimmed steering wheel, and elegantly simple instrumentation. The front seats were supportive, and the rear seats offered decent space for two adults — a genuine 2+2.

Lancia also offered a more powerful **Flavia Coupé 1.8 Sport** with twin carburettors producing 100 hp, and a rare **Flavia Coupé 2000** with a 2.0L engine.

<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRrn9Hxp2XWaTvJUgvSUCgmpGesVsebK9dA9Y8vbKfWwh/79a467a270403978.webp)</center>
<center>![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYnUCfAz5jTrMrEN3uMnWb5ENFYr24ixLxY9mbcd36cAk/ef92809aa290e46b.jpg)</center>

### Lancia in South Africa

Lancia has a fascinating history in South Africa. The brand was imported into SA from the 1950s and developed a loyal following among discerning buyers who appreciated Lancia’s engineering sophistication and style.

The **Flavia** was sold through official Lancia importers in South Africa, and a number of Coupés found their way to SA buyers. The Flavia was particularly well-suited to South African conditions — its front-wheel drive and robust flat-four engine handled SA’s varied roads with ease, while Pininfarina’s elegant bodywork was perfect for the country club set.

Lancia had a strong presence in South African motorsport as well, with the Fulvia HF and Stratos achieving notable success in local rallies. The Lancia Motor Club of South Africa keeps the brand’s legacy alive today, with regular events and a passionate community of owners.

Flavia Coupés are rare in South Africa today, but they are highly prized by collectors who understand their significance. A well-maintained example is a ticket to an exclusive club of Italian car enthusiasts who value engineering sophistication over flashy displays.

### Legacy

The Flavia Coupé remained in production until 1970, with approximately 30,000 Coupés built (out of a total Flavia production of around 100,000). It was succeeded by the Lancia 2000 Coupé, which continued the same formula.

Today, the Flavia Coupé is one of the more affordable classic Italian coupes, offering Pininfarina design and Lancia engineering at a fraction of the price of a Ferrari or Maserati of the same era. Good examples can be found for **$15,000–$30,000**, making them one of the best-value Italian classics on the market.

For those in the know, the Flavia Coupé represents the perfect combination of Italian elegance, engineering innovation, and everyday usability. It is a car that rewards the discerning enthusiast who values substance over show.

---

*Sources:*
- [Wikipedia — Lancia Flavia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancia_Flavia)
- [Lancia Motor Club (UK) — Flavia Register](https://www.lanciamotorclub.co.uk/)
- [Classic Driver — Lancia Flavia Coupé](https://www.classicdriver.com/en/car/lancia/flavia/1965/819361)
- [Pininfarina — Lancia Flavia Coupé](https://www.pininfarina.com/)

---

*Lancia is one of those brands that true car enthusiasts hold in high regard, but the general public often overlooks. Have you ever owned a Lancia, or is there another underrated Italian classic you love? Share your thoughts in the comments!*

body.body:
> ‎The rate at which people make use of public recording for different purposes is quite alarming. This is common among people who earn from content creation, such as prank videos or films. Lawfully, humans interaction with our environment is categorized into two segments, private space and public space. For private space; it can be understood to be our homes, private clubs and gatherings where recordings are forbidden. ‎ ‎While places like eateries, transit, tourist centre and in the street, these places are seen as public space. This is what we have accepted and tolerated over the years, so whatever recording is taken of us in places considered to be public space, we wouldn't care much about it. But those were days when there was less recording of our faces. People now make money filming people inappropriately, you can be walking through the street and someone suddenly pranks you to capture your reaction. ‎ ‎You see, in that moment you are not as composed as you would want to be in a public space not to talk of being recorded. But the person does it anyway without requesting your permission. For most people, they would let it slide since it has become a norm but is there any law protecting us from being recorded in a public space? there is. In my own country, under the NDPA - The Nigeria data protection act, capturing an individual image even in a public space is considered invasion of privacy because a person's image is part of his or her data, especially when done without seeking consent. ‎ ‎Here is where it becomes a little complex, in order for a person to raise an alarm or sue a person and have credible stand, he or she must be targeted in the recording, at least to an extent. This is why I specifically mentioned prank videos, these videos are created to capture people's reaction after they have been pranked. In a case like this, an individual face had become the focus of the filming not an incidental shot captured. In a case were a person accidentally appear in a recording, probably in a news report or some other kinds of recording, as long as the person is not captured in appropriate manner that might defame the person, it is not considered invasion of privacy. ‎ ‎Normally, such videos will go through editing and it is quite obvious that obscure scenes should be removed to avoid legal issues or to avoid scenes that would make the recording inappropriate for public consumption. For example, imagine someone recording in the street, probably street filming, and a passerby cloth suddenly drops. In a situation like this, the person is not the focus of the recording but despite that, the person's image and identity has been captured inappropriately. If whoever records the film still goes ahead without omitting that scene and broadcast it for public consumption. Then whoever produces such content will face serious legal issues without being able to hide under incidental shot. ‎ ‎It has become public knowledge visible to all, that a person has been captured inappropriately. This is why the broadcast industry goes through lot of lawsuit and scrutiny but in this era of content creators, these individuals have little or no knowledge of their legal boundaries. That is not the only issue, the citizens are not also aware of the law that protects them from being violated in public space. In a country where people don't know their boundaries, rights and limitations; right infringement becomes what we tolerate. ‎ ****** ****** ‎_This write-up was inspired by weekly featured content titled ***Your face alone*** in hive learners community._ ‎ ****** ***** ‎ ‎_***Cover Image - generated using chatgpt***_ ‎ **** ***** ‎ ‎ ‎ ‎![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmVNhTyUg4Aq2RTHWnTXsaS4758biE3M9xtHurNqYAe8XT/img_0.8353900969042101.jpg) ‎
***THANKS FOR VISITING MY BLOG***

body.title: ‎Haaland Did It Again! Norway's Late Winner Broke Ivory Coast Hearts
body.body:
‎I really enjoyed watching this match because it had everything you want from a World Cup knockout game, good football, plenty of drama, and a late winner that completely changed the story.
‎ https://img.leopedia.io/DQmYHNNaQfbwFgYKEaxXS9nDeNKJkSsX8NLGvPimwY169aC/LbT8pvYpWI1o_wWKScYfG9r93_1440x960.jpg 

‎[Source](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/ivory-coast-vs-norway-live-updates-world-cup-2026-score-result/XPK77E5y1hKM/)
‎
‎Before kickoff, I expected Ivory Coast to give Norway a difficult game, and they definitely lived up to that expectation. In fact, there were moments when I thought the African side looked more dangerous. They controlled large spells of the match, created good chances, and never looked intimidated by Norway.
‎
‎Even though Norway scored first through Antonio Nusa with a beautiful curling effort, I didn't feel the game was over. Ivory Coast kept pushing forward, and their determination was rewarded in the second half.
‎
‎The player who impressed me the most for Ivory Coast was Amad Diallo. What an impact he made after coming off the bench! He first made a brilliant goal-line clearance to stop Norway from doubling their lead, then went up the other end and scored a fantastic solo goal. That equaliser was fully deserved, and at that point I honestly believed Ivory Coast could go on and win the match.
‎
‎Then football reminded us why Erling Haaland is one of the best strikers in the world.
‎
‎For most of the match, he was surprisingly quiet. He barely had any clear chances and was not involved as much as we are used to seeing. But great strikers don't need ten opportunities to make a difference. They only need one.
‎
‎When the cross came into the box in the closing minutes, Haaland was exactly where a world-class striker should be. He calmly tapped the ball into the net and sent Norway into the last 16. It was not the most spectacular goal, but it was the one that mattered most.
‎
‎I feel sorry for Ivory Coast because I don't think they deserved to leave the tournament without taking the game to extra time. They fought hard, played positive football, and gave Norway a real test. Unfortunately, knockout football is often decided by tiny moments, and Norway had the player who could deliver in the biggest moment.
‎
‎Now all eyes turn to Norway's clash with Brazil. That promises to be one of the standout matches of the next round. Brazil have quality all over the pitch, but if they give Haaland even a small chance, he'll be ready to punish them.
‎
‎This game was another reminder that football is not always about who has the most possession or creates the most chances. Sometimes it's simply about having that one player who can step up when it matters most. Norway had that player, and his name is Erling Haaland.
‎

body.title: How the Premier League Became One of Britain's Greatest Exports
body.body:
The UK economy is struggling in many respects, but the Premier League is a real success story.... it is one of Britain’s biggest cultural and commercial hits. 

Premier League games reach people everywhere, on every continent. The audiences aren't just big; they're massive. Billions flow back into the British economy. 

Around 40 countries in the current world cup have at least one premier league player in their squad...

While politicians keep arguing about industrial strategy and chasing economic growth, English football shows what a world-beating brand actually looks like.

### A League for the Planet

The numbers almost don't look real.

Broadcast deals mean Premier League matches go out to 191 countries—pretty much the whole planet. The biggest games can pull in over 700 million viewers, which makes stadiums and even other major sporting events seem tiny by comparison. Even the Super Bowl—that all-American giant—draws less than half the crowd.

The Premier League has somehow burrowed its way into cultures everywhere. Bars from New York to Lagos pack out with fans. Kids across Asia walk around in Arsenal and Liverpool shirts. People even pick up English football slang: In South Korea, someone’s “Leeds days” means their golden era. Swedish politicians talk about being “Spursy” when they flop at the last hurdle.


### A Smart Business Story

Premier League didn’t just stumble into being the world’s richest football league.

The English game turned to television before anyone else realized how much money global broadcasting rights would bring. Those early international deals weren’t huge moneymakers, but building a global audience gave English football a head start nobody else could catch up with.

Now, overseas broadcasting rights are worth billions.

The Premier League pumps around £10 billion a year into the UK economy. It’s not just about football clubs.... there’s broadcasting, hospitality, tourism, marketing, and a raft of other jobs that rely on the league.

However most clubs don’t rake in huge profits. Last year, only four Premier League sides turned a pre-tax profit. Running a football club is expensive, especially when players’ wages keep rising.

But the league itself keeps thriving. The international appeal just keeps getting stronger.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23w2F6JQJavnvsfhPZhn1y8Ke4ZL7N17FjFvVJaYnEodJzbWcWbXXgyjnUt2u4RZyuY9S.png)


### More Than just a Game

There’s a bigger point for Britain here.

Too often, the country seems stuck talking about decline instead of looking for the next global success. The Premier League is that! 

It also proves British exports don’t have to be physical goods. The country can sell entertainment, stories, personalities—pure culture. As AI, creative industries, and tech keep growing, this kind of export will only get more important.

The Premier League is living proof Britain can still top the world, when it gets the right ingredients in place....

> Nowadays on social media it is getting common to just pull out the camera outta nowhere and put it on other people faces like it is a new normal.
but not everyone is a camera person who wants to appear in your videos, I've often seen people making vlogs and bringing other people in the videos without their consent and later those people find out randomly while scrolling on the internet. Recording in public places only makes sense as a tourist who wants to show people and the place that they've visited. Beside that it should be illegal to randomly record in public and putting camera on everyone face outta nowhere, that is quite an awkward thing to do.

Should be Illegal to Record in public

Most of people aren't comfortable being on a random person camera but the person with camera walking on street thinks he own everything and have right to capture everyone in that camera. There's a lot of those moments where I've seen other people being uncomfortable the moment a guy with the camera enters in a restaurant or shops Some people record while eating and the people sitting on the back table will be visibly uncomfortable yet they won't stop recording.

the confidence is something

I still respect the confidence some of these people have got out there in public to put the camera up on anyone face without expecting getting punched on face Like seriously it is that shameless behaviour that makes no sense, if you are confident be it but don't need to act like a weirdo, talking out loud in public or being disrespectful doesn't matter if you're talking to your audience through camera you're suppose to respect other people privacy and peace.

I hate it when

I'm sitting on a coffee shop minding my own business and outta nowhere some of so called influencer would walk into the shop And the first thought of them will be to start speaking like they own the whole shop, if you can't communicate in a tone that doesn't bother anyone else in surrounding than you're not meant to be in that place. People usually go out in restaurants or places to relax and be in peace but until these people bring out camera's and that tone they talk to people casually kind of give ick all the time. Some of these people just say that it is using free will like c'mon m, free will means bothering other people? Not at all, if you're comfortable while someone else doesn't feel that way, you should just think about putting yourself in the other person place. body.title: Mi mundo irreal
body.body:
![img-20260619-wa0335-5f86196abdf7.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/ikigaidesign/lkt-mr135l5z-pzo0eqv9/img-20260619-wa0335-5f86196abdf7.webp)

The power of artificial intelligence is incredible—and unsettling. It shows you the life you wish you had: that image, that tone, that smile—everything is beautiful, everything is perfect, everything is serene.

 But it is all a sham, too; it is an unreal life, an image that isn't you but one you would like to embody. Sometimes, that unreality becomes a dream you never want to wake up from.

---

El poder de la inteligencia artificial es increíble, y a la vez perturbador, te muestra la vida que desearías tener, esa imagen, ese tono, esa sonrisa, todo es bonito, todo es perfecto, todo está en calma.

Pero todo eso es falso también, es una vida irreal, es una imagen que no eres tú, que te gustaría ser, a veces lo irreal suele ser un sueño del que no quieres despertar.


Fotos: Géminis IA

body.title: WIP: Llavero de Maple ||  Maple crochet Keychain
body.body:
<center>![WIP_Maple_alce_crochet_Khawamaru.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTWtov7DxtQoi4gip9Pphwg3gjZ7PxFuwb3BEX94sMy8M/WIP_Maple_alce_crochet_Khawamaru.jpg)
</center>
¡Hola, espero te encuentres de maravilla!
*Hi, I hope you are feeling great!*

<div class=\

>

A veces las **piezas pequeñas** (muñecos tejidos) solo **necesitan lo preciso para que estén listas**. Esto implica: colores y saber en qué parte del tejido agregar tipos de puntadas exactas para obtener las formas y texturas deseadas. Esto fue lo que me pasa con Maple. Vamos a ver que otros detalles tomo en cuenta al momento de diseñar la cabeza. >*Sometimes **small pieces** (crocheted toys) just **need the bare essentials to be finished**. This involves choosing colors and knowing exactly where on the piece to use specific stitches to achieve the desired shapes and textures.* >*That's how it is with Maple. Let's see what other details I take into account when designing the head.* ---------------------------- ---------------------------- ###

¡Hamuy!
###
*Let's go!*
![mp-k.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRbFWzgi96udaG5iLNG96MTRP5bZxr4cYFU75PjRPC9Ke/mp-k.jpg)
*El Anillo mágico || Magic ring* Esta técnica es la más conocida si quieres empezar a tejer un muñeco a crochet. Tiene una **función de inicio** de la mayoría de las piezas. Este, debe estar **muy bien cerrado** porque sino se caerá gran parte de la estructura de la pieza. Más aún, si esta lleva relleno. >*This technique is the most commonly used if you want to start crocheting a toys. It has a **start function** for most pieces. This must be **securely fastened**; otherwise, a large part of the structure will collapse. What's more, if it's stuffed.*
![mp1-k.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQjjzw22zEtzpzqrXohQ2eAJuAXbM49XvrAkBf6cXoZHH/mp1-k.jpg)
*Avanzando... || Crocheting* Para formar el rostro, tengo que tener **contabilizado cada cuadradito** (punto). Con este dato, sé las áreas para **cambiarle los colores**. Antes, para esta parte hacía gráficos y los pintaba con colores y eso... Ahora, anoto los números de las secuencias en un cuaderno. En esta parte, me emocioné tanto con la forma que estaba tomando el rostro, y **olvidé colocarle su vincha (cinta) en la cabeza**. Y cuando me toca **destejer varias vueltas**, aprovecho para **hacer otros cambios**, jaja. >*To shape the face, I have to keep track of every little square**** (stitch). With this information, I know which areas to **change the colors in**. Before, for this part, I used to make graphs and color them in and stuff like that... Now, I write down the numbers in the sequences in a notebook with graph paper.* >*In this part, I got so enthusiastic about the shape the face was taking that **I forgot to put the headband on its head**. And when I have to **unravel a few rounds**, I take the opportunity to **make some other changes**, jaja.*
![mp2-k.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdkmZ4QMdkZ2HfniF3xBNgyatPZkueqPSbDWfsAnNhXgE/mp2-k.jpg)
*Hocico y vincha || Snout and headband* Uno de esos cambio fue el color de su hocico. En esta parte tenía dudas entre: Dejarlo con color piel o cambiarlo al color coral claro. Para salir de las dudas, **realicé una investigación**, y allí **supe que el Alce tiene el hocico y las orejas de color oscuro**. Con ese dato, comencé a formarle el hocico. >*One of those changes was the color of its snout. I was torn between leaving it skin colored or changing it to light coral. To resolve my doubts, **I did some research**, and that's when **I learned that moose have dark colored snouts and ears**. With that information, I began shaping the snout.*
![mp3.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWnE6oyXyzw1QLr2qejrJLWEWBqoQJu7JmUBzYGVmucd7/mp3.jpg)
*En proceso || WIP* Con la técnica de los \

y agregándole unos pelitos anaranjados por el rostro, ya estará listo. Luego diseñaré el cuerpo y a grabar el video. Espero este Maple sea una gran recuerdo para quienes viven en Canadá. >*Use the “sunken eyes” technique and add a few orange hairs around the face, and it'll be ready. Then I'll design the body and start filming the video. I hope this Maple will be a great memory for those who live in Canada.* ¡Y eso es todo! ¡Hasta la próxima! *See you next time!.* -------- ----------

body.title: ​My Splinterlands Journey Reaching Day 23, Unlocking a Pit Challenge, & Beating an Archmage Scholar in a 59 Mana Battle!
body.body:
​
​Hello Hive community!

​The momentum is real, and staying consistent is paying off big time. Today was another highly satisfying day on Splinterlands, loaded with milestone updates, a special challenge unlock,  and a fantastic victory against a tough automated opponent!

​Climbing Up Day 23 Streak & Pit Challenge!


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaWbMRGuT8UfuijNzgwM1TT7xGBhzkpPCaEe5FWcfs1nB/1782850473676.jpg)


​First up, my daily routine is going strong as I have officially reached a Day 23 Streak! My Spark Bonus II (+15%) is keeping my rewards optimized, and I am now just one week away from hitting the next tier.

​The daily wheel spin brought some extra excitement today.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTZi6JBpXa5VFpZxC3qxvSvoQpTwdzkVU2fVGLttbZm7C/1782850491836.jpg)


​+200 Sparks
​+30 Bonus Sparks

​Pit Challenge Available! I unlocked the option to challenge a Pit Fighter for extra rewards within the next 24 hours. I'll definitely look into taking this on!

​Defeating the Archmage Scholar.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmb2yg5yvfoCWC66rCRmDaK1YtPw7UvSezLSzcsPJSu2xo/1782850508282.jpg)


​When it came to ranked matches, I queued into a massive 59 Mana Modern Ranked battle against an opponent named RENOUX. This opponent is a scholar using the archmage.app bot system, which means their card placement and AI targeting are always highly optimized.

​With such a high mana cap, I focused on building a rock solid frontline capable of absorbing heavy hits while my backline archers and magic casters tore through their team. My strategy worked perfectly, dismantling the automated setup and bringing home a beautiful win!

​Keeping Steady in Bronze III


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYGsX91gSahZ1qonE8VmV5Mkc3Y7DaCQTQfvyL7bY53tw/1782850530394.jpg)


​Securing this victory keeps my standing solid and adds more loot to my collection.

​+20 Rank Rating (Keeping me steady right at a 300 rating total!)
​+91 Glint Tokens (More funds for my shop purchases)
​+0.011 SPS (A nice jump in my liquid token earnings per win!)

​My energy is sitting comfortably at 48/50, giving me plenty of fuel to potentially check out that Pit Challenge next. Winning against smart setups always makes me happy and proves that human strategy can still come out on top!

​Have you ever faced an Archmage scholar on the field? How do you prepare your lineup for huge 59 mana caps? Let me know in the comments below!

​Thank you all for the upvotes, tips, and constant motivation!

body.title: Premiación del concurso: La banda sonora de tu historia
body.body:
Saludos, estimados usuarios hispanohablantes de #Hive y amigos de la comunidad #Literatos. En este concurso [“La banda sonora de tu historia”](https://peakd.com/spanish/@es-literatos/concurso-la-banda-sonora-de-tu-historia) se recibieron muy buenos trabajos. Los participantes, para crear sus historias, acudieron a una gama de canciones que fueron desde el tango y la ranchera hasta la balada y el rock. Se presentaron relatos con historias muy vivas y vividas, de encuentros o desengaños amorosos, de eventos fatales o redescubrimiento del valor de la existencia, con personajes de carácter fantásticos o muy realistas.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/es-literatos/23vhz1bMUuQuUFQr5cbLzdAZh6d7xWkHtVpHp1npGu6LvYc77QjNJngYn6zS9YfNmbHHf.png)
[Fuente](https://www.unir.net/revista/musica/musica-literatura/)

A continuación, el veredicto:

Veredicto


Nosotros, integrantes del jurado para el concurso “La banda sonora de tu historia”, después de evaluar de modo integral los textos participantes, en consideración de su calidad literaria, respeto a las bases y sintonía con el espíritu del concurso, hemos decidido conceder el primer premio al texto [Mil violines](https://peakd.com/hive-179291/@mafalda2018/entrada-al-concurso-or-la-banda-sonora-de-tu-historia-de-literatos-or-mil-violines-es-en) de @mafalda2018.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/es-literatos/48HAXjdDYZdhRkwJ7SiKD1ojesBngjssoEMfrrvBsLxKYvqALtgnCXkeB9NUX8HGhV.png)

Nos presenta @mafalda2018, en una escritura de vuelo poético, usando el recurso del monólogo, el drama imaginario de una mujer que experimenta su singular locura amorosa y libre, hasta volver a la vida. Es una historia inspirada por la canción “Fuera de este mundo” de Franco de Vita. De igual manera, concedemos un segundo premio a [Mi flor de fuego](https://ecency.com/@sweetval/entrada-al-concurso-la-banda) de @sweetval.
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/es-literatos/23wCC9EccJbb8DvbM6zWRSGU5mszXS9vnquGec4aHVFTZQySRfBFmLaNFiP7LfqZ5ijRy.png)

@sweetval nos ofrece una historia de amor furtivo pero frustrado por las circunstancias, narrada con una cuidada escritura y un tono emotivo muy elocuente, con dos personajes de gran atracción. Esta creada a partir de la canción “Flor de fuego” de caramelos de Cianuro. Nuestras felicitaciones a los ganadores y el agradecimiento para todos los demás participantes. Firman: Graciela Acevedo @gracielaacevedo / Nancy Brito @nancybriti1 / José Malavé @josemalavem
Atentos al próximo concurso literario. Gracias y saludos.

;![vector libro.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/es-literatos/23tvyB54RqrbQb6FK34QmktER6U5YMFGdL1emgKij4vRGzvBfC5TdZXyqJo5s1CuaUjXf.jpg)
[Fuente](https://www.pinclipart.com/pindetail/iRwwRJx_free-png-download-research-icon-png-images-background/)

Nuestra gratitud a los usuarios que apoyan nuestra labor y hacen posible los recursos para otorgar el premio de este concurso.
