body.title: [EN/PT] Finally, My Master's Research Is Almost Complete!
body.body: > # [EN] ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/2458WoKnGJoT76LQrEpdbSZuW7wGvFoTLBisWnBhiqXz4mgsvMAHJwUQURS6TxnE9zJCx.png) There are moments in life when it feels like everything is at a standstill. That was exactly how I felt throughout much of my master's research, whose goal was to develop a methodology for detecting rotor faults in induction motors. A few months ago, I published the post *[We have finally made progress in detecting faults in electric vehicles](https://peakd.com/hive-196387/@elderdark/enespt-we-have-finally-made-progress-in-detecting-faults-in-electric-vehicles-6wa)*, where I shared that we had successfully developed a methodology capable of detecting faults in motors driven by frequency inverters, which are used in the vast majority of industrial applications as well as in many electric vehicles. That achievement unlocked many of the challenges we had been facing in implementing an embedded monitoring system for an electric vehicle. However, my master's research followed a different path. The objective was to develop a sensor capable of detecting faults directly on the motor without relying on a computer or microcontroller to process the current signals. In other words, the entire detection process would be performed exclusively using analog circuits. Our investigation began with a Gaussian digital filter, which had already demonstrated excellent performance in detecting and quantifying fault severity. From that point on, a new challenge emerged: finding filters with behavior similar to the Gaussian filter that could also be implemented using analog circuitry. The figure below compares the responses of the three digital filters we evaluated: Gaussian (A), Bessel (B), and Butterworth (C). In all three cases, two oscillations associated with the rotor fault can be observed, while the red signal represents the envelope of the filtered signal. Since the Gaussian filter has a linear phase response, its envelope remains almost perfectly aligned with the filtered signal. In contrast, the Butterworth and Bessel filters exhibit a slight delay due to their phase characteristics. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/Eo2BPrrRZwsL4j9R6cWssQ1DpCYGxgeQsUDQcsyMt4rF313X9kLF97qUYA6XiyoRBgR.png) Among all the alternatives evaluated, the Butterworth and Bessel FIR filters produced responses that most closely matched the Gaussian filter. After implementing these filters digitally, we obtained results that were remarkably similar to those of the Gaussian filter, despite its much higher order. With this stage successfully validated, we moved on to the analog implementation. To our surprise, a fourth-order analog filter was already sufficient to detect the faults. During this first phase of the experiments, the motor startup current was acquired, stored, and later reproduced using a function generator. This approach eliminated the need to repeatedly start the motor for each of the six faulty rotors and the healthy rotor. It also greatly simplified circuit calibration and ensured that all experimental tests were performed under identical conditions. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/2432N3qvLprYkpCyQxELEjysrfm996MnjSKaPh8GqNkLHnZ64bvpKkCrn8XNJA5yBGzSH.png) The analog circuit was developed up to the envelope extraction stage of the filtered signal. To accomplish this, it was necessary to design a 60 Hz notch filter, a band-pass filter with center frequencies ranging from 20 to 30 Hz, a peak detector, gain stages, and finally the envelope detection circuit—all implemented using only analog components. However, simply observing the fault-related oscillations was not enough. We needed a reliable indicator to confirm that these oscillations were actually caused by broken rotor bars. For this purpose, we analyzed the temporal distance between the peaks of the envelope signal. The expected behavior is very specific: as the filter's center frequency increases, the temporal distance between the envelope peaks also increases monotonically. This characteristic behavior is unique to broken rotor bar faults and makes it possible to distinguish them from other periodic faults. The responses obtained under all operating conditions were evaluated using an oscilloscope and are shown in the figure below. Case (A) corresponds to the healthy rotor, while the remaining cases represent different fault severities. In each waveform, the startup current is shown in yellow, the filtered signal in blue, and the envelope signal in green. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/23tmhWUPH8ApFK5sSRfdT3ziPwsJgtoJcnmG4Rm2wM7qwiq3ypBGyddBuLK7k6CcfnWbJ.png) The temporal distances between the envelope peaks are used to confirm that the detected fault is indeed caused by broken rotor bars. After all, other periodic faults may also generate similar oscillations, but they do not exhibit the same monotonic variation when the filter's center frequency is changed. Looking only at the final results, everything may seem relatively straightforward. However, reaching this point required many months of study, countless experiments, several frustrating setbacks, and a great deal of learning. As a reward, we were able to publish this work at an international conference that will take place in São Paulo this August: **Chip in SAMPA**. After so many challenges, seeing this research finally produce concrete results is incredibly rewarding. There is still one important stage ahead, but now the feeling is that we are on the right track. All that remains is to complete the final phase of the project and hope that everything performs just as well as it did during the experimental validation. **Wish me luck!** ---- # [PT] ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/2458WoKnGJoT76LQrEpdbSZuW7wGvFoTLBisWnBhiqXz4mgsvMAHJwUQURS6TxnE9zJCx.png) Há momentos em nossas vidas em que parece que tudo está travado. Foi exatamente assim que me senti durante boa parte do meu mestrado, cuja missão era desenvolver uma metodologia para detectar falhas no rotor de motores de indução. Alguns meses atrás publiquei o post *[We have finally made progress in detecting faults in electric vehicles](https://peakd.com/hive-196387/@elderdark/enespt-we-have-finally-made-progress-in-detecting-faults-in-electric-vehicles-6wa)*, no qual contei que conseguimos desenvolver uma metodologia capaz de detectar falhas em motores alimentados por inversores de frequência, que são utilizados na grande maioria das aplicações industriais e também em muitos veículos elétricos. Esse resultado destravou boa parte dos desafios que enfrentávamos para implementar um sistema embarcado destinado ao monitoramento de um veículo elétrico. Porém, meu tema de mestrado seguia por outro caminho. O objetivo era desenvolver um sensor capaz de detectar falhas diretamente no motor, sem depender de computadores ou microcontroladores para processar os sinais. Em outras palavras, toda a detecção deveria ser realizada exclusivamente por circuitos analógicos. Nossa investigação começou utilizando um filtro digital Gaussiano, que já havia demonstrado excelente desempenho na detecção e quantificação da severidade das falhas. A partir daí surgiu um novo desafio: encontrar filtros que apresentassem comportamento semelhante ao Gaussiano, mas que pudessem ser implementados de forma analógica. Na imagem abaixo é possível comparar as respostas dos três filtros digitais estudados: Gaussiano (A), Bessel (B) e Butterworth (C). Em todos eles aparecem duas oscilações características da falha do rotor, enquanto o sinal em vermelho representa a envoltória do sinal filtrado. Como o filtro Gaussiano possui fase linear, sua envoltória permanece praticamente alinhada com o sinal filtrado. Já os filtros Butterworth e Bessel apresentam um pequeno atraso devido às suas características de fase. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/Eo2BPrrRZwsL4j9R6cWssQ1DpCYGxgeQsUDQcsyMt4rF313X9kLF97qUYA6XiyoRBgR.png) Entre todas as alternativas avaliadas, os filtros FIR de Butterworth e Bessel foram os que mais se aproximaram do comportamento do filtro Gaussiano. Implementamos esses filtros digitalmente e obtivemos respostas muito semelhantes às do Gaussiano, que possui uma ordem bastante elevada. Com essa etapa validada, chegou o momento de partir para a implementação analógica e, para nossa surpresa, um filtro analógico de apenas quarta ordem já era suficiente para detectar as falhas. Nesta primeira fase dos experimentos, a corrente de partida do motor foi adquirida, armazenada e posteriormente reproduzida por um gerador de funções. Dessa forma, evitamos realizar partidas repetidas do motor para cada um dos seis rotores com falhas e para o rotor saudável. Essa estratégia facilitou significativamente a calibração do circuito e garantiu que todos os ensaios experimentais fossem realizados em condições exatamente iguais. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/2432N3qvLprYkpCyQxELEjysrfm996MnjSKaPh8GqNkLHnZ64bvpKkCrn8XNJA5yBGzSH.png) O circuito analógico foi desenvolvido até a etapa de extração da envoltória do sinal filtrado. Para isso, foi necessário projetar um filtro notch de 60 Hz, um filtro passa-faixa com frequências centrais entre 20 e 30 Hz, um detector de pico, estágios de ganho e, por fim, o circuito responsável pela obtenção da envoltória — tudo implementado utilizando apenas componentes analógicos. Entretanto, visualizar as oscilações da falha não era suficiente. Era necessário um indicador que comprovasse que aquelas oscilações realmente eram provocadas por barras quebradas no rotor. Para isso utilizamos a distância temporal entre os picos da envoltória. O comportamento esperado é bastante específico: conforme a frequência central do filtro aumenta, a distância temporal entre os picos também aumenta de forma monotônica. Esse comportamento é característico da falha de barras quebradas e permite diferenciá-la de outras falhas periódicas. As respostas obtidas para todas as condições foram avaliadas com auxílio de um osciloscópio e podem ser observadas na imagem abaixo. O caso (A) corresponde ao rotor saudável, enquanto os demais representam diferentes níveis de falha. Em cada captura são apresentados o sinal da corrente de partida (amarelo), o sinal filtrado (azul) e a envoltória do sinal (verde). ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/elderdark/23tmhWUPH8ApFK5sSRfdT3ziPwsJgtoJcnmG4Rm2wM7qwiq3ypBGyddBuLK7k6CcfnWbJ.png) Os valores da distância temporal entre os picos são utilizados para confirmar que a falha observada realmente corresponde a barras quebradas no rotor. Afinal, outras falhas periódicas também podem produzir oscilações semelhantes, mas não apresentam a mesma variação monotônica quando a frequência do filtro é alterada. Olhando apenas os resultados finais, tudo pode parecer relativamente simples. Mas chegar até aqui exigiu muitos meses de estudos, inúmeros testes, várias tentativas frustradas e muito aprendizado. Como recompensa, conseguimos publicar esse trabalho em um evento internacional que será realizado em São Paulo, em agosto, durante o **Chip in SAMPA**. Depois de tantos desafios, ver a pesquisa finalmente dando resultados concretos é extremamente gratificante. Ainda há uma etapa importante pela frente, mas agora o sentimento é de que estamos no caminho certo. Resta concluir a fase final do projeto e torcer para que tudo funcione tão bem quanto funcionou nos experimentos realizados até aqui. Me desejem sorte! Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@elderdark/enpt-finally-my-masters-research-is-almost-complete-6z7)

body.title: “Desde África Vinieron” (es/en)
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZzH53e5ZqnxBNpfK3UCNF2cvXfXeVLhYFHQMoGdd4hAT/1782575491881.jpg) Anunciaban agua el viernes y caí yo, de “flai” en el espacio “Desde África Vinieron” en el Centro Provincial de Artes Visuales. Fui invitado por su anfitriona Marcia Jimenez Arce, quien junto a Machin, abren debate entre el invitado y el público en temas que relacionan el arte, los mitos, la religión y yo diría que la sociedad en general. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcxZWiNpr4sfRbQ1667L4Jv1t1gBHW3Hwwe6ePhMZeqrU/1782575505076.jpg) Yo tenía miedo al principio, todavía me cuesta hablar en público. Y más si es en vivo y en directo. Pero cuando Marcia arranca, no hay forma de no dejarte llevar, no hay forma de no sentir el calor humano y profesional entre ellos, el público y tú. ¡Qué manera de pasarlo bien! ¡Qué manera de sentirme cómodo! ¡Y qué manera de aprender de Machin, el sacerdote de IFÁ y creador del Proyecto Casa Asheda Cultural! ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXUVDv2ZymR5Q7tzwmKz8DiRR8tW61wovCPZY1gbdVF6Q/1782575515654.jpg) Sin dudas un buen momento para cerrar este enero intenso. Les invito a no perderse este espacio que tiene lugar cada último viernes del mes. Yo no me perdono haberlo perdido durante estos últimos diez años… Gracias, Marcia querida por invitarme!!! Las imágenes utilizadas en la publicación son de mi propiedad tomada con mi móvil Xiaomi. Traducción al Inglés por [Deepl Traslate](https://www.deepl.com/mobile-apps/?utm_source=android&utm_medium=app&utm_campaign=share-with-friends). Puedes encontrarme en los siguientes perfiles de redes sociales: [Twitter](https://twitter.com/capote_iran?s=09), [Instagram](https://instagram.com/irankpotter?igshid=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ==).
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

They’d announced a talk for Friday, and I ended up popping in to the ‘Desde África Vinieron’ space at the Provincial Centre for Visual Arts. I was invited by the host, Marcia Jimenez Arce, who, together with Machin, facilitates a discussion between the guest and the audience on topics relating to art, myths, religion and, I’d say, society in general. I was nervous at first; I still find public speaking difficult. And even more so when it’s live and in front of an audience. But once Marcia gets going, there’s no way you can’t get swept up in it; there’s no way you can’t feel the warmth – both personal and professional – between them, the audience and yourself. What a brilliant time I had! What a relief to feel so at ease! And what a way to learn from Machin, the IFÁ priest and founder of the Casa Asheda Cultural Project! Without a doubt, a great way to round off this intense January. I urge you not to miss this event, which takes place on the last Friday of every month. I can’t forgive myself for having missed it over the last ten years… Thank you, dear Marcia, for inviting me!!! The images used in this post are my property and were taken with my Xiaomi mobile phone. Translation into English by [Deepl Translate](https://www.deepl.com/mobile-apps/?utm_source=android&utm_medium=app&utm_campaign=share-with-friends). You can find me on the following social media profiles: [Twitter](https://twitter.com/capote_iran?s=09), [Instagram](https://instagram.com/irankpotter?igshid=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ==).

![IMG_20230220_020217.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/irankpotter/23vhVr1JSoQGcPt5R2njAGV7uJwshAXm8hM83PiidCMpP8BmtCRbYyYx8GM1TibHLbniK.jpg) [![2dk2RRM2dZ8gKjXsrozapsD83FxL3Xbyyi5LFttAhrXxr16mCe4arfLHir9abEcfyUJdne2NmRpPev8XTWsNCo7d7QfjJweYZDGExmMB2f8Y8LJas2JagQetrn9vWVbZdCAfCUaoDLo2QcwREf41XPyKaPJMFsVnuxggjgWPbb.gif](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/eduardo900613/23u6aqopSakivScD67MLE749mXZcXDsSwcsogwBvE9x53XJaQQXLxiEwxzysfFGnGz3FB.gif)](https://vote.hive.uno/@hivecuba)

     Greetings ASEAN Hivers, I (@srey-yuu) am back again after trying to finish this week Raffle for 2 days straight, and I glad to say that I finally get it done. So it was raining here a lot last week and now it is burning hot this week, as of right now it is 91°F or 32°C. So it is very hot here but definitely not as hot as most SE Asian country where it can go to like 40°C. Even though it is 32°C in the afternoon, at night it went down to like 24°C so I am sick right now because of the temperature changes.

I think somewhere in Europe are experiencing the hottest weather in history. While there is an earthquake not that long ago in the Philippine as well as in Venezuela.      I'm glad that Cambodia don't really have to worry much about major natural disaster since we don't have earthquakes, tornadoes, or typhoons for as far as I know. I really hope these disasters would be less effective if not gone so that people can somewhat live in peace. Although natural disasters don't cause as many deaths as traffics accidents, that also includes diseases death which is also higher than natural cause. > Hello everyone, how are you doing today? Hope you are having a great time. This will be *Week 224 Edition 01* of our Weekly Featured Content. ![1000025609.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kronias/23zH3ihhxgjN5Ydxs9LGWWgZQUHDtgcBQZCamdrWRF3q1gTuNQiUs4P42GSFRi5ZE4H6C.png)
Made With Canva
So, last Saturday we had our hangout as usual, and it was just so much fun that we did not want it to end. We are currently on the first topic for this week, which is “YOUR FACE ALONE”. But before we proceed with the details of the topic, let us take a look at the winners of the last topic, which was “EASE COMES AT A COST”. This topic was geared toward each member of the community, telling us their thoughts on our continuous dependence on AI and the effects it was having on our creativity and our drive for efficiency. The more that AI can do for us, the less that we actually want to do these things for ourselves. We got to see that our dependence on AI, while making certain things more efficient and easier, also comes at a great cost. Because it shows that a time just might come when we might not be able to do anything without first resorting to AI. This was an enlightening topic, indeed. ***
> For this topic, we went through every entry post, and that is every post with the #hl-exclusive & #hl-w223e3 tag. And with the number of wonderful posts out there, it was quite difficult to make a selection. But eventually, we did just that. And so, the posts that will be featured not just for their exceptional content, but also for their level of engagement with other authors, will be listed below. ![hl_footer.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcnAnsqHA4KMYRqnS9QzWMpQUxM71wRhKabXz7paozHKJ/hl_footer.png)

Featured Contents


[AI: INTELLECTUAL CRUTCH?](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@michupa/ai-intellectual-crutch-en-pt) by @michupa
*For this author, he told us that due to the fact that AI is so easily accessible to everyone, it comes with its own downsides. People’s creativity and reasoning abilities have taken a huge blow and become fragile and it has also changed the way we come at problems. And not necessarily in a positive way. AI should amplify our intellectual abilities and not become an intellectual crutch!*
[USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE WITHOUT SACRIFICING HUMAN CREATIVITY](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@van.illa/using-artificial-intelligence-without-sacrificing) by @van.illa
*For this author, she told us that AI has become one of the most impactful evolutions of technology of our time, but it has also ended up raising certain questions that need answering. But then, the real problem isn’t AI; it’s only a tool to us. The problem is our overdependence on it for everything we need to do, things that we could do ourselves in the past. That’s where the problem lies.”
[THE HIDDEN COST OF EASY: WHAT AI IS REALLY TAKING FROM US](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@idksamad78699/the-hidden-cost-of-easy-what-ai-is-really-taking-from-us-gek) by @idksamad78699
*This author told us that AI has opened up all our eyes and now we know the ease and true cost at which things can be done. AI has made things easier and it’s having an impact on our jobs, and finances. The more we rely on it, it gets smarter, and we have less reasons to use our smartness.*

These posts were selected because of their special attention to detail and how they followed the topic. There were a lot of good ones out there, but we just could not pick them all. But then, we have some honorable mentions listed below:

Honorable Mention

[EASE COMES AT A COST](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@nkemakonam89/ease-comes-at-a-cost) by @nkemakonam89 [DOES COMFORT ENCOURAGE CREATIVITY](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@emrysjobber/s-4b0f00403a916) by @emrysjobber [SAVING TIME IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN CREATIVITY](https://peakd.com/hive-153850/@intishar/saving-time-is-more-important) by @intishar These are posts that were also found to be quite exceptional. ---- ---- ![hl_footer.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcnAnsqHA4KMYRqnS9QzWMpQUxM71wRhKabXz7paozHKJ/hl_footer.png)
AND NOW, WE MOVE ON TO THE NEW TOPIC!
***

Week 224 - Edition 01 Topic

**YOUR FACE ALONE**
*“Everyone has a right to take pictures and make videos in public places. So, it's likely that at one point or the other, you might appear in a random stranger's picture or video without even knowing it. This is a recording of you, taken without your permission. body.title: Blueberry Bread & Bulldozers
body.body:
<center>
![IMG_9151.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23u612PpCoUUtaGiwkZ88Fo7imx7CjjV8Tq36LMEPjZy61zCVLodLsK68MmLhVC6yepws.jpeg)</center>



<center>![paw divider transparent.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/48KZyd16wthLszaeq8fk7G1E4ouNCTPmsydXQQeMc23jdxuFbbxjwqu3LKfLB9x6LQ.png)</center>

----------

For many years I have often found myself pausing to ponder why so much happens around me all at once. Usually people get hit with one or maybe two things at a time. Heck, I am usually a-swirl with a good three to five on a slow day.

Right now there is a rather large amount of excavation and logging going on outside my office window. The Super Shop is going in, and I must say, it's aptly named. Apparently, we are also getting a super sled hill and little pond too, as they had to do something with the thousands of yards of material that they have to move in order to square the site away for the massive edifice to mechanical and constructive activities. 


![IMG_9164.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/243qDCb7q7ToQV8HzVXuUdAgW4DiEJcMUMQD4sDm3YTPzy7SHmrMA9iVn2WGaM3T219o8.jpeg)


The crew for the shop arrived yesterday, and it's a good thing I am feeling a bit better because every time I turned around someone was talking to me. Everything from water shut off valve locations, to water hose procuring, to random questions and inquiries, to meetings of the minds, it all happened all day long. 



Well, except for the end of the day. The ranch owner asked me if I wanted to go for a *quick* stroll with the dogs. I'm always up for a meander, but I also am recovering still, and after all the hoopla, I was a bit fatigued. Yep, an equivalent to a Montana Vietnam jungle walk later, I returned to the house, my legs saturated to the tops of my thighs, my hair resembling a clown in the East Texas humidity, and with the knowledge that my corg is a murderer. That's right, my cute little fox dog executed a little ground squirrel in the most efficient manner I had ever seen. What a walk that was! I saw everything from a plethora of wildflowers to a freshly snapped off deer leg.

Nature truly is metal.

I did get a smile out of seeing all the crew gape at my hobbit form striding back into camp with my shotgun slung over my shoulder and looking like Rambo's little sister. Was fun.

This morning I needed to do some chorin' in the house catchup, as the endless rain we have been having has left us with no small amount of endless mud. (The gigantic equipment has added to this sloppy effect). As I was sweeping the dried mud off the backdoor rug I got surprised by an unexpected visitor, the lucky house toad!


![IMG_9155.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23xVPTWopiR9HAvZWyJXzSLaDjpt11vEUWRNRyKRGSRedR8Yk9EGWNpyLbeRsQT3PYhFX.jpeg)


I suspect Jojo with regard to his arrival in my kitchen. She's ridiculous. 


![IMG_9157.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23xAcLoq6xDPb7EuyMFB12DMgLFxCJVg9mN9u3StqjHbiFESZFD55hHdK7YVjrjhai8DD.jpeg)


After cleaning, I needed to feed Buford, my sourdough starter, and decided to make the hubs a big old sourdough discard strudel-topped blueberry bread loaf.


![IMG_9158.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23wCJWwftxs3agFx4jBuBiimh97v7HgJJTqt6JwZWQQcXjfRweNqGhiFmfiVrGsHLsY4o.jpeg)


Yes, it was rather tasty. He and the ranch owners just ate half of it, still warm from the oven. I am not sad about this development, I mean, enjoyment was my motivation for making it. Plus, I got to deploy the sparkle sugar!


![IMG_9162.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23wqiH9LvQG8o97aacYoFqRMjKipSHSst2KTccFqWVS9rvgugWwJN14gi2c9uJbrjcnms.jpeg)


For the past hour I have been doing office work, but my window is full of a rather novel view, giant track hoes removing trees from the Earth like Orcs in the LOTR movies, an articulating dump truck keeps rumbling by my window, full of tree offal. I am sad about the trees, I love them so. Many of them are jack pines, at the end of their lifespan and on their way out of this existence, but the larch that are getting taken out are trees I loved and their removal is a bit painful on the ol soul. 





![IMG_9166.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23xKvZnNQpPVyCwjrgzDFywVk1mSvRNB5pAVB1JMDj3MzEuAbBc2XwL5zDPkitLbMGkAC.jpeg)




So is life though. 

And now, now I am going to go do some more computer work that I need to get caught up on, although I think I may take a page out of the Corg's book, and slump somewhere comfy cozy here in a bit...


![IMG_9149.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/23vhz6zzmnpQQ2abNooGZMsoN34zRmBDVrVLD2GQAxZ2srysSsfqWFfLBgnPH3D3yCvnU.jpeg)




--------------




<center>![paw divider transparent.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/generikat/48KZyd16wthLszaeq8fk7G1E4ouNCTPmsydXQQeMc23jdxuFbbxjwqu3LKfLB9x6LQ.png)</center>

------------------
<center>*And as most of the time, all of the images in this post were taken on the author's somewhat all over the place as of late iPhone.*</center>

-----------

body.title: No todo es ChatGPT: los mejores LLMs chinos en 2026 y para qué sirve cada uno 🇪🇸 ထ 🇺🇸 Not Just ChatGPT: The Best Chinese LLMs in 2026 and What Each One Is Good For
body.body: > En conversaciones sobre inteligencia artificial, suele mencionarse a ChatGPT de forma automática, como si no existiesen otros LLMs. Y no es que ChatGPT sea malo, pero hay que preguntarse si es el mejor para cada tarea. El problema es que el ecosistema de LLMs avanzó más rápido de lo que la mayoría de la gente pudo seguir. Y los modelos chinos, por ejemplo, llevan produciendo resultados notables que en varios casos superan a los modelos occidentales en algunos benchmarks específicos y a menor costo. Aquí no voy a señalar al mejor entre ellos, sino a mostrar qué modelo chino conviene más para cada tarea, con justificación.

> In conversations about artificial intelligence, ChatGPT tends to come up automatically, as if no other LLMs existed. And it's not that ChatGPT is bad — but it's worth asking whether it's the best tool for every task. The problem is that the LLM ecosystem moved faster than most people could keep up with. Chinese models, for example, have been producing notable results that in several cases outperform Western models on specific benchmarks — and at a lower cost. This article won't name the single best among them. Instead, it maps which Chinese model makes the most sense for each task, and explains why.

>

El contexto actual

Para el segundo trimestre de 2026, los modelos chinos son entre 15 y 30 veces más baratos para cargas de trabajo comparables. En general cuentan con arquitecturas MoE (Mixture of Experts, donde solo una fracción de los parámetros se activa por inferencia) que son más eficientes en inferencia y costos de energía más bajos. Además, muchos de esos modelos son de código abierto. Sería difícil entender por qué alguien no usaría el modelo más competitivo del mercado en codificación agéntica, estando disponible bajo MIT y costando $0.95 por millón de tokens de entrada.

>

Current Context

As of Q2 2026, Chinese models are between 15 and 30 times cheaper for comparable workloads. They generally rely on MoE (Mixture of Experts) architectures — where only a fraction of the parameters activate per inference — which makes them more efficient to run and cheaper in terms of energy costs. On top of that, many of these models are open source. It's hard to justify not using the most competitive model on the market for agentic coding when it's available under an MIT license and costs $0.95 per million input tokens.
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/richard-mvm/23t75CpLe392uSavtgPvCCkH4TWpw8xxb6ZhcwrHRvBEyvj95HX4dTqj1cERZTTD25maC.webp)

>

Advertencia antes de continuar

  • En cuanto a soberanía de datos. Si usas la API de cualquiera de esos modelos, tus datos pasan por servidores en China. Así que para código propietario o información sensible, la solución es el auto-hospedaje, que es posible en todos los modelos open-weight de la lista, aunque requiere buen hardware.
  • En cuanto a Benchmarks propios. Varios laboratorios reportan sus mejores resultados usando marcos de evaluación internos. Los números independientes suelen ser más modestos.
Con eso claro, pasemos a los modelos.

>

A Note Before We Continue

  • On data sovereignty. If you use the API of any of these models, your data passes through servers in China. For proprietary code or sensitive information, self-hosting is the solution — it's possible with all open-weight models on this list, though it requires solid hardware.
  • On proprietary benchmarks. Several labs report their best results using internal evaluation frameworks. Independent numbers tend to be more modest.
With that established, let's get into the models.

El punto de este artículo

No hay un modelo para todo. ChatGPT es bueno por la parte generalista. Claude es bueno en análisis de texto largo y conversación con matices, y GPT-5.5 lidera en razonamiento matemático. Esas ventajas no desaparecen porque existan modelos chinos. Pero si alguien paga $25 por millón de tokens de salida para procesar miles de documentos cuando DeepSeek V4 Flash hace lo mismo a $0.28, es un problema de hábito. Si necesita un agente que trabaje de forma autónoma durante horas en una base de código sin perder el hilo, y está usando un modelo que no fue diseñado para eso cuando Kimi K2.6 existe, eso tampoco es una decisión informada. El modelo adecuado para cada tarea existe, y a veces viene de San Francisco y otras de Beijing. Lo que importa es que el resultado sea el que necesites, al precio que tenga sentido para ti, y con las condiciones de privacidad que tu proyecto requiera.

There's no single model for everything. ChatGPT is strong on the generalist side. Claude excels at long-text analysis and nuanced conversation, and GPT-5.5 leads on mathematical reasoning. Those advantages don't disappear just because Chinese models exist. But if someone is paying $25 per million output tokens to process thousands of documents when DeepSeek V4 Flash does the same at $0.28, that's a habit problem. If you need an agent that works autonomously for hours inside a codebase without losing track — and you're using a model that wasn't designed for that when Kimi K2.6 exists — that's not an informed decision either. The right model for each task exists. Sometimes it comes from San Francisco, sometimes from Beijing. What matters is getting the result you need, at a price that makes sense for you, under the privacy conditions your project requires.

body.title: KISS BLOG IDEAS: WEEK #218: A beauty without adornment/ Una belleza sin adornos (ENG/ESP) 🌷🪻🌼
body.body: > Although I know that beauty is subjective and that beauty sometimes depends on the eye of the beholder, I admit that I am an admirer of beautiful things. I am one of those people who stop to contemplate, admire, and applaud all the beauty that surrounds me. I believe that beauty lies in the grand and spectacular, but also in the simplest and most unexpected things, which, precisely, don't need artifice to dazzle us, just as nature does. The sunset is beautiful with its orange and blue hues; the beauty of the fierce and tranquil seas is astonishing; landscapes impress with their color and immensity. Each of these things requires no makeup, editing, or Photoshop: they possess a real, unfiltered beauty.
></center>\n\nJust like those things in nature, so are we. We must let our essence be what impresses, what attracts, what dazzles, what speaks. When we \

our appearance, we are taking away that naturalness that makes us unique and different. In a society so demanding and focused on the beauty of people, especially women, we can be tempted to change our appearance to please and be accepted by others. Hence, we not only use clothes and makeup, but we also undergo expensive surgeries to change our appearance. This has resulted in almost identical women, with beauties created in laboratories or operating rooms, as if they all came from the same mold.\n\n

> I'm a 52-year-old woman, simple, who usually wears a dress and sandals, with my hair loose and flowing, and I wear very little makeup: for me, a touch of lipstick is enough. Because of the hot climate in the city where I live, it's stressful (or at least that's how I see it) to wear layers of clothing and makeup because you can easily turn into a melted ice cream cone. Sometimes I feel truly sorry for women touching up their makeup every half hour, or for 15-year-old girls putting on makeup as if they were 30 just to look perfect, beautiful, like dolls. And they do look like dolls, but that's because something about the beauty they display makes them artificial.

> I'm not ugly, or at least I don't think so, but there are days when I can look more haggard, with dark circles under my eyes, and if someone sees me, they know perfectly well that I'm not at my best because I'm not going to hide behind a mask of makeup or creams. But there are also days when my laughter is my best accessory, my wavy hair my best veil, and my tan my best makeup. And people recognize and applaud that: naturalness, simplicity, even unadulterated femininity. So, yes, I do believe we can be beautiful without a lot of embellishments or artifice. And if you don't believe me, smile in the next photograph, really smile, so you can see how beautiful you look in the picture.
>All images are from my personal gallery and the text was translated with Google
>Thank you for your support, for reading, and for your comments, friends. Until next time

>Una belleza sin adorno Aunque sé que la belleza es subjetiva y que a veces depende de la mirada de quien la contempla, admito que admiro las cosas bellas. Soy de esas personas que se detienen a contemplar, admirar y aplaudir toda la belleza que me rodea. Creo que la belleza reside en lo grandioso y espectacular, pero también en las cosas más simples e inesperadas, que, precisamente, no necesitan artificios para deslumbrarnos, al igual que la naturaleza. El atardecer es hermoso con sus tonalidades naranjas y azules; la belleza de los mares, tanto bravos como tranquilos, es asombrosa; los paisajes impresionan por su color e inmensidad. Ninguna de estas cosas necesita maquillaje, edición ni Photoshop: poseen una belleza real y sin filtros. Al igual que las cosas en la naturaleza, así somos nosotros. Debemos dejar que nuestra esencia sea lo que impresione, lo que atraiga, lo que deslumbre, lo que hable. Cuando retocamos nuestra apariencia, eliminamos esa naturalidad que nos hace únicos y diferentes. En una sociedad tan exigente y centrada en la belleza, especialmente en la de las mujeres, podemos sentir la tentación de cambiar nuestra apariencia para complacer y ser aceptados por los demás. Por eso, no solo usamos ropa y maquillaje, sino que también nos sometemos a costosas cirugías para modificar nuestro aspecto. Esto ha dado como resultado mujeres casi idénticas, con bellezas creadas en laboratorios o quirófanos, como si todas provinieran del mismo molde. Soy una mujer sencilla de 52 años que suele usar vestido y sandalias, con el pelo suelto y ondulado, y me maquillo muy poco: para mí, un toque de labial es suficiente. Debido al calor de la ciudad donde vivo, es estresante (o al menos así lo veo yo) llevar capas de ropa y maquillaje porque una se puede parecer a un helado derretido. A veces me da mucha pena ver a mujeres retocándose el maquillaje cada media hora, o a chicas de 15 años maquillándose como si tuvieran 30 solo para verse perfectas, guapas, como muñecas. Y sí que parecen muñecas, pero es porque la belleza que muestran las hace ver artificiales. No soy fea, o al menos no lo creo, pero hay días en que puedo verme más demacrada, con ojeras, y si alguien me ve, sabe perfectamente que no estoy en mi mejor momento porque no voy a esconderme tras una máscara de maquillaje o cremas. Pero también hay días en que mi risa es mi mejor accesorio, mi cabello ondulado mi mejor velo y mi bronceado mi mejor maquillaje. Y la gente lo reconoce y lo aplaude: naturalidad, sencillez, incluso feminidad pura. Así que sí, creo que podemos ser bellas sin muchos adornos ni artificios. Y si no me crees, sonríe en la próxima foto, sonríe de verdad, para que veas lo guapa que estás en la imagen.

body.title: Explore Freddies Santai Sumur Tiga // Marine Tourism Destination on Weh Island
body.body:
----
The sea has always been a favorite place in every trip of mine, and if you follow my blog lately then I often share some marine tourism destinations in the form of beaches where I find my own satisfaction and one of my favorite marine tourism destinations is Sumur Tiga beach, which is one of the most beautiful beaches in the western tip of Indonesia so that many people call it a sparkling pearl in Sumur Tiga, there we will find beach sand that is very fine grains, melts through the gaps of the fingers, and of course the place always provides a relaxing pleasure.
----

![IMG-20260701-WA0017.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNtzJ52Qwz62YmrRJiQ6JLaXij4rYBEPejApTXE3RoHFv/IMG-20260701-WA0017.jpg)

<div class=\

>

Good evening, friends, wherever you are, as usual. I hope you are all healthy and happy, allowing you to carry out your daily activities smoothly. I hope you all have a pleasant day.

In this simple blog, I will share one of the popular marine tourism destinations on Weh Island: Freddies Santai Beach, Sumur Tiga Beach. Here, I can hear the clear sound of the crashing waves and enjoy the exotic treats of this most remote island in my beloved homeland (Indonesia).

So, please continue to follow my simple blog to see some images of this tourist destination, along with a short article from me.

![IMG-20260701-WA0000.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmY6nV6EjZwm5VMX4x2QAk6qGgGJSZCDY8QEirAcwQEB4i/IMG-20260701-WA0000.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0003.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfKmTqAnjEyDTzprnr2WWEDLWPFiUJRp4Qwip3ZsP5Kmw/IMG-20260701-WA0003.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0001.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZZLmYh4UcohFgw5F7Np8f3bciYF4FUdmqJEsAtj8f5Mm/IMG-20260701-WA0001.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0002.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ4VgqMQtb7ZGGurspb6NetrGR9fiwev5bPUv6E69iMxo/IMG-20260701-WA0002.jpg)

While on vacation on Weh Island a few days ago, I stopped and enjoyed the atmosphere at one of its marine tourism destinations. My destination was Freddies Santai Beach, Sumur Tiga.

My friends...
It's located on Jalan KH Agus Salim, Le Meulee, Sukajaya, Sabang City, Weh Island, Aceh.
It's about 10 km from Balohan Harbor, a 20-minute motorcycle ride away. I found this marine tourism destination's location to be very strategic.
Upon arrival, I immediately headed to the motorcycle parking area provided by the destination and took some photos to show off the atmosphere and conditions in the parking area.

![IMG-20260701-WA0004.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTEoFQfhkWeEoV23poDsBJ1TtysrG3HjDs1vCdwnRjzVf/IMG-20260701-WA0004.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0005(1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW4aNhxU7uMQQ3icHvbzvwgfVZwYwySS5mEJRuwEJhJLu/IMG-20260701-WA0005(1).jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0005.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmW4aNhxU7uMQQ3icHvbzvwgfVZwYwySS5mEJRuwEJhJLu/IMG-20260701-WA0005.jpg)

Next, after parking my motorbike, I continued my journey to enter the tourist destination area and this is the view when we first enter the tourist area, where we will be greeted by a simple gate with the words Welcome to Freddies written on it.

![IMG-20260701-WA0007.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma9PC3MbXHvtBx7iD741sjgh7aytdK8RYjcknk4ogTcnu/IMG-20260701-WA0007.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0006.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQuvDZMN3nskS7fEsq61KsxY3i9cPDf83g3aynxDZ69HE/IMG-20260701-WA0006.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0010.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfW7vLajjyYFSq7d3AtAjwpyGK6tygB29NFfA1ZbUUXKe/IMG-20260701-WA0010.jpg)

From the outside I only saw this simple gate but after passing through the gate I was immediately amazed by the view I found in this marine tourism destination area which in my personal opinion Freddies is indeed a very stunning place as well as a strategic place to stay because it has an extraordinary view and all these simple buildings directly face the Indian Ocean which I can assure you if you linger sitting on the balcony or just enjoying the atmosphere in this area then you will not remember that time goes by quickly and of course you will feel at home in the area.

![IMG-20260701-WA0008.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWe8WuecyTV8Xjh5a4drF6cxV8U8c8qCw2ubhUtsfCNug/IMG-20260701-WA0008.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0009.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXjZJ1dqgqa8bKPrN9Vo6rcmNb8eqkmFLK36xMGfReKUH/IMG-20260701-WA0009.jpg)

My friend...
In my personal opinion, this tourist destination area is designed with simple, traditional-style accommodations, or what we often call \

made of wood and thatched roofs. However, they are certainly comfortable to stay in and enjoy the atmosphere, as I did.

And honestly, I personally don't think this place offers luxury, but it does offer natural luxury with stunning views, views that are always provided free of charge by the Creator.

And then I just followed my feet, unaware that this building area was so vast, built on multiple levels, with the lowest level leading directly to the open beach.

![IMG-20260701-WA0011.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSeFgAbBFtAyjs5ZGGzVEBrwg18FTdSnw1F7y52HVXLnd/IMG-20260701-WA0011.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0012.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP3R4SQcxvKWjRMkeH1AV2bXwkE2SmusSicVE4k3fDnV3/IMG-20260701-WA0012.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0013.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRQhRqXcM4nvRZSwYQMEUwJTcctjJFu8E5qgvEuDLfeT1/IMG-20260701-WA0013.jpg)

As soon as I arrived at the bottom level, I was once again amazed by this marine tourism destination. I was speechless, but I definitely recommend this place to anyone planning a vacation on Pulau Weh.

My friends...
At first glance, I could see this beach, with its soft white sand and views directly overlooking the Indian Ocean. It's also very welcoming to visitors, thanks to the friendly locals. Finally, the various water sports facilities make this place a favorite of mine, from renting paddleboards to diving to enjoying the underwater beauty.

![IMG-20260701-WA0014.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdEmAzHMyUtBxUQdfV5ERaTyctqPqKw4ZNqdgZPg3tQt8/IMG-20260701-WA0014.jpg)

![IMG-20260701-WA0015.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmf66ibTGhCXeT1RxVQ6yt3Ss6UawH67jTRssrRb1STTHk/IMG-20260701-WA0015.jpg)

Here, I only see the laughter of visitors with their happy faces, and I am personally very grateful to have been able to visit and see such an extraordinary sight.

Well, my friends, those are some images of one of the marine tourism destinations I visited and shared on this simple blog. I hope you all enjoyed and were entertained by what I shared. I also extend my heartfelt thanks to all of you who took the time to view and read my blog to the end.

Please leave your comments, support, and input, which means a lot to me so I can make this blog even better in the future.

That's all for now, and I'll see you in my next blog.

body.title: Cuban farmers
body.body:
Hello friends from the Black and White community, this is my first time here and one of my first publications on Ecency. Today I have decided to share these black and white photographs taken by me so that, in the opinion of the community, I can receive advice and feedback about my work.

Official entry for the #monomad  challenge hosted by @monochromes and @brumest

The Cuban black and white photography has the ability to stop time and reveal what often goes unnoticed. In this image, taken in Viñales, the protagonist is not only a farmer, but an entire story drawn through his hands, his gaze, and every element surrounding him. The absence of color allows us to focus on textures: the skin marked by the passing of years, the guano hat, the working tool, and the simplicity of a life connected to the land. Black and white transforms an everyday scene into a portrait of memory, identity, and resilience.



![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXnYbH17JwFowAck7MpybnGH9XZokrWZiT8eSaszATeES/1782837802973.jpg)






Capturing Cuban farmers is also capturing an essential part of our culture. This photograph shows a moment of conversation, exchange, and humanity. Beyond the landscape of Viñales, there is an invisible richness: the wisdom of those who understand the cycles of nature, the value of daily effort, and the traditions passed down from generation to generation. Documentary black and white photography allows us to approach this essence without distractions, making every gesture carry a deeper meaning.








![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeGCVr4zQBtKm1MM1vbaeBcntKWsM4KwEJDF1zUQTsqpk/1782839814246.jpg)




The Cuban countryside holds stories that deserve to be told. In this image, the tranquility of the surroundings and the presence of the farmer create a scene where it seems that time moves slower. Black and white photography is not only an aesthetic choice; it is also a way to honor memory, connect the present with the past, and show the beauty of authenticity. Viñales, with its landscapes and its people, continues to be a place where traditions, crafts, and ways of life survive as part of the soul of Cuba.




![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYwo9ErTyVpV2vZMKuHzGsnnMrUb2DauLSniAyXHT4wna/1782838269368.jpg)


*This picture are my property*

body.title: COTI Tokenomics/ Distribution Changes Due To Market - Common Sense
body.body:
/></center>

Yesterday we had a community announcement with COTI with regard to the COTI Earn program which will be placed on hold when this current earn season ends. The concern is the rewards being distributed which ultimately dilutes the value of the COTI token having more distributed. The community has spoken and these ultimately were factored in to the final decision which is the right decision.

This what is happening on COTI resonated with what is happening on HIVE and you would hope commonsense takes place here as well because paying out HIVE tokens via the DHF is ultimately impacting everyone who has invested in HIVE.

The inflation of HIVE is not what we are used to and every HIVE hitting the exchanges is impacting price whether we like it or not. More coins in circulation means less dollar value even if you hear people saying having more coins distributed is good for the eco system.

If HIVE was at $1 or $0.50c then things would not feel or seem so bad, but at $0.05c this is no joke and is serious and why we need to be using common sense with the DHF spending. COTI and HIVE like any other crypto right now has to be careful in how they handle their distribution and flooding the market is not the smart option if you want to try and keep some type of dollar value.

A business in financial difficulty or testing times has to adapt and adjust in order to see through the difficult times. They would not be spending with arrogance thinking that this would not impact their value as we all know the saying \
so no one is immune from these market conditions.

/> I have no idea how many coins are distributed from these COTI Earn seasons and just checked and the number is rather large being 20 million COTI. This may seem like a drop in the ocean and the bigger question is how many are staking their rewards or are they going straight to the exchanges? Looking at the COTI Treasury knowing that the number of staked COTI fluctuates slightly over the last year or so it hovers around 400 million up to 412 million. They have had 3 COTI Earn seasons thus far having paid out 60 million COTI so these earnings are not being staked and a high percentage are being sent to the exchanges. This therefore is directly impacting the COTI price like HIVE has been impacted over the last few years with the DHF payouts for various projects.
/></center>\n\nIf the COTI Earn rewards were being staked by \

then I would not be overly concerned about the distribution because those earning the rewards have long term thinking and care what happens.

The COTI team mentioned that they will still focus on development and adoption through various solutions they will be actively working on. I know certain projects that joined the COTI eco system have been receiving support via COTI tokens, but those are locked and cannot be spent. This was agreed upon from the start and is the only way not to flood the exchanges with COTI tokens which is self inflicted damage if not managed responsibly.

links.title: End of Season Reward
links.body:
Hello Splinterlands and Hive Fam!

I hope life is treating you well wherever you are in this part of the world, and that the weekend is going great.

My Splinterlands Game account is - FinPulse9.

The game season is officially over, and now it is also the time for the players to claim their end-of-season reward. I have not claimed my reward,d so today I am going to claim it, and we'll also talk about the experience that I had in the season, which has already ended, and my strategy to start gameplay in the new season, which is already on. I ended the last season in Diamond Two League with a rating of 316,0 and as part of the end-of-season reward, I got more than 88,000 tokens, which I think is a good amount. 

My winning ratio was more than 51% in the season, which I consider good again because I know that anything above 50 is great and not at all easy to achieve. I have claimed the token, and obviously I will be utilising the balance to buy something from the reward shop also, but for now that is not my focus at the moment because I am more interested in starting the gameplay in the new season, which is what I'm going to finish and complete the required steps.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/finpulse/Eo8QrifaVzD9PAGawFRAWP4D7eJiFBRBs4pVtCEEBHwfUiHjHW3nyJwL9X9rzJvPkPG.png)

Now, since I am done with the last season, it is time for me to buy the wild pass so that I am eligible for gameplay in the new season. This is a primary requirement to pay for the wild pass, and then only a player can start playing in this format of the game, so here I am going to finish this and purchase the pass so that I am eligible to play the battle in this format of the game.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/finpulse/EoJy8t5z3xaz3S3eiSkefntXFgS5njqsGnMZiqnyHjuc1rDNx7V4N1zbz1TC2HTvrS4.png)

I did not have the DEC tokens in my game account, so I purchased them from the market and also initiated the transfer from the marketplace to the game account, which is a kind of process that happens instantly. After doing this, I will move ahead and purchase the Wild Pass, which is again a process that does not take more than one minute.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/finpulse/23swiJgSMAGt4EJrawupE9pMSzxsdkv74xuVt9f91uSMboAhFtbQYytjCzbVU99ZQCLGh.png)

As I already mentioned, I will be using DEC tokens for the payment, so here I am making the payment for the wild pass, and this should be done ASAP.

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/finpulse/23tRxRmSinqagADmhG8w1GPq47tgs6kkHBMr7ZvkDs71sGxq6XLGTShs1Rg1PAcjcWgy1.png)

Now the purchase is done for the wild pass, and I'm all set to start the gaming in the season, but before that, I also need to do one task which is even more important, and without that I can't start the gameplay. 

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/finpulse/Eo8LWYWZFiWugnfemcncWA3CPT7MgfHw5PLNsNqUy9YqNmwvytRsT8kTA1FN37J6NXD.png)

Basically, that task is to get the renewals done for the card that I require to play the game. I think that will take time, so I'll be trying to finish it tomorrow, and in the meantime my energy count will also recharge, but not much because I only stand at 48. So after two energy recharge this will be idle. I'll be trying to finish that task as soon as I can so that the energy count does not waste anymore. But since it takes time, I will have to do it tomorrow only and not today.

links.title: Another day of unseasonable heat in Italy: exhaustion, photos, and cases of illness./ Otro día de calor inusual en Italia: agotamiento, fotos y casos de enfermedad.
links.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmT3y3z9usStvq29ys8cPiKrhLH1FK9B7qx6JxCN8BzXp6/1782843204555.jpg)


Good evening, blog friends—how are you doing? Europe is still in the grip of sweltering heat; it is crucial to stay hydrated, eat well, and try to avoid moving around during the hottest hours of the day. There have been various deaths and cases of heat-related illness; a friend of mine fell ill today, and I confess I even feared heatstroke myself when I went grocery shopping. I felt like I was going to faint and was overheating—I felt really unwell, which you can even see in the photos. Fortunately, I turned on the air conditioning once I got home, and after resting in the cool air and taking a cold shower, I felt better. In fact, I even cooked a simple meal—two chicken burgers with salad and mayonnaise—quick to prepare yet nutritious. I felt even better after lunch!

> Buenas noches, amigos del blog: ¿cómo están? Europa sigue bajo un calor sofocante; es fundamental mantenerse hidratado, comer bien e intentar evitar desplazarse durante las horas de más calor del día. Se han registrado varios fallecimientos y casos de enfermedades relacionadas con el calor; una amiga mía se sintió mal hoy y confieso que yo misma temí sufrir un golpe de calor cuando fui a hacer la compra. Sentía que iba a desmayarme y que mi cuerpo se sobrecalentaba; me encontraba realmente mal, algo que incluso se puede apreciar en las fotos. Afortunadamente, encendí el aire acondicionado al llegar a casa y, tras descansar en el ambiente fresco y tomarme una ducha fría, me sentí mejor. De hecho, hasta preparé una comida sencilla —dos hamburguesas de pollo con ensalada y mayonesa—: algo rápido de hacer pero nutritivo. ¡Me sentí aún mejor después de almorzar!


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU3v3cpLKLDQCuwf18QfqKMHEq9hPaAD5jkyBLF7p5pe7/1782843204795.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRmqg4943MTSKJuKk1Ydm2kCRe2eZi7WFTxr45BBKaYqb/1782843204987.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcum19gHbuxtJLyrjMtDNT9CSKHotmUd68HAJxzLxfpJ7/1782843205197.jpg)

Anyway, after lunch, it was impossible to go outside because of the scorching temperatures; I did a few chores but was sweating profusely even when moving slowly. Then I called a friend of mine who had been unwell—he’d actually ended up in the hospital, where they put him on an IV drip before sending him home. He’d suffered a heat-related illness, but by the time I called, he was feeling better and was resting somewhere cool. In this kind of heat, you tire easily and feel completely out of sorts. In any case, I only stepped outside again about half an hour ago, once the sun started to dip a little. I took a walk nearby to admire some local flowers, then got lost in taking photos of the square near my home—and especially the sky and the surrounding area, which looked lovely. Naturally, I also snapped a picture of my neighbor’s cat, who was lying in the street to escape the heat. Let’s hope this heatwave ends soon, because living in these temperatures is truly difficult!

> En fin, después de almorzar fue imposible salir porque las temperaturas eran insoportables; hice algunas tareas domésticas, pero sudaba a mares incluso moviéndome despacio. Luego llamé a un amigo que había estado indispuesto —de hecho, terminó en el hospital, donde le administraron líquidos por vía intravenosa antes de enviarlo a casa; también había sufrido un problema de salud relacionado con el calor, pero para cuando lo llamé ya se sentía mejor y descansaba en un lugar fresco. Con este calor, uno se cansa rápido y se siente totalmente desganado. De todos modos, solo volví a salir hace cosa de media hora, cuando el sol empezó a bajar un poco; di una vuelta por los alrededores para admirar algunas flores de la zona y me entretuve sacando fotos de la plaza cercana a casa —y sobre todo del cielo y del entorno, que se veían preciosos— y, por supuesto, del gato de mi vecino, que también estaba tumbado en la calle para escapar del calor. ¡Esperemos que esta ola de calor termine pronto, porque vivir con estas temperaturas es realmente difícil!

links.title: My first 24 hours on Hive: what I learned?
links.body:
I joined Hive through Ecency yesterday. Less than 24 hours in and I’ve learned a ton.

My intro post got upvotes quickly. It was reblogged by newbie-follower within minutes, even. Maarnio, Galberto, and Godfish personally welcomed me. This surprised me in a good way coming from other platforms where new accounts get ignored for weeks.

I made a mistake early on too. I was trying to be active; I commented on about 8 posts in 12 minutes. Someone called me out on it, saying it looked fake, maybe even AI-generated. It was a little hard to accept, but they were right. Then I slowed up.

That night, I used all my resource credits from all the activity. Had to pull over and wait for it to recharge. Lesson learned there too: don’t rush things to “look active.\

body.title: Relato «Quinto Piso» (ESP/ENG)
body.body:
>

El teléfono de Carlos emitía un suave y constante parpadeo, una luz fantasmal en la penumbra de su salón. No era una llamada, ni un mensaje urgente. Era la temida notificación: Carga de Facebook.

Para un hombre de su carácter metódico, aquel letrero era una afrenta. Era la prueba fehaciente de que la tecnología, lejos de ser una aliada, era una criatura caprichosa que se deleitaba en su frustración. Llevaba tres días intentando exhibir una fotografía de su gato, un persa de nombre Moriarty, y el progreso de la carga era nulo, como un reloj de arena cuyo grano se hubiera negado a caer.

Fue en ese momento de irritación absoluta cuando, en lugar de la foto del felino, su pantalla le reveló un mensaje de una desconocida. El nombre: Luna_Estrella20. El contenido del mensaje era directo, casi cortante, carente de la cortesía habitual de los extraños.

—¿En serio? ¿Otra foto de un gato? Eres más aburrido que un manual de instrucciones.

Carlos arqueó una ceja. El ataque era injustificado, pero tenía la precisión de un relámpago. No era un hombre dado a las disputas banales, pero aquella insolencia requería una respuesta. Tecleó con la frialdad de un detective interrogando a un sospechoso.

—No me meto en sus asuntos, señorita Luna. Quizás mi gato posee una vida social más activa que la suya. ¿Suele usted espiar perfiles ajenos en horas tan poco productivas como las tres de la tarde?

La respuesta fue inmediata, como si ella estuviera al acecho. La conversación se convirtió en un duelo dialéctico. Ella lo tildó de \

. Analizaron la calidad de los memes, debatieron sobre las preferencias musicales y, en un giro absurdo, discutieron con pasión sobre la temperatura ideal del café. Carlos sentía que estaba interrogando a un testigo hostil en un juicio, sin poder ver su rostro.

Cansado de aquella, y con la sangre ligeramente alterada, Carlos tecleó una sentencia definitiva:

—Ojalá viviera a mi lado, para poder decirle esto en persona y ver la cara que pone.

Transcurrieron dos minutos, durante los cuales el silencio en el apartamento 5B era absoluto. De repente, un sonido seco, un golpe contundente, retumbó en la pared de su dormitorio, justo a la izquierda de su escritorio. Las 4:45 de la tarde.

Carlos, con el corazón latiendo como un péndulo desbocado, escribió de nuevo, esta vez con cierto temor.

—¿Acaba usted de golpear la pared?

—¿Usted también lo oyó? —respondió ella, y en esa pregunta Carlos detectó un atisbo de incredulidad que le heló la sangre.

Se levantó de su butaca. Con la cautela de un investigador que se aproxima a una escena del crimen, salió al pasillo y se detuvo ante la puerta de su vecino, el departamento 5A.

Antes de que pudiera decidir si llamar o retroceder, el cerrojo interior se descorrió con un chirrido metálico. La puerta se abrió. En el umbral, una joven de cabello castaño, envuelta en una camiseta holgada, lo miró con una sonrisa que no auguraba nada bueno.

—¿Carlos_88? —inquirió ella, con un tono que mezclaba la burla con la incredulidad.

—¿Luna_Estrella20? —logró balbucear Carlos, mientras sentía que el suelo se hundía bajo sus pies.

La revelación fue más extraña que una novela policiaca. Su nombre real era Lucía y, para su absoluta sorpresa, trabajaba en la humilde cafetería de la esquina que Carlos siempre había evitado por considerarla \

. Ella, por su parte, había padecido los maullidos del tal Moriarty a las seis de la mañana, culpándolo de su insomnio.

Hubo un silencio denso, un momento de tensión. Pero entonces, Carlos, olvidando todo su método y control, soltó una risa estridente. Ella le secundó, y el eco de sus risas llenó el angosto pasillo del quinto piso. Llevaban un año y medio viviendo pared con pared, intercambiando saludos glaciales en el ascensor, sin saber que sus alter egos digitales llevaban días discutiendo con una ferocidad digna de un juicio en Old Bailey.

Las máscaras cayeron. Carlos_88 y Luna_Estrella20 dejaron de existir. Una semana después, Carlos publicó la ansiada foto de Moriarty. En los comentarios, bajo el nombre de Lucía, apareció una nota: \

. Ella aceptó. Y así, de aquel insignificante misterio tecnológico, de aquella carga interminable y de dos nombres falsos, surgió la más inesperada de las alianzas en el edificio 5. El ascensor, se transformó en el escenario de sus encuentros. Carlos, sonríe con la satisfacción del que ha resuelto el mejor de los crímenes: el de la soledad. Porque, como bien sabía la señorita Marple, a veces los secretos más oscuros no se esconden en las grandes mansiones, sino en la pared que separa dos departamentos. ***

Carlos's phone emitted a soft, constant blink, a ghostly light in the dimness of his living room. It wasn't a call, nor an urgent message. It was the dreaded notification: Facebook Uploading.

For a man of his methodical nature, that message was an affront. It was irrefutable proof that technology, far from being an ally, was a capricious creature that delighted in his frustration.  He'd been trying for three days to upload a photo of his cat, a Persian named Moriarty, and the upload was making no progress, like an hourglass whose sand refused to fall.

It was at that moment of utter irritation that, instead of the feline's photo, his screen displayed a message from a stranger. The name: Luna_Estrella20. The message was direct, almost curt, lacking the usual courtesy of strangers.

\

Carlos raised an eyebrow. The attack was unjustified, but it had lightning-fast precision. He wasn't one for petty arguments, but that insolence demanded a response. He typed with the coldness of a detective interrogating a suspect.

\

Do you usually spy on other people's profiles at such unproductive hours as three in the afternoon?\n\nThe answer was immediate, as if she were lying in wait. The conversation turned into a verbal duel. She called him \

They analyzed the quality of memes, debated musical preferences, and, in an absurd turn, passionately argued about the ideal coffee temperature. Carlos felt like he was cross-examining a hostile witness in a trial, without being able to see their face.

Tired of this, and with his blood slightly running hot, Carlos typed out a definitive statement:

\

Two minutes passed, during which the silence in apartment 5B was absolute. Suddenly, a sharp sound, a resounding thud, echoed against the wall of his bedroom, just to the left of his desk.  4:45 p.m.

Carlos, his heart pounding like a runaway pendulum, typed again, this time with a hint of fear.

\

she replied, and in that question, Carlos detected a hint of disbelief that chilled him to the bone.

He rose from his chair. With the caution of an investigator approaching a crime scene, he stepped into the hallway and stopped in front of his neighbor's door, apartment 5A.

Before he could decide whether to knock or back away, the inner lock slid open with a metallic squeak. The door opened. In the doorway, a young woman with brown hair, wrapped in a loose t-shirt, looked at him with a smile that didn't bode well.

\
she inquired, her tone a mixture of mockery and disbelief.\n\n\

Carlos managed to stammer, feeling the ground give way beneath his feet.\n\nThe revelation was stranger than a detective novel. Her real name was Lucía, and, to his utter shock, she worked at the humble corner café that Carlos had always avoided, deeming it \

She, for her part, had endured Moriarty's meows at six in the morning, blaming him for her insomnia.

There was a heavy silence, a moment of tension.  But then, Carlos, forgetting all his method and control, let out a raucous laugh. She joined in, and the echo of their laughter filled the narrow fifth-floor hallway. They had been living side by side for a year and a half, exchanging icy greetings in the elevator, unaware that their digital alter egos had been arguing for days with a ferocity worthy of a trial at the Old Bailey.

The masks fell. Carlos_88 and Luna_Estrella20 ceased to exist. A week later, Carlos posted the long-awaited photo of Moriarty. In the comments, under the name Lucía, a note appeared: \

She accepted. And so, from that insignificant technological mystery, that endless cargo, and two false names, the most unexpected of alliances emerged in building 5. The elevator became the stage for their encounters. Carlos smiles with the satisfaction of one who has solved the best of crimes: the crime of loneliness. Because, as Miss Marple well knew, sometimes the darkest secrets are not hidden in grand mansions, but in the wall that separates two apartments. ***

body.title: Introducing Hive All Weekly Authors Analytics Dashboard
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWNPgupRG1Xq9e34XaWERDYN1NbjP2cCywYMze7nznq1n/image.png)

## Introduction

I am excited to share the newest addition to my growing suite of Hive analytics tools: the Hive All Weekly Authors Analytics Dashboard.

You can use it here:
https://seattlea.z5.web.core.windows.net/authors-dashboard.html

This report gives a full, transparent view of author rewards activity on Hive for the last 7 days, with high performance and no dependency on public Hive API servers for the analytics itself.

## Why I Built This
My strategy is simple: build a full suite of tools that puts real Hive data into the hands of all users, not just developers who can write SQL against HAF.

I started with [Curator Analytics](https://ecency.com/@seattlea/announcing-top-600-curator-analytics), and now I am expanding into author analytics with the same approach:

* Fast data pipeline
* Repeatable automation
* Visual dashboards anyone can use
* Frequent refreshes
* Full transparency

This is just the beginning of the project and I intend to build out the most extensive analytics and analysis suite that Hive has.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcNH51hXUCwVzheL6mk8p2YyQZyPJmYDBMHSiEf3aYJ13/image.png)



## What Makes This Dashboard Different
This is not just another JavaScript HTML Page using Hive API calls to display data that is publicly available via API.

This dashboard is built on top of HAF sources data, then pushed into a static analytics experience that loads fast and is easy to explore. The key difference is that the heavy lifting happens in SQL and automation pipelines, not in live API pulling from the browser.

That means:

* Better performance - no need to place extra load on publicly available Hive APIs
* Stable reporting - data is queried once every four hours 
* Scalable foundation for more analytics tools

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc5ZLxztCr9BqwyrSPs7WGPmp7SPKS7p568ugr97BMmek/image.png)




## What I Built
The dashboard includes a full analytics layer for weekly author rewards, including summary KPIs, distribution analysis, tiers, rankings, filtering, and export.

Current snapshot in the dashboard shows:

1. Total Authors Rewarded: 2,110
2. Total Author Rewards: 257.17K HP
3. Average HP per Author: 121.88
4. Median HP Earned: 28.84
5. Top Author HP Rewards: 67.22K
6. Bottom 50% Average HP: 8.59

One number that really surprised me was a total authors that were active on Hive in the last seven day period that has paid out the rewards: 2,110! That is a very low number, which made me come up with a dashboard that shows everything you could possibly want to know about the last five years of weekly active authors on Hive. That dashboard is coming soon...

It also highlights Top 5 weekly authors and includes multiple analytical views:

1. Top 15 Authors by HP Rewards
2. Curation Events Distribution
3. Top vs Average Author Comparison
4. Author Rewards Distribution (all authors)
5. Author Rewards Distribution (authors at or under 6000 HP)
6. HP Earned by Author Tier (Top 3, Next 10, Next 87, Rest)
7. Top 100 Authors by HP Rewards (filtered to <= 6000 HP)

What I see interesting here is that top rewarded authors on Hive are actually not real authors: hbd.funder, buildawhale and poshtoken. The first real author and most rewarded one in the last seven day period is actually cryptoandcoffee! Congratulations man, you have been around for-ever, stayed consistent and definitely deserve it! 

In the second place is tarazkp who has been around forever and is very consistent as well.

In the third place is oflyhigh I don't really follow him as he seems to be writing in Chinese :) He has also been around for a while as you can see from my [ Hive Report Card tool fork](https://seattlea.z5.web.core.windows.net/report-card.html?user=oflyhigh&range=all&autofetch=1&mode=100):

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP5kKhUBhJjqQTw9ML56D3G4cYA8XX9Dwk4qj3LwYChvr/image.png)

The real authors in the top 10  for this week are:
1. @cryptoandcoffee - Read his posts 
2. @tarazkp - Read his posts 
3. @oflyhigh - Never read as he writes in the language I don't know :)
4. @erikah - I have read posts from this author before
5. @avdesing - Never seen any posts from this author
6. @bozz  - Definitely read his posts regularly
7. @tattoodjay - New to me
8. @daveks  - New to me
9. @steemychicken1 - Seen a couple posts in the past
10. @meno - Seen quite a few posts of his.

That wraps up  the Hive Authors top ten for last week and there is also a complete sortable table with:

1. Author search
2. Minimum HP filter
3. CSV export for downstream analysis
4. Click-through links to deeper author report cards

## How It Works
I built a custom automated pipeline that:

1. Runs SQL against HAF data for the latest 7-day window
2. Aggregates author-level curation reward metrics
3. Converts reward values into approximate HP
4. Publishes data to cloud storage as JSON
5. Publishes dashboard updates to static hosting

Data refresh is automated every four hours, so users get fresh numbers throughout the day. I believe that a four hour refresh strikes a good balance between freshness of the data and load on back-end services.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmekfCGYRXkc2hvuuihTRnaEeFH1xfDMALf3GEVCwwGyo6/image.png)


## Why This Matters
For me, this is about making Hive analytics practical and open. If we want better decisions, better strategy, and better transparency in the ecosystem, we need tools that are:

* Fast
* Trustworthy
* Easy to use
* Available to everyone

If this is useful to you, test the dashboard and tell me what you want added next. I have lot's of my own ideas of what I want to see, but I definitely welcome feedback from Hive community members.

body.body: > After failing to open the door, I tried a bar roll jump to reach the gyro device. The ground suddenly collapsed beneath BD-1, forcing Cal to dive down to save the bot. After resting at a meditation point, I braved dangerous wall runs and aerial jumps to deliver the component. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdmnKVAPVLaBwogRc72cNRg5hzfdQi99D1Mvy1o6JJyLv/screenshot_1_.png) Now that I failed to open that door, I tried this bar roll jump. That was a cool feature of the game. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUipkRMQ7AbgA64VjWpAe5H1dkzTJD1m1mRcsYs7ptS7P/screenshot_2_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZX6Wf1oboUXaBaUMhQ9AhHv29mrXK8bMdECkiqAyhQ5k/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmatn1bJ7zP1K4jjziSJ5wkDQXHDhmdZaSNEGb9sYwMV5h/screenshot_4_.png) And then I reached this place where I found the gyro module I was looking for, while BD-1 noticed something around, scanning the ancient technological component buried under the dust. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSP6xim4kh9jWboK6QeXcticHvi7SAM3o5hiCFDQJPkEh/screenshot_5_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPsYNoHQ7vYkEw54qKL1HSg9hSwyi1pFc31XqAMPmPEZe/screenshot_6_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVaeiKgkcJpfanqqTwK3zTRXRxoUEry7HSq1Hiy71Lt95/screenshot_7_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRkaCpcHPpsKmXy79zK1VvEyv2ULjexoNsgoGx787WH4F/screenshot_8_.png) As the bot was checking around, suddenly the ground beneath it collapsed, and the bot fell down. So Cal jumped to save BD-1, and he fell along with it down as well, tumbling into the pitch-black darkness of the lower cavern level. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmS9aWfjJdgbjzdaVC5ohb1Dbt9oYu29p5ZExRcM2hje8Q/screenshot_9_.png) After getting back on foot in one piece, I noticed this meditation point right in front of me that I used to save my progress and heal up, watching the soothing blue light envelop the platform as I rested. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdMzsCLd7fQgJ3wGpugTkF3vxPj5LMB4MDyXmo2zrYa1j/screenshot_10_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUkK2T1DXW4BksADmTFhZQRU4DnJRqEu1CzSB56k5XR9m/screenshot_11_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdqW8cTRfmnAVbmTr6oxg3qyMejtDiBbjXxGVY8cFXdP6/screenshot_12_.png) My new objective was to bring the gyro model to Greez. But Cal noticed this strange place that almost reminds him of the Jedi training grounds, as he kept staring at the massive stone pillars lining the subterranean architectural structures. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQLnTpyd7Vm4wYw1LW5CkzDTdNZPgLBSoXk1eAEucEqTq/screenshot_13_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbrtxwA8EbKdygDD4EAZHL18G4xy4XNRER7ANFcQtuPFK/screenshot_14_.png) Well, then I had to try some wall runs that looked quite dangerous because I had to jump from one wall to another when there was literally nothing below. I was just trusting my momentum to carry me across the massive abyss. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmevX2NDKSMBaAtXKQu9b7cGP3M4Yxc1HbzEsoDWUHdvZL/screenshot_15_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaQLLDNR2iUVzgftYAbSRjH5wwB4HiU8DPjUR5xR3q8dq/screenshot_16_.png) I used the photo mode to capture some good photos while I was doing a risky wall run, and I even tried to show those stones that were blocking me from climbing up. I just paused the frantic action to frame the crumbling geological structures perfectly. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWbYB1z2nZrXroGsCnvbc32XAFPZyWVTfdSGcdeaYXu5Q/screenshot_17_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX6p7e9mTq53WpnNHChybkaiis3TRE9QBeg7EGc92zLtJ/screenshot_18_.png) When I thought the wall runs were done, I had to try this aerial jumping next where I had to jump from one side to another and then the other side to reach the top, bouncing off the vertical rock, faces with precise timing. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeE4Cgb7WyFGu7GYp7rjqW35QYSFn5jLyszwta3dvPC2Z/screenshot_19_.png) And at last, I reached some ground below my foot, and after scanning the place with the help of BD-1, I found huge masses of rock fell through the roof and slammed around. Bd-1 was helping me analyze the ancient structural damage that shattered the pathway. That's all for this session. More moments coming soon and thanks for checking it out. --- ▶ [Watch on 3speak.tv](https://3speak.tv/watch?v=ridwanan/remnants-of-a-familiar-plac-395)
