links.title: House of the Dragon (2022) : Queens Landing - S03E02 - RECAP
links.body:
https://chv.ai25.site/images/2026/06/30/House-Of-The-Dragon-2022-S03E02--RECAP-000.gif
[Source](https://www.amazon.com/House-Dragon-Season-3/dp/B0H4DSTMNQ)

https://i.imgur.com/PGNq5Ek.png

House of the Dragon season three episode two, cooked again, they really learn from their mistakes from Season 2 and seem to found the balance between drama an action, this episode is the perfect example of it. Start with that opening silent underwater moment, floating dead bodies, bright dragon flames cutting right through murky water. There is one poor guy struggling to get to his feet on a capsized boat and a passing dragon burns him right up, thats some awesome dramatic picture, its the little details that count. Then the camera drifts past Jace dead in the water and his dragon Vermax gone with him, but the most painful is Baela who carry Jace stretched across Moondancer and brings his body back home to the dark halls of Dragonstone. This is the second son Rhaenyra has lost during this war and damn Emma Darcy did a great job in that sad scene at Dragonstone when Rhaenyra looks at her fallen boy lying on a stretcher, sobbing hard, crying out asking what he has done, like she is denying it and wont accept it, telling him how could you do this to me, some might say this was a casualty of war although I dont it, it was all Rhaena's fault and where does Daemon lands here if he is going to be on the Queens side or his daughter??. We got so many threads on this single scene, how did we got here?, well Sir Lorent had locked Rhaenyra in her room earlier to keep her safe from battle and at first she says killing him will not bring her child back. I know some people might not have a clue whats next but its here where Dragon seeds start to form cracks in their relationship with true blood Targaryen. Daemon returns to Dragonstone to pull Rhaenyra out of that state, steps up, reminds her that her son died fighting for his queen and its funny how that little boost her up wearing armor and a sword, leaving strategy behind, and Mysaria hands her father's Targaryen crown before they fligth to Kings Landing. That opening left me a little disappointed because they speed run how fast all of this happens but the cast made it watchable and the grief does a great job even when things are a bit rush out.

- IMDB: https://www.imdb.com/title/tt11198330/
- Platform: [PRIME VIDEO](https://www.amazon.com/House-Dragon-Season-3/dp/B0H4DSTMNQ)

https://i.ibb.co/XkKj9HFq/313bc51cb3c7.png
<div style=\

> https://i.ibb.co/zVQ8wN4t/27f54dc85a39.png [Source](https://www.amazon.com/House-Dragon-Season-3/dp/B0H4DSTMNQ) What worked best was finally seeing Rhaenyra approaching Kings Landing on Syrax, with Daemon and the new riders flying guard, four dragons coming in as a show of force. Alicent goes down to the Gold Cloaks to deliver her message, talking about treason and she convinces them to stand down for peace but after all they only need to know Daemon was coming since the Gold Cloaks were still loyal to their commander. The CGI when the four dragons approaching the city was not the best to be honest and I say this even when watching the episode on a 4K rip. The soliders were not in terror as many decided to kneel down as a sign of peace, many dont even know the business between the two families and just follow orders while there were others, not many, but did decide to stand up to the end and its when Daemon cuts through the Red Keep courtyard, puts down stragglers, yells who else dares rise against us in our house and then push open the doors into the throne room with Rhaenyra next to him, it was interesting how one White Cloak and with him some castle soldiers decide to stand against them and its obvious nothing would happen to Daemon and Rhaenyra but you had to be a fan of the show to see the Gold Cloaks saving them both at the last minute so even though it was satisfying seen Rhaenyra take the throne if felt like they got out of that situation too easy, was too cheap. Finally Rhaenyra holds court and starts punishing everyone who stood against her, we start to see real treason when Grand Maester Orwyle offers up Lord Jasper to save his own neck, then it comes out that Larys Strong had trapped Otto Hightower down in the black cells the whole time after Aemond fire him, I was also wondering where the fuck he was. Rhaenyra executes Otto right in front of the court, swings Daemon Valyrian steel sword Dark Sister and it takes two hacks to get his head off, leaving a mess and she walks up to the throne with blood on her boots, what a start to rule. She sits down on the iron throne crying because she is not of blood and war, just right as Alicent gets hauled in with Helaena, I wonder if Alicent going to take it slight after Rhaenyra killed her father, we will truly see if she has finally accept that putting Aegon on the throne was a mistake and her father was just collateral damage. It is dope seeing Rhaenyra finally take that throne and Daemon walking her through the Song of Ice and Fire prophecy and those visions of a silver haired girl with three dragons, although anyone who have seen Game of Thrones knows Rhaenyra is not that girl but it seems like they both think she is, Targaryen have this tendency of go mad, not all of them but many so if they both continue this prophecy relgious path they might both tip over and start murdering people left and right just as Daenerys did. https://i.ibb.co/N2qQtVLX/0e56b0a78a92.png [Source](https://www.amazon.com/House-Dragon-Season-3/dp/B0H4DSTMNQ) https://i.ibb.co/HDp0gKHH/c47ce1d17e44.png [Source](https://www.amazon.com/House-Dragon-Season-3/dp/B0H4DSTMNQ) If we compare this episode to earlier seasons, the show is clearly making big adaptation choices that must shift away from the original source and consider this is coming from a guy who have not read the books but I'm damn sure on the books Rhaena doesnt go to the Veil for hidding trying to get on Lady Jayne Arryn good faith as she fear Vhagar but the question is who she really fear the most Vhagar or the queen who has more than one dragon, besides Sheapstealer would never take down Vhagar alone considering how unexperience he is at battle, might be a strong dragon but has zero battle skills, plus some other events like the dramatic way Rhanyra takes the throne and the same for how during the Gullet Battle its Jace who leads the charge it just sounds ridiculous how Rhenyra's court would allow it like nobody is watching them, there is the excuse he is the prince and rides a dragon so who is going to stop him. The series keeps leaning harder into human behavior and bad choices, like Lord Jasper trying to blackmail Alicent right before he attacks her, and Grand Maester Orwyle stepping in to arrest him, proving that the smaller chess pieces have to play smart to survive, Orwyle knew Alicent might have made some bad choices but at that very moment he knew what he just saw, of that he was certain . We also get Corlys watching High Tide burn in the distance, offering Alyn his name on the beach in a moment that points toward acknowledging both Alyn and Addam as his sons and actually question if this was really a victory because for his personal interests it doesnt look like it after watching everything he owns burn down. https://i.ibb.co/zWCND5pK/c598d1352728.png [Source](https://www.amazon.com/House-Dragon-Season-3/dp/B0H4DSTMNQ) https://i.ibb.co/JRVBRP46/4ebbd990b910.png [Source](https://www.amazon.com/House-Dragon-Season-3/dp/B0H4DSTMNQ) What did not work was Aemond arriving at Harrenhal acting like a lunatic, riding Vhagar into the castle walls, torching the garrison, storming into the dining hall where Simon Strong is just sitting there eating dinner, he didnt accomplish anything other than feeding his ego like he was Aegon The Conqueror when he was not, he didnt even melt the castle as Aegon did. Simon wipes his mouth with a napkin, tells him we were not expecting you and Aemond demands he draw a sword, that was a funny moment if you knew how Simon got alone with Daemon back then. The thing is Simon has no sword, tries to talk his way out of it so there is no real danger or oposition at all and still Aemond just kills him unarmed and picks up the ancestral sword Blackfyre off the table to cut down Simon sons in cold blood, acting unhinged but then one of those sons manages to stick a blade right into Aemond from behind that at first because of the heat of the moment look like he took it like a champ and I was like that cant be true, its that moment when he rapidly falls to the floor begging for help. The whole thing felt stupid without any accomplishment and Aemond ends up on the floor losing blood, crawling at the feet of Alys Rivers like a helpless mess. Alys just kind of appears in the background, says nothing, stands over him with all the power, she could do a Daemon a solid and kill him right there but she wants Harrenhal for herself and already knows Daemon is not going to give it to her. The Triarchy fleet stuff is also trash, slowing everything down just like to fill up space, watching those blue haired soldiers ambush a caravan is a complete waste of time and let Aegon get off too easy and too convinient. Whats remaining of the Triarchy attack the cart holding Aegon and Larys Strong, chaos breaks out and Aegon grabs a arrow tip to stab some squire, this is when Larys suggests making for Duskendale after they break free but Aegon refuses and pushes for Rooks Rest instead, which just makes the desicion feel all over the place like where are we really going?. https://i.imgur.com/uwwnjtd.png

>\nhttps://i.imgur.com/r0yj9oi.png\nI am giving this a 8 out of 10, mainly because of Rhaenyra, nothing else, it was not as awesome as the first one and I even saw comments online like this is the second best episode ever, probably it is the most satisfying seen Otto been cut down and Rhaenyra taking the throne but is no contender for \

where Rhaenys gets killed by Vhagar and Aemond. Yes, Rhaenyra is finally on that throne and taking what she came for, but the episode rushes to get there and a few times just feel like dead weight. That final throne room scene brings Alicent and Helaena right in front of Rhaenyra, both of them looking down at Otto lifeless body on the floor with all the blood spreading, that was neet. Alicent did her part, let Rhaenyra walk into the city unopposed but she never knew Otto was rotting in the black cells downstairs, so seeing her face when she find him dead on the ground was probably the best surprise moment of the episode. Rhaenyra goes from stunned to something colder in about two seconds, Im grieving my son and now Im not because Vhagar just left the Red Keep; it was hilarious they really decided to do it that way. Mysaria hovering close, reminding Rhaenyra about who has been faithful tells you just how much pull she has now but Im sure her ambitions are probably just to be part of her court, be her eyes across Kings Landing but nothing bigger. Rhaenyra leaving bloody footprints up the iron throne steps is the kind of shot you keep thinking about because for me its just a sign of how bloody and messy this battle is going to get, Im really want to see armies clash at each other but as usually GOT fashion it will most likely become a story of alliances and treason, thats without couting how much impact is going to make Aegon when he rides again, you can already see what getting this throne is going to cost her. There is plenty of action and dragon battles to keep things moving fast, but rushing the fall of Kings Landing definitely took a chunk of the story and mostly the tension that moment deserved.

links.title: Beenham Church
links.body: Beenham Church sits at the top of a hill overlooking the surrounding West Berkshire (Wessex Downs) countryside and is at the end of a lane that trickles out into a bridleway. There is a footpath to the rear that looked like a great option for a future walk. It commands a peaceful spot, where only the whispers of the breeze may be heard, stirring the dancing grasses that grow tall during the summer days. The only sound punctuating this idyll was the call of a Buzzard flying overhead, announcing it's presence as it soars in the meandering wind. Us Tombstone Tourists continue our study of the local resting spots, an endless fascination for my wife and I. We often scribble down notes, finding incredible names, some that sound like they were inspired by a Dickens, Austen or De Maurier novel. The Benney family, a name that wasn't that unusual but the story behind this couple, very interesting. Read on to learn about them! We will continue our research well into the distant future amongst many other topics that we wish to cover across many Hive communities but these posts will always feature as part of the #worldmappin and #churchproject projects I am involved in, mainly to record history like this on the blockchain. You can also find this location via [Google Maps](https://maps.app.goo.gl/jvLVTmTAdk6KVodS9) and [What3Words](https://w3w.co/missions.bullion.snooze).

/> > Gerald Benney, a renowned British gold and silversmith, was born in Hull in 1930. He studied at Brighton College of Art and the Royal College of Art, where he was awarded the Prince of Wales Scholarship. Benney’s innovative designs, including the “Benney bark finish,” and his business acumen, notably his work with Viners of Sheffield, established him as a leading figure in the industry. The only craftsman in any field to hold four royal warrants simultaneously. > Janet Benney, organiser of the Highclere horse trials for over 20 years, passed away at 76. A passionate eventing supporter, she produced horses with Mark Corbett, including Society Spice, who placed 15th at Badminton in 2010. Her funeral will be held at St Mary’s Church, Beenham, on 17 April at 2pm.

/>

Bibliography
------------

*   Find out more about this church [here](https://www.beenhamonline.org/church.htm)
    
*   Another interesting document on the Church was written by archaeologists from Oxford University, that you can find - [here](https://eprints.oxfordarchaeology.com/4784/1/BEEN96.pdf)
    
*   George Benney obituary - [here](https://www.thetimes.com/travel/destinations/uk-travel/england/london-travel/gerald-benney-goldsmith-and-silversmith-dhk7zvgbsns) - Janet Benney obituary - [here](https://www.horseandhound.co.uk/eventing/janet-benney-of-highclere-horse-trials-has-died-387139)

links.title: Битва, яку ми майже програли: як наука знову відкриває нам очі на антибіотики
links.body: >Ми звикли вважати антибіотики чимось на кшталт магічної палички: захворів — випив таблетку, і через пару днів знову готовий підкорювати вершини чи, як мінімум, викладатися на лекціях. Але як хімік, я не можу ігнорувати той факт, що ми опинилися в центрі справжньої війни. І, чесно кажучи, довгий час здавалося, що ми в цій битві повільно, але впевнено здаємо позиції. Багато хто з вас, напевно, чув про «супербактерії» — тих самих «термінаторів» мікросвіту, на яких сучасні ліки діють приблизно так само, як горох на стіну.

>Останніми роками ця тема не давала мені спокою. Це не просто сухі формули з підручників, це реальна загроза, яка дихає нам у потилицю. Але сьогодні у мене є новини, які змусили мене, старого скептика, щиро посміхнутися. Вчені з Scripps Research нещодавно опублікували результати, які виглядають як справжній тактичний маневр у цьому нескінченному протистоянні.

>Precise and efficient eradication of resistant bacteria through β-lactamase-triggered activation and accumulation of photosensitizer BIN-3I. (A) Chemical structure and β-lactamase-mediated hydrolysis of BIN-3I. (B) Selective accumulation of BIN-3I in β-lactamase-positive methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) upon enzymatic activation. (C) Counterselection against resistant bacteria BIN-3I-mediated eradication of MRSA in co-culture with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA).

>Суть ось у чому: замість того, щоб намагатися створити черговий «супер-антибіотик», який бактерії з’їдять на сніданок вже через рік, дослідники вирішили вдарити по їхній «ахіллесовій п’яті». Вони сфокусувалися на ванкоміцин-резистентному ентерококу — штуці, яка в лікарняних умовах є справжнім жахом. Ці бактерії навчилися ігнорувати ванкоміцин, останній рубіж оборони проти найнебезпечніших інфекцій.

>Але вчені знайшли фермент, який бактерії використовують для розбудови своєї клітинної стінки — SagA. Це як архітектор, який будує фортецю навколо мікроба. Виявилося, що якщо «вимкнути» цього архітектора, фортеця стає вразливою. Уявіть собі: бактерія стає настільки слабкою, що навіть той самий старий добрий ванкоміцин, який раніше на неї не діяв, раптом знову стає смертельною зброєю. Вони знайшли сполуку під кодовою назвою pghi-4, яка діє як вимикач для цього ферменту. Це не новий антибіотик, це, якщо хочете, «ключ», який відкриває двері, замкнені бактерією зсередини.

>Коли я читав про це, в голові одразу виникли паралелі з моєю роботою в лабораторії. Ми часто шукаємо складні реакції, вигадуємо хитромудрі синтези, а геніальність, як виявляється, часто криється у простоті стратегії. Це стратегія ад’ювантів — помічників, які самі по собі не вбивають, але змушують «класику» працювати з новою силою. Це дає нам шанс виграти час. А час у науці — це найдорожча валюта.

>Звісно, хтось скаже: «Це лише миші, лише лабораторні досліди». І матиме рацію, бо шлях від пробірки до аптечної полиці — це марафон, а не спринт. Але той факт, що ми навчилися фармакологічно «вимикати» ферменти, які раніше вважалися недосяжними — це великий крок. Це інша філософія боротьби. Ми більше не намагаємося пересилити бактерію в гонці озброєнь, ми вчимося її обхитрити.

>Зараз, дивлячись на те, як швидко змінюється світ, я все частіше думаю про те, що такі відкриття повертають нам відчуття контролю. В останні роки ми звикли відчувати себе заручниками обставин — чи то пандемії, чи то воєнних конфліктів. Але такі моменти, коли інтелект людини перемагає еволюційну хитрість мікроба, нагадують, що ми все ще здатні тримати удар.

>Чи змінить це наше життя завтра? Навряд чи. Але це фундаментальна зміна в парадигмі медицини. Коли ми перестаємо вважати себе слабшими за невидимого ворога, ми починаємо шукати шляхи до перемоги, навіть там, де двері здавалися зачиненими назавжди. І, знаєте, мені приємно бути сучасником часу, коли наука знову стає схожою на мистецтво стратегії. Чи готові ми до майбутнього, де антибіотики будуть лише частиною комплексного «розумного» підходу до лікування?

links.title: Being Seen Isn't The Problem; Being Misrepresented Is. \n\n
links.body:
We are in the era of social media, and almost everyone today is trying to do one thing or the other on the media space. That is why wherever you go or turn to you will definitely see someone taking pictures or recording a video or even live streaming. And aside from all of that, people who go to work at event centers as photographers or videographers will definitely take pictures and do videos of you that you're not aware of. The same goes to journalist too who could be covering a news and such.



![1001199317.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/23rBBjRMyAfYXsHLnArbrXiMbfJchwvobELpMc7McAdBv2GyW4qJ512gxVKkoxWn8S66f.png)



And since the topic made use do the word *\

* I really do not see anything bad in it. If I get tro see myself online either in persons picture or video which I'm not aware of when it was taken, I won't count it, honestly. It just obvious it is accidental, anyone could have been passing at that time, and it could have been anyone, so to me it shouldn't be a crime. Public space or public places are places open to everyone. Most of the time, those recording or taking pictures aren't even paying attention to the passers by and all, they are most times focused on what they are actually capturing.



Go to our markets, motor parks, church, events and all today and see how people take pictures, do videos and livestream. Even on the road. Do you expect a videographer or content creator to ask each and everyone for consent before going ahead to do what he or she wants to do. It is not possible, hundreds and thousands of people are usually in public spaces, even this people we are talking about are not usually one in a public space, you even find them videoing and capturing themselves unintentionally at times. So how will such a law exist talk more or work.




Now, in as much as I see nothing wrong with it ther should be limit. Meaning that such videos or pictures must not b sued to spread lies, sway the public, embarrass me or promote something I know absolutely nothing about. If it breaches any of that, then I think such cns be seen as a crime and the law can take it full course. Now, I'm saying that because I came across a video online about two years ago where a young lady was seen shouting and promoting her business in a public space while claiming that all the crowd behind her were there to patronize her and can testify to the authenticity on what she's selling.



![1001199332.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marsdave/242Nyw5ZJ9UszZ3W8tZxHPA8SEbbaf8eosvZXjQyvcsReLDGzwNbYBh9eFGQMzgCPKLBf.png)



Meanwhile,nshe actually had her goods there, but something happened right in front of where she displayed her goods by the roadside, and because everyone came to see what was happening the place became crowded and she used that opportunity to quickly sway everyone online. You will agree with me that such content is misleading, because innocent people are being used to sell a false story. She sells what the call *\

* now imagine if a woman's face got captured in it and her husband whose home got to see it, it would have led to misunderstandings and all before anyone would know the woman wasn't patronizing her.



So, the issue isn't appearing in a public video and such, the real issue is how such picture or video is being used. If it is harmless then it is fine, but if it is being used to rob people, sway the public, or damage my reputation then it is a crime.

links.title: Artist Mustafa Monowar: A beacon of creativity and our responsibility
links.body:
Hi friends. Today  I am going to tell about a person of Bangladesh who won the 90s kids hearts. He is my country's renowned artist Mustafa Manwar has left us today. He was not just a painter or puppeteer, but a great figure of art and culture. The versatile Mustafa Manwar was originally hailed as the 'magician of puppetry' of Bangladesh. His talent in every medium of art  painting, directing television programs and stage decoration was unparalleled.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPjRjqDQGwfS9sSxb1gMjkbcFkT4WnocUDhFNtv4yKQdk/1782840647621.jpg)

Image source : Online news portal ' Ajker Potrika'. 
https://www.ajkerpatrika.com/entertainment/ajpswkjzboxfp

In my previous posts I posted some creative arts which were painted by me and I was inspired by him. He was my inspiration from my childhood. He has been awarded many national and international honors, including the Ekushey Padak and the Swadhinata Puraskar, for his unique contribution to art. Popular programs like 'Notun Kudi' for children and teenagers on television screens are his creation. He taught us how to bring art closer to the hearts of the common people, especially children. The 'Parapet' puppet play he created has become an integral part of our society and culture.

Why should we practice creativity? Because creativity means the courage to create something new. It breaks the inertia of human thought and frees life from monotony. Creative people not only develop themselves, but also show the path of new light to the entire society.

Creativity can bring profound changes in our society. It makes a society tolerant and humane. When people are engaged in creative practice, mutual respect and rational mentality are created among them. Art practice removes prejudice from society and spreads positive outlook in people's minds. Mustafa Manowar's entire life has shown us that art and creativity can strengthen the cultural backbone of a nation. His departure is an irreparable loss to us, but the creative works he left behind will inspire us from generation to generation.

links.title: Just Because You Can, Doesn't Mean You Should
links.body: ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTqJDX1XiYY1MY85dybEiF4xETisz97EU2mDCnXc9LFFu/1782840545109.png) Where should we draw the line between the freedom to film in public and an individual's right to privacy? I personally think that everyone should be able to feel respected and safe. It doesn't matter if it's a public place or not. Being in a public place shouldn't be an excuse to ignore basic respect for other people's privacy. We should have basic manners, and that should be taught from childhood. In this generation everyone has a phone with a camera, so it is very easy to take pictures or record videos without asking the people around them. Even when I take pictures outside l, sometimes there are people in the background but I never posted those pictures online. It is common to appear in the background of someone else's photo, I think people may find it uncomfortable if it's posted online only. If it's posted by a celebrity then they may let it go because they have the craze for getting famous as well. And for some people like me it can still make them feel uncomfortable if they discover they have been recorded without knowing. To be honest, I don't care if someone is famous or a celebrity, I do not wish to appear on social media at any cost. If I had found myself in a stranger's or celebrities video online then I would feel uncomfortable. Even if I was only in the background, I would not like it because many people will be watching me. What if the videographer presented me in a wrong way? I think everyone should have some control over how their image is used, specially if the video becomes popular on social media. Let me share my reasons, I have always been very private about my photos. I have never shared my pictures online unless it's necessary. I do not feel comfortable at all to share my image on social media, because it's gonna be there forever. I also do not like it when my friends post pictures that include me. My friends are very understanding, I had told them once about how much I dislike it, after that they always respected my feelings and deleted them. They started to post other pictures that did not include me. To be honest, I felt respected. As you can already see that asking for someone's permission is not difficult when you care about their feelings. I know a stranger wouldn't care about my feelings because they don't know me. So, if a stranger recorded me in public and uploaded the video without my knowledge. I would have no opportunity to ask them to take it down, even if I had contacted them, what if they declined my request? Even though I have an opinion against these stuff, I still do not support that public photography and filming should be prohibited. It can not be the best solution. People who are journalist or an artist, they depend on filming in public places to earn for their livelihoods. However, If they had to ask permission from every single person who appeared in the background, it's an impossible thing. I don't think that it should be considered as a crime to record people in public, it should depend on how these recordings are used. Moreover, If someone deliberately focuses on a specific person to invades their privacy and defame them then there should be legal consequences. In conclusion, balance is everything. Nothing should be done excessively, otherwise it could get worse. Everything should have some limits. A little kindness and consideration is all we need. ____ The pictures are created with [Gemini](Gemini.google.com). ____

links.title: Lo que no puede decirse con palabras [ESP-ENG]
links.body:
>
ENGLISH VERSION (click here!)

Hello dear community. A few days ago I had the topic to write this post, and without realizing it (contradictorily) I was already paying tribute to the title. While there are moments when words flow like a spring, there are others when everything seems to stall. Not finding the words to write about the topic, even having a draft and its structure, was one of those moments. Contradictory, isn't it? This kind of situation is more common than it seems. There are moments that leave us speechless. Not for lack of thought, but for excess. A piece of art that pierces you, a landscape that disarms you, news that you don't know if it's good or bad. Psychology calls this 'ineffability': the impossibility of translating an experience into language. Many times, more than the intensity of the emotion, it's that we don't know how to name it. But the silence of words does not always arise from intensity. Sometimes it arises from waiting. There is a stillness that also disarms us, and that we rarely name. Take, for example, faith. I'm not speaking directly about religion. I'm speaking about that trust we place in something or someone, that hope we launch into the world like a silent prayer. Once launched, there are no more words. Only the waiting remains. And when that silence settles in, seeking other paths is not a consolation. It is a natural extension of what is already happening. When we find ourselves immersed in situations where words are insufficient, we can accompany ourselves with all our other senses to express ourselves. There are various forms: sounds, drawings, gestures, and so on. This path is also valid. Personally, we can channel our feelings and perceptions using these channels to free the mind somewhat from those thoughts that affect us so much. Many times we are afraid or feel ashamed of the result, but we must understand that it's not about that, only about expressing ourselves. You don't have to be a writer to write a poem or study at a conservatory to make music. The artistic value that our creations possess is purely spiritual and should be seen as such: an alternative form to words. To carry out these activities, there is no need to have the intention of being a professional or having an impeccable technique; only to have faith in the process and enjoy it without expectations. In my personal case, I practice various forms and I like to constantly improve what I do, even if it means studying it in depth, but always at my own pace. When words are not enough for me, I move on to other manifestations: I walk and take photos, compose music, or draw in my notebook. Many times the results never see the light of day. And fortunately, there are spaces where this way of creating finds an echo without asking for credentials. Platforms like Hive are an example of this, where we can be authentic and where we are supported more for the personal value we offer than for commercial value. This creates a space of safety without so much competition, where everyone has their own voice without fear of being judged, with a very genuine feeling of community and cooperation. Perhaps that's why this post took so long to arrive. Not because the topic was missing, but because the topic itself was the absence of words. And sometimes, to write about silence, you have to learn to inhabit it first. Seek out a situation that you cannot name. Do not try to put words to it. Just stay in it. Observe how your body feels, how your mind moves. You don't need to explain it. Just describe its weight. Perhaps that lack of words is not a lack. Perhaps, like that emptiness I spoke of some time ago, it is a door. If you dare, tell me: what situation has left you speechless? You don't need to explain it. Just name it with an image, a gesture, a silence.

Contenido en Español Hola querida comunidad, hace varios días que tenía el tema para escribir esta publicación y sin darme cuenta (contradictoriamente) le estaba haciendo gala al título. Si bien hay momentos donde las palabras fluyen como un manantial, hay otros donde todo parece estancarse. No encontrar las palabras para escribir sobre el tema, aun teniendo un borrador y la estructura del mismo, fue uno de esos instantes. Contradictorio, ¿no? Este tipo de situaciones son más comunes de lo que parece. Hay momentos que nos dejan mudos. No por falta de pensamiento, sino por exceso. Una obra de arte que te atraviesa, un paisaje que te desarma, una noticia que no sabes si es buena o mala. La psicología llama a esto 'inefabilidad': la imposibilidad de traducir una vivencia al lenguaje. Muchas veces, más que la intensidad de la emoción, es que no sabemos cómo nombrarla. Pero el silencio de las palabras no siempre nace de la intensidad. A veces nace de la espera. Hay una quietud que también nos desarma, y que rara vez nombramos. Como, por ejemplo, la fe. No hablo directamente de religión. Hablo de esa confianza que depositamos en algo o alguien, esa esperanza que lanzamos al mundo como una plegaria silenciosa. Una vez lanzada, ya no hay palabras. Solo queda la espera. Y cuando ese silencio se instala, buscar otras vías no es un consuelo. Es una extensión natural de lo que ya está pasando. Cuando nos vemos inmersos en situaciones donde las palabras son insuficientes, podemos acompañarnos de todos los demás sentidos para expresarnos. Existen diversas formas: sonidos, dibujos, mímicas, etc. Esta vía también es válida. De manera personal, podemos canalizar nuestros sentimientos y percepciones utilizando estos canales para así liberar a la mente un tanto de esos pensamientos que tanto nos repercuten. Muchas veces tenemos miedo o sentimos vergüenza por el resultado, pero debemos comprender que no se trata de eso, solo de expresarnos. No hay que ser escritor para escribir un poema ni estudiar en un conservatorio para hacer música. El valor artístico que poseen nuestras creaciones es meramente espiritual y debe ser visto como tal: una forma alternativa a las palabras. Para realizar estas actividades no hay por qué tener la intención de ser profesional o tener una técnica impecable de realización; solo tener la fe en el proceso y disfrutarlo sin expectativas. En mi caso personal, practico varias formas y me gusta mejorar constantemente lo que hago, incluso si implica estudiarlo en profundidad, pero siempre a mi paso. Cuando las palabras no me son suficientes, paso a otras manifestaciones: camino y hago fotos, compongo música o dibujo en mi cuaderno. Muchas veces los resultados no ven la luz pública. Y, afortunadamente, hay espacios donde esta forma de hacer encuentra eco sin pedir credenciales. Plataformas como Hive son un ejemplo de ello, donde podemos ser auténticos y donde nos apoyan más por el valor personal que se ofrece que por el valor mercantil. Eso genera un espacio de seguridad sin tanta competencia, donde todos tienen su propia voz sin temor a ser juzgados, con un sentimiento de comunidad y cooperación muy genuino. Quizá por eso este post tardó tanto en llegar. No porque el tema faltara, sino porque el tema mismo era la ausencia de palabras. Y a veces, para escribir sobre el silencio, hay que aprender a habitarlo antes. Busca una situación que no puedas nombrar. No intentes ponerle palabras. Solo quédate en ella. Observa cómo se siente tu cuerpo, cómo se mueve tu mente. No necesitas explicarla. Solo describir su peso. Quizás esa falta de palabras no sea una carencia. Quizá, como aquel vacío del que hablé hace tiempo, sea una puerta. Si te animas, cuéntame: ¿qué situación te ha dejado sin palabras? No hace falta que la expliques. Solo que la nombres con una imagen, un gesto, un silencio. Gracias por leer!!!

links.title: Splinterlands Leaderboard: Ultimately, I ended the season in Gold 2!🔥
links.body:
>Another season has finally come to an end; although I didn't achieve my specific goal, the numbers aren't bad considering how little I played throughout the season. I played slightly fewer Frontier battles compared to Modern, and my win rate took a significant hit in both formats. While my win rate in Modern hovered around 51%, it dropped below 47% in the Frontier mode. When comparing this to the previous season, the main reason for the decline was my busy schedule; spending less time on Splinterlands caused my focus to waver, and a few losing streaks further demotivated me. Nevertheless, by the end of the season, I managed to unlock Silver League Tier 3 in Frontier and maintained my position in Gold League Tier 2 in Modern mode.

\n\n

>Despite playing so few battles and having a low win rate, I earned a significant amount of Glint. While my currently visible total earnings stand at 35k, the actual figure should be considered closer to 50k; this is because, midway through the season, I used my earnings from the previous season—plus an additional 10k—to purchase a Legendary Draw, and later bought 10 Common Draws along with some consumables. Yet, my total Glint balance reflects an amount roughly equal to what I had spent, because at the end of the season, I also received the accumulated leaderboard Glint—a reward that accrues with every battle and is awarded to the player in a lump sum when the season concludes. I now have a total Glint balance of around 53k, putting me just 20k Glint away from another Legendary Draw purchase; so, I plan to earn that remaining 20k and add another Legendary card to my deck.

\n\n

>Apart from all this, I finished the season ranked 180th in the Gold League on the leaderboard. I don't recall my exact ranking from the previous season, but it was likely around the same mark; this means I still have a long way to climb in the rankings, and hopefully, I’ll see some improvement in future seasons. As for the new season, one constant goal is to first earn 20k Glint to purchase a Legendary Draw—though I might buy 10–20 Rare Draws first—but the bottom line is that I must acquire a Legendary Draw before the season ends. Additionally, I’ll aim to improve my win rate and push beyond the Silver League in the Frontier format, while also aiming to advance past Gold in Modern and achieve a new milestone.🔥

\n\n

>Splinterlands isn't an easy place, but that's what makes it even more fun. A perfect strategy takes into account many factors, including stats, abilities, rulesets, mana caps, and more. That's why it's even more important to consider all these factors when developing a strategy. Add good cards to your deck, but also work on improving your strategies, and strive to win as many battles as possible!🔥\n\n

Look closely at the world around you.

Clouds are never identical.

Mountains all have different shapes.

Stone, wood, sand, and water all contain tiny imperfections.

Nature is full of randomness.

If every pixel had exactly the same value, everything would look perfectly smooth and artificial.

Shaders become much more interesting when we introduce controlled randomness.

## Is GLSL Really Random?
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQme7nAhi82895g1rRVizVw5HruuiaqumYoRUPRa6ZJK6JN/ChatGPT%20Image%20Jun%2030,%202026,%2010_14_49%20PM.png 

The short answer is no.

GLSL cannot generate truly random numbers.

Instead, it creates **pseudo random** numbers.

That means the same input always produces the same output.

For procedural graphics, this is actually an advantage.

Every frame remains stable while still appearing random.

## A Simple Random Function

One of the most common random functions looks like this.

```glsl id=\

dot(st, vec2(12.9898,78.233))
```

The dot product converts the two dimensional coordinate into a single number.

Different coordinates produce different values.

## Step Two: Passing Through `sin()`

Next comes

```glsl id=\

sin(...)
```

The sine function scrambles the values into a repeating wave.

By itself, the result is still predictable.

## Step Three: Multiplying by a Large Number

Now multiply the value.

```glsl id=\

43758.5453123
```

The exact number isn't important.

Large values help scatter the decimal places into a more random looking pattern.

## Step Four: Keeping Only the Decimal Part

Finally,

```glsl id=\

fract(...)
```

keeps only the decimal portion.

The final result always stays between

```glsl id=\

0.0

and

1.0
```

Every UV coordinate now receives its own random value.

## Using the Random Function

Generating a random number is easy.

```glsl id=\

float r = random(vUv);
```

You can display it directly.

```glsl id=\

gl_FragColor = vec4(vec3(r),1.0);
```

Instead of a smooth gradient, the screen fills with scattered grayscale values.

## Complete Shader

```glsl id=\

float r = random(

vUv + uTime

);
```

Now the values constantly change.

## Creating Random Tiles

Randomness becomes much more useful when combined with `fract()`.

```glsl id=\

vec2 tile = floor(vUv * 10.0);

float r = random(tile);
```

Instead of every pixel being different, each square receives one random value.

This technique is used in procedural maps, terrain generation, and pixel art.

## Adding Random Colour

Random values don't have to remain grayscale.

```glsl id=\

vec3 color = vec3(

r,

r * 0.5,

1.0 - r

);
```

Every tile now receives its own colour.

## Where Is Randomness Used?

Random values appear almost everywhere.

* Procedural textures.
* Terrain generation.
* Fire.
* Clouds.
* Rain.
* Snow.
* Particle systems.
* Pixel art.
* Noise generation.
* Visual effects.

Almost every advanced shader starts with a simple random function.

## Try These Experiments

Display random grayscale values.

Animate the randomness.

Create larger tiles.

Create smaller tiles.

Colour each random value differently.

Try combining random numbers with circles or rectangles.

Notice how quickly procedural graphics become more interesting.

## A Small Challenge

Can you create these effects?

* A colourful mosaic.
* Random glowing squares.
* A flickering display.
* Animated static.
* A field of randomly coloured circles.

Everything begins with the same small random function.

body.title: 再见六月
body.body:
![1-360220eafad7.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/love5200/lkt-mqzgysby-3nef1mwg/1-360220eafad7.webp)

![3-cde84530d0a0.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/love5200/lkt-mqzgysby-3nef1mwg/3-cde84530d0a0.webp)

![4-16060c48851b.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/love5200/lkt-mqzgysby-3nef1mwg/4-16060c48851b.webp)

![2-e9f2766bef03.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/love5200/lkt-mqzgysby-3nef1mwg/2-e9f2766bef03.webp)

时间来到了六月的最后一天，今日气温直破30度,一场小雨匆忙落下后，天空便开启了晴暖模式；我已许久不在东街天桥上拍照，今日特意绕回到熟悉的电信大楼，却发现营业厅门口赫然立起巨幅华为广告，气势张扬地铺满整面外墙。

我寻思着这里将要开启新一家华为旗舰店，这规模瞅着还挺大的，在东街最热闹的地段，看来华为这一次又要抢占先机。

看到华为，我不由想到它的老对手--苹果，我们本地苹果旗舰店，位于东泰禾广场一楼，规模尚可，这些年稳稳当当，生意始终不淡。每次路过，透过落地玻璃墙都能看见店内有不少客人光顾，有来体验新机的，有来选购的，还有可爱的小朋友们玩着手机游戏的，哈哈。

许久没来人民影院门口早餐车关顾了，这一次只见阿姨一人在忙活着，她依旧是面带笑容，暖心问候着我的近况，几句家常过后，我买了熟悉的早套老三样--肉包，豆浆，鸡蛋。

熟悉的味道，一遍又一遍冲击着我的味蕾，说是喜欢，更多的是“口味习惯”在作祟，不浓烈，却踏实，是每个寻常的日子里最不费力的果腹之选。

再见六月，已带走所有的不快！喜迎七月，愿万事顺遂，喜乐平安。

OK，今天先分享到这儿哈，晚安，祝好梦！

**感谢大家的阅读和喜欢，您的点赞给予我莫大的鼓励，感恩❀**

body.title: Why Convenience Is Making People Less Patient
body.body:
https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPgUbdJyNhDpsoeRT7bLDhH3o9qKDfMDDM1GBRnqoEovk/IMG_9241.jpeg 






Happy Tuesday to my #web3 family and I wish you a blissful week. 
Looking at this beautiful topic before you, might have made you rolled your eyes but don’t be mad at me yet… im not tryna displace convenience or make comfortability seem less important to humanity, at least that’s one major bane or trump card of technology and modern civilization. 

Technology has made things in life Ai easy and super fast that we now skip a lot of processes, gratitudes and most importantly moments that we should have experienced. 
As we all know, anything with an advantage must have a disadvantage, it’s just an existential phenomenon in life, we can’t beat or avoid it. I can boldly say that modern life has become incredibly convenient in so many ways and diverse ramifications, no one can deny that fact and it is a major advantage. 


Most of us that are born into this era of technological convenience can testify that we live an easier life when we look at the lives of our parents, fore fathers, ancestors, especially when they tell us their stories. 
We can also see how fast it evolves in our own time/dispensation, from the era of fax machines to computers and now we have iPhone 17s  lol. We live in an era where unlike before Food arrives in minutes, information appears instantly and communication happens almost immediately. 

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmPgUbdJyNhDpsoeRT7bLDhH3o9qKDfMDDM1GBRnqoEovk/IMG_9241.jpeg 

[source]( https://pin.it/6WWkAgijy)

Now like I said before it’s always more than how we see it because it has impacts on us in other ways. While these developments have improved many aspects of life, they have also brought a change in how people deal with waiting. This is one very important aspect of the disadvantages of speed. Patience used to be built into everyday experiences without a special script or compelling. 
In those days people waited for letters, stood in lines, saved  money for purchases and accepted that some things simply took time. It somehow inculcated the culture and idea of doing things one at a time and made people appreciate the value of taking one step at a time but today, many people become frustrated when a website takes a few extra seconds to load or when a response doesn’t arrive immediately, isn’t that crazy? Now we are so entitled to speed that we can’t overlook some little things anymore, automatically our spirit of patience is diminishing and we don’t see it but instead we think the other party is not adapted enough to the modern world meanwhile its us who don’t have patience anymore. 

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZDJsC8FsiLuqTUA959P1LrtvY57QEtDri3KVay3VFwCz/IMG_9242.jpeg 

[source](https://pin.it/2wtnN1o3R)


If you look at the world closely and deeply today, you’d notice that we fight over irrelevances and our sudden lack of patience has made conflict and wars easier. 
We forget that patience itself is a life skill that our ancestors have passed on to us based on their experience and philosophy about life, we shouldn’t toil with patience for any reason tho we all agree that convenience is a good thing and one reason we all struggle to earn what we get but still if we don’t practice the culture we can’t pass it on to our generations like our ancestors did to us and what does that mean? 

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmZDJsC8FsiLuqTUA959P1LrtvY57QEtDri3KVay3VFwCz/IMG_9242.jpeg 



We are building a more deficient world where patience wouldn’t exist anymore The interesting question is whether convenience is improving life while quietly reducing our ability to tolerate delay and with time we won’t be able to tolerate things or one another like we should. 

Patience has always been connected to discipline, emotional control and longterm thinking so now if everything becomes instant, what happens to those skills?

Thank you for reading 

SAINT HEROD 

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@herod/why-convenience-is-making-people-less-patient-dep)

body.title: Combining Translation, Rotation, and Scaling in GLSL
body.body:
By themselves, translation, rotation, and scaling are useful.

Together, they become incredibly powerful.

Almost every animated shader, game effect, motion graphic, or procedural interface combines these three operations.

The exciting part is that the drawing code usually stays exactly the same.

Only the coordinates change.

## Thinking Like a Shader
 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmeiycRarj8JKYbURuqBHg79TUEWUgLSiSXyKqvzhx1cbK/ChatGPT%20Image%20Jun%2030,%202026,%2010_10_38%20PM.png 

Imagine you have a rubber stamp.

The stamp always draws the same square.

Instead of carving a new stamp every time, you simply move it, rotate it, or resize it before pressing it onto the paper.

Procedural shaders work in the same way.

The shape never changes.

Only its coordinate system does.

## Starting with Centered Coordinates

As before, we'll begin by centering the UV coordinates.

```glsl id=\

vec2 uv = vUv - 0.5;
```

Every transformation will happen around this point.

## Step One: Translation

Let's move the coordinate system.

```glsl id=\

uv -= vec2(0.25, 0.0);
```

The rectangle now appears slightly to the right.

Translation decides where the object lives.

## Step Two: Scaling

Next, resize the coordinate system.

```glsl id=\

uv /= 1.5;
```

The rectangle becomes larger.

Remember that dividing the coordinates makes the shape appear bigger.

## Step Three: Rotation

Now rotate the coordinates.

```glsl id=\

float rect =

step(-0.20, uv.x) *

(1.0 - step(0.20, uv.x)) *

step(-0.10, uv.y) *

(1.0 - step(0.10, uv.y));
```

Notice that the drawing code is identical to previous lessons.

Only the coordinates changed.

## Complete Shader

```glsl id=\

uv = rotation * uv;

uv -= vec2(0.25,0.0);
```

The animation changes completely.

Instead of spinning around its own center, the rectangle now travels in a circular path.

Nothing else changed.

Only the order.

This is one of the most important ideas in computer graphics.

## Another Example

Scale after rotating.

```glsl id=\

uv = rotation * uv;

uv *= 2.0;
```

The rectangle rotates exactly the same way, but now appears smaller.

Every transformation affects those that come after it.

## Building a Transformation Pipeline

Professional shaders often follow a simple sequence.

```text
Center coordinates

↓

Translate

↓

Rotate

↓

Scale

↓

Draw shape
```

Keeping transformations organized makes complex shaders much easier to understand.

## Creating Multiple Objects

Every object can have its own coordinate system.

```glsl id=\

uv -= vec2(sin(uTime),0.0)*0.2;

uv /= 1.2 + sin(uTime)*0.2;
```

Now the rectangle moves while changing size.

Add rotation as well, and all three transformations work together.

## Where Is This Used?

Transformation pipelines appear in almost every graphics application.

* Game user interfaces.
* Motion graphics.
* Animated logos.
* Particle systems.
* Interactive backgrounds.
* Scientific visualizations.
* Procedural artwork.
* Audio visualizers.
* Loading screens.
* Mobile applications.

Learning this workflow prepares you for much larger shader projects.

## Try These Experiments

Translate before rotating.

Rotate before translating.

Scale before rotating.

Rotate before scaling.

Animate every transformation.

Create two objects with different transformation orders.

Watch how dramatically the motion changes.

## A Small Challenge

Can you create these effects?

* A spinning button that grows and shrinks.
* Two rotating rectangles moving in opposite directions.
* A loading animation with several rotating objects.
* A simple solar system.
* A procedural logo built from multiple transformed shapes.

Every challenge uses exactly the same transformation techniques you've learned over the past few lessons.

Welcome to my new little post. I woke up in the morning and went outside to brush my teeth. When I went outside, I saw that the sky was quite cloudy but it seemed like it was going to rain. Because it has been raining every night for the past two days and I don't like anything in this rain. I feel bored sitting at home. But I have my phone with me, due to which I can pass the time. Anyway, I have been at home for the past two days and I couldn't go out. Due to which I decided to go out. In the morning, I had breakfast and after breakfast, I went out for a walk. I basically set off for our neighboring market. I always walk along this road because this road is a very easy way to go to our market. Anyway, after a while, I went out on the road. Then I took quite a few pictures. The sky was still quite black. It seemed like a light rain was falling in the sky at that time. I started coming back from the market through the road. While passing through the road, I saw a small tractor standing by the side of the road. But I did not see any people there. Maybe those who cultivate various agricultural products here have kept this tractor here. They will take their products to the market. Then I took quite a few photographs. I liked them very much. I hope you like my post, thank you all. *** ![1000019308.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRW9rHroSFBSAKdERxzaNWNAnWKCXRUdrHF4LbDABXrT6/1000019308.png) --- Divce | realmi c67 -|-| Photographer | @nahid43 ### Kind Regards @nahid43 ![1000019308.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRW9rHroSFBSAKdERxzaNWNAnWKCXRUdrHF4LbDABXrT6/1000019308.png)

body.title: No need for criminalisation of ...
body.body:
Greetings!

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQSSAtj6Vpc31N8EM9evLWWaC5Xa8WousAX7ofZh1FxAh/1782839369151.jpg)

Everybody wants his or her privacy and for this reason, this fact must be strictly adhered to so as not to violate the rules and regulations guiding the private life. Not everyone likes to be captured in public space and now seeing themselves in a picture or video without prior notice can be somehow disturbing and offensive.

Having said this, I would like to delve into the topic of the prompt right before me which is all about, “your face alone.”

According to the content of the topic, it would be wrong to capture one's picture without the consent of the fellow, but even at that, when the originality of a content is needed, I think there's nothing we can do to avoid the situation knowing fully well that for someone who is making a content to make it original, such a person need a random video or picture which can only be captured on a random basis. 

We have seen the situation that taking a personal picture which is not meant for content creation would even capture passersby. To me it would be kind of difficult to make such a law work in our land and this is because no one content creator would even know who doesn't like him or herself to be captured in a public video or picture. If such a person could be known, then it would be easy to go and inform the person to leave the scene where the picture is to be taken.

As for me, if by mistake I was being captured in an unknown video by a stranger,  I would not have any issue with that stranger knowing fully well that it's a random photo which he or she has no power to determine who or not should be captured in the video or photo.

So. Per adventure I found myself in the video, I would just overlook it and move on as such is life to me.

On so many occasions I have found myself in such a photo which was captured in the public space and I have never taken any offence seeing myself in such an uniformed photo or video.

So, such a set up should not in any way be criminalized and this is because it is beyond the power of those who are trying to make their content look original. To me, the only thing that can be done instead of criminalizing it is to look for a picture of a video village where people with such a mind of creating original content can take a picture without capturing such a picture where no one who is not interested in being captured would not be present.

In conclusion, it would be kind of unfair to criminalize such a scenario whereby one who is not ready or willing to be captured is being captured by another who wants to make his or her content original.

This is my entry to the week 224 episode 01 of the weekly featured contest in the Hive learners community.

Thanks for reading.

body.title: Being a lady is power
body.body:
![IMG_2576.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dwayne16/23x17JdpPq7FHUqZypxQErZnnSjPPNivUnrTBazzfEcCzoDG3a7Bg8Rmaap6niU7UV4JC.jpeg)
***

Being a lady is power because true strength goes far beyond physical appearance. It is found in confidence, resilience, kindness, and the ability to keep moving forward even when life becomes difficult. Every woman carries a unique influence that can shape families, communities, and even future generations.

A lady has the power to inspire through her actions. She can lead with wisdom, encourage those around her, and create positive change simply by believing in herself. Whether she is a student, entrepreneur, professional, or homemaker, her contributions matter. Every achievement, no matter how small it may seem, adds value to the world around her.

Being a lady also means knowing your worth. It means refusing to let other people’s opinions decide your value. Confidence comes from understanding who you are, embracing your strengths, and learning from your weaknesses. A woman who respects herself naturally earns the respect of others.

There is also great power in compassion. Showing kindness, supporting friends, listening without judging, and helping someone through a difficult moment are qualities that leave lasting impressions. Real power is not about controlling others. It is about making people feel seen, heard, and valued.

Throughout history, women have broken barriers, challenged stereotypes, and achieved remarkable things in every field imaginable. Their stories remind us that determination and courage can overcome even the greatest obstacles. They prove that dreams are worth pursuing regardless of the challenges along the way.

Being a lady is power because it is about purpose, influence, and the courage to stand tall in every season of life. Every woman has the ability to grow, inspire, and make a meaningful difference wherever she goes. When she believes in herself, carries herself with dignity, and chooses to uplift others, she becomes a powerful example of what true strength really looks like every single day for everyone.

body.title: Where Choice Ends and Belief Begins
body.body:
One discussion seems to follow me wherever I go these days.

![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVN5setygNci4J4WPisqRykkfb1JF9vJPR7eVTJTFoGiP/image.png)

Can you choose what you believe?

It's a question that appears constantly in debates about religion, particularly between believers and atheists. Usually it goes something like this: believers argue that faith is a choice, while atheists respond that belief simply doesn't work that way.

The more I listen to both sides, the more convinced I become that they're often arguing about different parts of the same process.

As is so often the case in philosophy, the answer depends entirely on which question you're actually asking.

If you're asking whether you can wake up tomorrow morning, snap your fingers, and sincerely believe something you currently think is false, then I don't think the answer is yes. Unless of course, you are a machine yourself.

Belief doesn't behave like a light switch.

It behaves more like gravity.

Your mind is constantly weighing experiences, conversations, evidence, emotions, habits, and relationships. Most of this happens beneath conscious awareness. Then, slowly—or sometimes all at once—your internal map of reality shifts. You don't watch it happen. You simply realize one day that what once seemed impossible now feels obvious.

That's how belief usually works.

Choice enters the picture much earlier.

You choose what books to read. You choose which conversations to have. You choose who you spend your time with. You choose whether to attend church or avoid it. You choose which ideas deserve another look and which ones you'll dismiss after five minutes.

Those choices matter.

In fact, they matter enormously.

They determine the environment in which your beliefs develop. This is the soil the will grow from after all.

Think about soccer. Fitting at the moment, right?

Imagine you barely care about the sport. Then you move to a new city, become friends with your neighbor, and discover that everyone around you lives and breathes soccer. Before long you're playing every weekend, watching every big match, celebrating victories, suffering defeats, and arguing over questionable referee decisions. (Iran got screwed, by the way)

You made plenty of choices along the way.

You chose to spend time with those people.

You chose to keep playing.

You chose to become part of that community.

But there was never a Tuesday afternoon when you consciously declared:

*\

*

You didn't choose the feeling.

The feeling emerged from the life you chose to live.

That's why I think these debates become so frustrating to me.

When atheists say you can't choose to believe in God, they're usually talking about belief itself. You can't force genuine conviction any more than you can force yourself to believe the sky is purple.

When many believers say you can choose God, they're often talking about something different. They're talking about choosing the path that might eventually lead to faith: attending church, praying, reading Scripture(although sometimes this one backfires), asking questions, surrounding yourself with believers, and remaining open to the possibility.

Those aren't the same claim at all. Don't you see?

One is about belief.

The other is about the conditions that often give <u>rise to belief</u>.

Maybe that's why these conversations rarely go anywhere. People leave thinking they've disagreed, when in reality they've been describing different stages of the same journey.

Language has a funny way of doing that.

Sometimes our biggest disagreements aren't about reality at all.

They're about which part of reality we think we're discussing.

— MenO

body.title: Un día de juegos
body.body:
by Hilaricita on Hilaricita 
View my bio on Blurt.media: https://blurt.media/c/hilaricita [![Un día de juegos](https://blurt.media/lazy-static/previews/af97f2ab-01e1-42fd-8468-cd702f5a6e46.jpg)](https://blurt.media/w/47BiLBD8HzcD38vEqMZGkJ) 
 
 ![Versión español.png](https://img.blurt.world/blurtimage/hilaricita/0c2eef4b843038ffa91c5c76126870fbaa369559.png)

Marte 30 de junio, 2026

¿Quién no ha jugado un partido de bolos después de salir del trabajo?

Yo sí, lo hago con frecuencia porque es una manera para distraerme, para alejar mi cuerpo y mi mente de la tensión laboral. 

Se dice que el origen de este entretenido juego, en algunos sitios considerado deporte, no está en las pistas brillantes de hoy, sino en la tierra húmeda y oscura de los patios traseros alemanes hace más de dos mil años. Los romanos ya lanzaban piedras contra otras piedras, pero fue en la Edad Media cuando la cosa se puso seria con el juego de los nueve palos, una actividad que mezclaba la destreza física con una curiosa carga religiosa; si derribabas todos los palos, se consideraba que habías alcanzado la pureza espiritual, aunque muchos simplemente lo hacían por la apuesta o el orgullo. Martín Lutero, sí, el mismo de la Reforma, terminó estandarizando el número a nueve porque le parecía el formato más justo y equilibrado, estableciendo reglas que perduraron siglos en Europa antes de cruzar el océano.

Cuando los colonos llevaron el juego a América, se encontró con un problema inesperado: la moralidad victoriana. Las apuestas descontroladas y el alcohol asociado a los salones de bolos de nueve palos hicieron que varios estados prohibieran la práctica, lo que obligó a los entusiastas a buscar un vacío legal. La solución fue ingeniosa y sencilla: añadieron un décimo palo. Al cambiar la configuración geométrica y el nombre, el juego dejó de ser ilegal y comenzó su transformación hacia lo que conocemos ahora. No fue hasta finales del siglo XIX, con la fundación del Congreso Americano de Bolos, que se unificaron las reglas, el peso de la bola y las dimensiones de la pista, creando un estándar que permitía competir de Nueva York a California bajo las mismas condiciones.

La verdadera revolución, sin embargo, llegó con la automatización. Durante décadas, colocar los palos era tarea de unos jóvenes conocidos como \

, chicos que trabajaban entre el humo y el ruido, recogiendo madera caída y devolviendo bolas pesadas a mano. Era un trabajo duro, lento y propenso a errores humanos que frenaban el ritmo del juego. La invención de la máquina colocadora automática de palos en la década de 1940 cambió la dinámica por completo. De repente, el juego fluía sin interrupciones, permitiendo partidas más rápidas y una experiencia más limpia para el jugador casual. 


Hoy en día, la evolución continúa, aunque sea menos visible a simple vista. Las bolas ya no son solo de madera dura o caucho; son núcleos complejos envueltos en cubiertas reactivas diseñadas con precisión aerodinámica para engancharse en el aceite de la pista de maneras que hubieran parecido magia hace cincuenta años. Las pistas se mantienen con máquinas computarizadas que aplican patrones de aceite específicos para desafiar incluso a los mejores profesionales, obligando a ajustar la técnica constantemente. 

Todo empieza con la elección de la bola, que es mucho más personal de lo que parece a primera vista. No se trata solo de agarrar la más pesada del estante; un profesional sabe que el peso ideal ronda las 14 o 15 libras para los hombres y entre 10 y 12 para las mujeres, pero lo crucial es el ajuste de los agujeros. Los dedos deben entrar con firmeza pero sin apretar, permitiendo que la muñeca tenga libertad de movimiento. Si los agujeros están muy holgados, la bola se sale antes de tiempo; si están muy justos, te quedas pegado y pierdes la rotación. 

Los zapatos son otro elemento distintivo, diseñados no por estética sino por funcionalidad pura. La suela del pie dominante, el que desliza al final del lanzamiento, está hecha de cuero o materiales sintéticos lisos que permiten un desplazamiento fluido sobre la madera encerada. El otro pie tiene una suela de goma normal para frenar y mantener el equilibrio. Sin este contraste, sería imposible generar la velocidad y la precisión necesarias sin resbalar de forma incontrolable o, peor aún, lesionarse la rodilla al frenar en seco. Algunos jugadores incluso llevan consigo sus propias suelas intercambiables para adaptar el deslizamiento según cuán pegajosa o rápida esté la pista ese día.

En cuanto a las reglas, la estructura básica es engañosamente simple pero estratégicamente profunda. Una partida estándar consta de diez cuadros o frames. En cada uno, el jugador tiene dos oportunidades para derribar los diez palos, dispuestos en un triángulo equilátero. Si los tumba todos en el primer lanzamiento, es un strike, que se anota con una X y otorga diez puntos más la suma de los siguientes dos lanzamientos. Esto es clave: un strike no vale solo diez, vale diez más lo que hagas después, por eso una racha de strikes puede disparar la puntuación hacia los 300 puntos perfectos. Si necesitas dos tiros para limpiar la mesa, es un spare, marcado con una barra inclinada, que vale diez puntos más lo que consigas en el siguiente lanzamiento único.

El décimo cuadro tiene sus propias peculiaridades dramáticas. Si haces un strike, tienes derecho a dos bolas extra; si haces un spare, tienes una bola extra. Estas oportunidades adicionales no son solo para sumar puntos directos, sino para completar el valor de los strikes o spares anteriores, cerrando la partida con justicia matemática. Fuera de la pista, la etiqueta no escrita es tan importante como el reglamento: no cruzar la línea de falta, esperar a que el compañero de la pista contigua termine su aproximación para no distraerlo, y mantener la calma tanto en la victoria como en el error. Al final, aunque la tecnología haya cambiado las bolas y las máquinas hayan eliminado a los chicos de los palos, la disciplina mental de leer la pista y ejecutar el movimiento sigue siendo lo que separa a quien juega a bolos de quien realmente entiende el juego.

Participar en este deporte ofrece beneficios que van mucho más allá de la simple diversión social o de pasar una tarde con amigos. Desde el punto de vista físico, es una actividad de bajo impacto que mejora notablemente la coordinación mano-ojo y el equilibrio. El movimiento repetitivo de la aproximación y el lanzamiento ayuda a tonificar los músculos de las piernas, el core y los brazos sin someter al cuerpo al estrés intenso de deportes de contacto o de alta intensidad cardiovascular. Para muchas personas, especialmente aquellas que buscan mantenerse activas sin correr riesgos de lesiones graves por colisiones o caídas bruscas, los bolos representan una puerta de entrada sostenible al ejercicio regular. Además, la concentración requerida para leer la pista y ajustar la trayectoria de la bola actúa como un ejercicio mental, fomentando la paciencia y la estrategia en tiempo real.

Sin embargo, la aparente facilidad del gesto puede ser engañosa y llevar a descuidos peligrosos si no se toman las precauciones adecuadas. La lesión más común no proviene del lanzamiento en sí, sino de la falta de calentamiento previo. Los tendones y ligamentos de la muñeca, el codo y el hombro están sometidos a tensión rotacional; lanzar una bola de varias libras en frío puede provocar esguinces o tendinitis. Por eso, es fundamental realizar estiramientos suaves antes de empezar, enfocándose en la flexibilidad de la espalda baja y la movilidad de los hombros. También hay que prestar atención a la técnica: intentar forzar la bola con pura fuerza muscular en lugar de dejar que la gravedad y el impulso hagan el trabajo suele resultar en dolor lumbar o problemas en la rodilla de apoyo al frenar bruscamente.

El calzado es otra línea roja que no debe cruzarse nunca. Jugar con zapatos de calle, incluso si tienen suela lisa, es una receta para el desastre. La fricción incorrecta puede hacer que el pie se quede pegado mientras el cuerpo sigue avanzando, torciendo la articulación de manera antinatural. Siempre hay que usar el equipo adecuado proporcionado por la bolera o invertir en un par propio bien ajustado. Asimismo, la hidratación es clave, ya que las boleras suelen ser ambientes cerrados con aire acondicionado potente o calefacción seca, lo que puede deshidratar al jugador sin que este lo note durante la competición.

Finalmente, existe un aspecto de seguridad colectiva que a menudo se pasa por alto en el entusiasmo del juego. Respetar los turnos y mantenerse atento a lo que ocurre en las pistas adyacentes evita accidentes innecesarios. Una bola perdida o un resbalón pueden afectar a otros jugadores. Mantener una actitud respetuosa, no invadir el espacio personal de quien está en plena aproximación y asegurar que los niños pequeños no corran cerca de las zonas de retorno de bolas son medidas básicas de sentido común. Cuando se combinan estos cuidados con la pasión por el juego, la experiencia se transforma de un pasatiempo ocasional a una práctica deportiva segura, saludable y profundamente satisfactoria.

Como ya casi se acaba el número de caracteres de la caja de información, les dejo con la canción que le pedí a SUNO, esperando que esta publicación les haya servido, no solo como entretenimiento, sino que les haya aportado un poco, una chispa de contenido que genera valor.

body.title: The essential eating implements : Huzka
body.body:
![53f61463-eab4-41c1-9b27-85c3e7083103.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/dinglehopper/23tvegbbNKeauoADJ7x1YUJLH1fZHLwcnRhgMEDPBL5DQ36sdT6iUXZdW2yWaNNTbMQ52.png)
*Putting it all together, this is LohummTi carrying his huzka or eating kit*
## huzka /ˈhuz.ka/ n.

Definitions

1. A personal eating kit which consists the vessels and implements required for preparing and eating meals while traveling.
2. The standard dining set carried by scouts like LohummTi, traditionally composed of a hymru (bowl), glikka (spoon), and bokka (wooden cup).
3. By extension, it is a complete set of items kept together for a single meal.

Etymology

An old Nivukti word whose original sense referred specifically to a traveler's bundled dining implements. Among the nomadic clans, a huzka was one of the first personal possessions entrusted to a young scout, symbolizing self-reliance and readiness for life on the trail.

Over time, the importance of the huzka caused its name to become synonymous with any neatly assembled bundle of essential belongings. This usage eventually gave rise to the shortened form uvka, which developed into the general word for a kit or bundled set.

Cultural Notes

A huzka represents hospitality, survival, and personal responsibility. Every scout is expected to maintain their huzka carefully, as sharing a meal is considered an affirmation of trust and companionship. A complete huzka traditionally includes:

- Hymru — carved wooden bowl
- Glikka — carved wooden spoon
- Bokka — carved wooden cup

body.title: Learn Zig Series (#94) - NAT Traversal and Hole Punching
body.body:
-- and how to build and parse a STUN binding request from the raw bytes;
- How the **XOR-MAPPED-ADDRESS** attribute hides your endpoint behind the magic cookie, and how to un-XOR it correctly;
- The four flavours of NAT behaviour, and which single one (**symmetric**) quietly defeats hole punching;
- How **UDP hole punching** works: both peers fire packets at each other at the same time so each side's outbound packet opens the door for the other's inbound packet;
- Why a **rendezvous server** is unavoidable, and how little it actually does;
- How a hand-rolled Zig punch compares to the heavy ICE machinery you'd reach for in C, Rust, or Go.

### Requirements
- A working modern computer running macOS, Windows or Ubuntu;
- An installed Zig 0.14+ distribution (download from ziglang.org);
- The ambition to learn Zig programming.

### Difficulty
- Intermediate

# Learn Zig Series (#94) - NAT Traversal and Hole Punching

## Solutions to Episode 93 Exercises

Last episode we built a **SOCKS5 proxy** from its three honest phases -- a method greeting, a single CONNECT request, and a dumb bidirectional relay. The exercises pushed it toward something you'd actually deploy: username/password auth, a connection budget, and the client half of the protocol. Each solution leans on the same `readExact` discipline we've used since the DNS episodes -- every read bounds-checked, because a network-facing parser talks to hostile peers by definition.

**Exercise 1: Add username/password authentication**

After the no-auth greeting, RFC 1929 defines its own little subnegotiation: `[version=0x01][ulen][username][plen][password]`, and the server answers `[0x01][status]` where status `0` means success. The whole thing is four `readExact` calls and a constant-time-ish comparison:

```zig
const std = @import(\

{
    var lim = ConnLimiter{ .max = 2 };
    try std.testing.expect(lim.acquire());  // 1 of 2
    try std.testing.expect(lim.acquire());  // 2 of 2
    try std.testing.expect(!lim.acquire()); // full -> refused
    lim.release();
    try std.testing.expect(lim.acquire());  // a slot freed up
}
```

In `handleClient` you'd call `lim.acquire()` first thing; if it returns false you send reply `0x01` (general failure) and close _before_ relaying, and you `defer lim.release()` so the slot comes back no matter which exit path the handler takes. The optimistic add-then-subtract avoids a compare-and-swap loop -- under contention a couple of connections briefly see the counter above `max` and bounce, which is exactly the behaviour you want.

**Exercise 3: Build a SOCKS5 client**

Writing the other half is the most satisfying test of your own server. `connectThrough` performs the greeting, sends a domain-name CONNECT, validates the reply code into a typed `ProxyError`, and drains the bound-address tail so the returned stream starts exactly at the tunnel:

```zig
