body.title: Television Review: Battle Lines (Star Trek: Deep Space Nine, S1x13, 1993)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/tF7roCnfMbl4kvESW4ozdLc7dR.jpg)

**Battle Lines (S01E13)**

Airdate: 25 April 1993

Written by: Richard Danus & Evan Carlos Sommers
Directed by: Paul Lynch

Running Time: 46 minutes


Star Trek has changed immeasurably since the days of *The Original Series*, particularly in the ways the shows of the so-called Golden Age of the franchise—*The Next Generation*, *Deep Space Nine*, and *Voyager*—strove to be more complex and nuanced than their predecessor. *Deep Space Nine*, with its frontier setting, morally ambiguous characters, and stories steeped in the aftermath of occupation and war, looked very far indeed from the original utopian vision of Gene Roddenberry. Yet, even in *DS9* there were episodes that wore their TOS-like idealism on their sleeve, and one of the earliest examples in Season 1 was *Battle Lines*, an instalment that wears its anti-war allegory as conspicuously as a Bajoran earring.

The episode opens with Major Kira being infuriated after Sisko and the rest of the crew retrieve Gul Dukat’s personnel files from the days of Cardassian rule, which describe Kira as a minor and insignificant operative—a calculated slight that cuts deep for a woman who fought in the Resistance. Kira is, on the other hand, given the high honour of hosting Kai Opaka, the Bajoran religious leader who has never left Bajor. Kai Opaka expresses a desire to inspect not only the wormhole but the area beyond—the Gamma Quadrant. Sisko grants her wish and boards her onto the *Yangtze-Kiang* runabout, where they are also accompanied by Dr. Bashir and Kira.

During their expedition, they stumble upon a signal and begin to investigate. It leads them to a moon with a network of satellites, one of which fires upon the *Yangtze-Kiang*, forcing it to crash-land on the moon. The moon has a habitable atmosphere, but Kai Opaka has died in the crash. Soon the survivors find themselves dealing with a group of locals called the Ennis, whose leader, Golin Shel-la (Jonathan Banks), explains that they are at war with a rival group called the Nol-ennis. The ensuing attack by the Nol-ennis leads to vicious hand-to-hand combat, which is interrupted by Kira’s use of a phaser. Kira is then amazed to find Kai Opaka alive, apparently resurrected, but also many Ennis killed in the battle.

As Chief O’Brien and Dax on Deep Space Nine begin to search for the missing runabout and slowly reconstruct its flight path and a way to make contact with the survivors, it turns out that the Ennis and Nol-ennis have been locked in endless warfare over an issue they have actually forgotten, and that the war continues because none of the participants can die. Dr. Bashir discovers that both factions were put on the moon as punishment, and that their immortality is the result of a special kind of local nano-robot-like microbes. Sisko tries to end the war through negotiations, but this fails. Just as contact with O’Brien and Dax is re-established, Kai Opaka—who has learned that the microbes will not work outside the moon, resulting in instant death if she leaves—volunteers to stay behind and help both factions reach a peace in a way Sisko failed to achieve.

The script, by Richard Danus and Evan Carlos Sommers, based on a story by Hilary Bader, posits an interesting scenario: two factions embroiled in an endless and pointless war that they cannot end because they have become so accustomed to it, and so consumed by hatred. In some ways, the premise is very much like the classic, albeit over-didactic, TOS episode [*Let That Be Your Last Battlefield*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-let-that-be-your-last-battlefield-star-trek-s3x15-1969), which featured the black-and-white Cheronians Lokai and Bele locked in a similarly futile conflict over the colour of their skin—one half white, one half black. Roddenberry’s heart was in the right place, but the message was delivered with all the subtlety of a sledgehammer. *Battle Lines* suffers from a similar didacticism, though it at least benefits from a more interesting setting and a less cartoonish depiction of its warring factions.

What saves this episode is decent direction by Paul Lynch, some great stunt work in the battle scenes, and Jonathan Banks, one of the most formidable character actors in the business—best known to modern audiences as Mike Ehrmantraut in *Breaking Bad*—playing one of the faction leaders with a weary, lived-in gravitas. Camille Saviola, who played Kai Opaka in the *DS9* premiere, is also very good, bringing dignity and gravitas to her character; her decision to stay on the moon is genuinely affecting.

On the other hand, Nana Visitor goes to absolute hamminess while conveying deep sorrow over the death of the Bajoran spiritual leader. Her overwrought performance in the crash-landing aftermath is one of the episode’s weaker elements, a rare misstep for an actress who usually handles Kira’s emotional range with more restraint.

The episode nevertheless works, and it ends just in time for the audience not to notice many of its flaws, such as the character of Dax being misused and, despite being the ship’s science officer, relying on Chief O’Brien to find solutions to the problems. It is a classic case of an episode that coasts on its premise and pacing rather than on the rigour of its character work.

In the end, *Battle Lines* is not essential viewing, and it is not particularly memorable in the grand pantheon of *Deep Space Nine* episodes. But it is nevertheless a solid piece of *DS9*—a competently executed, thematically earnest work of television that, while never reaching the heights of the series’ best, does not embarrass itself either. For fans of the franchise, it is a worthwhile, if unspectacular, entry in the early, still-finding-its-feet first season.


RATING: 6/10 (++)

body.title: Flautista con esperanza, una historia sobre Angie.
body.body:
Angie es una flautista que toca con tanta naturalidad que parece que nació con la flauta pegada a los labios, bueno, no pegada literalmente, pero da esa impresión por lo bien que toca. Es de esas personas que se levantan temprano, toman café y empiezan a preguntarse si ese día sucederá algo importante o, al menos, algo que las saque de la rutina. A pesar de su talento, cualquiera podría sorprenderse al conocer la verdad, nadie le enseñó a tocar la flauta, o al menos nadie lo hizo en persona. No estudió música ni tuvo profesor; todo lo que sabe sobre tocar la flauta lo ha aprendido de forma autodidacta.

Por lo general, le gusta leer mucho y, de vez en cuando, ve tutoriales en internet para mejorar su técnica. Así fue como aprendió a tocar. Sin embargo, a pesar de su gran habilidad, hasta la fecha no ha conseguido un trabajo importante ni ha alcanzado la fama.


![1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/andrewq/23wXG5xQxM4UsQJEFvymg64jBoZe3xaYjmeVYyged9CuFjU8fLsSRfspKq4HrBk3jKHaA.png)


Para mantenerse hasta ahora realiza grabaciones e interpretaciones de canciones famosas con la flauta y las sube a sus redes sociales. Sus seguidores le dan propinas y otros regalos simplemente por verla tocar,  así es como se ha sustentado hasta ahora. Pero últimamente ha notado que el número de visualizaciones y los ingresos han disminuido considerablemente. Empezó a revisar los comentarios en sus publicaciones para averiguar cuál era el problema, y lo que descubrió la dejó atónita. Muchos decían que era más de lo mismo, que no innovaba y que estaban cansados de ver siempre su habitación de fondo. En realidad, lo que le pedían era que se tomara el asunto más en serio y aportara más dinamismo a sus vídeos.

En ese momento, no sabía qué hacer, ya que carecía de los recursos necesarios para montar un estudio de grabación que permitiera utilizar diferentes planos. Además, no tenía dinero para contratar a un editor de vídeo que aprovechara bien la pantalla verde. Por lo general, ella misma hacía la edición, pero los cortes no eran muy buenos, por así decirlo. La gente se lo echaba en cara constantemente.

Angie la verdad descubrió que debía hacer algo para cambiar la dinámica de sus vídeos y de sus grabaciones de flauta. Así que empezó a buscar en internet alguna inspiración para mejorar los nuevos videos de su canal. En una de las publicaciones vio un desafío que los organizadores querían hacer viral. El reto consistía en tocar canciones populares en lugares inesperados y grabarlo todo para luego subir los videos. Ganaría quien consiguiera más visualizaciones, y el premio era, nada más y nada menos, que un millón de dólares. Angie vio esto como una oportunidad de oro, ya que si ganaba ese dinero podría mejorar considerablemente su estudio y, de ese modo, satisfacer los deseos de sus seguidores. Y, por supuesto, con el resto del dinero se daría algún que otro capricho.


![2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/andrewq/23vsavbiVFU9w2pzqEcpRxPKpVb3EEWawjxTM2dS4TcUvsXy5roi4bbX8PBLsnMzkm5Nx.png)


Así que contactó con los organizadores para inscribirse también. Los organizadores pertenecían a una agencia que buscaba promocionar los mejores lugares de la ciudad para hacerlos populares y virales entre los visitantes. De esta forma, más personas los conocerían antes de viajar al país y también querrían visitarlos. Le dijeron a Angie que revisarían sus videos para confirmar si realmente tenía suficientes seguidores para participar en el desafío y optar al millón de dólares. Al cabo de unos días le confirmaron que sí: podía participar con sus videos tocando la flauta. Angie se puso muy contenta, pues sabía que, si todo salía bien, se le abrirían nuevas oportunidades. El desafío comenzaba en una semana y duraría más de un mes. Había que grabar tres videos, y el que obtuviera más visualizaciones sería el ganador.

El reto arrancó en el mercado central de la ciudad, un lugar con gran afluencia de gente que vería cómo grababa y que, muy probablemente, buscaría luego los videos con la esperanza de verse de fondo. Para este primer video, se le ocurrió hacer una versión de una famosa canción. Que nunca antes se había interpretado a flauta. Sería la primera persona en interpretarla con la flauta, lo que seguramente atraería a algunos seguidores de esa cantante original, esto, sumado a la gente del mercado y a sus propios seguidores, sin duda le reportaría muchas visualizaciones. Y así fue, tuvo éxito. Esa semana, su video estuvo a punto de ser el más visto de todo el desafío, aunque otros concursantes acabaron superándola con algunos de los suyos. Sin embargo, no todo estaba perdido, ya que la semana siguiente habría otra oportunidad.
La segunda semana decidió correr un riesgo mayor. Optó por tocar en un vagón de metro durante la hora punta, momento en que había mucha gente yendo y viniendo. Esperó a que el vagón estuviera abarrotado para empezar a tocar. 

Esta vez eligió la canción Life, muy popular en su ciudad; sin embargo, no abundaban las interpretaciones de flauta, y menos aún en el metro. En cuanto empezó a tocar, observó las reacciones de los pasajeros, algunos se mostraron encantados y comentaron que verían el vídeo más tarde para ayudarla a sumar visualizaciones, mientras que otros la miraban como si estuviera interrumpiendo su meditación diaria de enfado con el mundo.

El vídeo obtuvo menos visitas que el anterior; ella pensó que perdería, pues el primer vídeo no había logrado ser el más visto quedó dos puestos por detrás y este iba aún más rezagado. Empezó a creer que ya no había nada que hacer, pero aún quedaba una oportunidad, ya que el reto constaba de tres vídeos. Así que no se rindió y decidió intentarlo una última vez.

<div class=\

> ![3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/andrewq/23s9Xz946SN7HTujDsSZcUrkaq9FNej1jNJVdMEjf8puigMPMuxrnmYWNBEponcohsMPT) Como solo quedaba una oportunidad, debía planificar cuidadosamente cómo realizar el vídeo. Por ello, contrató a un director para que le aportara ideas y pudiera aprovechar al máximo esta última ocasión. El productor le sugirió que lo ideal sería tocar la flauta en la planta superior de la torre más alta de la ciudad. Aquella parte aún no estaba terminada se encontraba en obras, pero la altura y el riesgo inherente podrían atraer la atención del público. También le aconsejó incorporar a artistas que escupieran fuego para hacer el vídeo más impactante. Y eso fue exactamente lo que hizo: con el poco dinero que le quedaba, contrató a escupidores de fuego, máquinas de pirotecnia y bailarines para que la acompañasen en lo alto de la torre. Este vídeo era crucial para ella, pues se lo jugaba todo a una carta, había invertido todo su dinero restante en la producción y, además, era la última oportunidad del desafío. Pero no iba a echarse atrás. Grabó el vídeo por la noche, contando con bailarines y artistas que escupían fuego, mientras ella interpretaba un tema de heavy metal con la flauta, acompañada por un guitarrista del mismo género. Para terminar, utilizó pirotecnia y fuegos artificiales. La gente que estaba al pie de la torre presenció el espectáculo, al igual que varias cadenas de televisión y periodistas. La noticia se difundió rápidamente y muchas personas comenzaron a comentar el video. ![fin.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/andrewq/23wX9zfKvqoLRFqp3dMuBpVJCPVk8xxQyaM7bZAn61fzNcxCDnrnuMrC6fNLovqNZhL4g.png) El resultado fue que el video se hizo viral casi de inmediato. Nadie podía creerlo, las visualizaciones aumentaban por miles cada hora. Fue el video más visto de todos los participantes del concurso juntos. Fue una locura, Angie por fin pudo respirar tranquila, pues sabía que el premio estaba asegurado. Todo fue gracias a la ayuda del director, al riesgo y la inversión que decidió asumir y, por supuesto, a sus seguidores. El día de la entrega de premios, obviamente obtuvo el primer puesto, lo que le valió el premio de un millón de dólares. Pero no solo ganó dinero, algunos empresarios de la zona quisieron contratarla para realizar videos publicitarios. Así, su futuro quedó asegurado, había ganado el desafío. Con ese dinero comenzará por fin a producir canciones propias y mucho más. ![1782828757355.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/andrewq/23wX1dJTpRTsaEEgtwDU97cU7gAtkCv7iR6Nwv9Ue1GvPkkjvKC5adkSMfedgJBTnZVrY.jpg)

body.title: Guild Brawls With Pizza 2 - Back To Perfection!
body.body:
<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23uFcH8GDdYWRsixYPTsvDPf9JmL6DpTYvChjYcXZmXabsdzQYzVvDcjqjtdZzdBqG3cQ.png)</center>

Time flies! Just completed the 281st brawl with my awesome guild, which is none other than Pizza 2 The Deep Dish!

***

- *Moving Back To Bronze Fray*

Had 4 battles this time and it was not an easy round, especially when they have recently introduced 3 rulesets for each battle. Moreover, I have rented out most of my cards because I was playing lesser these days.

- We Got 5th!!!

So for the final result, we were 5th out of 7 guilds and got 50 Merits and around 3 SPS! Good result?
<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23tkp4N8ye4u3gtGBjZwYuNRL88WveBAyQk9WmTHqRzcPr4YGunHwEUrG9GaAPmE9QSZz.png)</center>



Individually, I had 4 fights this time and I won all 4 of them this time! Finished 1st within the guild. Due to change in format, wins are actually awarded to the players present in the fray if guilds decided to skip the fray. For this round, there were 2 additional wins for me.
<center>![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23tRsvdBo3CtJZUcCg9ZZwjwzCZ6ksMT4Na3oDajPHrCUvj56WJECNEbYeaSrCPE7QvWS.png)</center>

***
**Battle 1 - WIN**

*Gladius Card Used: None*

My opponent used two Gladius cards but fortunately I had Silent Sha-vi with Sneak ability, and the Sneak hits made a great deal of difference to ensure that my team secure the win comfortably.

**MVP: Silent Sha-vi**



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23t797v3eRAPEBV3Z9sw6nK4Ca3L54SArCLanU3oqVhP4ronVwHyoEGfeJ3swS34CqRc4.png)




***
**Battle 2 - WIN**

*Gladius Card Used: None*

This battle could have easily turn out the other way, but fortunately Pelacor Deceiver had enough speed to fend off a Bloodlust boosted Chimney Wallstop in the opposing team. Close shave!

**MVP: Pelacor Deceiver**



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23t7BBxjNhBdTrdnZz2rGTm6FTC15J7NBV16irVpJChGNA4TpcPQ1K2fCCqtfv53rSPjG.png)











***
**Battle 3 - WIN**



*Gladius Card Used: Flagulon Reine*

Mindless Thrall is such a strong card in this one! High speed, and with Bloodlust, it was such a solid tank at the front and broke the stalemate in the early stages. Definitely a must have in one's card collection!

**MVP: Mindless Thrall**



![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/Eo22moFwC5hPEKKanpgokbBURKFcGWShNfQRgdt1YydLLeBexbPTQ6WCh5ETykFp4fH.png)



***
**Battle 4 - WIN**



*Gladius Card Used: Larissa Kerato*

Larissa Kerato is one of the few cards that has a good chance of overcoming Quora Towershead and this was the case in this battle. Very good showing, and credit to Delwyn Dragonscale for the boost across the team, as well as the Weapons Training ability from Skok Duskblight. Takes an entire village to win a Quora Towershead led lineup.

**MVP: Larissa Kerato**


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/relf87/23t7D8HzdCTXqRoGTaUUUmsGHwRk4P5fb4oxoNmf3cBxPkMs4apCXdHJuTvBe3QS9sLyg.png)


So that sums up my 4 battles for this brawl! 100% win rate this time, definitely a good result! Let's keep fighting PIZZA 2!

No new Gladius cards to review this time round.

body.title: (EN-ES-PT) Movie Review: Wild Target
body.body:
This post was translated from English into Spanish and Portuguese with Google Translate

(English)

Hello, dear members of the [Scrobble.life](http://Scrobble.life) community!

I've found this community after reading a relevant post made by @wiseagent.

So here is my review of this movie.

An attractive young woman is a prolific thief and works with an art forger to sell a fake work of art for a big amount of money.  
Unfortunately for her, the buyer of the fake painting finds out the truth and hires a top hitman to hunt and kill her.  
Through a series of fast action scenes, the roles change, and instead of killing her, the assassin is hired by the young woman to protect her.  
The movie has a happy ending, if you can call it that, as the hitman and the woman fall in love with each other, settle together, and have a child who, from a very young age, shows that he has taken after his parents.

**Characters**

**_Rose (Emily Blunt)_**

Rose is a dynamic young woman, to say the least.  
She can’t fit into the mold.  
She is restless and wild by nature, and definitely not your average female.  
In my mind, she resembles the adolescent crooked figures of the Oliver Twist novel who live a life of delinquency with no escape.  
The difference is the setting of modern London and the stakes that are higher, which also come with a higher risk for the thief to lose her life on the spot.

**_Victor Maynard (Bill Nighy)_**

Victor is an unbelievable character.  
He is a very traditional and conservative man who is also a professional assassin.  
How strange is that?  
He is hired to kill people without leaving a single trace after him, and he does his job so well that he is believed to be invisible.

**Themes**

**_Opening musical theme_**

The movie starts with an according playing a French tune, which makes you think that the movie will probably be a romantic comedy or something similar.

It’s in stark contrast with the movie’s main theme which is about the relationship that develops between a young female con artist and a middle-aged assassin.

**_A career-focused hitman_**

Victor Maynard is a hitman who puts his career above everything else.

It sounds funny how a criminal proves to be a better professional than other people who do ordinary jobs.

He leaves nothing to chance, because it’s human lives that are at stake.

This is how he has built his reputation as a third generation hitman who always accomplishes his mission at all costs.

He even learns French to be able to serve the French market!

He is so cold-blooded when he executes the victim that he has been paid to kill that makes you wonder if he takes a human life or plays a video game.

I don’t think that you would be able to tell that he is a paid killer if you happened to see him on the street.

He looks more like a corporate executive.

Thinking of it, in a dog-eat-dog world, unscrupulous businessmen who step on others to get ahead, and destroy other people’s careers and lives, as a result, are not very different from our hitman, Victor, in their methods and approaches to amassing wealth and reaching the pinnacle of personal success.

**_An austere mother like no other_**

Too much love can kill you.

I never expected to say this, but in the case of Victor’s mother, she is a living example of a strict mother who has killed her son’s personality, and indirectly killed her son’s victims, as she is the real instigator of the murders that her son has committed for money.

She has raised a professional killer, and she is proud of him.

I guess it has something to do with the screenwriter’s sense of black humor.

A paid killer’s instinct runs in the family.

Since he was a little boy, Victor was left with no choice but to become a trainee assassin himself, being given guns as gifts, and following the steps of his father, in order to continue the family business.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbmd6aMyS84

(Español)

¡Hola, queridos miembros de la comunidad [Scrobble.life](http://Scrobble.life)!

Encontré esta comunidad tras leer una publicación interesante de @wiseagent.

Aquí les dejo mi reseña de esta película.

Crítica de la película: Objetivo salvaje

Una atractiva joven es una ladrona consumada que trabaja con un falsificador de arte para vender una obra falsa por una gran suma de dinero.

Para su desgracia, el comprador del cuadro falso descubre la verdad y contrata a un sicario de primera para que la persiga y la mate.

Tras una serie de escenas de acción trepidantes, los papeles se invierten y, en lugar de matarla, la joven contrata al asesino para que la proteja.

La película tiene un final feliz, si es que se le puede llamar así, ya que el sicario y la mujer se enamoran, se establecen juntos y tienen un hijo que, desde muy pequeño, demuestra ser muy parecido a sus padres.

**Personajes**

**_Rose (Emily Blunt)_**

Rose es una joven dinámica, por decir lo menos.

No encaja en los moldes establecidos.

Es inquieta y rebelde por naturaleza, y definitivamente no es la típica mujer.

En mi opinión, se parece a los adolescentes rebeldes de la novela de Oliver Twist, que viven una vida de delincuencia sin escapatoria.  
La diferencia radica en la ambientación en el Londres moderno y en las mayores apuestas, que también conllevan un mayor riesgo de que la ladrona pierda la vida en el acto.

**_Victor Maynard (Bill Nighy)_**

Victor es un personaje increíble.

Es un hombre muy tradicional y conservador que, además, es un asesino profesional.

¿Qué extraño, verdad?

Lo contratan para matar gente sin dejar rastro, y hace su trabajo tan bien que se cree que es invisible.

**Temas**

**_Tema musical de apertura_**

La película comienza con un acordeón que interpreta una melodía francesa, lo que hace pensar que probablemente se trate de una comedia romántica o algo similar.

Esto contrasta fuertemente con el tema principal de la película, que trata sobre la relación que se desarrolla entre una joven estafadora y un asesino de mediana edad.

**_Un sicario centrado en su carrera_**

Victor Maynard es un sicario que antepone su carrera a todo lo demás.

Resulta curioso que un criminal demuestre ser mejor profesional que quienes realizan trabajos comunes.

No deja nada al azar, porque hay vidas humanas en juego.

Así se ha forjado su reputación como sicario de tercera generación, siempre cumpliendo su misión a cualquier precio.

¡Incluso aprende francés para atender al mercado francés!

Es tan frío al ejecutar a la víctima por la que le han pagado que uno se pregunta si está matando a alguien o jugando a un videojuego.

Si lo vieras por la calle, no te darías cuenta de que es un asesino a sueldo.

Tiene más bien el aspecto de un ejecutivo de empresa.

Pensándolo bien, en un mundo despiadado, los empresarios sin escrúpulos que pisotean a los demás para progresar, destruyendo carreras y vidas ajenas, no son muy diferentes de nuestro sicario, Victor, en sus métodos y estrategias para amasar fortuna y alcanzar la cima del éxito personal.

**_Una madre austera como ninguna otra_**

Demasiado amor puede matarte.

Nunca pensé que diría esto, pero en el caso de la madre de Victor, es un ejemplo vivo de una madre estricta que ha aniquilado la personalidad de su hijo y, de forma indirecta, ha matado a sus víctimas, ya que es la verdadera instigadora de los asesinatos que su hijo ha cometido por dinero.

Ha criado a un asesino a sueldo y está orgullosa de él.

Supongo que tiene algo que ver con el humor negro del guionista.

El instinto de asesino a sueldo es hereditario.

Desde pequeño, a Victor no le quedó más remedio que convertirse él mismo en un asesino en formación, recibiendo armas como regalo y siguiendo los pasos de su padre, para continuar con el negocio familiar.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sbmd6aMyS84

(Português)

Olá, queridos membros da comunidade [Scrobble.life](http://Scrobble.life) !

Encontrei esta comunidade depois de ler uma publicação relevante feita por @wiseagent.

Então, aqui está minha resenha deste filme.

Crítica de Cinema: Alvo Selvagem

Uma jovem atraente é uma ladra prolífica que trabalha com um falsificador de arte para vender uma obra de arte falsa por uma grande quantia em dinheiro.  
Infelizmente para ela, o comprador da pintura falsa descobre a verdade e contrata um assassino de aluguel para caçá-la e matá-la.  
Através de uma série de cenas de ação frenéticas, os papéis se invertem e, em vez de matá-la, o assassino é contratado pela jovem para protegê-la.  
O filme tem um final feliz, se é que podemos chamar assim, pois o assassino e a mulher se apaixonam, se estabelecem juntos e têm um filho que, desde muito jovem, demonstra ter herdado os traços dos pais.

**Personagens**

**_Rose (Emily Blunt)_**

Rose é uma jovem dinâmica, para dizer o mínimo.

Ela não se encaixa nos padrões.

Ela é inquieta e selvagem por natureza, e definitivamente não é uma mulher comum.

Na minha opinião, ela se assemelha às figuras adolescentes delinquentes do romance Oliver Twist, que vivem uma vida de delinquência sem escapatória.  
A diferença reside no cenário da Londres moderna e nas consequências mais graves, que também acarretam um risco maior de a ladra perder a vida instantaneamente.

**_Victor Maynard (Bill Nighy)_**

Victor é um personagem inacreditável.

Ele é um homem muito tradicional e conservador que também é um assassino profissional.

Que estranho, não é?

Ele é contratado para matar pessoas sem deixar nenhum rastro, e faz seu trabalho tão bem que é considerado invisível.

**Temas**

**_Tema musical de abertura_**

O filme começa com uma música francesa tocando ao fundo, o que leva a crer que se trata de uma comédia romântica ou algo do gênero.

Isso contrasta fortemente com o tema principal do filme, que gira em torno do relacionamento que se desenvolve entre uma jovem golpista e um assassino de meia-idade.

**_Um assassino de aluguel focado na carreira_**

Victor Maynard é um assassino de aluguel que coloca sua carreira acima de tudo.

Parece irônico como um criminoso se mostra um profissional melhor do que pessoas com empregos comuns.

Ele não deixa nada ao acaso, pois vidas humanas estão em jogo.

É assim que ele construiu sua reputação como um assassino de aluguel de terceira geração, que sempre cumpre sua missão a qualquer custo.

Ele até aprende francês para atender ao mercado francês!

Ele é tão frio e calculista ao executar a vítima que foi pago para matar que nos faz questionar se ele está tirando uma vida humana ou jogando videogame.

Não acho que você conseguiria dizer que ele é um assassino de aluguel se o visse na rua.

Ele parece mais um executivo de empresa.

Pensando bem, em um mundo onde a lei do mais forte impera, empresários inescrupulosos que passam por cima dos outros para se dar bem e, consequentemente, destroem carreiras e vidas alheias, não são muito diferentes do nosso assassino, Victor, em seus métodos e abordagens para acumular riqueza e alcançar o ápice do sucesso pessoal.

**_Uma mãe austera como nenhuma outra_**

Amor em excesso pode matar.

Nunca imaginei que diria isso, mas, no caso da mãe de Victor, ela é o exemplo vivo de uma mãe rígida que matou a personalidade do filho e, indiretamente, matou suas vítimas, já que ela é a verdadeira instigadora dos assassinatos que ele cometeu por dinheiro.

Ela criou um assassino profissional e se orgulha dele.

Acho que isso tem algo a ver com o senso de humor negro do roteirista. O instinto de assassino profissional corre nas veias da família.

Desde pequeno, Victor não teve escolha a não ser se tornar um assassino em treinamento, recebendo armas de presente e seguindo os passos do pai para dar continuidade aos negócios da família.

body.title: Tak mě nevzali na magistra
body.body:
Mělo to tak být,

některé skladby mám dobré, ale byla silná konkurence a je pravda, že já už na té škole nemám moc témat, které bych chtěl rozvíjet.

Víc vyrostu jinde, mám doučko z matiky a přihlásím se v zimě na matfyz.

Aspoň nebudu překážet Čoudelce, v nejhorším se na magistra můžu dostat za rok. Prý mám zkusit se přihlásit do nově akreditovaného kurzu celoživotního vzdělávání, kde bych se mohl věnovat jen tvorbě.

A mohl bych mít hodiny asi s Lubošem, eventuálně se domluvit s dalšími učiteli.

Tedy značka ideál, nechápal jsem většinou, co se na jiných předmětech děje, teď můžu chodit jen na hodiny a věnovat se třeba té matice.

Jen obhájit bakalářku, snad se to zadaří.

Jako matematik budu v tvorbě dál, snad se naučít procesy, které používám částečně zprogramovat, snad se naučím nové koncepty a tvary, které mi budou v hudbě pomáhat.

Ale mrzí mě to, hlavně nevím, proč mě nevzali, udělal jsem pár bot s kdysi s Duškem a později s Opl. a mohl jsem je naštvat, do toho mám každej rok minimálně jednu dvě hospitalizace a tak se studuje blbě...

Jestli se jim zároveň dostal do ruky ten dokument s mými strachy, tak jsem je mohl vylekat, vyvolat odpor.

Možná to mám brát tak, že prostě pro jiné je ta škola užitečnější a já bych si z ní tolik neodnesl.

Je hezké, že jsem uspěl v Generaci, je hezké, že rozvíjím své světy, jen ten studijní program by mi stejně nesedl.

Zkusím ten kurz...

Chjo.

H.

body.body:
Recently, I joined the Singapore Recreation Club (SRC) Pickleball Section for a friendly match against Warren Golf & Country Club. We had a fantastic time playing some really fun games. I took country club shuttle bus from Choa Chu Kang. It was a comfortable little bus that brought us straight to their main building.
最近，我跟随新加坡康乐俱乐部（SRC）匹克球组，前往华伦高尔夫乡村俱乐部进行了一场友谊赛。我们玩得很开心，打了几场非常精彩的比赛。我在蔡厝港搭乘俱乐部的接驳巴士。这是一辆挺舒适的小巴士，直接把我们载到了俱乐部的主楼。

>

🎶Meanwhile, some music for you to enjoy as you read. This piece is part of Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons, particularly the first of the 4 violin concertos, called Spring.
🎶让大家继续读的时候，欣赏一点音乐。这件作品是维瓦尔第的“四季”的一部分 - 4小提琴协奏曲中的第一首，名为“春天”。

在车上往外看，可以看到非常漂亮、绿意盎然的高尔夫球场和沙坑。

>

\nSoon, we arrived at the grand entrance of the Warren Golf & Country Club.
很快，我们就到达了华伦高尔夫乡村俱乐部大堂的宏伟入口。

>

\nWalking inside, we passed through a long corridor. I noticed the lovely sports-themed drawings on the wall on the right, which added a lively vibe.
走进里面，我们经过了一条长长的走廊。我注意到右侧墙壁上画着可爱的运动主题壁画，增添了不少活力。

>

\nOn the way to the courts, I also caught a glimpse of their large, sparkling blue outdoor swimming pool. It looked so refreshing under the afternoon sun.
在前往球场的路上，我还看到了他们宽敞透亮的室外游泳池。在下午的阳光下，看起来特别清凉。

He sentido la pausa

de un nuevo amanecer,

y clamado los besos

y sueños de placer.

Ignorando las grietas

que me han dejado,

por sentir la locura

de un amor hurtado.

Y con la tristeza

del vacío infinito,

he sentido tus besos

este domingo triste.

I have felt the pause

of a new dawn,

and craved the kisses

and dreams of pleasure.

Ignoring the cracks

that have been left in me,

for feeling the madness

of a stolen love.

And with the sadness

of the infinite void,

I have felt your kisses

this sad Sunday.

body.title: How Saylor Can Make Strategy Great Again
body.body:
![ea147683 ffdb 499f 81d5 4e51acea899e](https://img.leopedia.io/DQmXnv6ZLXqKQLFPQBMBzoiQdDLETkB91KSG5pHf5MU43AQ/ea147683-ffdb-499f-81d5-4e51acea899e.png)

Yield is at the heart of finance. It is literally everywhere you look. Michael Saylor’s Strategy is in a world of hurt right now from a perception standpoint. They have a roughly $1.7B per year debt obligation from their preferred shares, and they seemingly have no way to pay it over the long term.

This is the issue they’re facing now, and why everyone calls it a Ponzi scheme: if they can’t raise new capital, they won’t have the money to pay dividends.

The fix is actually incredibly simple and obvious. In my opinion, there’s a two-fold *strategy* here that would completely turn around the company and make it a behemoth in finance that would make BlackRock shake in its boots.

**The two-part strategy is simple:**
1. **Make their BTC productive**: Start earning yield on the $50 billion worth of Bitcoin they already own.
2. **Build FinTech products for BTC:** Use the incredible brand leverage they have to build simple BTC financial products that generate real revenue.

Let’s dive in.

## Make BTC Productive Again

Strategy owns 847,363 BTC. It is currently worth $50 billion.

That’s not a small amount of money.

If this BTC were deployed and earning 5% yield, it would generate $2.5B per year in annual yield for the company.

The current yield obligations of Strategy are about $1.7B. The yield generated solely from using the BTC they already own would cover **100%** of their yield obligations, operational overhead, and it would leave extra cash leftover to buy more Bitcoin and accretively grow **MSTR shareholder** Bitcoin per share (BPS), which Saylor has talked about so much in the past.

Warren Buffett would never do what Saylor is doing. But if he did, he would absolutely be generating yield on it.

That is a no-brainer. If you have the capability of safely generating yield, then you should take advantage of it.

This leads us to the real issue with this strategy: you *can’t* be 100% positive that there is zero risk in leveraging your BTC to earn yield. There is always going to be some degree of custodial risk.

That being said, there are **many options** to deploy BTC and earn yield.

Saylor used ChatGPT to build STRC. He can use ChatGPT to build a risk/reward model for deploying his $50B worth of BTC as safely as possible, ensuring there isn’t blow-up risk.

This would likely involve deploying some material % of the BTC — not all of it — plus buying insurance on the deployed capital (yes, you can do this), and spreading it around to multiple CeFi and DeFi protocols that don’t have contagion risk.

The great news: Saylor can chase mild yields. 3% per year. 4% per year. 5% per year.

Lower yields will likely indicate safer, more saturated protocols. Coinbase has yield products, Binance has them, Aave has them.

There are hundreds of options for BTC yield products these days.

This is **not to mention** that he can also go out and privately lend BTC for yield. Imagine he goes to companies like BlackRock and other institutions/ETF managers and lends BTC at attractive 3–5% rates.

Mix all of these together, slap some insurance on it, and you have a 3–5% yield machine on a $50B balance sheet. It solves Strategy’s debt crisis overnight.

## Make FinTech Products

Once you’ve established a great model and implemented it for yield, start building real FinTech products around Bitcoin.

Strategy and Saylor have a now-infamous brand in the world of Bitcoin. They can build and service incredibly simple financial tools and services for their Bitcoin audience.

These tools can generate additional revenue for the company. This won’t be billions of dollars, **however**; it would likely be enough to more than cover core operations and overhead.

This is a game of perception. When it comes to growing Strategy, perception is truly the key.

If Strategy can say, “We are a profitable company” in terms of building products and services that generate more revenue than they spend, this would change the entire perception of Strategy.

Setting aside dividend obligations, of course. But those are already covered through the yield generated on their BTC stack.

To sum this all up:
1. Get the $50B Bitcoin productive **today**
2. Build out a team to make simple but effective FinTech products leveraging the Strategy brand to generate additional profits

The immediate effect will be a recovery of STRC, MSTR equity and general market perception.

From there, they can use both profit + additional ATM sales to buy even more BTC and continue scaling. The scaling will be even more effective during a bear market when BTC is cheap.

body.title: From Preseason To The Future, Where WOO Is Really Headed
body.body:
A Big Hello to all WOO Fans! 🥳🥳🥳 WOO! 

Every time a major system update drops in a game like WOO, there are two ways to look at it. You can look at what is happening right now. Or you can try to understand where it is all leading. The Summer Circuit, the shift to weekly events, the Battle Pass structure, land utility improvements, and the upcoming ranked system all point in a very specific direction.

WOO is not just adding features. It is building a long term competitive ecosystem.

---

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/blitzzzz/23tRzfXZYmFBVCcfdXC2HEBnrVdZvUAaErPZmqrxK4K7Z6wWFXB8dZbKwjioZoQm13Kzo.png)

---

## 🏗️ The Summer Circuit Is A Prototype

• June is not just content, it is testing.

The Summer Circuit feels like an experiment in structure. How do players respond to weekly cycles? How do reward types influence participation? How does engagement change over short bursts instead of long stretches? These are the kinds of questions this format helps answer.

• Feedback loops are being created in real time.

Each week provides data. Each event provides insight. Each participation pattern reveals behaviour. That information likely feeds into future design decisions.

• Preseason framing is intentional.

Calling June a preseason is important. It signals that this is not the final form of the system. It is the beginning of refinement.

## 🏆 The Long Term Vision Is Becoming Clearer

• Battle Pass creates structured progression.

It gives players a consistent framework for advancement.

• Weekly events create consistent engagement.

They keep players active between larger milestones.

• Ranked play introduces competitive identity.

It gives players a long term goal beyond rewards.

• Land systems build economic depth.

They anchor the ecosystem with utility and ownership. When you step back, these systems are not random. They are interconnected layers. Each one supports a different aspect of player motivation.

## 🌍 WOO Is Moving Toward A Full Ecosystem Model

• Games evolve from features to systems.

Early stage games often feel fragmented. Later stage games begin connecting those fragments. WOO appears to be moving into that second phase.

• Player activity becomes multi layered.

Instead of engaging with one system at a time, players interact with multiple overlapping systems. Battle Pass progression. Weekly event participation. Asset ownership through land. Future ranked competition. That overlap increases depth.

• Retention improves through structure.

When systems reinforce each other, players have multiple reasons to return. That reduces reliance on any single feature.

## 🔥 Why Weekly Events Matter More Than They Seem

At first glance, weekly events might look like a simple scheduling change. But in the bigger picture, they serve a very important function.

• They connect all systems together.

Events sit between Battle Pass progression and ranked competition. They act as the active layer of engagement.

• They create pacing for the game.

Without pacing, systems feel static. Weekly cycles introduce movement.

• They give the ecosystem a heartbeat.

Every week brings activity. That rhythm keeps the game feeling alive.

## 🎭 The Importance Of Foundation Building

One thing I have learned from watching games evolve over time is that the most important updates are not always the most exciting ones. Sometimes the most important updates are structural. They define how everything else will function later. The Summer Circuit feels like one of those updates. It is not just about rewards. It is about structure. And structure is what everything else depends on.

## 💭 My Personal Thoughts

What stands out to me most is that WOO is not rushing. Instead of adding everything at once, it feels like systems are being introduced step by step. Battle Pass first. Land improvements next. Events restructuring now. Ranked play coming soon.

That kind of pacing suggests intention. It suggests a roadmap rather than isolated decisions. As a fan, that is what gives me confidence in the direction of the game.

## 🎤 Final Thoughts

The Summer Circuit may be branded as a June preseason, but in reality it feels like something more important. It feels like the foundation of WOO’s next stage of growth. Weekly events create rhythm. The Battle Pass creates structure. Land creates depth. Ranked play will create competition. Together, these systems form the outline of a complete ecosystem.

We are no longer just looking at individual updates. We are looking at a connected framework being built piece by piece. And if this is only the preseason, then the real season ahead could be something very interesting indeed.

---

Well, that's it for today. We will continue again tomorrow! 😁 WOO! 🎉

body.title: Privacy vs Public Recording: Where Should the Law Draw the Line?
body.body:
We have the right to privacy and also have the right/ freedom to record in public spaces. These are two significant rights. It's quite difficult to balance both, because the law doesn't prohibit public videos, it only becomes an issue when the intention is to ridicule, embarrass or mock a person. It's quite funny that people expect to be private in public places. This can be compared to attending a seminar or program and intending to sue them for making a video of your face in their program. I believe if you really want to stay private, then you can avoid visiting certain places. Asking for privacy in a public space is almost impossible. |
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWV3VjA13uDpCdN9q75mA6LYTR2qGmpPAi1n6MeqmQQ4t/1782815114728.jpg)
***Image is generated with Gemini Ai***| |-------| There's a very low expectation of privacy in a place full of people, especially in this time and age when everyone wants to take a picture or keep documentaries of their life for content. If finding yourself in a strangers video should be treated as a criminal offense, then it should be based on the person's intentions, not because you appeared in their pictures or videos accidentally. I understand no one loves or wants their face to appear in a strangers pictures or video online without their consent. I also don't like it, but if it wasn't captured to mock, defame my reputation or even embarrass me, I can't treat it as a criminal offense. We can all agree that these public videos capture authentic moments most times, help with different documentation, like events, accidents, crimes and many others. |
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXW5Nt6tvysiXKDWxxTi3UUsvSbVsHbLKjhUiS1LffUCo/1782815135590.png)
***Image is generated with ChatGPT***| |-------| Noone steps into a public place and expects to be private, there's visibility in the public, people get to see you, observe you, and when seen overtime they have a memory of what you look like in their head. In this time, if you choose to be private, then you just have to make up your mind to stay indoors, because there's also CCTV cameras capturing. The fear isn't just for content creators, we also have tourists around to capture memorable moments, film makers looking for originality in every video and pictures they capture and the journalists reporting events. It's almost impossible to stay private. The only way to stay private might be to stay indoors for the longest, and you have the right to do that too. I also understand how people feel about their videos being on the Internet with millions of views and most times the public might see a reason to just make you a topic of discussion, bring up false assumptions, create a trend with your look or even use your facial expressions as stickers. It's something I wouldn't like to happen to me and I understand how others feel about this too. I see these a lot, but I can't totally blame the creator either, because they were just doing their things and you came around unknowingly to them. Unwanted exposure on the Internet really hurts, considering how people drop different opinions about others to ridicule them. |
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmedFeEwuXVQXdzq7M7FuHB3eENRj7wrr7dNCUcZ9JG8tr/1782815152235.png)
***Image is generated with ChatGPT***| |-------| The law should be against those who do it deliberately, with the intention of mocking, harassing and damaging a person, because I can understand appearing accidentally, but when it's deliberately done to mock a person, they should face the law. To me, that's a harmful use of people's image and defamation. Nobody will be happy with that, and they have the right to seek for justice and sue the offender. This gives room to cyberbullying, defaming their character, an invasion of their privacy and a content created to humiliate them. To protect our rights to privacy and freedom, a fair point would be that people should be allowed to make their videos in public places, but should face consequences if they record others with the intention of harming them, damaging their reputation , exposing them to Cyberbullying and other mischievous experience that would affect them emotionally and mentally. While exercising your creative freedom, it's necessary to also respect other people's privacy and make your videos responsibly.
### Thanks for reading ♥️ ### Vanilla 💗

body.title: No one talks about how severe Money depression is.
body.body:
![299718.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/23vsfaVTSLhouaHPXsFPwijbynBZjwVBXFkHd88Tr2UZrycUPcjYKBBLhmQQoqFJty1Eo.png)


<hr>


A lot of people are more depressed than they realize, but because we picture depression as a state of pain or evil, we tend to see it as a zone that is meant for some type of people in the society.

 Being excessively conscious about life, being deeply aware, thinking about things that the average people don't, looking at life from a realistic rather than position point of view is a mild form of depression, that can actually graduate to something more severe. 

Being aware is a proof of our consciousness, without that we can't think, deduce, reason or even come to any form of conclusions. 

Without our consciousness we're nothing, sometimes people don't even pay deep attention to their consciousness, they're just living, breathing, working attending parties and functions without stopping to self reflect, indulge in women deep thinking and understand their realites differently.  

The only time people do this is when they're stopped in their track by some tragic events in life, and they begin to think deeper. 



### Deep thinking & depression 

A lot of deep thinkers are depressed, because they're applying or using their highest form of self awareness, applying it generally to life, but depression is always likened to a state of mental disorder and this is why people would rather not admit they're depressed, because of the stigma, stereotype and label that's attached to it. While in reality, depression is just a phase of sadness, only that it this time you're in that state of sadness for longer periods of time. 


When people are broke for long, they're depressed, a person chronically sick is the same, and even someone who suffering the loss of a loved one. Pain varies in degree, and while people are expected to be sad today but already happy by tomorrow, reality is quite different. 


A person can be sad for 90% of their lives more than they can be 90% happy all their lives, and this possible when people begin to think critically or deeply. In my opinion the reason why we have some nabr drinking houses and party center is because these places helps people ro escape deep thinking.


 This is why a substance like alcohol *(when taken in abundance)* numbs the brain. It takes you away from a place of intentional things, you're unaware, living in a state of nothingness, feeling nothing but heaviness and a little sense of goodness.

 Even without alcohol, most people who are regular lifers, vacationists or those setting out to simply enjoy their lives are always happy, and you will be surprised that some of these people may have money and other good things of life but they're still depressed or unhappy. 


This is why businesses that are built to please people are psychological more than regular. A person eats to stay alive, so a restaurant is not one of such places, but a drinking place is one of such. This is why places of pressures has been in existence since the 15th century in different continents. These business are tailored to make people shallow thinkers even if it's for a brief period of time. 


Although we don't originally need people to be happy when doing their jobs or being mentally alert, overly or excessively happy people can still perform optimally, but chronically sad people cannot. This is why man designed more places to make himself happy and less aware. 

This is reality because, when people are unhappy they generally don't do the thing they love doing, they're withdrawn and are thinking deeply, these thoughts occupies their mind so much that they begin to lose focus, their mind is not as sharp, they cannot do their jobs properly, they're always lost in thoughts so much that they cannot have proper conversations anymore. 

### The money depression

Nowadays I can say the thing that makes people more depressed in this modern era is not having money. This is because the 21st century is tailored or optimized to be money driven. 

In the 15 or 16th century it could be different things entirely and this will be equally different as the 10th century. I'm not saying depressed people can't be rich, of course, chronic depression that might not be clinically spelled might come from so many things, but imagine feeling pressure and ache from having no money no matter how hard you've tried. 


Broke people are the most self aware, because they're constantly plugged in to the depth of their self awareness. If you're someone who thinks deeply, maybe more than anyone on their circle, then you might be depressed and you don't even know it.

body.title: The magic of fog
body.body:
Another great subject for the @Qurator photo quest: FOG Although I'm not a morning person, I do like the scenes that can appear on an early morning when it's foggy. On my cycling route to work the cycling path I take passes through some meadows. In between the meadows are some ditches. On cold mornings the moist in the air can create a blanket of fog over the meadows. A while ago, when I was cycling to work it almost seemed like the power pylons were hovering above the ground. I really liked the cold, blueish tint of the sky which in the back was slowly coloring orange by the sunset. It resulted in a bit of a mystical atmosphere.
This is my photo for the Qurator Photo Quest ![pillars](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/AL1dTcwYXdQgtkNBWdpEz4bZm2T9BAh25hzA2vWNrfehxLP6tpZhFxgRKeFBzYX.png) The next photo was taken during a cold and misty winter morning. The mist was above the trees around the lake. I really liked the reflection of the tree in the water. Although there wasn't a lot of color, I did turn this one into black and white. ![kaag](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/242DLNQunUeWRctdoNnoVWb4DvddyA9191MxzKUm1J16KbjrfWnpxGubQw8M5Nn2iXmRe.png) You might recognize the following shot because it is my profile picture. I really like this shot because of the emptiness and the fact that the fog resulted in the disappearance of the horizon. ![banner-image](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/friendlymoose/2458QtTctnLhEkMybvoQJ6oDBZ1xsVm6V4bNdvUoRJTLv79RLbMs8fJeY5ovbFEi9cEGe.png) Here is another early morning shot I took while commuting. body.body:
by @ericdubay on Eric Dubay 
View my bio on Vigilante.TV: https://vigilante.tv/c/eric.dubay [![Predators Don't Regulate Prey](https://vigilante.tv/lazy-static/previews/87b0ffb6-d805-42ff-88b5-dd0459f3003f.jpg)](https://vigilante.tv/w/uLFTsF8fXnJZ9DTGYLoj24) 
 
 When pressed on the question of why the world must have such a predatory food chain of life feeding upon life, both theists and atheists alike, tend to claim that the reason is because predators serve the function of regulating the numbers of their prey, preventing them from becoming over-populated, and this is their purpose.  This belief that predators regulate prey is nearly ubiquitous and unquestioned by both ecologists and lay people.  If an animal has become a pest or is found proliferating in a new environment, the immediate assumed response is that this is because its natural enemies are absent or that it has somehow escaped from being regulated by its various predators.  The idea has been repeated so often and for so long that most assume it to be a settled scientific fact of nature.  The reality is however, that the evidence from a wide range of studies conclude that predators in fact have little to no effect on the overall population of their prey...

body.title: Is Voting A Crime?
body.body:
![1000029391.png](https://rpc.blurt.blog/m/775d42a994623e5aa185d1fd881fd5fe)


The core question in this essay was inspired many years ago through a lecture from Eric WhoRU Williams. The argument presented here as follows, however, is my own exploration of where that question has lead me.

## Defining The Terms



Before I take a deep dive into this lecture, I need to make it explicitly clear that this has nothing to do with what is legal or illegal. For all who know me enough, throughout my years of essays, I have never used legalities as a foundation, and likewise this essay is not going to rely on it.

When I use the word ***criminal*** I do not mean it in the legalese sense in any way shape or form, but in the moral and ethical sense. Someone who bears responsibility for empowering or participating in acts that would otherwise be considered crimes. These crimes are those actions of which cause harm to a victim's reputation, such as defamation, or direct violence ,to their own person or theft of property and through scamming them. 

Again, **Crimes**, as I use the term, are actions that violate another person's life, liberty, property, or reputation through force, fraud, coercion, or deception.

When one hires a hitman to do harm to their neighbors, the hitman is not the only one who is acting in criminal behavior, but also the one who did the hiring. Ordering a thief to do the dirty work for you doesn't negate you from the deed itself. You are as equally guilty of criminal behavior if you do. Hiring a proxy to commit criminal acts does not absolve you of responsibility for those acts.

In shorter words, delegating violence doesn't erase accountability.

The central claim of this essay is that voting for a master to rule over others is itself a criminal act. This isn't because it is illegal, nor is it about voting being legal, but because casting a vote \

(empowers, appoints, or delegates) another person to commit acts that would be considered criminal if you carried them out yourself. 

## The Ballot as Delegation

If we could agree that hiring a hitman does not absolve the one who hired him from accountability, nor from ordering a thief to coming theft absolve the one who gave the order, then we must ask whether that same principle applies to political elections. What, after all, is a vote?

A vote is often described as \

, but it is actually an attempt to select which individual or group of individuals will exercise coercive power over everyone else. The names, uniforms, and procedures may differ from location to location but the principles remain the same. The underlying question remains the same also, does casting a ballot change the moral nature of delegating coercion?\n\nLet's consider what \

actually do. If private individuals use coercion as violence to tax, imprison, enforce regulations, wage war, confiscate property, etc. would the private individual be commiting acts of crime? Would you see them as criminals of they did? Is it a crime for private people to do what government does to the masses every single day?

If these acts would be crimes when committed privately, why would selecting the person who carries them out absolve the selector of moral responsibility? 

## \

At first glance, this seems like a reasonable defense. After all, if your intentions were peaceful, how could you possibly be held morally responsible for everything a politician later does?

The problem, of course, with this objection is that it confuses motive with accountability. 

Imagine hiring someone knowing that, as part of the job, they will periodically rob your neighbors. You may have hired them because they were an excellent accountant, mechanic, or builder, but if you knowingly empowered them despite their predictable acts of aggression,  your accountability is not erased regardless of motivation.

Likewise, when someone votes for a political candidate, they are not only selecting a single policy in isolation, but selecting an office that comes with the power to tax, regulate, imprison, confiscate property, wage war, and enforce countless decrees through the threat or use of violence. Whether the voter personally approves of every one of those actions is beside the point. The office itself is inseparable from those powers.

Voting is therefore not merely an endorsement of preferred policies, but the selection of who will wield coercive power over everyone else. If you knowingly place someone into a position whose very function depends upon the use of coercion, can you completely separate yourself from the coercion that predictably follows?

Suppose I have no moral right to rule (authority) to therefore tax my neighbor, imprison him for refusing to pay me, regulate his peaceful behavior, or conscript him into war. If I possess none of those rights myself, by what process do I acquire the ability to delegate them to someone else?

Delegation transfers a power that already exists. It cannot magically create a moral right that never existed in the first place. 

If I cannot rightfully appoint a hitman to murder my neighbor because I possess no such right myself, why should voting enable me to appoint a politician to perform acts I could never morally perform?

Where did the supposed moral right to delegate aggression come from in the first place?

The answer is that no such process exists. Voting cannot create a moral right that no individual possessed beforehand. If an act is wrong for one person to perform, placing that same act behind a ballot box or an elected office does not transform it into something morally permissible. Delegation cannot create what did not previously exist.

## “Consent of the Governed”

Another common objection is the idea that political authority is legitimate because it rests on the “consent of the governed.” 

At first glance, this sounds like a moral escape hatch. If people consent to being governed, then whatever follows from that governance is presumably justified. But this raises a more basic question. What does consent actually mean in this context?

Consent is not a symbolic gesture. It is not participation in a ritual, nor is it the mere existence of a voting mechanism. Consent, in any meaningful moral sense, requires a clear, informed, and voluntary agreement between identifiable parties, with the ability to refuse without coercion. 

Now compare that standard to political systems.

Refusal to “consent” to being governed does not exempt any person from taxation, imprisonment, regulation, or violence enforced through law. The consequences of non-participation are not neutral. They are enforced regardless of individual approval.

If a relationship continues to impose consequences on a person regardless of their refusal, then calling that relationship “consensual” becomes a category error. It replaces actual consent with presumed consent. In short, if it is consensual, then it is voluntary, and if it must be governed(coerced with threats of violence) then it's not consensual. 

Voting is often presented as evidence of consent. But participation in a system is not the same as agreeing to its terms. Being placed inside a structure and then given limited input into its operators is not equivalent to consenting to the structure itself. 

By comparison, imagine being told you consent to a contract simply because you were given the ability to choose which manager enforces it, while never being allowed to opt out of the contract itself. In that case, selection is not consent, but a constrained participation inside an imposed framework.

Thus, “consent of the governed” does not at all function as consent in the moral sense being claimed. At best, it describes participation within an unavoidable system, that is not voluntary agreement in any fashion shape or form to its legitimacy. And if consent is not actually present in the relevant sense, then it cannot be used as a moral justification for coercion.

In shorter words, there is no such thing as \

, because if you are governed then there is no consent.

If voting merely selected policies, this essay would fail. But voting selects rulers. Those rulers exercise powers that would be considered criminal if exercised by private individuals. Delegating those acts does not erase accountability, nor can voting create a moral right that no individual possessed beforehand. 

Finally, appeals to the \

fail because genuine consent cannot exist where refusal is met with coercion. If these premises are true, then the conclusion follows naturally. Voting is not morally neutral. It is an act by which one attempts to empower another to rule over others through coercion.

 Whether one accepts or rejects that conclusion is less important than whether one can identify where the reasoning itself fails. If the premises stand, then so too does the conclusion.




***
***
***

body.title: Visiting the Rafael Urdaneta Centre on the outskirts of the city. | Visita al Centro Rafael Urdaneta, en las afueras de la ciudad.
body.body:
> **Gratos saludos tengan todos mis queridos amigos de esta linda comunidad de Lifestyle este martes es un placer para mí saludarles.** >**A warm greeting to all my dear friends in this lovely Lifestyle community; it’s a pleasure for me to say hello to you all this Tuesday.** El centro Rafael Urdaneta, o mejor conocido como el museo de arte centenario en Maracaibo, es un lugar y que busca recordar almacenar cada uno de los recuerdos de aquellos fragmentos que han sido históricos en nuestra localidad, una manera de recordar, los tiempos pasados de nuestra ciudad, este espacio recientemente restaurado para todos y totalmente abierto al público, ya que había tenido muchos años totalmente cerrado en esta oportunidad, vamos a describir su fachada externa que, sin duda, alguna es completamente fascinante nos ofrece un contraste único a nuestros ojos a través del diseño y arquitectura que posee. >The Rafael Urdaneta Centre, better known as the Centenary Art Museum in Maracaibo, is a place that seeks to preserve every memory of the historical moments in our town a way of remembering our city’s past. This space has recently been restored for everyone and is now fully open to the public, having been completely closed for many years. Here, we will describe its exterior façade, which is undoubtedly utterly fascinating, offering a unique visual contrast through its design and architecture. ![Collage de fotos horizontal Feliz San Valentín Creativo Multicolor_20260630_095412_0000.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcRVujh9Fnz9XqGST16wTgqDPsHvUnZVQfmTJJZVgnPWg/Collage%20de%20fotos%20horizontal%20Feliz%20San%20Valent%C3%ADn%20Creativo%20Multicolor_20260630_095412_0000.png) ![20260619_105552.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfXRAzECYX5f3wt4sReLSfe9VwJYMZ1LZ1BYWq96EmwCv/20260619_105552.jpg) ![20260619_105607.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ6CrELzd4om6Zn5wby7oyxqnMfEmFFsZvw3qBwXkFNA1/20260619_105607.jpg) --- En su facha de externo, podemos observar y que existen un sin fín de ventanas estrechas alargadas de madera con rejillas, que dan un toque único, su arquitectura es netamente clásica colonial característica de las cazonas de antaño de la ciudad de Maracaibo, al ser un museo que se encuentra justamente distribuido en una parte de la calle Carabobo, en donde se encuentran las casas más antiguas de la ciudad, es notable su característica en la vivienda, que es bastante antigua y un reflejo de lo clásico. >On its exterior façade, we can see that there are countless narrow, elongated wooden windows with grilles, which lend it a unique touch; its architecture is distinctly classical colonial in style, characteristic of the old mansions of Maracaibo. As a museum, it is situated on a section of Carabobo Street where the city’s oldest houses are found, the building’s distinctive character is striking; it is quite old and a reflection of classical style. ![20260619_105615.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZvNxjs5acfQgmrx3ESgLXcCRUPGPhRkfTZEosVtZ1mCy/20260619_105615.jpg) ![20260619_105617.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUC7vGF2rKfG3dLaL5pqj9Qoxrroxm37vzzbk3SubofSR/20260619_105617.jpg) ![20260619_112053.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNpH3TAUCUzBC584jojE44raAP9CYqaD28tZkvLzCQvvZ/20260619_112053.jpg) ![20260619_112107.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRMcTeKRtyKHyWqdcDxDyfdKeis4cj4owUk7QLxga6qCS/20260619_112107.jpg) --- Podemos ver que de un lado se encuentran distribuidas muchas ventanas estas le dan el toque fantástico, la arquitectura clásica que posee el museo qué lo hace importante, no solamente los elementos que pueda tener de gran valor histórico en su interior, sino también cada una de las partes que posee su fachada que a la vez de hacer clásica suele ser bastante imponente, así como también su pequeño, póntico que tiene sobresaliendo a su puerta en las alturas, qué es un balcón que permite la visibilidad a toda la calle, estará un toque fantástico a esa arquitectura, afectan impresionante que tiene. >We can see that there are many windows on one side; these lend a fantastic touch to the museum’s classical architecture, which is what makes it so significant, not only the elements of great historical value inside, but also every part of its façade, which, whilst classic in style, is also quite imposing. The small, projecting balcony above the entrance, which offers a view of the entire street, adds a fantastic touch to the architecture and enhances its impressive appearance. ![20260619_112125.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYGX6pqrbPyG4HLnnSwtcF3JbjJXmJRNeZhcyqDznsYXE/20260619_112125.jpg) ![20260619_112136.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQy7kXnzttGGya3jUuApaVMkj7b63NCoVB24suBwZi5YV/20260619_112136.jpg) ![20260619_112206.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUiN6MGTJMUSfJRKrpJNSDBx7Sdqu2YGG2N9HU1XjwPTm/20260619_112206.jpg) ![20260619_112252.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSAg1boxC5AALXVXLNLtZiKpoZBWy5smSCMfchmWd7D8d/20260619_112252.jpg) --- Este espacio funciona abierto todos los días en 3 semanas de 9:00 de la mañana a 2:00 de la tarde, ahí se encuentra todo el personal trabajando para darte recorridos guiados y para intruirte acerca de cada uno de sus espacios, este lugar fue fundado justamente en el año 1987, es grandioso ver que hemos recuperado recientemente un museo para que podamos tener más espacios como estos que como podrán darse cuenta, los museos son bastantes escasos en la ciudad de Maracaibo son contados con las manos pero esta calle de Caraobo, aparte de su gran cultura tradición y arte ofrece muchas historias, pues podemos ver qué tiene dos museos en su distribución como lo es el museo de obispo Lasso de la Vega y el museo de arte centenaria o centro de Rafael Urdaneta. >This venue is open every day for three weeks from 9.00 am to 2.00 pm, where the staff are on hand to offer guided tours and tell you about each of its areas. The venue was founded in 1987; it’s wonderful to see that we’ve recently restored a museum so that we can have more spaces like this as you’ll realise, museums are quite scarce in the city of Maracaibo you can count them on the fingers of one hand but this street in Caraobo, apart from its rich culture, tradition and art, offers many stories, as we can see that it is home to two museums: the Bishop Lasso de la Vega Museum and the Centenary Art Museum, or Rafael Urdaneta Centre. ![20260619_112345.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVtHn6ggv3USyXNXQzph4PBV5zY6E6b1JGU91gSY4EebA/20260619_112345.jpg) ![20260619_112214.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTX3gn2YZJWVkBBmTSGPn8DEVsiFYwJwkBZQZAbvFkKez/20260619_112214.jpg) ![20260619_112346.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZVQvT7viaFTqfrfyrUY8V3usjzmV6EmXSPF8vAqSCKLL/20260619_112346.jpg) ![20260619_112025.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcWcwbK3Cky3L3vmbnuZDtWjTvcDdZswo9HpVWex6pm2Z/20260619_112025.jpg) ![20260619_112032.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWd3j21U8h6cxDMNecZQYaedQohnXqe5bxDGUBptKGUEh/20260619_112032.jpg) Me despido hasta una próxima oportunidad mis queridos amigos, hasta pronto les pido por favor que oren por nuestro país Venezuela y por todas las personas afectadas y las víctimas del terremoto, me despido. >I bid you farewell until we meet again, my dear friends see you soon please do pray for our country, Venezuela, and for all those affected and the victims of the earthquake. body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVMNBp5u2zrwaPt5oUdoNdHe7EGuhVnK8P8V6KwBUuRrm/img_7966.png)

Mouth Mastery — How To Dominate The Marketplace And Crush The Competition

FTC Disclosure: This post contains affiliate links. I may earn a commission if you purchase through my links, at no extra cost to you. I'm not a graduate of this program — my views are based on research and observations from my work at Qredits Microfinance.

---

Why Most Entrepreneurs Blend In Instead of Standing Out

There's a mistake I see constantly. An entrepreneur creates a business that looks and sounds exactly like every other business in their market. Same offer. Same messaging. Same target audience. Same everything.

Then they wonder why they can't compete.

This is the problem the \
component in Myron Golden's Mouth Mastery course tries to solve. And the wording in the course description is interesting. It says the training will help you \

Say that again. Distinguish yourself so you don't extinguish yourself. That's not just clever wording. It's a real thing that happens.

What Happens When You Don't Differentiate

When your business looks like everyone else's, you compete on price. That's the only lever you have left. And competing on price is a race to the bottom that nobody wins.

I see this in business plans all the time at Qredits. Someone wants to open a restaurant, a clothing store, a consulting firm, an online shop. And when I ask what makes them different from existing options, I get vague answers. \

That's not differentiation. That's table stakes. Every business claims those things. None of it is memorable.

The Extinction Problem

Here's what actually happens. You enter a crowded market with an undifferentiated offer. You struggle to get customers because there's no clear reason to choose you. You cut prices to compete, which kills your margins. You spend more on advertising to compensate, which makes things worse. Eventually you burn out or run out of money.

This isn't a hypothetical. The failure rate of small businesses is well-documented. And while there are many reasons businesses fail, a huge one is the inability to stand out in a market full of noise.

This component of the Mouth Mastery program addresses exactly that. How to position yourself so you're not just another option. How to communicate what makes your offer different in a way that actually matters to your ideal customer.

Why This Is Hard

Most entrepreneurs struggle with differentiation for one of two reasons.

First, they're too close to their own business. They know everything about their product, every feature, every detail. And they assume those details are obvious to potential customers. They're not. What feels obviously different to you might be invisible to everyone else.

Second, they're afraid to niche down or take a specific position. They worry that by clarifying who they're for, they'll exclude potential customers. But the opposite is true. The clearer you are about who you serve and why you're different, the more attracted your ideal customers become.

How the Course Approaches This

Without having gone through the program myself, what I can gather from the course materials and Myron Golden's overall philosophy is that this training focuses on positioning yourself in a way that makes you the obvious choice for a specific group of people.

It's not about being everything to everybody. It's about being something very specific to someone very specific. That's how you dominate a marketplace. Not by being the biggest, but being the most relevant to your ideal customer.

This connects directly back to the selling skills taught in the \

component. Because once you've positioned yourself clearly, selling becomes easier. You're not convincing people to buy. You're helping the right people recognize that what you offer is exactly what they've been looking for.

Who This Applies To

If your market feels crowded and competitive, standing out isn't optional. It's survival.

If you've been lowering prices to compete, that's a sign your positioning is weak.

If customers seem confused about what makes you different, that clarity problem starts with you, not them.

The \

training is part of the Mouth Mastery component inside the full Mind Over Money Mastery program. It includes the complete sales training (Sell Your Way To Wealth), the Self-Talk training, and the Click And Order strategies.

Full program details and current pricing ($4,997): https://www.mindovermoneymastery.com/momm?affiliate_id=4302472

Here's something to think about. If a potential customer visited your website right now and a competitor's website right now, would they be able to tell you apart? If not, that's a problem. What would you need to change?
