body.title: VIEWPOINT AREA // A favorite place to enjoy natural scenery and capture memorable moments
body.body:
## Good night to all my beloved hive friends ❤️ ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcV2xj6AagHPbLiz46dAQ8aK2wwxkfPReTh7aM62wnGGs/1782817480397.jpg) Area viewpoints are always the favorite and most popular spots at every tourist destination,I tried to understand and learn what makes them so appealing. At Pamah View Tourist Destination, there is also a Viewpoint located at the lowest area.Naturally,this place made me very curious about how it manages to leave so many visitors feeling satisfied and happy. In my opinion, there are several reasons why viewpoint areas are so popular among tourists. One of the main reasons is that they are usually built in strategic locations or on higher ground, allowing visitors to enjoy a wider and more breathtaking view of the surrounding natural scenery. Because of their beautiful landscapes, these areas naturally become favorite spots for tourists to take photos and capture their memorable moments. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW6VkEMYWppSMjbiSgrJ4NNxF3dAjMFUAWEGCauQGpxuz/1782817480474.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbwxvjmBQbWEcYV41VGHR3deB9Ew5zatGFx8dJ22XsT9c/1782817480561.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUpbnQWYuetGmYdVgMqK5gyTVs6t8RhjHJtHZfH5Dv1GH/1782817480647.jpg) And this is the viewpoint area at Pamah View Tourist Destination. There are three viewing decks here, allowing many visitors to enjoy the spectacular scenery at the same time. During major holidays, I would probably have to wait in line to take photos on the viewing deck. Fortunately, I visited this place early in the morning, when there were still relatively few visitors. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmas3CvrB12ttvjqgfiGFFC7KwaeqneCZi34bumUphg8Bm/1782817480712.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbmwj8DR77oXhkmKUkSCukRbryM3AhPnCPtEEJ7aMuprb/1782818430033.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRnvBB7wEbvEQxZBsSeaZm1QLVzPk8KYvwnQ8neZPpSMs/1782818430141.jpg) Of course, the mountains are the main attraction of this place, and there is no doubt that the scenery is truly breathtaking. What makes it even more interesting is that at the foot of the mountains,we can also see several small huts and even local houses,they seem to be hidden among the lush greenery, but in reality, this is one of the best ways to live in harmony with nature and experience its beauty up close. Gaining new experiences and spending quality time with the people closest to us are some of the main purposes of traveling. So, there should never be any hesitation about embracing every moment we experience along the way,I always try to preserve each of my trips through photos and videos because I want those memories to last a lifetime. That is also one of the reasons why I choose Hive Blog as the place to share every travel experience and unforgettable moment. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmW3D3xi9dHfuHicnX3pmSLKaVQ8ryszNW6VvkJWCNHBAQ/1782818612478.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUBbzcnKwuM8YuYUeKZiMn5jcKFhJWqEwcbmr8x53Rseg/1782818612558.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdoPatuRwj7vFModXdMhwhbaYbEH8mxV1t6jaam2jizkD/1782818612640.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRTdp3haR2AxXyWUY81SC1LCcboMadmCWyYSNYcRNQocX/1782818612716.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbGZ7vn2C2QrdHjHSNbKxmQhJzviKEqSM2Dr3b3qWS3oW/1782818612819.jpg) The natural scenery before my eyes was truly breathtaking. From one side, I could see the vast stretches of rice fields lying at the foot of the mountains, while the surrounding villages looked incredibly charming from this elevated viewpoint. I also spent a few minutes sitting on the viewing deck,because this place offered more than just beautiful scenery,in this area I can also feel the natural atmosphere which is so calm and refreshing . Throughout this tourist destination,we can also find many gazebos neatly arranged in every corner. Without many people realizing it, this is one of the reasons why visitors feel so comfortable and satisfied during their visit. It's no surprise that this place is always crowded with tourists. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTHSWeqFFMSR1S2wCWtwDm9ZHANmKvghsVzjP9BT9iJgB/1782819472275.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUGKTzTMs6BkF19HX6yHvxa9mNuBgtmfkm5TnQ3QnViRd/1782819472380.jpg) In the lower area of this tourist destination, you can also find a camping area, where several tents have already been set up. Spending a night here would surely be an unforgettable experience,we can enjoy the beautiful natural scenery at any time, even the moment we wake up in the morning. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNTchmemokpztczjb6Xj7hCxrM7HfA8Jm4krH6KpYcUYm/1782819643680.jpg) -----

Life is a responsibility Be yourself, keep learning and don't hesitate to start😉

If you like other travel posts, you can see them on [Worldmappin Community](https://v3.ecency.com/created/hive-163772) and you can also participate there. If you are curious about the places I have visited so far, you can see them on [my personal worldmappin map](https://worldmappin.com/@riyat) And you can also find me on [Ecency Discord](https://discord.com/invite/m9MyMSWx)

----

Thank you very much for reading my post till the end, I am here to say thank you very much 🙏

---- ----

All images are mine, I took the photos using the Infinix 10 pro cellphone and I edited the images using the Lightroom application. I'm @riyat. See you again in my next post ♥️

body.title: Introducing Randoria.app - a web idle strategy game where decisions matter
body.body:
# Welcome
Hello Hive,

This is my first post here, so I wanted to use it to introduce the project I have been building on my own: [Randoria.app](https://pre.randoria.app/)

Randoria is my solo project. I am building it as a web-based idle strategy game with long-term progression, economy systems, and room for real player decisions.

I enjoy idle games, but I do not want Randoria to become another mindless parade of “upgrade everything and watch every number go up.” If numbers grow here, they should grow because the player made a smart decision.


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/randoria.app/23tGVTro8xrT1LCDoFeUEPbadBsv2t2teFk6BSNG9UqLnQaSiaRTYMucMQLiifpUpiPUC.png)


## What Randoria.app is
At its core, Randoria is a web idle strategy game where you build a village, assign workers, send them to maps, gather resources, craft equipment, improve your economy, and gradually unlock stronger systems around production, progression, and trade.

The important part is that “idle” does not mean “brain-off.” My goal is not to create a game that demands endless clicking or several hours every day. I want Randoria to have relatively slow progression, but still respect real life. 

You should be able to log in, make meaningful choices, set things in motion, leave, come back later, and still feel that your decisions mattered.

The core gameplay today is web-based and off-chain. A future utility token is planned as an additional layer for selected systems, not as the entire reason the game exists.

Randoria is fully web-based and designed to work comfortably on both desktop and mobile, with no client download required.

## Project philosophy

I am building Randoria alone, which is both the difficult part and the exciting part. It means every system, balance change, interface improvement, and edge case ends up on my desk. But it also means the project has one clear direction behind it.

The idea from the start is simple: no pay-to-win. I want a game that rewards planning, tradeoffs, timing, specialization, and smart resource management. Not a game where the best strategy is just opening your wallet harder than the next person.

I also do not want a fake “strategy” game where all choices are basically cosmetic and the only real mechanic is increasing every counter at once. Randoria is meant to be slower, more deliberate, and more readable. A game where progress feels earned, but does not require living online 12 hours a day like a part-time goblin accountant.

## Test version on pre.randoria.app

There is already a playable test version available at [pre.randoria.app.](https://pre.randoria.app/)

This version exists so the systems can be tested in practice, improved in public, and balanced against real player behavior. Because of that, it comes with important limitations.

It is still an early test environment, so it can be unstable. Bugs may happen. Balance can change. Some parts of the game may evolve quickly. In some cases, progress resets may become necessary if a major system changes too much.

There is also an important limitation around RND. On pre.randoria.app, RND is an internal balance used for testing only.

It is not a live token there. It cannot be deposited, it cannot be withdrawn, and it should not be treated as a real public token flow. 

The point of that environment is to test systems safely, not to pretend that unfinished mechanics are already final.

So yes, it is playable. But it is still closer to a working forge than to a finished castle.

## What is already implemented
A solid part of the core game is already working:

- village building and expansion, driven by Town Hall progression
- production buildings assigned to maps through an idle tick-based system
- map progression with risk, win chance, regional drops, unique rolls, and lock-based strategy
- Workshop systems for crafting, upgrading, assigning, and sacrificing tools
- Runemancer systems for crafting, upgrading, assigning, and sacrificing runes
- Alchemy Lab with account-wide mixtures, per-building oils, recipe mastery, quality tiers, and item variants like longlasting and concentrated
- profession progression with mastery XP, perks, specialization elements, and progression roadmaps
- a unified inventory for resources, tools, runes, and alchemy items
- an in-game marketplace for resources, tools, runes, and unused alchemy items, already integrated into the game world, although RND is not yet publicly earnable, so the economic loop is still incomplete for now, but that will change soon
- leaderboards with active ranking windows
- Codex and in-game knowledge pages that explain the world, systems, and roadmap
- minimal data policy and flexible sign-in options: Randoria processes only the absolute minimum technical data needed to let players sign in and keep their accounts working. You can log in with Hive Keychain, HiveAuth, MetaMask, or Google. I do not store email addresses, I will not spam anyone, and there will be no newsletters. If the game is good, players will come back on their own ;)


So this is not just a concept with a logo and a brave paragraph. The foundation is already playable, and I am actively building on top of it.


## Nearest plans
The next stage is where Randoria starts becoming much more than a basic idle loop.

One of the closest goals is to introduce a controlled way to earn tokens on the test version, so reward logic can be tested properly before anything truly live is opened up. I want that phase to be useful for balance testing, economy validation, and anti-exploit thinking, not just empty hype.

After that comes the actual deployment of the utility token and the first real token-connected gameplay loop. The plan is not to glue blockchain onto the game like a decorative sticker, but to make it serve the economy in a way that actually belongs there.

I also plan to add ads and a subscription model, because a project has to sustain itself somehow. But this will not turn into paywalls, pay-to-win pressure, or predatory loot boxes. 

The goal is a fair free-to-play structure with optional support, useful quality-of-life value, and sensible monetization without locking the real game behind a wallet check.

And then comes the milestone that matters most: releasing the first true live alpha version with a working token mechanic, a stronger economic loop, and a clearer bridge between gameplay and utility systems.

## Screenshots

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/randoria.app/23t78trMrVp3wszaQNpe8g4Wiw4RtKWWc4c7A51aFPk1GzSohtNPn9UDuT7eFa1tdSNpF.png)

![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/randoria.app/23tRtVqLUqpzFuhKseoKhigsvcRCTv9uwc1fr4ZmSbTdVfMU3YdPBog6Vbmk7oZJhwLvd.png)


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/randoria.app/23t76y19jwthceDdPeFg7Ubq5iw4w5PtFGDpjwEvzXjFW8GhLzjoBg1QYEchFZTXiZbtF.png)


## Closing
Randoria is still early, but it is real, playable, and growing. I am building it step by step as a solo project, with a strong focus on meaningful decisions, fair progression, and an economy that feels like part of the game instead of a gimmick attached to it.

If you enjoy idle games but want something more deliberate than “make every number green,” there is a good chance Randoria will be worth watching.

body.title: Ruleset change the whole game.
body.body: Greetings everyone! When we play the game we need to read the ruleset first, but if we ignore it ruleset really makes you lose. So understand and make the deck according is the most precious and important thing. It also happens many times that you are just about to lose or either win the game but ruleset really changes the whole game and turn the table, so everything were very unexpected. So today I play the game something like that watch it till the end you will enjoy the battle a lot for sure. Let me share in detail:-
/> The name of the ruleset was \*\*Collateral Damage: All units have Reckless (Each successful attack also deals 1 damage to adjacent allied units\]-\*\*.

/> So of course we need to choose the strong monsters because other monsters will lose the health when first will attack. The battle was of only 25 mana cost, so it was looking hard for me to make the deck. Opponent bring five monsters and I have only 2 monsters. But still anyhow my monsters face the opponent and help me win the game.
/> Now let me share you the battle in detail-
/> In AMBUSH round opponent monster attack on lord shield and break his by -1. Then the actual game starts.

/> So as the round starts lord attack on opponent first monster and eliminate him after that opponent monster attack on lord and even swamp meanwhile every monster was getting reckless as per the ruleset and losing health. In this round only single opponent front monster was knock and everyone was getting weak because of the attacks and ruleset.

/> So again lord attack on opponent front monster and eliminate him from the battle. And swamp was getting the reckless and losing health. After that opponent monster attack on swamp and eliminate him while they were also getting the reckless ability. So now the game was 1v3. It was looking hard for my monster.

/> So again as you can see the position of the monsters. Lord attack and make opponent monster weak, after that opponent monster attack on lord and other monsters get the reckless. In this round opponent lose his second monster because of the ruleset. And lord was also getting weak.

/> So lord attack and make him weak, opponent last monster attack on lord and opponent first monster get the reckless and get eliminate from the battle. So now the game was 1v1. And here I know I will win the game because lord will attack and eliminate opponent monster.

/> So as you can see opponent was left with the last monster as round starts lord attack on opponent last monster and eliminate him within single attack by -3 and even lord was almost very weak as you can see if he get attack by any monster he was about to die. But I think there was also an advantage of single monster left in the game because when lord was attacking on opponent monster no one was getting the reckless ability so it was very plus point, and opponent all the monster face the reckless as per the ruleset and many of them get eliminate because of this. And if this ruleset was no there for sure I will lose the battle. As I said that ruleset win me the game the battle was in opponent hands but it changes at last.

/>

[https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl\_83863f54e24960a46a08648c53f0a140?ref=chinay04](https://splinterlands.com/battle/sl_83863f54e24960a46a08648c53f0a140?ref=chinay04)

body.title: Garden Stories: Some Sadness, and a Sweet Smile.
body.body:
> ![IMG20260629124957~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcGNomTxSuPvWJU4AqBowGRmjUMPwUcKS1CRdVyc2jDM7/IMG20260629124957~2.jpg) Only a garden lover knows the infinite joy that lies between green nature and caring for a tree planted by one's own hands. The feeling of waking up every morning and seeing the green leaves and new buds in the garden is different. For quite some time, I have been spending a lot of time behind the rice pumpkin tree in my garden, and seeing the tree growing in the loft with its tips spreading out would fill my chest with a strange peace. But along with the joy of nature, sometimes there are also stories of intense sadness, and today I have come to share with you a rollercoaster experience of my garden. ![IMG20260629124944~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaADDqh4QZRhhhSv1S2do4f2xK2zJ8Jwrj7673oaePpcH/IMG20260629124944~2.jpg) Let's start with some bad news, which honestly broke my heart and I was quite upset. When the small rice pumpkins started to grow on the tree, my joy knew no bounds. But suddenly, the garden was attacked by flies and these harmful insects pierced my young pumpkins and made holes in various places. As a result, the pumpkins started rotting due to the insects inside and I was really sad to see how a young pumpkin was ruined. Who likes to see such an outcome of so much hard work and love. ![IMG20260629125206~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeLjY4cFFT6jLNNx47QAnAzJkYpbe1dHeZ6bf4qRKbott/IMG20260629125206~2.jpg) However, as the saying goes, There is a ray of light in all darkness, and that is exactly what happened in my case. Just when I thought that all my hard work had gone in vain, I saw a great happiness hidden behind the leaves. Miraculously, one of my pumpkins had been completely saved from the flies and, Mashallah, it had become quite beautiful, perfect and quite a bit bigger. After seeing this healthy pumpkin hanging among the thick green leaves, all my sadness disappeared in an instant and I regained my joy. ![IMG20260629125211~2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeeFU46JfQu15Nhmtfe6dajpcwtNrAHHVnnUhoRRbVZBH/IMG20260629125211~2.jpg) Nature knows how to take away as well as give back, so forgetting the pain of the rotten pumpkins, I carefully collected this beautiful surviving rice pumpkin from the tree today. When I collected this rice pumpkin, which was absolutely fresh for cooking and free of poison, and brought it home to eat, a different kind of satisfaction was working in my mind. Gardening actually teaches us patience, and even though it was damaged by an insect attack today, this one achievement made me forget all my troubles. I feel very happy to think that I will cook a great dish tonight with this first rice pumpkin from my garden. This was my arrangement for today. I hope you liked the pictures I took and the nature observations. Wishing everyone good health, I bid you farewell here today. |

body.title: 「Vicky's Life」短剧｜《白昼焚野》（蔡欣洋x申浩男）
body.body:
![IMG_1049.jpeg](https://s2.loli.net/2025/09/19/DnRNQo3m8qGTuX1.jpg)

姐妹们！我没想到我居然在短剧平台上看到那么精彩的双男主+刑侦题材的短剧！晚饭时看完的，直到凌晨我还在回味当中。这会儿激动写下评论，分享给我的好姐妹。

从剧情的角度来说，这部刑侦题材的悬疑推理剧故事线很完整。我觉得原著应该会更好看，拍成短剧势必有很多删减。剩下的内容环环相扣，总体来说闭环的很不错啦。

从颜值的角度来说，两位男主都非常帅气。蔡欣洋是那种阳光小狼狗的帅，申浩男则是年长者的好看。双男主的剧自然会磕他俩啦，我脑补了一幕年上兄友弟恭的戏码。

从摄影和服化道的角度来说，这部剧的画面绝对是电视剧甚至电影级别的。除去有些画面过暗看不清以外，不少场景看得出都是花了钱布置的。服化道也很不错，加鸡腿。

从演技的角度来说，两位男主虽然年轻但演技稳当。我之前是没有看过他们的剧的，因为这部剧被妥妥的种草了。尤其喜欢申浩男，脑补了好几部耽美男主角的脸，哈哈。

为避免剧透关于剧情的部分我没展开来写，但有些关于作案动机的点我还是很疑惑的。比如那个同学就很奇怪，强行说是幕后真凶的棋子也说得过去，但似乎又觉得不是。

总的来说特别棒的剧，五星推荐！大家都去看呀！！！


（本篇完）


————————


喜欢影视剧、美食和旅行的天秤座80后妹纸，喜欢一切新奇温暖的事物

如果你喜欢我的文章，欢迎留言与我交流

body.title: Lo que aprendí cuando dejé de hacerlo todo por mi cuenta
body.body:
<center>
![image.png](https://images.hive.blog/768x0/https://images.pexels.com/photos/6915247/pexels-photo-6915247.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=800)
[LINK](https://images.pexels.com/photos/6915247/pexels-photo-6915247.jpeg?auto=compress&cs=tinysrgb&w=800)</center>

## Hay verdades que uno sabe pero que no siempre entiende. Las sabe porque las leyó, porque las escuchó en la iglesia, porque alguien se las dijo. Pero entenderlas de verdad lleva tiempo, y a veces dolor.

> Y todo lo que pidáis en oración, creyendo, lo recibiréis.

Mateo 21:22

##### Me acuerdo de una vez que estaba tan frustrado con una situación que le hablé a Dios como nunca antes. Sin filtros, sin protocolo, sin las palabras bonitas que uno usa cuando ora en público. Y fue la oración más sincera que hice en mucho tiempo.

##### A veces me pongo a pensar en las personas que conocí en el camino. Cada una con su historia, con sus batallas que nadie ve. Y me doy cuenta de algo: todos estamos lidiando con algo que los demás no saben.

##### Dios no te pide que llegues perfecto, te pide que llegues. Así nomás, como estás, con tus dudas, tu cansancio, tus preguntas sin responder. Llegá y confiá en que El sabe lo que hace.

> La luz brilla en las tinieblas, y las tinieblas no han podido apagarla.

Juan 1:5

##### Una cosa que aprendí: Dios no te llama a ser exitoso según el mundo, te llama a ser fiel. La fidelidad es lo que realmente importa.

*****
*******

*Bueno, eso quería compartir hoy. Si llegaste hasta acá, gracias. Ojalá resuene en tu corazón como resonó en el mío.*

<center>![](https://cdn.steemitimages.com/DQmYH4hAwopGmcAs8LgkwPjZ16zjiUAzunvLxFfFWRpGGfr/image.png)</center>

body.title: STREET ART #259 – Some finds from the city of Porto, Portugal
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTQDqoDSyWtfM3CjjfbKbfeCpbT9BYowDGd7CZUArTrqF/01.jpg)
Porto is probably the second largest city in Portugal, after the capital Lisbon. It is quite a big city, but I chose to stay in the historical part of town. That seemed to be a good choice. Everything I wanted to see and do was in walking distanse. On some of my walks I came across some great street art. This is some of the stuff I had the opportunity to take pictures of. A few times I took some daytrips out of the city by bus. From the bus window I saw a lot of great things, but I don't have any pictures of that. The first photo is a great portrait of an elderly woman. Possibly a local woman from Porto. A nice way of paying tribute to elderly residents. What I have managed to find out is that the artist is Daniel Elme. However, it is someone I know nothing about.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmcwx6MEft8wLhEc7HR7F1qLbWMkWZQEjydmF1Tzo25abD/02.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQma2A6V2cGGmbfRnpCJeP3U2tmqvTb1s5HYyTauhAViaMS/3.jpg I noticed that many of the electrical boxes were painted, like the one in the photo above. Many did look a bit worn and some were had the kind of graffiti that didn't really appeal to me.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmaoqrd9SG7fd5HQ3qpZK7R9Ncmh7Z62rgJqWan6KqeLWe/04.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmXHfnpj2njfpAVthAURe1qxBGaezPDVN36aCmLXRxdLcm/05.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmXGGhmmhUnDmEYf918aqiRTCpRHJjdSL4gAL6RaWBMnLg/06.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmWJJQRKQ84Y37oRtKZsQ8FAextWYtdcdVXUXTQRtWdBj1/07.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmTuZvAwu9wXpmZGKTVeqUHF85Ygkg7Xhqn7SQQ7CTUpNc/08.jpg This beautiful, blue cat became one of my favorites. As you can see, it was impossible to take pictures! The street is a very narrow pedestrian street, so I got too close to be able to get the whole painting on the photo. I took several close-ups, because when I could see the cats head, I couldn't see where he was sitting. And vice versa. But it's interesting to see the cat with the boat in front of him. The oar is so long that it sticks into the ground the cat is sitting on. At the cat's feet, you can see a number of other mysterious figures.
https://i.ecency.com/DQmcQD3xNf7fPBse8GVTRezQm9ZU6Rv6yACGWYLspxGPUYe/9.jpg https://i.ecency.com/DQmUYR2kCcxEKY2CZfk3AFCGR2Zno9grT8wc7eSJ1DptM8t/10.jpg This electrical box has a nice little dog framed by the typical blue and white tiles. These painted tiles are seen almost everywhere on buildings in Porto. I could have googled street art and planned to go hunting for if, before arriving. But I knew I wouldn't have enough time, so I desided to justtake it as it comes. It was nice to come across a small part of what Porto has to offer.

title.title: New Printer for the home/Nueva Impresora para el hogar  [ENG/ESP]
title.body: > Hello dear friends of @Geekzone, greetings and happy day, on this occasion I want to tell you about a purchase that we made together in my house to achieve this, since as we constantly had to make prints or copies and very apart from my son who is growing he needs to make things, we decided to make a joint purchase that would facilitate that point, and that was a multifunctional printer, Epson L3250. --- ![REVIEW (10).jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23wWpSUvszdpJNkxgeV4K66ysEfABZYX3RYzRzzbEvX3rPNUbKYRwBuq7KogPRfzv6LUv.jpg) **Design in CANVA** ---

> Lately we had thought about buying it but we had not had the opportunity until we saw this brand at a considerable price compared to others, especially because it is not a cartridge but a continuous ink, which yields more, very apart it is not only a printer, but as I said before it is multifunctional, it makes a copy and scans as well, it can also be used with its cable connected directly to the computer, as well as Wi-Fi, which is excellent because if you have the document on your cell phone so you are not transferring it to the computer and then sending it to print ps directly from there it sounds better. --- ![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-09 at 9.02.00 PM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/EowEi6oB22ZFBJZ9ZPNrqvvpoSEckSNgujqZSpDsC3TRBkatvgYaMveRVmgh8yMB8bf.jpeg) **Image by me** ---

> Of course, I didn't see the installation process as simple as others I had, of course the multifunction printer I had at home was HP with cartridges and with its times it was easier to organize its connection with the computer, but in this case the Epson has to be downloaded from the internet since it doesn't come with its installation disk and the fact that it's new wasn't because they had removed it or well it was the manufacturers maybe hehe, but you had to go to the internet to download the relevant programs for it, of which there are several since some are to see the control of what you print, another to adjust the sheets and inks and another when you want to scan, each separate package, quite apart, the process first asks you to fill the ink, which brings the 4 colors at once, black, yellow, cyan and magenta, ready to be poured into it. --- ![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-09 at 9.02.00 PM (5).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/23vsFw6nHnYRgArGATg6wBvX19cpbAemHcYL9Nu1J4eMo2sxUZ3YKr37HUi842UUqnfHR.jpeg) **Image by me** ---

>Then its installation begins, you must also register it on the Epson website with its product code, certainly a process there to have it ready to use, take out the test page, connect either by cable or by Wi-Fi to carry out the process, in the case of Wi-Fi through the cell phone if it is required to download an application which is the one that will connect with the printer, having this the printing can be executed from there, without it not, very aside what I liked is that the process of printing, copying or scanning is fast, and it is seen that there are savings ink since he took advantage of printing several that we had pending and if he spent anything it would be like 1% and there were several, it is very useful especially when he comes with my son to take it out hehe. --- ![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-09 at 9.02.00 PM (3).jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/EoptShSnhFEN1dHSF3ynin7pWJnawML5x9airLNt2n7mXJWWVqpL2kibii2MhPFz4nJ.jpeg) **Image by me** --- ![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-09 at 9.02.01 PM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/Eonj2mf67m8AoUuU3zMfwwjWz16ssNKND1dcZLbLJg8QsnWAA4V2HrfJQUrssUQBdN3.jpeg) **Image by me** --- ![WhatsApp Image 2026-06-11 at 5.27.37 PM.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/yasmarit/Eoc8wBXWuwooXPDBntLycXEwKcMYqhCEdATJ9c9djjvBmZYJS3wYZKmMqA8j9u3Fgbw.jpeg) **Image by me** ---

title.title: 放松两天，后面继续努力
title.body:
![img_20260630_090432-ff634e21b955.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/angelina6688/lkt-mr0k0j3d-lh46weod/img_20260630_090432-ff634e21b955.webp)

![img_20260630_090425-a37911f7ee27.webp](https://cdn.liketu.com/liketu/angelina6688/lkt-mr0k0j3d-lh46weod/img_20260630_090425-a37911f7ee27.webp)

今天终于考完试了，先不管考得如何，先好好放两天假再说。娃放假没作业，我也好好休息休息。之前跟他一起备考，搞得我也神经紧张了。
 
这几天也不用管学校作业，也没有学校老师艾特我，关注群消息之类的。哎呀，感觉还是挺开心的。
 
不过接下来的暑假两个月，估计学校布置的暑假作业又不会少。
 
就算是学校布置的作业看起来还好，但是每次寒暑假，老师都会在最后一两条明里暗里的暗示大家，要根据自己的能力做一些什么什么什么的东西。然后你如果什么课外的教辅都没做的话，开学之后可能会被艾特家长。所以其实这个暑假作业算下来还是并不少的。
 
而且听不少同学家长交流，他们已经在为初中的小四门开始打基础提前学了。哎，我的天呐，我真的是被动被卷，没办法，我也买了一些初中小四门的参考资料。
 
目前阶段还是以激发兴趣然后让他自己当课外书慢慢阅读为主。后面再看看怎么样和语数外这三门主科合理分配时间安排比较好。因为毕竟暑假两个月时间，除去培优班以后，大概就只剩一半的时间了。
 
这一半的时间又要写暑假作业，又要写培优班的作业，还要写其他教辅的作业，其实孩子剩下能玩的时间并不多。哎，现在的小孩暑假根本就不是放假，太惨了。

title.title: Views Over Humanity: The Problem with Viral Culture
title.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdkGZWPaV13HLtuSRZYZ2pUVXApea3jtcTDDFsErrfUjq/1782817835695.jpg)


As a man I care about the safeties of the ladies in my family. Nowadays, people can take your pictures and generate deepfake with it. Just imagine someone who doesn't wear bikini, but a stranger generated it with Ai and made them wear a bikini, also posted it online, it's totally invading ones privacy. if someone wants to record themselves or take pictures of themselves, they can do it without harming others privacy. Some people doesn't mind being in the picture or video, so that is acceptable. But there are many people who does not even post their pictures online and if you are posting them online that's invading their privacy. 

If someone is in the background of the picture which you have taken, you can crop them out or make it blurry before posting it online. But if you don't post it online then I think it's alright to have them. So, it totally depends how the person who took it, is using it. There a many people with bad intentions so we need to protect our privacy. When I go outside, most of the time I have seen two people or a group of people are fighting and no one is bothering to stop them. Instead, the people in the public they took out their phone and started to record the fight. See? they are not worried about someone getting hurt, they just want to record and earn views from it.

In this way, people are already losing their humanity. We should help each other not enjoy another's pain. Even if it's a public place it doesn't mean you can capture someone and post it online, I think it's fine as long you don't post it. Because sometime we go to places where is too much gatherings and we try to take picture then somehow someone gets in the background. So, let's not post everything online, I think that's the best solution. How would you like it when you were pricking your nose and someone took a picture later posted it online? It would be embarrassing right? How about you got viral overnight for pricking your nose? Would you still agree for such things?

When my daughters and wife goes out, I don't want a creep to capture them and post it online. It's truly invading ones privacy. We all have privacy and no one has the right to invade it. I understand that public places are open to everyone, but we are human beings not animals. We don't need to bite like a lion as it hunts down a deer, because the deer was in the lion's territory. I believe that people deserve respect and should not have to worry about becoming part of someone else's video or picture without their consent and knowledge.

Not everyone wants to be on social media and get viral. Not everyone is a clout chaser. Young people, specially children, are more vulnerable to online misuse and once an image is uploaded to the internet, it can never be deleted. However, I do not think making all public photography a criminal offense is the right solution. We should focus on the intention of a person. There could be some accidental cases so we should re-think about it. Instead of banning public photography, I believe it should be illegal to use someone's image to exploit, harass, defame, or profit from them without permission. There should also be stronger protections for children and vulnerable people. In my opinion, the best balance is to protect both personal privacy and creative freedom.

title.title: Stakeout
title.body:
<div class=text-justify>



![IMG_5991.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teknon/EpLeTmevTXPAH9ZTdzcCDWYRXJ3ZkReVN1JJjQHFFvyYUwRzTzwBQDkwVXoz5MB2jef.jpeg)


It was morning, and the rain had just stopped. The ground outside was swallowed by floodwater. I had an 8 a.m. appointment, so I needed to leave as early as possible.
My hair was already perfectly laid, my lip combo flawless, and my mascara exactly how I wanted it. I gave myself one last twirl in front of the mirror before stepping outside, hoping I’d find a cab willing to take me to the major road.

The fresh and cool air greeted me first and trees swayed gently to the rhythm of the wind. I inhaled deeply and quickened my pace.

The street was empty. Not a single approaching vehicle. Not even another commuter. I sighed, silently praying for a taxi.

By 6:45 a.m., there was still none in sight, and I found myself blaming myself for choosing to live on the outskirts of town. Just as my brain was busy staging a protest, a motorcycle pulled up in front of me.

“You dey go?” the rider asked in pidgin. 
“Oh, yes,” I replied after a brief hesitation and climbed on, sitting sideways.


I don’t particularly like motorcycles. Their riders have earned a reputation for recklessness. But that morning, the road looked almost deserted, so I convinced myself the risk was smaller than usual. The wind grew heavier as he sped along so I shut my eyes and, for those few minutes, trusted a complete stranger with my life.

Five minutes later, we reached the major road. I got off and paid him.

“Thank you,” he said. I nodded and hurried away to catch a bus.

By 7:30, I was standing in front of the building where my meeting was supposed to take place. It was locked. I dug through my bag for my phone to confirm the address. Same building, same location. Then, I let out a long sigh and looked around for somewhere comfortable to wait. A low ledge by the entrance would do. As I settled down, my eyes wandered across the road. 

![IMG_6289.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/teknon/EoGw2MU6xRdNMtmMukfKHKfhup8Hw11XbYZFAxmcLStJ3r9dek3XTaoDDzMprbGkg6Z.jpeg)

Partially hidden behind overgrown bushes stood another building. Even with the foliage, I could make out several street children scattered across its frontage. Some were still asleep. Others were already awake, chatting among themselves. Judging by their appearance, they couldn’t have been older than seven to fourteen. A wave of unease washed over me. Then, almost immediately, relief followed. Cars were passing by steadily. If anything happened, surely someone would hear me scream.

I watched them more closely. Why were they there? Where were their parents? They looked tiny, dusty, and painfully thin. Their oversized, mismatched clothes hung loosely on their bodies, almost runway-worthy if Balenciaga had ever designed a collection inspired by neglect. I felt sorry for them. Still, I didn’t dare walk over to offer money. I’d heard stories about street boys like these. People described them as unpredictable, capable of turning aggressive without warning, especially toward young women. So I stayed where I was and minded my business or at least, I tried to.

By 8:30, the building had finally opened, and I was led upstairs to the second floor. From there, the bushes no longer obstructed my view.

“The MD isn’t on seat yet,” the secretary said politely. “You’ll have to wait a little longer.”

“That’s okay,” I smiled.

Secretly, I hoped he took his time. I wanted to keep watching and I wanted to know how these boys lived—what they ate, where they washed, how they survived.

Almost as though they had heard my thoughts, the answers began revealing themselves. One of the younger boys, he couldn’t have been older than eight, wandered toward the opposite side of the road.


>To be continued.




</diva>

title.title: What did you think of the ending of The Bear?
title.body:
Was the last service good? https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/aJtG4txtmiRHwAAqENQHZvBs6kY.jpg
[Source ](https://www.themoviedb.org/tv/136315-the-bear/images/backdrops)
Edited in Photoshop & Canva App
https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jcrodriguez/245cUBXzvWF8QVukk8UvqTFX6FutvCzv1TyGDA8ybnR5QKA1v6nMvGS4j6y81Qg9M2HLn.jpg
Cooked in the storm. That phrase could sum up the final season of The Bear. It has come to an end; the creators have decided to conclude the story. I think it's the right decision, because it simply couldn't be stretched out any longer. When The Bear premiered, I was one of the enthusiasts who recommended it. I loved this series, which I started watching after its star won a Golden Globe. Here's the post from back then, where I wrote enthusiastically about it and, of course, recommended it. I also thought the second season was very good; at that time, it was still one of my favorite series, but it was from the third season onward that my perception began to change. The third season had some good episodes, but, unfortunately, overall, it felt somewhat slow in its development. By the way, I always considered this series more dramatic than comedic, even though it was nominated in the comedy category at the awards. But it was with the third season that I began to feel that its characters had already evolved enough and had stagnated. The characters' stagnation made me lose a lot of interest in the show; it just didn't appeal to me anymore. So much so that I put the fourth season on hold. It premiered, but I didn't watch it. Just a few weeks ago, when I saw that the fifth season was airing its final episode, I reluctantly started watching the fourth, and I have to say it was quite a struggle to finish it. There's an episode in that fourth season focused on Sydney that was unbearable. And speaking of unbearable things, some characters who became truly unbearable starting in the third season were Neil and Teddy. Neil is played by one of the show's producers. They're supposed to provide the comic relief, but there comes a point where acting like idiots becomes ridiculous. We don't know if Neil has some kind of mental disability; he acts so foolishly. There's a wedding scene in the fourth season, and the whole episode was incredibly ridiculous. In that episode, Neil acts almost like a baby, and they even treat him like an idiot. What a stupid episode, for God's sake! The worst part is that in the end, all the characters end up under a table, something that would be impossible for anyone in real life, just because of a little girl's whim that she didn't want to dance with her stepfather. How stupid! The truth is, I had already stopped liking the show, and I watched the fifth season just to see how on earth they would end it. Although it received critical and audience praise, for me it no longer has any charm, and the fact that they develop the entire season in a single day, where it rains heavily and the restaurant is at a critical point, where it could be the last service before closing its doors due to lack of profit. That's how the entire last season unfolds. The last service, with that air of sadness, farewell, and a ton of problems, one after another. Thank goodness it's over. I was fed up with Carmy's whims; she seems like a spoiled brat who doesn't know what to do. Her existential angst meant absolutely nothing to me. The same goes for Sydney and her doubts about whether to continue: another character drowning in her own tears. Richie is still stuck; his character reached his peak in the third season, and here he's still struggling with the same issues. The same is true for the other characters, and it wore me out. This last episode didn't excite me. I watched it out of inertia; I no longer felt the same frenetic pace that captivated me in the first season. Each episode seemed designed solely to get one of the actors nominated for an award. The magic has vanished, or at least I no longer see any magic in this story, and thankfully it's the end. Was this finale up to par? Well, let's just say it was mediocre. It's like the restaurant: elaborate dishes with small portions served on large plates, but they lack a bit of flavor. What did you think of the finale? Let me know in the comments. ---- > Cocinada en la tormenta. Esa frase podría resumir la última temporada de The Bear. Ha llegado a su fin; los creadores han decidido concluir la historia. Creo que es una decisión acertada, porque simplemente no se podía alargar más. > Cuando se estrenó The Bear, fui uno de los entusiastas que la recomendó. Me encantó esta serie, que empecé a ver después de que su protagonista ganara un Globo de Oro. Aquí está la publicación de aquel entonces, donde escribí con entusiasmo sobre ella y, por supuesto, la recomendé. También me pareció muy buena la segunda temporada; en ese momento, seguía siendo una de mis series favoritas, pero fue a partir de la tercera temporada cuando mi percepción empezó a cambiar. > La tercera temporada tuvo algunos buenos episodios, pero, por desgracia, en general, se sentía algo lenta en su desarrollo. Por cierto, siempre consideré esta serie más dramática que cómica, a pesar de que fue nominada en la categoría de comedia en los premios. Pero fue con la tercera temporada cuando empecé a sentir que sus personajes ya habían evolucionado lo suficiente y se habían estancado. > El estancamiento de los personajes me hizo perder muchísimo el interés por la serie; ya no me atraía. Tanto es así que dejé la cuarta temporada en pausa. Se estrenó, pero no la vi. Hace solo unas semanas, cuando vi que la quinta temporada estaba emitiendo su último episodio, empecé a ver la cuarta a regañadientes, y debo decir que me costó bastante terminarla. Hay un episodio en esa cuarta temporada centrado en Sydney que fue insoportable. > Y ya que hablamos de cosas insoportables, algunos personajes que se volvieron realmente insoportables a partir de la tercera temporada fueron Neil y Teddy. El primero lo interpreta uno de los productores de la serie. Son los que aportan el toque cómico, pero llega un punto en que comportarse como idiotas se vuelve ridículo. No sabemos si Neil tiene alguna discapacidad mental; actúa de forma tan tonta. Hay una escena de boda en la cuarta temporada, y todo el episodio fue increíblemente ridículo. > En ese episodio, Neil se comporta casi como un bebé, y hasta lo tratan como a un idiota. ¡Qué episodio tan estúpido, por Dios! Lo peor es que al final todos los personajes terminan debajo de una mesa, algo que en la vida real sería imposible para todos, solo por el capricho de una niña que no quería bailar con su padrastro. ¡Qué estupidez! > La verdad es que ya había dejado de gustarme la serie, y vi la quinta temporada solo para ver cómo demonios la terminaban. Aunque ha recibido elogios de la crítica y del público, para mí ya no tiene ningún encanto, y el hecho de que desarrollen toda la temporada en un solo día, donde llueve mucho y el restaurante está en un punto crítico, donde podría ser el último servicio antes de cerrar sus puertas por falta de ganancias. > Así es como se desarrolla toda la última temporada. El último servicio, con ese aire de tristeza, despedida y un montón de problemas, uno tras otro. Menos mal que se acabó. Estaba harta de los caprichos de Carmy; parece una niña mimada que no sabe qué hacer. Su angustia existencial me daba completamente igual. Lo mismo ocurre con Sydney y sus dudas sobre si continuar o no: otro personaje ahogándose en sus propias lágrimas. Richie sigue estancado; su personaje alcanzó su punto álgido en la tercera temporada, y aquí sigue con los mismos problemas. Lo mismo pasa con los demás personajes, y eso me agotó. > Este último episodio no me entusiasmó. Lo vi por inercia; ya no sentía el mismo ritmo frenético que me cautivó en la primera temporada. Cada episodio parecía hecho solo para que uno de los actores fuera nominado a un premio. La magia se ha esfumado, o al menos ya no veo magia en esta historia, y por suerte es el final. > ¿Estuvo a la altura este último servicio? Bueno, digamos que regular. Es como el restaurante: platos muy elaborados con porciones pequeñas servidas en platos grandes, pero les falta un poco de sazón. > ¿Qué te pareció el final? Cuéntame en los comentarios.

title.title: From Elsewhere. The Home Office’s mad mad migration plan.
title.body:
![signpost--777x437.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mrfahrenheit211/23xAqCUkcWCYxdiRieDG2uiwrdLkP3oWMKKfWbFRQQNbnxtiamXnurdhm8rDJT2KjGbuq.jpg)



I was going to do a long form disassembly of the Home Office’s new plan for ‘sponsored migration’.  This policy is going to be disastrous. It will not restrict migration numbers but in crease them.

However whilst I was researching what I was going to write about this issue I came across a statement on what’s wrong with this policy by the Social Democratic Party.  I don’t think I can improve on what they’ve written.

The SDP said:
*
London (29 June 2026) – The Social Democratic Party (SDP) condemns the plans announced by the Labour government for a new community refugee sponsorship scheme as ill-conceived, counter-productive, and further damaging to social cohesion.

On its own terms, the scheme is highly likely to be a failure. Labour’s claim that the numbers will be small to start with means it won’t make any sort of dent in the small boat flows, given unchecked incentives using that route for immigrants and gangs alike. The idea that communities and universities will be “approved” begs the question over assessment criteria, transparency and enforcement within a system that continues to fail on the basics. And the suggestion that numbers within this new scheme will build over time without any indication of limits creates yet another uncapped framework likely to run out of control.

William Clouston, SDP Party Leader, said: “This statement contains yet more dangerous and magical thinking from Labour. The idea that the Home Office is competent to manage the verification of refugee status, strict biometric screening, criminality checks and health assessments before arrival, let alone manage a myriad of third parties with high incentives to maximise throughput, is simply not credible. The public will see it for what it is, another smoke-and-mirrors scheme that will simply lead to more arrivals at a time when the British state’s social fabric and public finances are stretched to breaking point.

“The new migrant flows prompted by Mahmood will be additional to – rather than instead of – existing illegal entries. Further, the evidence on the ongoing social and economic costs of accommodating large asylum populations is overwhelming. Against the backdrop of continued large-scale illegal entries via small boats and other routes, the growing number of tragic cases of appalling criminal acts committed by immigrants, and the lack of trust by the public in the capability of Home Office and Border Force to manage immigration generally, this announcement will come across to many voters as further fuel on the fire.”
*
The SDP’s Mr Clouston is correct.  It’s ‘magical thinking’ by the political classes again. It will not just do nothing to stem the flow of migration it will make things worse much worse. This is a policy that will be abused to hell and back just mark my words. 

Link
Statement by SDP
https://www.sdp.org.uk/sdp_condemns_proposed_community_sponsorship_scheme


Transparency statement:  I am a supporter although not a member of the SDP.

title.title: Learn Creative Coding (#109) - LED Art: Addressable Light
title.body:
# Learn Creative Coding (#109) - LED Art: Addressable Light

![cc-banner](https://images.hive.blog/DQmS97emj8DdhzqfkHd8Bx5YD1zhjJeoZkSdG4Rk7oKwY6g/cc-banner-orange.png)

Last episode I left you holding a freshly laser-cut coaster and promised that next time we'd give our physical work a *pulse*. I also told you to bring a spare USB cable. Well, here we are :-). Today the thing your code makes doesn't just sit on a shelf looking pretty - it glows, it shifts, it breathes. We're going to take a generative sketch, the exact kind we've been writing since episode 1, and pour it out of the screen and into a strip of actual lights you can hang on your wall.

This is genuinly one of the most satisfying leaps in the whole series, because the gap between \

chapter: the same code, pointed at the physical world.

## Going wireless: ESP32 and UDP

Serial over USB is great for a strip on your desk, but the cable is a leash. The moment you want lights across the room, or several installations at once, you switch to an **ESP32** - a microcontroller with WiFi built in for a couple of euros. Instead of bytes down a cable, you fire colour data as **UDP packets** over your network. No wire, and you can drive many panels from one computer.

```javascript
// node.js: send a frame to an ESP32 over the network instead of a cable.
// UDP is perfect here - it's fast and we don't care about a dropped frame.
const dgram = require(\

:
- Swap `noiseStrip` for your favourite old sketch via the `canvasToStrip` pixel trick - resurrect a particle system from episode 11 as physical light.
- Bend the strip into a 16-wide serpentine and use `serpentineMap` to run a 2D pattern on it.
- Wire in episode 19's audio analyser and make it dance to music.
- Go wireless with an ESP32 and `sendFrameUDP`, then put the panel across the room with no cable in sight.

Do at least the basic ribbon if you possibly can. There's a specific kind of joy the first time a pattern you wrote rolls down a real strip of light in your hands - it's the same feeling as holding your first plot or your first laser-cut piece, but this one *moves*. The screen has never felt further away.

## 't Komt erop neer...

- Addressable LEDs (WS2812B / NeoPixel) are a chain of individually-controllable RGB lights on a single data line. The mental model is dead simple: a strip is just an *array of colours*, exactly like a row of pixels from episode 10. Fill the array, send it, done
- Your computer can't drive the lights directly - the timing is too fussy - so a cheap microcontroller (Arduino or ESP32) sits in between. Your computer is the artist (decides colours), the microcontroller is the courier (delivers them with exact timing). They talk over serial or WiFi
- The protocol is just raw bytes: r, g, b for each LED, in order. Your `sendFrame` writes them, the Arduino's loop reads them. As long as both agree on the count and the order, the colours arrive intact. At 115200 baud you get a comfy 30fps for ~60-300 LEDs
- A strip is 1D but your art is 2D, and panels are wired in a zig-zag serpentine. Build a coordinate map (LED index -> real x,y) ONCE, and your 2D sketch never has to know about the wiring. The map absorbs all the physical messiness - strips, rings, spirals, even 3D
- The pixel pipeline is the killer trick: render ANY existing sketch at LED resolution, read the pixels with `loadPixels`, send them as a strip. Every sketch from all 108 previous episodes can drive real light for free, untouched
- Go wireless with an ESP32 and UDP packets - almost identical code, just a different transport. Once your art produces an array of colours, how you ship them (cable, WiFi, ArtNet) is a swappable detail
- POWER is the thing that bites: 60mA per LED at full white means a 300-LED strip wants ~18 amps. Never run a big strip off USB. Budget the amps, buy a real 5V supply, inject power along long strips, and cap brightness in software so you can't accidentally hit full white
- Diffusion turns harsh LED dots into a soft continuous glow - frosted acrylic, ping pong balls, even baking paper. It's a real-world blur kernel; bigger gap = softer light. It's the difference between christmas lights and art
- Tie it together with episode 19's audio analysis and you get a physical audio visualiser pulsing on your wall. Old code, new output

So that's three machines now that take our code into the physical world - the plotter drew it, the laser cut it, and now light *animates* it. And notice the theme holding steady: almost nothing today was new maths. Noise, HSV colour, pixel reading, a coordinate map - all things we already owned, pointed at photons instead of a canvas. The strip is an array of colours, and we've been filling arrays of colours since episode 1.

But a flat panel of light is just the start. Once your code can drive lights and read sensors, it can throw images onto whole *buildings*, wrap them around your body, or live inside a little computer that costs less than lunch and runs your art forever. We're going to keep walking deeper into the room. Bring your curiosity - and maybe charge up that ESP32 :-).

Sallukes! Thanks for reading.

![Driving the Kashmir Circuit.jpg](https://waivio.nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com/c4d101fec9039916b9a38344cccbc508095649afb0ef3f06295284b09df68462)

Planning a road trip through Kashmir? The Kashmir Circuit offers breathtaking landscapes, smooth highways in many sections, winding mountain roads, and unforgettable stopovers. Popular routes cover Srinagar, Gulmarg, Pahalgam, Sonamarg, and nearby valleys, making it one of India's most scenic driving experiences.

Before you travel, check the latest road conditions, especially during winter and the monsoon, as weather can affect mountain routes. Start early each day, carry warm clothing, and allow extra time for sightseeing and photography.

Must-visit stopovers include **Dal Lake**, **Mughal Gardens**, **Gulmarg Gondola**, **Betaab Valley**, **Aru Valley**, **Thajiwas Glacier**, and the picturesque meadows around Sonamarg. Each destination offers a unique glimpse into Kashmir's natural beauty.

If you're travelling with family or a group, a [Tempo Traveller](https://delhitempotravels.com/)provides a comfortable and hassle-free way to explore the entire Kashmir Circuit while enjoying the flexibility to stop at viewpoints and attractions along the way.

title.title: 5 حيل ذكية في الديكور لتوسيع غرف النوم الصغيرة/ 5 Clever Decor Tricks to Expand Small Bedrooms
title.body:
اليوم بدي شارككن بعض الاسرار من مجالي بالتصميم الداخلي جميعنا يلاحظ أن المساحات الحديثة اصبحت اضيق وخاصة غرف النوم... لذلك كتبت لكم اليوم حيل بسيطة وذكية في الديكور لتمنح غرفكم مدى اوسع وشعور بالراحة.
Today, I want to share with you some insider secrets from my field of interior design. We all notice that modern living spaces are becoming more compact, especially bedrooms. That is why I wrote down these simple and smart decor hacks to give your rooms a wider sense of space and absolute comfort.
أولا: قوة الالوان: ركزوا على الوان الطلاء الدرجات الفاتحة مثل الابيض والسكري تمنح العين شعور بالاتساع وتجعل الغرفة تبدو مضيئة وكبيرة أكثر.
First: The Power of Colors: Pay close attention to your paint choices. Light shades like white and off-white give the eyes a sense of openness, making the room look brighter and much larger.
ثانيا: سحر المرايا: المرايا عنصر اساسي جدا بالغرف الصغيرة وضع مرآة كبيرة مقابل النافذة يعكس الضوء الطبيعي، وهذا يمنح المكان عمق ومساحة مضاعفة.
Second: The Magic of Mirrors: Mirrors are an absolute essential in small rooms. Placing a large mirror directly opposite a window reflects natural light, which instantly adds visual depth and doubles the perceived space.
ثالثا: والأهم اختيار الاثاث بذكاء: اختارو الاثاث الناعم والبسيط لاتضعوا خزانة ضخمة وكبيرة لانها ستستنزف نصف الغرفة استعينوا بالرفوف المعلقة لتوفير مساحة الارضية واعطاء الغرفة متنفس او خزانة صغيرة.
Third: Smart Furniture Selection: This is the most crucial step! Choose sleek and minimal furniture. Avoid oversized, bulky wardrobes that swallow up half the space. Instead, use floating shelves to free up floor space, giving the room a breathing area, or opt for smaller wardrobe designs.
رابعا: تعليق الستائر: نصيحة ذهبية قوموا بتتعليق الستائر من السقف إلى الارض توحي بان السقف اعلى والغرفة اكبر بكثير، وهي خدعة بصرية قوية في الديكور.
Fourth: Hanging Curtains: Here is a golden tip. Hang your curtains from the ceiling line all the way down to the floor. This powerful visual illusion tricks the eye into thinking the ceiling is higher and the room is significantly wider.
خامسا: توزيع الاضاءة: وهي الحيلة الأخيرة لا تعتمدوا على مصدر ضوء واحد بمنتصف السقف وزعوا الاضاءة باستخدام الاباجورات او الليد المخفي لأن تعدد مصادر الضوء يخفي الزوايا الضيقة.
Fifth: Layering the Lighting: This is our final trick. Never rely on a single light source in the middle of the ceiling. Distribute the light using lamps or hidden LED strips; having multiple light sources works beautifully to blur tight corners and boundaries.
نصيحة من القلب: أهم خطوة تخلصوا من الفوضى تماما تجنبوا وضع اي غرض ليس له مكان مخصص ولا تبالغوا في كثرة التحف والقطع الصغيرة في الغرف الضيقة لان كثرتها ترهق العين وتزيد من الشعور بالضيق.
A Heartfelt Tip: The most important step of all is to completely declutter. Avoid keeping any items that do not have a designated place and do not overdo it with accessories or small trinkets in tight rooms. Too many details strain the eyes and make the space feel restrictive

title.title: RVC Seed-coding: A prototype/experiment vibe-coding  alternative ?
title.body:
![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/pibara/23u5ZXxg9C1iDSzTopajrnvhdpFS5NC3sZGMSiCk4Pv3wq9xSzJXH8UAtYx9M8U1EwpYK.png)
(Image by Gemini AI)
This is the 4th post in this series on Reverse Vibe-Coding or RVC. The previous posts can be found here: 1) [The semi-manifesto](/hive-169321/@pibara/a-reverse-vibe-coding-semi-manifest) 2) [Workflow for refactoring](/hive-169321/@pibara/a-reverse-vibe-coding-workflow-for-refactoring) 3) [Context regarding reengaging with syntax, embracing provenance and more](/ai/@pibara/ai-for-software-engineering-about-asics-for-ai-reengaging-with-syntax-embracing-provenance-rvc-model-in-a-box-and-what-to-think) In this post we want to have a look at the concept of seed-coding as an alternative for vibe-coding for bigger experiments and non-PO prototyping. Seed-coding is something I ran into by accident independently of my RVC efforts. At first I thought its properties were not real, a pure chance fluke, but after about a work-week of experiments, it turned out seed-coding works. It is a human-time equivalent alternative for vibe-coding for bigger experiments and prototypes. Its maturity is still low enough that like many things in the RVC workflow every shop should find its own way in. Remember RVC isn't a hard workflow, it's an outline for building bespoke team-specific workflows, and as such seed-coding fits right in. # Where to use seed-coding | Type of work | who | timeframe | coding practice | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | new business logic | developer | - | 100% manual | | RVPP template/routing repo | developer | - | manual and/or [Lode Coding](https://fjzeit.github.io/coding/lode-coding-basics) | | refactoring | developer | - | RVPP-based | | scaffolding | developer | - | RVPP-based | | boilerplate | developer | - | RVPP-based | | living runnable specs | **product owner** | - | Vibe coding | | prototype | **product-owner** | - | Vibe-coding | | prototype | developer | - | **Seed-coding** | | experiments | developer | < half a day | Vibe-coding | | experiments | developer | > half a day | **Seed-coding** | Seed coding is filling only two slots in the Reverse-Vibe-Coding workflow. Note that the half-a-day threshold above is just indicative for now, more on that in the section about experiment results. Because we don't expect product owners to code, prototypes made by the PO don't qualify, but prototypes made by a developer are an important slot where seed-coding should come to its right. A second slot where seed-coding is valuable is when doing some code experiments, but not blanketly. Experiment results showed no benefit from seed-coding over vibe coding for experiments taking up significantly less than than half a working day of human time. # Code as intent for prototyping and experiments. Where with vibe-coding you try to express intent with natural language, English, asking the language model to translate your English intent into architecture, design and code, when doing seed-coding you manually create code, but the code isn't meant as implementation, instead it is meant to more accurately outline intent in the form of code. It is essential that you don't waste time on anything not intent conveying. It is in the instinct of trained developers to want to write good quality code, at least do some error handling, document with comments not just for intent, but for future maintenance. This is an urge you need to step over. All code should be a happy path. Worry about an off-by-one bug? Don't! Code doesn't compile? Spent 10 minutes max, if it's not enough, tough luck. It is useful to timebox the intent creation. One to two thirds of a workday worth of coding seems like a good sweetspot. Smaller and the benefits of seed coding over vibe coding evaporate, bigger and you will end up needing to get back into the flow the next working day on an uncompleted seed which is suboptimal from a human perspective. Tomorrow just starts a new timebox on another part of the prototype or bigger experiment. It is really important to stress we aren't trying to write prototype-pluss-grade code here, the model(s) will help us get there, we are purely codifying intent. # Intent-code to clean-ish experiment and proto-type code As we saw with the RVPP driven workflow for refactoring, the seed-coding flow too is a triage oriented workflow. But unlike the refactoring workflow, triage doesn't happen on variants, it happens on proposals. The flow is a multi-batch flow with triage interruptions for human interaction. Please note, the below four batch phases are **just an example** of a seed-coding agentic workflow. Think about and make your own bespoke phases. The only fundamentally RVC part of this example is the strong focus on triage as main human input and no unbounded repair rounds. ## Batch-phase 1: The smoke-test loop In the first batch phase, a small model phase for low drift deterministic results, we route the seed code to language models with prompts and repair loops, prompting the model to: 1) Embed the code to make it runnable as fuzztest commandline with built-in fuzz generator. 2) If a build is needed, build the fuzztest commandline tool 3) Do a minimal-fuzz smoketest run of the commandline tool and the fuzz generator. 4) Give the model up-to 8 chances to get past #3 After batch-phase 1, we have code that at least compiles and doesn't crash on minimum fuzzing. ## Batch-phase 2: adding error flows In the second phase we move our routing from our regular 15b..32b models to 70b or bigger models, more on that later, and we set think=true to enable reasoning. Using cloud models here can be a valid option. In this zero human batch we present the (potentially patched) seed code to two models and: 1) Ask model A and B to make a list of missing error flows, one line per flow. 2) Ask model A about model B's list to split up dual responsibility lines and vice versa 3) After merging the lines and shuffling them, ask model A to deduplicate 4) Ask model B to deduplicate. 5) For each error flow line, ask a 15b..32b model to implement the error flow and give it 8 tries to make sure it builds and survives the minimal fuzz. ## Triage-batch 3: high confidence bugs and code review issues Like the previous batch, we again use two bigger models in this step. We are very explicit we only want high-confidence code issues and bugs and ask both models for a one-line per issue code review. So we end up with two lists again that we treat similar up until and including the deduplication and with a boolean denoting if it's a bug. We ask model C to write a regression test to show that the bugs are real and unconfirmed bugs are removed from the list. At this point we bring a human into the loop and ask the human to go through the list as triage and remove the lines we don't need. Then we: 1) Ask model C to address the bug or issue 2) Make sure the build and minimum fuzz test still work and the regression test now succeeds. 3) Repeat up to 8 times until #2 passes ## Batch-phase 4: Fuzz testing Now for the last batch, here we actually run the fuzz test for a few hours and make a collection of inputs that made the fuzz test trigger. We present the results from the fuzz test to a model and ask it to group the triggers into likely related clusters. 1) Ask the model to describe the bug underlie a cluster in a single line 2) Ask the model to fix the bug 3) Re-run the fuzz triggers 4) Repeat max 8 times until #3 passes # Bigger and cloud models for seed-coding So how to choose between the usual 15b..32b range local models and routing of most of the RVPP bits of RVC and the >70b range models and cloud frontier models common in vibe-coding? The trick is that larger excel in finding things. Bugs, solutions, etc while smaller models are way better at producing reliable and reproducible results from canned prompts and prompt templates. You could say small models obey better but they won’t from my experience suggest an out of memory error flow or point out code that isn’t necessarily wrong ‘yet’, but is fragile. It is always advised to pick the smallest model that can do the job, but as a rule of thumb, when you want to use a 70b+ model or even a frontier cloud model or a 300b+ local model, it will usually be just before you introduce a human triage step, If you find yourself choosing a 300b+ model and after it has done it’s thing there is no human triage in sight, it might be a good idea to experiment with 70b+ or even a 15b..30b+ range model. # Fuzz testing and regression testing as main testing handles in seed-coding Because we are “only” making a prototype or an addition to our experiment library, the TDD bit of this part of the RVC workflow doesn’t need to be anywhere close to perfect. The focus is on relatively clean inspirational code that **wont** make it to production but that **will** convey the ideas we need to start with clean hand-written business logic later in the process. As we discussed in earlier posts, unit tests and agentic loops don’t mix, and for production level code we need extensive property testing, but for prototypes and experiments we are going for the quick low-human-effort wins, and regression tests (for validating bugs were actually there and checking they **might** be solved), fuzz tests, and smoke-tests are all we logically need for the level of quality we are aiming for. It is important to note that we don’t actually make smoke tests. Instead we turn down the fuzz generator to a uselessly small burst from a fuzz testing perspective and call that the smoke test. It is relatively easy for a language model to autonomously write a fuzz test and fuzz generator for your code, and computer time comes cheap, so let the fuzz test rip for an hour, or two if you like. We don’t pretend it will find all the bugs, but if there are glaring ones that the LLM reviews didn’t spot, chances are the fuzz tests will tease them out with zero need for human interaction. # Experiment results and limitations: vibe-coding vs seed coding So far this post asked you to believe me on my big amber eyes, and I must admit the threshold value in the table of when to use vibe coding and when to use seed-coding is currently chosen on too little and too narrow data. I’m just a single person with a limited amount of time available for doing things in a scientifically sufficient way, but I am a data guy, so I make do with the hours I have available. For this subject, it was a well filled week where I ran 10 coding sessions in pairs or two. My first experiment was just a what-if thing. I had set up most of the experiment code improvement pipeline on my new homelab Forgejo server, and I wanted to test the idea: “Hey, what if I try to let an LLM write all the error flow code” ? I did just that. I took a bit of hash based signature ideas and coded it in Python, no error handling whatsoever, all prototype level. Took me 3:30 to code. Add 30 minutes for the triage bits and manual tuning, and two hours of machine time, mostly spent on fuzzing, and I had what turned out to be a useful base. The result: Pretty good error handling code, a few bugs found by the LLM, one by the fuzz test, but what stood out most was the error flow code didn't have the usual vibe-coded smell. Then I got curious: What If I try to vibe-code the same code. I was ready for the vibe coded version to win because it was tainted by my knowledge from running this pipeline, so I thought about a comparable setup. I decided to spend 4 hours vibe coding, make sure the vibe generator created by the first run would fit, and then plug things into the bugfind/bugfix and fuzz part of the pipeline directly. The result: * 55% more lines of code not counting spacing and comments. * Equal amount of bugs found by the LLM * Three distinct bugs found and fixed by fuzz testing. * The vibe-code code-smell was back, undeniably At this point I didn’t know what to think, My seed code was still relatively clean, so I wasn’t sure. I decided I needed to do a second and a third run. I stuck to python and crypto related things, and I found two subjects that I had worked with earlier. But I decided to dial down the quality meter of my own seed code. For my second attempt this was easy because I ran out of time on my self imposed 3:30 timebox and I ended up running the run with non-compiling code (a adjusted the pipeline to handle that). After the three runs, the first 55% more lines of code had reduced to 45%, and the other findings pretty much centered around my first attempt. Now I had three data points that all agreed, but they all used the same time window. So my next question to myself was: “What if the time prompting/seed-coding was significantly longer or shorter. So I thought about two other problems to experiment with. For the first I halved the prompting and the seed-coding time to 1:45 and 2:00 respectively, and for the other experiment I doubled it to 7:00 and 8:00. Results: Both vibe-coding and seed-coding results got a little bit worse, nut the scaled ‘relative’ numbers for the long version fit right in. It was a little bit above the mean on the important metric, but well below the best of three for the three base experiments. In conclusion, throwing more time at the comparison doesn’t make seed-coding less better than vibe-coding on the quality of the outcome with equal human hours invested. The 1:45 and 2:00 results though weren’t as positive. In fact, the difference between the vibe-coding result and the seed-coding result was roughly zero, and seed-coding was even worse on one point. The below table shows the vibe-coding version of the experiment against the seed-coding version: | experiment | human time | LOC | LLM bugs found | fuzzing buggs found (vibe/seed)| | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | | hash-based signatures WOTS | 4h | 155% | Equal | 4/1 | | json-rpc & ecdsa | 4h | 130% | Equal | 4/2 | | certificates & ecdsa | 4h | 150% | Equal | 1/0 | | hash-based signatures WOTS + Merkle-tree | 8h | 150% | Equal | 5/2 | | hash based crypto, rumpeltree & aes | 2h | 105% | 50% | 1/1 | It is important to note that the code in my benchmark was all code experiments, not full prototypes, it was all python, and it was all code without any kind of GUI, so do with this what you must and run your own experiments to find the right thresholds for choosing between vibe-coding and seed-coding for experiments and prototypes in **your** workflow. # About the inspiration wall that we won't climb. As stated before, I started my experiment while playing with my new homelab Forgejo server. I’m configuring this server as separate from my RVPP git server (that I hope to move to Forgejo too at some point in the future) because RVC values provenance very highly and seed- and vibe-coding are very casual with generated code. Unless we would limit ourselves to starcoder alone, what isn’t a pleasant option, vibe coded and seed-coded code contain relatively free form LLM generated code bits that are likely to contain more or less regurgitated code bits from restrictively licenced open source training data. While fitting in strong due diligence into an RVC workflow is a valid choice, it brings in a lot of technical and logistical overhead. For that reason RVC advocates defaulting to a so called **inspiration wall**, a git-server where the code from prototypes and experiments lives as a relatively decent quality wall with inspiration. You don’t copy from the wall, you look at the wall, get expired, then go and hand-write initial business logic. One way to create an inspiration wall is to disable direct git interaction with the experiments and prototypes git server, make it web-only. How you make your inspiration wall is up to you, but consider that copyright and quality concerns make it a solid choice to forgo with the need for due diligence by simply not allowing experiment and prototype code to find its way into production other than through inspiration for human developers. # Conclusion In this post we discuss an RVC sub-workflow that I ran into by pure chance. I resisted my findings from a natural repulsion from the poor coding practices seed-coding not only allows but actually demands. It feels quite unnatural to ignore good coding practices, but in the end you aren’t really coding, you are using code to express intent. I admit that more data is needed to determine when to use vibe-coding for experiments and prototypes and when seed-coding gives better results as shown in my experiments. Nevertheless I think seed-coding deserves its place within the RVC framework, and maybe it has its use outside or RVC as well.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) is currently attracting increasing interest due to its ability to produce extraordinary masterpieces, one of which is an AI-generated image from a photo with just a prompt.

To create hyper-realistic images that can be used for various social media platforms, you only need a prompt that suits your needs.

In this article, I'll try to create a masterpiece photo that you might want to try and use on various social media platforms.
How to Create an AI Cinematic Portrait:
1. Open ChatGpt, Gemini AI, or Dola AI
2. Upload Your Photo
3. Paste the Prompt
4. Open, Save, and Post Your Cinematic Portrait.
Prompt:

This Netflix-style, ultra-realistic, cinematic fantasy portrait of an IMAX-quality, 9:16 vertical composition creates a stunning scene of a mountain lake at golden dusk. A skilled painter (referring to the face in the photo) stands waist-deep in the still, reflective waters, wearing a worn black hat, sunglasses, and a slightly wrinkled pale gray linen shirt with rolled-up sleeves. He holds a wooden paint palette filled with vibrant colors in one hand while painting with a brush in the other. His face conveys deep creative focus, quiet intensity, and serene artistic devotion.

The most important detail is that the young man (referring to the face in the photo) in the lake should not look like a real person lying under or in the water. Instead, the image should appear like a large-scale portrait painted directly on the water's surface, like liquid oil paint and artistic pigments floating on the lake, as if the water itself has become a living canvas.

The face should resemble a beautiful work of art, with visible brushstroke textures, soft, blending edges of pigment, flowing strokes of color, a subtle canvas-like artistry, and the distortion of the water reflecting light, while still maintaining strong masculine features and striking visual appeal.

His skin should have a smooth, warm, natural tone, depicted as a painterly effect with a very clean texture, subtle highlights, and elegant, artistic shading. His expressive eyes should remain softly open with a calm, thoughtful gaze, his lips relaxed, and his dark hair dissolved in swirls of flowing paint and colorful reflections, rather than realistic wet hair.

The man's clearly painted face should be positioned diagonally and horizontally in the lower water area, with his forehead and eye area closest to the painter's brush, while his chin and lips are away from it, making it visually correct, as if the painter were adding details to the upper part of the face. The tip of the brush should touch the painted forehead and eye area, creating realistic circular ripples that radiate outward.

Rich pigments bloom around the portrait in vibrant reds, blues, oranges, yellows, turquoises, and whites. The entire portrait should feel like a magical watercolor masterpiece, not a submerged human.

The backdrop features misty Alps, silhouetted pine forests, a soft golden sunrise sky, radiant sunlight reflecting off a lake, a thin atmospheric mist, distant birds, and a beautiful morning fog.

Cinematic light falls beautifully on the painter's face, sleeves, hands, palette, and painted water portrait, creating magical highlights, subtle shadows, and rich artistic contrasts.

Extremely rich cinematic color processing with warm golden yellow sunlight, cool reflective lake tones, vibrant floating pigments, cinematic golden fog, HDR lighting, global illumination, a premium wide-angle portrait lens, photorealistic rendering with a surreal painting illusion, masterpiece quality, ultra-detailed textures, and 8K production detail.

Negative Notes: Realistic drowned man, realistic body underwater, underwater face, wrong face orientation, distorted portrait, extra hands, blurry eyes, uneven skin tone, weak paint effect, flat lighting, messy reflections, cartoonish, anime, CGI look, text, watermark, logo, low quality.
