title.title: Film Review: Dune (2021)
title.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/h3HsfV8Kn9Sz2QWUYYdP5ya23hx.jpg)


Few works of science fiction literature have proved to be as inspiring and intriguing as *Dune*, Frank Herbert's 1965 novel. Its popularity has reflected not only in a long-standing novel series or a video game that helped develop an entire new RTS genre, but also through three high-profile and very distinct screen adaptations. The first, [David Lynch's 1984 film](https://peakd.com/film/@drax/retro-film-review-dune-1984), received a cult status despite being disowned by its creators, while [the 2000 television miniseries](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/television-review-frank-herbert-s), although highly regarded, was considered not grand enough for those who believed that Herbert's classic could be given justice only through a grand epic on the big screen. The efforts to redo *Dune* in a \

way finally bore fruit with the 2021 film by Denis Villeneuve, which, despite critical and commercial success, in many ways embodies some of the most annoying things about twenty-first-century Hollywood.\n\nThe main problem Villeneuve faced when he tackled the new and ambitious adaptation was the epic scope of Herbert's novel. The 1984 version was a feature film, and, despite enormous efforts to be faithful to the source and provide fan service to readers, it compressed and rushed much of the plot. The 2000 miniseries was more suitable for the task with its multi-part format but faced limitations of budget and production, looking, at times, like a stage play. Villeneuve tried to square this circle with a simple solution: he would make the film in two parts, attempting to exploit the best of both worlds. Yet this solution came with a caveat: the first part was produced as a sort of test run, with the second part to be put into production only if the first proved commercially viable. This meant that fans of *Dune* and the film itself had to wait years for the conclusion of the saga to arrive. This practice made *Dune* look conspicuously like Hollywood adaptations of popular Young Adult fantasy and science fiction series that had been all the rage in the previous decade. The cynical, risk-averse approach of \

is precisely the kind of corporate thinking that has drained much of the artistry from modern blockbuster filmmaking.\n\nThe script, co-written by Villeneuve, Jon Spaihts and Eric Roth, follows roughly the plot of the first half of the novel. It begins in the year 10191, when the known universe is ruled by an Imperium – a political entity ruled by an Emperor, but with power also shared by the great noble houses, the Spacing Guild, and the order Bene Gesserit. \

is the nickname for Arrakis, the desert planet where the Spice – a psychoactive substance necessary for space travel – is mined, giving ultimate power to whoever controls it. Until recently, Arrakis was ruled by House Harkonnen, whose leader, Baron Vladimir (played by Stellan Skarsgård), is the sworn enemy of House Atreides, led by Duke Leto (played by Oscar Isaac). However, the Emperor has recently switched control of Arrakis to the Atreides, but Leto is wary, suspecting a trap. He, his concubine Lady Jessica (played by Rebecca Ferguson), and their teenage son Paul (played by Timothée Chalamet) arrive on the planet, where Leto tries to forge an alliance with the Fremen, mysterious desert-dwelling locals who have learned to hate outworlders and savagely resisted the Harkonnens. The Duke is betrayed by his physician Dr. Yueh (played by Chang Chen), which allows the Harkonnens, with the help of Imperial Sardaukar troops, to attack, overwhelm the Atreides force and retake the planet. The Duke is killed, while Jessica and Paul are left in the desert to die. Paul, with his mother's Bene Gesserit training, manages to capture an ornithopter and escape. They manage to reach a band of Fremen led by Stilgar (played by Javier Bardem), which also includes a young woman called Chani (played by Zendaya), who was part of his visions.

Whether you will like or dislike the film depends very much on whether you have seen the previous two versions before. Most of the contemporary audience – especially the younger generations to whom this film, one of the more ambitious Warner Bros. projects of the decade, is tailored – is probably unaware of previous adaptations. For them, Villeneuve's *Dune* is more likely to be hailed as a grand film, unlike the hair-splitting grognards who remember what came before. This is a convenient strategy: by aiming at an audience with no frame of reference, the filmmakers can get away with shortcomings that would be immediately obvious to those familiar with the source material or earlier adaptations.

To be fair, Villeneuve did try to do some things differently, and some of those differences are definitely an improvement over the two previous versions. The extremely high budget resulted in much more spectacular yet believable scenes, which, together with Villeneuve's eye for visuals and great care with costumes, sets and production design, makes the film truly impressive in a strictly technical sense. There is also a great deal of effort in worldbuilding, and, for example, David J. Peterson, the creator of constructed languages for *Game of Thrones*, actually made the Harkonnen, Sardaukar and other factions speak their own languages. The film looks and sounds expensive, and in an era where visual spectacle is often the primary selling point, this cannot be dismissed.

Yet, at the same time, Villeneuve abhors exposition, and tries to make dialogue as sparse and laconic as possible, making the film difficult for anyone not already familiar with Herbert's world. This also narrows the space for the new cast to show some of their range, which, for example, makes Timothée Chalamet less impressive and less believable as Paul Atreides than Kyle MacLachlan was four decades earlier. MacLachlan, in Lynch's flawed but passionate film, managed to convey the inner turmoil, the prophetic visions, and the gradual transformation from sheltered noble youth to messianic leader. Chalamet, by contrast, spends much of the film staring into the middle distance with a blank expression, his character's interiority sacrificed on the altar of Villeneuve's minimalist aesthetic. The supporting cast fares little better: Oscar Isaac and Rebecca Ferguson do what they can with the material, but the script gives them little to work with beyond functional dialogue.

Another issue with the film is the rather forgettable music score by Hans Zimmer. The main lamentation theme, which repeats ad nauseam throughout the film, sounds more annoying than it adds atmosphere. Zimmer, usually a reliable composer, seems to have mistaken loud, droning noise for emotional depth. Compare this to the haunting, otherworldly soundtrack of Lynch's film by the band Toto and Brian Eno, which, whatever its flaws, was memorable and distinctive. Villeneuve's score is merely functional and, at times, actively distracting.

Some of the criticisms directed at the film concern minor alterations to Herbert's source material. The character of Dr. Liet Kynes, originally a male, was cast as a Black woman, played by Sharon Duncan-Brewster. This decision, which many saw as another example of modern Hollywood pushing DEI quotas and a \
agenda, was perhaps inevitable considering that the main plot point would have been, regardless, attacked by many ideologically driven critics as an unacceptable \

narrative. The irony is that by pre-emptively caving to such criticism, the filmmakers ended up alienating another segment of the audience while satisfying no one. The gender and race swap adds nothing to the story and feels like a checkbox exercise rather than a creative choice.

*Dune*, which, like many films of its time, had its release postponed because of the COVID-19 crisis, had decent commercial success – just enough to warrant the second part, which was released in 2024. The third part, based on Herbert's 1969 novel *Dune Messiah* and titled *Dune: Part Three*, is scheduled for release later in 2026. One cannot help but feel that the entire project has been structured around commercial viability rather than artistic vision. The first film feels like a prologue, a teaser, a proof of concept designed to convince the studio to greenlight the real story. This is no way to adapt a classic.

In conclusion, Villeneuve's *Dune* is a technically accomplished but narratively hollow film that exemplifies the worst tendencies of modern blockbuster filmmaking: risk aversion disguised as ambition, minimalism mistaken for sophistication, and corporate calculation passed off as artistic patience. It is a film for an audience that has never read the book and never seen the earlier adaptations – which is, conveniently, the largest possible audience. For those who love Herbert's novel, it is a frustrating experience: beautiful to look at, but ultimately unsatisfying, a half-told story that asks for patience it has not earned.


RATING: 5/10 (++)

title.title: [ENG/ESP] A trip to Santa Cruz, north of Havana, Cuba
title.body:
>Once again, we left the institute for fieldwork to investigate one of the most beautiful ecosystems in western Cuba, located in Mayabeque, the country's youngest province.

As I often explain, these trips are more than just work; they represent an opportunity to discover the country's natural wonders and be in direct contact with the environment. Here are some more photos from my work, research, and leisure trips. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPnhbDRPzbdbLLdrP3xdqSkHJvgmNJWudRCtRXFXS8reP/cte_de_santa_cruz_desde_punta_j_jira.jpg) **Welcome to Santa Cruz del Norte** Santa Cruz del Norte, on the northern coast of Mayabeque, is a place that reveals itself as a bridge between geography and memory. My personal research journey to this municipality began with the certainty that every corner holds a story, and that its geographical features are more than just shapes: they are symbols of identity. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdZo7eqEMu4kEnUbibJN59FxziVQyiyo9Gm4hRDo4EqkK/carso_costero_en_pe_as_altas.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQdBksMkX6cnjZzN12sH7R1LoAhESgwaE5r1CggAmNKkk/costa_de_punta_j_jira.jpg) Located about 45 kilometers east of Havana, Santa Cruz del Norte opens onto the sea with beaches that, although less well-known than those of Varadero, possess a serene and authentic quality. Its light-colored sands and constant waves invite contemplation rather than the tourist bustle. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVByBKM59PEUa5vGt2xAa5vQ4Z1Nth3SBQyia3fmob6cC/cueva_de_la_desiluci_n.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQMFH4oUjuwvrJ2HYxUE48qHxiYMUrbuXurtAaazvnrLd/playa_jibacoa.jpg) The typically tropical climate offers warm temperatures year-round, with sea breezes that temper the humidity and make the place ideal for relaxation and field research. The hydrography is defined by the mouth of the Santa Cruz River, which brings freshness and life to the area, and by the proximity of coastal formations that reveal the interaction between sea and land. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZYWAhZzQWDJdNmWvuR4mnrcxq2uKdvmj5VrcH3WBtmNJ/pe_n_del_fraile.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSA1XJyQMyfMg9oAzdQz1Puasv7wzdJfNd1EtAGxWV52S/agujas_de_romanal_jibacoa.jpg) Among the most prominent geographical features is Peñón del Fraile, a rock formation that rises like a guardian along the coast. Its importance is not only scenic: it is a cultural and natural symbol. For us, their visit represented an encounter with the history and spirituality of the country. The Peñón has been a landmark for fishermen, travelers, and communities who recognize it as a point of reference and a place steeped in legend. Its shape, resembling the silhouette of a friar, evokes contemplation and resilience, reminding us that geography can also be a metaphor for life. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeZN6SfDrewY3GSp7p65GSgsJqi3BBgiaBWEZe4yg8zv4/la_costa_en_punta_j_jira.jpg) Walking along its beaches and observing the Peñón del Fraile was, in my experience, an act of connection with the nation. There I understood that Cuba is not only defined by its large cities or its most famous tourist destinations, but also by these enclaves where nature and culture intertwine. Santa Cruz del Norte, with its mild climate, secluded beaches, and unique geographical features, speaks to a country that thrives on the diversity of its landscapes. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYaphLwrD2VbukxEMB6wRhiidw5T9nnGMerEWhNDX9pb3/cueva_de_las_cenizas_o_de_los_bandoleros.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQcBpVaxBfXcdd6c5tu7QjoA14JHdeDhoeQHrtz9nLnax/terraza_marina_al_oeste_de_santa_cruz_del_norte.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeooBSrVnMeq98nM6ChMxSdyCj5GxghB8B4iPcG7NSuzm/terraza_marina_entre_pe_as_altas_y_santa_cruz_del_norte.jpg) **A final comment** The The trip, beyond the research, became a time for reflection. El Peñón del Fraile is not just a rock: it is a symbol of permanence, of resistance against time and the tides. For Cuba, it serves as a reminder that national identity is also built in these seemingly small spaces, yet laden with meaning. And for us, their visit was an act of recognition and gratitude toward the land that sustains us. *Note: I used DeepL Translate*. *The images are my own*. ***ESPAÑOL*** **Una introducción necesaria** Nuevamente salimos del instituto en trabajo de campo para investigar uno de los ecosistemas más bonitos del occidente del país ubicado en Mayabaque, la provincia más joven de Cuba. Como acostumbro a explicar, estos viajes más que trabajo representan una oportunidad de conocer las maravillas naturales del país y estar en contacto directo con el medio ambiente. Aquí les dejo otros de mis viaje de trabajo, investigación y esparcimiento. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPnhbDRPzbdbLLdrP3xdqSkHJvgmNJWudRCtRXFXS8reP/cte_de_santa_cruz_desde_punta_j_jira.jpg) **Bienvenidos a Santa Cruz del Norte** Santa Cruz del Norte, en la costa norte de Mayabeque, es un lugar que se descubre como un puente entre la geografía y la memoria. Mi viaje de investigación personal hacia este municipio comenzó con la certeza de que cada rincón guarda una historia, y que sus accidentes geográficos son más que simples formas: son símbolos de identidad. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdZo7eqEMu4kEnUbibJN59FxziVQyiyo9Gm4hRDo4EqkK/carso_costero_en_pe_as_altas.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQdBksMkX6cnjZzN12sH7R1LoAhESgwaE5r1CggAmNKkk/costa_de_punta_j_jira.jpg) Ubicado a unos 45 kilómetros al este de La Habana, Santa Cruz del Norte se abre al mar con playas que, aunque menos conocidas que las de Varadero, poseen una calidad serena y auténtica. Sus arenas claras y el oleaje constante invitan a la contemplación más que al bullicio turístico. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVByBKM59PEUa5vGt2xAa5vQ4Z1Nth3SBQyia3fmob6cC/cueva_de_la_desiluci_n.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQMFH4oUjuwvrJ2HYxUE48qHxiYMUrbuXurtAaazvnrLd/playa_jibacoa.jpg) El clima, típicamente tropical, regala temperaturas cálidas durante todo el año, con brisas marinas que suavizan la humedad y hacen del lugar un espacio propicio para el descanso y la investigación de campo. La hidrografía está marcada por la desembocadura del río Santa Cruz, que aporta frescura y vida a la zona, y por la cercanía de formaciones costeras que revelan la interacción entre mar y tierra. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZYWAhZzQWDJdNmWvuR4mnrcxq2uKdvmj5VrcH3WBtmNJ/pe_n_del_fraile.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSA1XJyQMyfMg9oAzdQz1Puasv7wzdJfNd1EtAGxWV52S/agujas_de_romanal_jibacoa.jpg) Entre los accidentes geográficos más relevantes, destaca el Peñón del Fraile, una formación rocosa que se levanta como guardián frente al litoral. Su importancia no es solo paisajística: es un símbolo cultural y natural. Para nosotros, su visita representó un encuentro con la historia y la espiritualidad del país. El Peñón ha sido referencia para pescadores, viajeros y comunidades que lo reconocen como un hito de orientación y como un espacio cargado de leyendas. Su figura, semejante a la silueta de un fraile, evoca recogimiento y resistencia, recordándonos que la geografía también puede ser metáfora de la vida. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeZN6SfDrewY3GSp7p65GSgsJqi3BBgiaBWEZe4yg8zv4/la_costa_en_punta_j_jira.jpg) Caminar por sus playas y observar el Peñón del Fraile fue, en mi experiencia, un acto de conexión con la nación. Allí comprendí que Cuba no solo se define por sus grandes ciudades o por sus destinos turísticos más famosos, sino también por estos enclaves donde la naturaleza y la cultura se entrelazan. Santa Cruz del Norte, con su clima benévolo, sus playas discretas y sus accidentes geográficos singulares, nos habla de un país que se sostiene en la diversidad de sus paisajes. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYaphLwrD2VbukxEMB6wRhiidw5T9nnGMerEWhNDX9pb3/cueva_de_las_cenizas_o_de_los_bandoleros.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQcBpVaxBfXcdd6c5tu7QjoA14JHdeDhoeQHrtz9nLnax/terraza_marina_al_oeste_de_santa_cruz_del_norte.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeooBSrVnMeq98nM6ChMxSdyCj5GxghB8B4iPcG7NSuzm/terraza_marina_entre_pe_as_altas_y_santa_cruz_del_norte.jpg) **Un comentario final** El viaje, más allá de la investigación, se convirtió en reflexión. El Peñón del Fraile no es únicamente una roca: es un símbolo de permanencia, de resistencia frente al tiempo y las mareas. Para Cuba, significa un recordatorio de que la identidad nacional se construye también en estos espacios aparentemente pequeños, pero cargados de significado. Y para nosotros, su visita fue un acto de reconocimiento y gratitud hacia la tierra que nos sostiene. *Nota: Utilicé el traductor DeepL Translate*. *Las imágenes son de mi propiedad*. 23.15037 lat, -81.92814 long. 22.79515 lat, -82.43594 long. 23.11823 lat, -82.36453 long.

title.title: [ESP/ENG] Recordando mi presentación en Hive: El eco de una nueva vida
title.body:
Cuando crucé el umbral de @hive hace tres años, no venía nada ni con un destino claro. Llegaba cargada con el peso de más de cuarenta años de trabajo, con las manos aún temblorosas por el reciente cese del ruido docente de la rutina. La jubilación, ese gran silencio, me había devuelto a mí misma, pero también me había dejado frente a un espejo que no sabía cómo mirar. Y entonces, como quien encuentra una ventana en un cuarto cerrado, apareció esta plataforma.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma1yvPTn66kQLF93cxLYjWdpSujSCzjZSdTGKhSdhePvb/screenshot_2026_06_29_at_13_56_46_my_hive_intro.png)


Al principio, Hive fue un territorio desconocido, un bosque de nodos y claves privadas donde mi voz parecía un susurro perdido. Pero pronto entendí que no se trataba de ser escuchada por muchos, sino de encontrar mi propia frecuencia. Cada publicación se convirtió en un cimiento con el que reconstruía mi identidad más allá del oficio. Ya no era la profesional de décadas, sino la narradora de mis días, la observadora de las pequeñas grandes cosas que antes pasaban de largo por la prisa.

El significado emocional de esta travesía ha sido profundo. Aquí he encontrado una comunidad que no me juzga por mi pasado, sino que valora mi presente. Los votos y los comentarios no son monedas, sino abrazos digitales que me recuerdan que sigo siendo útil, que mi experiencia tiene eco y que mi creatividad no ha caducado. Hive me ha devuelto la curiosidad que creía perdida y me ha regalado el placer de aprender cada día, ya sea sobre arte, tecnología o la simple poesía de una fotografía.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVrFzBak7LLvGwkLQbpBkmjYRhUQyn29cJynwP9mcS8sm/img_20241121_wa0020.jpg)





Pero quizás lo más valioso ha sido el desarrollo integral. Hive me ha obligado a ordenar mis pensamientos, a escribir con claridad y a exponerme con honestidad. Ese ejercicio diario ha sido mi gimnasia mental, mi terapia y mi bitácora. 

Al compartir mis reflexiones, he descubierto que mi visión de la vida se ha ensanchado: ya no veo el mundo desde la cima de una carrera, sino desde el llano fértil de la experiencia compartida. He aprendido a escuchar tanto como a hablar, a valorar la diversidad y a entender que cada usuario es un universo con su propia historia.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWHKLRu8qYBrZxqJYVQc8Z4WivXxyTDdksxjW1iajkBbp/img_20230826_132311.jpg)

Tres años después, miro hacia atrás y veo que no solo he contribuido a Hive; Hive ha contribuido a mi bienestar. Me ha dado estructura en el caos del retiro, propósito en la aparente quietud y, sobre todo, la certeza de que aún tengo mucho que decir. 

Esta plataforma no ha sido una distracción, sino una extensión de mi ser, un lugar donde la jubilada que fui se encuentra con la creadora a que siempre llevé dentro. Y hoy, más que nunca, sé que mi viaje aquí apenas comienza.


Créditos: Las imágenes son de mi álbum personal.
Como no domino el idioma inglés utilicé traductor de Google.


ENGLISH


When I crossed the threshold of @hive three years ago, I came with nothing and no clear destination. I arrived burdened by the weight of over forty years of work, my hands still trembling from the recent cessation of the daily grind of teaching. Retirement, that great silence, had returned me to myself, but it had also left me facing a mirror I didn't know how to look at. And then, like someone finding a window in a closed room, this platform appeared.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma1yvPTn66kQLF93cxLYjWdpSujSCzjZSdTGKhSdhePvb/screenshot_2026_06_29_at_13_56_46_my_hive_intro.png)

At first, Hive was uncharted territory, a forest of nodes and private keys where my voice seemed like a lost whisper. But I soon understood that it wasn't about being heard by many, but about finding my own frequency. Each post became a foundation upon which I rebuilt my identity beyond my profession. I was no longer the professional of decades past, but the narrator of my days, the observer of the small yet significant things that I used to miss in my haste.

The emotional significance of this journey has been profound. Here I've found a community that doesn't judge me for my past, but values ​​my present. Votes and comments aren't currency, but digital hugs that remind me I'm still useful, that my experience resonates, and that my creativity hasn't expired. Hive has rekindled a curiosity I thought I'd lost and given me the joy of learning every day, whether about art, technology, or the simple poetry of a photograph.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVrFzBak7LLvGwkLQbpBkmjYRhUQyn29cJynwP9mcS8sm/img_20241121_wa0020.jpg)

But perhaps the most valuable aspect has been my holistic development. Hive has forced me to organize my thoughts, to write clearly, and to express myself honestly. This daily exercise has been my mental workout, my therapy, and my journal.

By sharing my reflections, I've discovered that my perspective on life has broadened: I no longer see the world from the summit of a career, but from the fertile ground of shared experience. I've learned to listen as much as to speak, to value diversity, and to understand that each user is a universe with their own story.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWHKLRu8qYBrZxqJYVQc8Z4WivXxyTDdksxjW1iajkBbp/img_20230826_132311.jpg)

Three years later, I look back and see that I haven't just contributed to Hive; Hive has contributed to my well-being. It has given me structure in the chaos of retirement, purpose in the apparent stillness, and above all, the certainty that I still have much to say.

This platform hasn't been a distraction, but an extension of myself, a place where the retiree I once was meets the creator I've always carried within. And today, more than ever, I know that my journey here is just beginning.

Credits: The images are from my personal album. Since I don't speak English fluently, I used Google Translate.

title.title: Hidden Lagoon – Exploring and hiking in a natural setting 📷 Málaga – Spain
title.body:
> --- >I always love seeking out new challenges to explore, new things, new places, learning a little more each time. Not only does it keep my brain active, but it also allows me to discover new places in nature and see landscapes that are different from those I usually visit. --- ![20260628_214706.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xAgetkmSWqvhZkYzGpJGCUDEieD1aF2TCP1dnCY7DoJNpZWRELxNxCBeDu4XZTgqHDz.jpg) --- Quite some time ago, whilst looking for natural areas in or near the city, I spotted a large area on the map that I’d never visited before, and, what’s more, it hadn’t even crossed my mind that there might be anything special there. I was wrong. There is a large river that runs through much of the province of Málaga and flows into the city of Málaga itself; this is the River Guadalhorce. Right at its mouth lies a natural area that remains in its wild state, largely untouched by human intervention. Of course, there is some human presence, as there are beaches and neighbourhoods nearby, but a certain part of the area is very well protected. --- ![20260623_183843.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/246axcdgPPAYoUpy5TUSUfvcK6SGN97xUCbypcPh7fwCDUxHSkdWQvxYDY57jXg6DyVSy.jpg) ![20260623_183845.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23rzAuHe8KBpybuBNs2UHQPuSxsdckFneEvzBYgZLNysgqxJYxtZKSz7nBD3G9ELR41ck.jpg) ![20260623_183851.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/246azu5kQtQ7DoieGXbfJicLPt4uXVwTEYAjGFVJ58rGJVs4bpJCGbhWNizVxa1qGyLZN.jpg) ![20260623_183903.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23uQvwfEou4akXhbGVTPkyME8MXMx7p6XLqgHnHHNz6K6iKRuFPkbsF1g8HMsJhvZs5n4.jpg) --- It is a nature reserve covering 64 hectares, situated on a large island at the river’s mouth, which itself spans 122 hectares. Naturally, it is impossible to explore the entire area in a single day, but I decided to make several visits to get to know the place. The large island, which is home to the nature reserve, has numerous protected lagoons and, depending on their depth and location, is home to a wide variety of birds. I was really excited to explore this place and, a few days ago, I paid my first visit, knowing absolutely nothing about this part of the city. To get there, I took two buses, as it’s quite a few kilometres away from the city centre; it’s situated to the west, very close to the airport, almost on the outskirts of the city. --- ![20260623_183722.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xp4L7M6zYFc5bqet229CN7amq7yHFVYGFvDQQ3bB4tMhAKH85MetxdTDZY86bnDMzhc.jpg) ![20260623_184311.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23vYjtRpb9Njr6fU1ZYwENUCV2ZWo4ApAkSFh1K7wnr52gjMARkmTHNRpiXBLER4v5hZw.jpg) ![20260623_184446.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23sdhcPxcecfpB1o7aNrBus13Yue6qABRogpDS4STU7k6wb8BCM35gKvuJCBBgQcjDoYT.jpg) ![20260623_184450.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23zvPkukVVD7qNjSYkR6bYufKro2FdupBL8P7nYKdLMBnJ7xnGAPc2Uagzcu95YfjMBt3.jpg) ![20260623_184507.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/242rwdLtsZ8dKhgPsVyimaB4gL3R9quBC1Gj2jh5ntVEx5XuiKoYVs21TGtA4jb3wp5d7.jpg) --- After getting off the second bus, I walked quite a distance until I reached the first signpost, but I still had a long way to go before reaching the entrance to the nature reserve. This signpost describes the routes along the mouth of the River Guadalhorse, which begins at Sacaba Beach. The paths aren’t tarmacked, except for the bridge crossing one of the river’s branches, and I could see vegetation different from what I’m used to, everywhere I looked, both before reaching the nature reserve and within it, from poplars, eucalyptus trees, taraje trees, reeds, sea lilies, cane, rushes and more. The sign announced the presence of the lagoons I mentioned earlier and their respective birdwatching hides, as this place is one of the main migratory routes between Europe and Africa. It serves as a resting and feeding spot for the birds. As for the wildlife, there are foxes, rabbits, otters, chameleons and a wide variety of birds, such as the common flamingo, mallard, little grebe and cattle egret, amongst others. I don’t know much about birds, but I tried to read every sign along the way, and there were plenty of them. --- ![20260623_184610.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23uaMgX5LNDHjrsTFwygkqASEfk86gaS3HDdFixJxdQyvVmxnsSjfxYhKVDzESgNwfyfz.jpg) ![20260623_184850.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xp2BJ2iPvn4T5pL3WukZecumM6Q6GZUWF1RtHDfdNr9oDpFJznhNhJqqPrYcArLkdJ4.jpg) ![20260623_184904.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23ynUXEuqYqGrHtj7GwCsaeQFFzLaJXKZJ5sZ1u7YRbGKye6RQNrdqPrxRwAzHs589DJh.jpg) ![20260623_184956.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23yd1Uo4whoMv7DhjGeytUu9FYL4rBPbarZ7gCVULxhQL7enLLmnfkoU2Lq1HTBoL3R2D.jpg) --- Once I’d crossed the river and walked a long way, I came to a junction where the path split into two: one section was for cyclists and the other for walkers, where neither bicycles, scooters nor dogs off the lead were permitted. I had no idea where the path would lead me, but as I entered the nature reserve, I imagined that at some point I’d reach one of the lagoons I could see on the map, apparently there are three, though there might be smaller ones that aren’t properly marked. --- ![20260623_185005.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23tvkkN9Dyboj6Hx9g34dtZxKfwumQkjrqWtDr4mmnERur9RktjfqwGRiXesduoPhZt2B.jpg) ![20260623_185128.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23ryzofzoLcxNev2WMzBrKEwBcxDkGP3TwPmU46PGMHvyS7QqcwmqPoVntK8NpnFFrgyn.jpg) ![20260623_185242.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23zGcSGKNfErgzgnNrzKPZEXjsUhjmDsmL3KCHSDHfpxNhmayo1dL4ebzGwn7R9oTSEEk.jpg) ![20260623_185323.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23yTfLb8PrydH91dUncTTZpqRpwTynQi8muexL9s3SNMFzxRnv84dJoWyyUyJ67XDTSYU.jpg) ![20260623_185514.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23zS35y24dtFPWprdqeJixXqXVJ1wR3pmxymenyhxac47YQ67ZEqMpNTBV5ntvpVgPhKK.jpg) ![20260623_185624.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/243WVXTs2miHHBnCaweNJH4iehHbSk1c4DHUsvdcHpP7QjThySUjvacDMjLM5ERHdZQYo.jpg) ![20260623_185645.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23sJveN2NMQQ8kL8o1ynpu163JkDLyvSW4JfY5bozMB17L7e2i8Gp3T3LAT842a8LeK82.jpg) --- As it was my first time there, I was full of excitement and anticipation, but I wanted to take it slowly, as I wasn’t familiar with the terrain; I would examine every spot thoroughly. The path wound its way through dense vegetation on both sides, and often I couldn’t see where it ended; instead, it would fork at certain points. More vegetation, a variety of trees, just as the sign had indicated, and I could hear lots of birds, but I couldn’t spot the animals I’d read about. In some places, the ground looked arid, with a yellowish base, but then there was lush vegetation and a variety of shades of green. --- ![20260623_185727.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/246azh6HUPqkHx7SxHdnZUn3Vn1mPSQrVBVWjRAcqhhyUB6LMchGExw99zPkUFVRB82wW.jpg) ![20260623_190304.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/246azyUcSiYz2dELC6sw39aoGpdHbRL3Exs2C3HUFQ4GXM37WpbQ4xXJ9ZgarL8h1S254.jpg) ![20260623_190448.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/246atEwuBWYMCcKs6KhXFcXoqstXWv1ZWto4CgQqVYgBd1YAPrmf8oNdmjsnuk8bT5uEt.jpg) ![20260623_190454.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/246b14Fa9FhKDL6yfV5nowBkAuTsmb3MkuJq4ADjWR6dpCniwug4ikeVJJLh5YoeWGzgH.jpg) ![20260623_190643.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/241F6bsBKQ54ZP4Hq4f5wggSMigH8wssALKncc78gtDpMzoDtr94bVdra1XoamX3b8CWY.jpg) --- In the distance I could see mountains, bridges, the city or part of it, though not the centre but the surrounding areas. I turned onto a path where there seemed to be nothing, and I had no idea how far away the first lagoon might be or which one I would come across first. --- ![20260623_191338.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/246atc9q7HiRyuhxvWLpcevdC26BcTuHkBWHHbzAv3hJ1jPRYEmFPuCb3YC2s1uppiGiP.jpg) ![20260623_191325.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/242Nf6MZmyY7jcfwdDcDoQdLNZsdYotPv4GtRefecdnxgknzMiiH3MUTXM5pR1PwKFv1n.jpg) ![20260623_191346.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wWyPbrYcBfa65u1S7W1th2zvdfYPMn9tLgSbk1RqhFNecrjLN9sMPqsyRn29LcAqJKB.jpg) ![20260623_191349.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23vhweo3aufmPv81onBGSfyVRZTjL6nkHhr6TDqJoGqSiLWQo2GS1bU8jXBMpE4o8aruZ.jpg) ![20260623_191418.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wMgpWHAQ7g8ZdXD3smP1a6WJeo82AdQJsSAvvemuVgxisx9GJNRcGdmM3Etev5wBTFr.jpg) --- Until, on that very path, another path crossed it and I could see the first observation point. I was very happy. I approached it and found several signs containing a wealth of information. It was Laguna Escondida, and there were several viewing holes from which to look out over the lagoon. The lagoon was fenced off and, apart from that observation point, there was no way to access it or get a closer look at the birds. The signs recommended watching the birds from there, as they are wild and easily frightened by humans. There was also information on what to do if you come across a tagged bird. --- ![20260623_191402.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wMga7zLdNKMTbxK7zBS3TtG4YwL6ue412gn22DXERF92BCdsBdmVr165Exw9T2ENKjb.jpg) ![20260623_191438.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23sUK2T2syMAEF3DTMZKGAyzQMpZHetcdzesZciyuhHrcgjndMW8BjZWkYnhLqiv28Lgp.jpg) ![20260623_191445.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/242YFwLHrXrj2ACQ7ZNt77KMDUjT9kyEyvkWmwhnyCdq7BdhkDsqXDTDasx56QgjxWChd.jpg) ![20260623_191448.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/243g11ZMNWf9xvh3TuubWEHy44vo3arz6h8jKVPAGjq83cVSRYPTuspjuPiQfWJnTGJTN.jpg) ![20260623_191453.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23yd69i1bJtFj91RAjUY1YwY2hZKhDzYLsXKScqGQWo8dL5gvi35gDggxJe7NnZxWrZ6w.jpg) ![20260623_191456.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23r1njrND8SYTCjEnWUpzxL6MhCaQitfkeEngowXoKHWnZh4QzJ4QVz3ahjDDHA99WwGV.jpg) --- One of the signs listed the birds that could be found at this lagoon, namely: the European flycatcher, little bittern, common reed warbler, northern shoveler, crag martin, common moorhen, barn swallow, blackcap and European bee-eater. There was quite a wide variety. As the sun was in my eyes whilst taking photos, it was difficult to make out the species clearly, and not being able to get closer made it even harder. Even so, the place was a paradise and, from what I could see on the map, this wasn’t even the largest lagoon. --- ![20260623_191415.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wMjGHfCe7aiwCvxquag2gbo6JRikFsi9UMzKff5TFZKz9AAb9EY1LRojuXyZBJaQ1Rm.jpg) ![20260623_191554.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/242DVBr2gWYu3UkyvNfDc2zV1eXFJAYmMrHhVsSoVj8TzDs4J4rguxo5Dp49C9rTbRVA9.jpg) ![20260623_191557.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/2458UwhnqzkVzarWDGawsJKEPjQhLP2aNAxtooQ1VWPhTEkNksoo1BhTLiSu24xrLpEYa.jpg) ![20260623_191600.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23ujpHM1BvKE9xdji7SFm2KhKjjF6kyDimRxjb6EzWiN9HarDc62g9wK6H1TpXWN9NkUJ.jpg) ![20260623_191606.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/245wSCiCz6XjakvC2RXNiLy1ijdtPs7PycEoomGG4LaPwjWR9LnbFwKe2HFAV6aotnGsF.jpg) ![20260623_191613.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/245wPkXzJtQuhtabLdjdShrfixfgNXQwhWTjHQnWKSPeQDqAq4j7JV73MJbr7aAToyMDJ.jpg) ![20260623_191621.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23uFgcBMV6PGa1Mj887gQhGwKvz53yn4WcZjsSB18o72Kuxmght1EavVbKkUwSzZKjazw.jpg) --- At the observatory, I also found information boards with plenty of details about the area, such as the fact that the ‘hidden lagoon’ is the deepest and has the freshest water of all the lagoons in the nature reserve, which allows for the growth of macrophytes, submerged plants, making it a vital habitat for diving waterbirds. There is a very dense strip of vegetation dominated by tamarisk, reeds and rushes. Small birds such as the common chiffchaff can be found there, identifiable by their song. Kingfishers can also be spotted in late summer and autumn, so I’ll be returning at that time of year. And although the sign said there were otters, I didn’t see any, or at least I don’t think I did. --- ![20260623_191627.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23v4btQoGJiosKX7MnZJ64LjxX6ZjYMENJMc71nMVrW2tc8gUSPkduWa1EDhZN8kq1ysK.jpg) ![20260623_192633.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/243zpGAVdv4v6vJ4J1bDqfTiYUR9R3iphmtn7ZRzfYiMWDojKgh5PefVGPVEA51dt8QAj.jpg) ![20260623_192637.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/245TJCqMop9D477zZ8LhjsjMEgBc6TitANtk5vL3AeWBk3VSrRQtW5B7ocMcJj7vXf23p.jpg) ![20260623_192642.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/242NqZiUF35N54gq967f9hz56U6TLNAesSyBmWhLX5oFkkDRL6RzAVFWv6cKDaDcViHGw.jpg) --- There are also camouflaged little bitterns hunting along the banks of the lagoon, and occasional visitors arrive, such as bee eaters and summer birds that nest there. I sat there for quite a while, looking out over the lagoon, taking photos and enjoying this new sight, this new part of nature for me, which I loved seeing. --- ![20260623_193237.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xAZuWoQQg7qfqN9yKCmphHRWwMXKXzhZyoHF7KfpcyCJKSP4nY23U6grgsG1Dde5vLs.jpg) ![20260623_193251.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wMiixQb55riyDZBv5aRrgWv95HWQsssaPJBiCWiiTYHf7fpSkr6PzxHy2i1zTfA7Jfc.jpg) ![20260623_193545.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/241ZtTx2xfk1A4YX4sEifW2tPDawb9JbpfXULZaSx6Sxrk4juuFMQ72Can5SPdaPQ7FuR.jpg) --- The sun was already beginning to set a little, so I set off on the long walk back; I had a long way to go to catch the bus, but I promised myself I’d return to explore this paradise in its entirety. Thank you very much for joining me today; I send you my warmest regards. See you soon. Amonet. --- ---
All photographs are my own. Separators created by me in Photoshop. Used translator [Deepl.com](https://www.deepl.com/translator) free version. [//]:# (!worldmappin 36.673169 lat -4.458411 long Hidden Lagoon – Exploring and hiking in a natural setting 📷 Málaga – Spain d3scr)

body.title: [PL / ENG]  My Actifit Report Card: June 29 2026
body.body:
> ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdxX6cHkY6kvtdxQjj858FtPZWSWkAqA5bHgwjhn7Uze6/obraz.png) Młody rozpoczął prowadzenie Wakacyjnego Dziennika Letnich Przygód i dwie strony już zapisane wczorajszymi wydarzeniami. Jak widać działo się! Ale rozpoczęło się od wizyty u lekarza, l4 do piątku, w piątek na kontrolę, zakaz basenów nawet w taki upał. Okazuje się, że kiedy przeziębione dziecko przebywa w upale, jego naczynia krwionośne w skórze mocno się rozszerzają, aby schłodzić organizm. Gdy nagle wejdzie do chłodniejszej wody w basenie, dochodzi do błyskawicznego skurczu tych naczyń, co gwałtownie cofa krew do wnętrza ciała i powoduje chwilowe osłabienie lokalnej odporności, m.in. w drogach oddechowych. W efekcie ułatwia to bakteriom i wirusom (które już namnażają się w gardle czy oskrzelach) głębszą penetrację, a zwiększony przepływ krwi przez zainfekowane obszary może ułatwić patogenom przedostanie się do krwiobiegu, co grozi rozniesieniem infekcji po całym organizmie i nagłym pogorszeniem stanu zdrowia. Upał niemiłosierny, Bombel w domu na wagarach, bo też nie miałam serca go słać do przedszkola w taki gorąc, planowałam szczerze mówiąc ten basen ;) Cóż więc robić. Biedna Dzidzia do Babci, a my myk na basen obok. Myślałam, że pójdziemy tylko na godzinkę, ale ciężko było wyjść z wody, taka była cudowna, i byliśmy dwie godziny. Bosko. Szkoda, że Młoda nie może. > The Bombel has started a Summer Adventure Diary and has already filled two pages with yesterday's events. As you can see, things have been happening! But it all started with a doctor's appointment. Sick leave till Friday, then check-up. Swimming is forbidden, even in this heat. It turns out that when a child with a cold is exposed to heat, their blood vessels in the skin dilate dramatically to cool the body. Suddenly entering the cooler water of a pool, these vessels rapidly constrict, which rapidly forces blood back into the body and temporarily weakens local immunity, including in the respiratory tract. As a result, this makes it easier for bacteria and viruses (already multiplying in the throat and bronchi) to penetrate deeper, and increased blood flow through infected areas can facilitate pathogens' entry into the bloodstream, which can spread the infection throughout the body and cause a sudden deterioration in health. The heat is unbearable, Bombel is skipping preschool at home because I didn't have the heart to send him to preschool in such heat. Honestly, I was planning on going to the pool ;) So what can I do? Poor baby, off to Grandma's, and we're off to the pool next door. I thought we'd only go for an hour, but it was hard to get out of the water, it was so wonderful, and we stayed there for two hours. Divine. It's a shame the little one can't go with us. ![obraz.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX7ziwi7ywePS8dkjmDAprz5g3Ab6mdow5ryiYdWoKmth/obraz.png)
_This report was published via Actifit app ([Android](https://bit.ly/actifit-app) | [iOS](https://bit.ly/actifit-ios)). Check out the original version [here on actifit.io](https://actifit.io/@asia-pl/actifit-asia-pl-20260630t085519115z)_

body.body:

![20260630_145121.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kiwibloke/23xebXBQ9AbZAX48M3FC2pRKcnPGuXXhagsFZm3GM5VYF7BTfEsYitBZdyX6QVuscsv3A.jpg)

|  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|![Screenshot_20260630_164337_Huawei Health.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kiwibloke/23t77FNxg5EyeN7vfM93RnZtQZi7eAhGbDJEsBTjHFeU7T2GWZmA1Q5U6z6JwmEJHsh4v.png)|![Screenshot_20260630_164403_Huawei Health.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kiwibloke/23t74bAXk2KmBot5PSMFjYQuJRxen9Qi7Yb73Zdszg4SHcRrYuM8nkY5haf4yMshvGnJG.png)|![Screenshot_20260630_164419_Huawei Health.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kiwibloke/23swdrj5LzNbupLNRxWFMmNsPccjKpszvz1YHbEsStBCkdVHVRYnRoij4NoqP2QuzJ2zk.png)|

We've been having atrocious bad weather here over the last 2 weeks our small suburb made the news, kinda cool. Landslides, tree felling, property damage, flood warnings ('cept they was for real, warnings pfft) the normal stuff. 

Today was a stunner, little cloud, a little trip around the suburb was calling. Apart from the easy slow pace ride, I have finally settled on this dashcam mount, once again testing a new setting 720p at 240fps LoL. Why? because that's what I like to do, fiddle with stuff. Can't wait to see the footage.

<center>
![20260630_151826.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/kiwibloke/23wMW1PGyMtkznk5j59hjTXeTPS75bgBccFR26C8qgCCD3AMfCmrRYjYvGgoGTZnvpXYo.jpg)
</center>

I stopped at this pedestrian bridge wondering why the ducks were freaking out. On closer inspection there's a HUGE eel harassing them. I didn't stay long, I needed to visit the local bakery for a healthy steak and cheese pie with accompanying cream donut.

<center>
https://youtube.com/shorts/aRUaD_GV_6Q?si=dnfUKXNbbAIxHzZw
</center>


Love making these short clips in YouCut, looks good if you playback in 1080p. Until next time, be safe out here!!

---

### My Gear
- Huawei Band 10 Watch (heart rate monitor)
- Samsung Galaxy A33 5G (HuaweiHealthApp for Android: GPS Mapping)

</center>

body.title: Movie Review: The Passion of the Christ
body.body: > Passion of the Christ is a powerful Christian film that was directed by Mel Gibson. The film is about the last few hours of Jesus Christ's life, prior to His crucifixion. It emphasizes His suffering, sacrifice and tremendous love for humanity. Although the story is familiar to many from the Bible, this film does a wonderful job of conveying the reality and the emotion thereof. The one thing I observed while watching this movie is how much Jesus' pain and sacrifice are portrayed in this movie. The acting is quite believable, and the emotions are real. The film makes viewers aware of the arduous path Jesus went through in preparation for His crucifixion on the cross. There were some scenes that were very emotional because they depicted the extent of His love and commitment to God's purpose. ![1001625784.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/julie100/23u5xvrY7jDUNNk3y3f9RiWxyfdvwQHDZrPJdWucLDjQuuN8kj9oKDzugzTLPGWTR4wyf.png) The film's cinematography is another aspect that's good. Beautiful visuals, and costumes and locations bring the biblical setting to life. The cinematography and lighting sets the tone for the film as serious and respectful. I was able to see history happen before my eyes, from Biblical times. The acting in the film is superb. The portrayal by the actor playing Jesus is excellent, and represents both strength and humility. The other cast members also do a pretty good job of what they're supposed to do and make this story believable and engaging. Their facial expressions and emotions bring dimension to the movie, and allow the viewer to relate to the characters. What is striking is the emphasis of faith, forgiveness and sacrifice in the film. It is a reminder to viewers of the core message of Christianity and the need for love, mercy and redemption. I believe that many Christians will be inspired by the movie because it portrays an important facet of their faith in a very moving manner. But it's not a easy viewing. Emotionally heavy and intense some scenes are, due to Jesus' suffering. These scenes are integral to the film, but some people may find them hard to watch. It is also one of the most serious films ever produced, featuring few light moments in what is a very serious film. I also believe that the movie has been successful in getting viewers to think about what it means to sacrifice and believe. Religious or otherwise, the film asks viewers to ponder the key values of love, courage, forgiveness and compassion. It's a type of film that lingers in your mind long after. The Passion of the Christ is a deeply moving (emotional) movie which tells one of the most important stories in Christianity. It sets up with great acting, stunning visuals and a profound message. It's an emotionally charged film that can be hard to watch, but it's still a memorable and impactful film. I think it's a decent movie to watch if you wish to learn more about Jesus Christ and His sacrifice. My Rating: 9/10 ⭐ Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@julie100/movie-review-the-passion-of-the-christ-ark)

body.title: Why I Love Using a Bicycle as My Favorite Mode of Transportation
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRTVZ7vds33hid4aNbcAsDwppVkiUujRhX1MhS2eQ23wf/1782808686515.jpg)


I wasn't aware that a new @indiaunited prompt is out until I stumbled on @nsigo post this morning. Just as I always say and it came out as a prompt this week and I am saying it again If someone asked me to choose my favorite means of transportation, I wouldn't hesitate to say, the bicycle. While many people dream of driving luxury cars or riding powerful motorcycles, I have found genuine joy in something much simpler. For me, riding a bicycle is more than just moving from one place to another—it is an experience that refreshes my body, clears my mind, and reminds me to enjoy life's simple pleasures.

One of the biggest reasons I love using a bicycle is the sense of freedom it gives me. The moment I begin to pedal, I feel connected to my surroundings in a way that I never do inside a car. I can hear the birds, feel the cool breeze against my face, and appreciate the beauty of nature as I ride along. Every journey becomes an opportunity to slow down and enjoy the moment instead of rushing through life.

Another reason I choose a bicycle is because it keeps me physically active. In a world where many of us spend hours sitting behind desks or staring at screens, cycling gives me a natural way to exercise without feeling like a chore. Every ride strengthens my muscles, improves my endurance, and contributes to my overall health. It reminds me that taking care of my body doesn't always require a gym membership—sometimes all it takes is a bicycle and a willingness to ride.

I also appreciate how economical cycling is. A bicycle doesn't require expensive fuel, costly maintenance, or frequent repairs compared to motor vehicles. Knowing that I can travel while saving money gives me peace of mind. The money I would have spent on transportation can be invested in other meaningful areas of my life, such as learning new skills, buying books, or pursuing my dream of becoming an author.

Beyond the personal benefits, I enjoy knowing that riding a bicycle is environmentally friendly. Every time I choose to cycle instead of using a fuel-powered vehicle, I feel like I am making a small contribution toward reducing pollution and protecting the environment. It may seem like a small act, but I believe that many small actions can lead to significant positive change.

Cycling has also taught me valuable life lessons. It has shown me the importance of balance, persistence, and consistency. Just like in life, I have to keep pedaling to move forward. There are steep hills that challenge me, rough roads that test my determination, and long distances that require patience. Yet every successful ride reminds me that progress comes through steady effort rather than sudden leaps.

Most importantly, riding a bicycle brings me happiness. It gives me time to think, reflect, and appreciate the journey rather than focusing only on the destination. Whether I am commuting, exercising, or simply riding for fun, every trip leaves me feeling refreshed and grateful.

For many people, a bicycle may just be another means of transportation. But for me, it represents freedom, health, simplicity, and purpose. It reminds me that life's greatest joys are often found in the simplest things. As long as I am able to ride, I know my bicycle will remain my favorite companion on every journey.

body.title: Money Is a Tool, Not the Meaning of Life
body.body:
Have you ever noticed how easy it is to get caught up in chasing money? Every day we are surrounded by people telling us that success means having more and more money, a bigger house, a nicer car, or the latest gadgets. Social media doesn't make it any easier either. We constantly see people showing the highlights of their lives, and before we know it, we are comparing ourselves to them.

 https://img.leopedia.io/DQmVDxcFfXXmTgjSrt7emGAhYoWQNWctcQzKBoT8DZp5ze7/1000236820.jpg 

[Pixabay](https://pixabay.com/illustrations/ai-generated-glitter-crystal-gold-8369386/)

Don't get me wrong. I don't believe there is anything wrong with being rich. In fact, I think financial success is a good thing. If you have worked hard, made smart decisions, and built wealth honestly, you should enjoy the rewards. Being able to provide for your family, travel, invest, or simply live without worrying about every bill is a blessing that many people hope for.

But there is one thought that has stayed with me for a long time. People think everything that glitter are gold but even with that, Gold is not food.

Gold has value because we give it value. Money is important because it helps us meet our needs and gives us opportunities. But when you strip everything else away, there are things that money simply cannot replace.

I've seen people who seem to have everything money can buy, yet they still aren't happy. They have successful businesses, beautiful homes, and expensive cars, but behind closed doors they are dealing with loneliness, stress, broken relationships, or poor health. Looking at that reminds me that wealth can make life more comfortable, but it doesn't automatically make life meaningful.

On the other hand, I've also met people who don't have much in terms of material things, yet they are some of the happiest people I've ever known. They value family, friendship, laughter, and peace of mind. They may not have overflowing bank accounts, but they have something many wealthy people spend years trying to find which is contentment.

That really makes me think about what success should look like. There is nothing wrong with wanting a better life. We should work hard, set goals, and build a future we are proud of. We should save, invest, and make wise financial decisions. There is absolutely nothing wrong with enjoying the fruits of our labor but the danger comes when we allow money to become our only focus.

Sometimes we are so busy trying to earn more that we forget to enjoy the people we are earning it for. We postpone spending time with family because we are chasing another opportunity. We neglect our health because we are always working. We forget to appreciate the small moments that actually make life special.

Money is a tool. It's a very useful one, but it's still just a tool. It should help us live better lives, not become the reason we stop living them. I've learned that some of life's greatest treasures can't be bought. A peaceful mind, good health, genuine friendships, a loving family, and people who stand by you during difficult times are worth far more than any amount of gold.

At the end of the day, nobody remembers us because of how much money we had in the bank. People remember how we treated them, the kindness we showed, the lives we touched, and the values we lived by. So yes, dream big, Build wealth, Create opportunities for yourself and your family. Celebrate your achievements because you have earned them.

Just don't let success cloud your judgment, Stay humble, Stay grateful. Remember the people who supported you before you had anything. Help others when you are in a position to do so. And never let the pursuit of wealth cause you to lose sight of what truly matters.




**Thanks for checking on my blog and have a wonderful day**

### Right -- on to the main event

So. Eleven episodes ago we couldn't get an agent to balance a stick. Today we're going to talk about agents that beat the best humans on the planet at the hardest games we ever invented. And here's the thing that still gives me a little thrill after all these years: **games have been the proving ground for reinforcement learning since the very beginning**, and almost every big idea in modern RL was born trying to win one.

A quick roll of honour. Tesauro's **TD-Gammon** taught itself Backgammon back in 1992 -- in stead of copying human play, it found moves that surprised grandmasters. DeepMind's **DQN** (our episode #107) chewed through dozens of Atari games straight from pixels in 2015. **AlphaGo** toppled the world Go champion in 2016, a decade earlier than anyone sane predicted. **OpenAI Five** dismantled professional Dota 2 teams in 2019, and **AlphaStar** hit Grandmaster in StarCraft II the same year.

_Why_ games, though? Because they are very nearly perfect laboratories: the rules are crisp, the reward is unambiguous (you won, or you didn't), the simulator runs faster than real time, and difficulty comes pre-graded from \

. And -- this is the part that matters far beyond games -- the algorithms born here travel. AlphaZero's MCTS planning grew into MuZero's general model-based RL. PPO, invented to wrangle game agents, now trains language models. The toy was always a Trojan horse for something serious.

## AlphaZero: one algorithm, three games, zero human knowledge

**AlphaZero** (Silver et al., 2018) is, to me, one of the most beautiful results in the whole field. The same code, with no game-specific tweaks, learned Chess, Go _and_ Shogi from scratch -- three games with wildly different boards, pieces and tactics. No opening books, no endgame tablebases, no hand-crafted features. Just the rules, and an awful lot of self-play.

The recipe has three ingredients, and that's genuinely all:

1. **A neural network** that reads the board and outputs two things at once -- a *policy* (a probability over legal moves) and a *value* (who is winning, from -1 to +1);
2. **Monte Carlo Tree Search** that uses that network to look ahead intelligently;
3. **Self-play** (the episode #111 trick) that generates the training data out of thin air.

The network is a dual-headed beast sitting on a tower of residual blocks (remember those from the CNN episodes? they show up everywhere):

```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import numpy as np
import math


class ResidualBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, channels):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn1 = nn.BatchNorm2d(channels)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(channels, channels, 3, padding=1)
        self.bn2 = nn.BatchNorm2d(channels)

    def forward(self, x):
        residual = x
        x = torch.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
        x = self.bn2(self.conv2(x))
        return torch.relu(x + residual)   # the skip connection


class AlphaZeroNetwork(nn.Module):
    \

def __init__(self, board_size, n_actions, n_res_blocks=5, channels=128):
        super().__init__()
        # 17 input planes is the Go encoding (stone history + side to move).
        self.conv_input = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(17, channels, 3, padding=1),
            nn.BatchNorm2d(channels), nn.ReLU(),
        )
        self.res_blocks = nn.ModuleList(
            [ResidualBlock(channels) for _ in range(n_res_blocks)])

        self.policy_head = nn.Sequential(            # probability over moves
            nn.Conv2d(channels, 2, 1), nn.BatchNorm2d(2), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(2 * board_size * board_size, n_actions),
        )
        self.value_head = nn.Sequential(             # who is winning? (-1..1)
            nn.Conv2d(channels, 1, 1), nn.BatchNorm2d(1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Flatten(),
            nn.Linear(board_size * board_size, 256), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 1), nn.Tanh(),
        )

    def forward(self, state):
        x = self.conv_input(state)
        for block in self.res_blocks:
            x = block(x)
        return self.policy_head(x), self.value_head(x)
```

Two heads, one body. The shared residual tower learns to \

the board; the policy head turns that into a hunch about good moves, and the value head into a verdict about the outcome. Having said that, the network alone is a strong _intuition_ but a weak _player_ -- it reacts, it doesn't plan. The planning is where MCTS comes in.

## Monte Carlo Tree Search: thinking by simulating

MCTS is how AlphaZero \

. Rather than glance at a position and blurt out a move, it imagines hundreds or thousands of continuations, growing a search tree, and uses the network to decide which branches are worth exploring. Four steps, repeated over and over: **select** a promising path down the tree, **expand** a new leaf, **evaluate** it with the network, and **backpropagate** the verdict up to the root.

## The training loop: the dog that teaches itself new tricks

Here's where the whole thing becomes a perpetual-motion machine (well, almost). Self-play with the current network generates games. Each position, paired with the MCTS visit-distribution and the eventual game result, becomes a training example. The network trains on that, gets a little sharper, which makes MCTS a little sharper, which produces better games, which... you see where this goes.

```python
def alphazero_training_loop(game, network, n_iterations=100,
                            games_per_iteration=100, mcts_sims=200):
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(network.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

    for iteration in range(n_iterations):
        # Phase 1: self-play generates fresh training data
        training_data = []
        mcts = MCTS(network, n_simulations=mcts_sims)
        for _ in range(games_per_iteration):
            state = game.new_game()
            history = []
            while not state.is_terminal():
                pi = mcts.search(state)
                history.append((state.to_tensor(), pi))
                actions = list(pi.keys())
                action = np.random.choice(actions, p=[pi[a] for a in actions])
                state.apply_action(action)
            # Hand the final result back to every position, alternating sign
            result = state.get_reward()
            for board_tensor, pi in history:
                training_data.append((board_tensor, pi, result))
                result = -result

        # Phase 2: train on the self-play data
        for epoch in range(10):
            np.random.shuffle(training_data)
            for start in range(0, len(training_data), 64):
                batch = training_data[start:start + 64]
                boards, pis, results = zip(*batch)
                boards_t = torch.stack(boards)
                results_t = torch.FloatTensor(results).unsqueeze(1)

                logits, values = network(boards_t)
                # Policy loss: cross-entropy against the MCTS visit-distribution
                targets = torch.zeros_like(logits)

                    for action, prob in pi.items():
                        targets[i, action] = prob
                policy_loss = -(targets * torch.log_softmax(logits, dim=1)).sum(1).mean()
                # Value loss: MSE against who actually won
                value_loss = nn.functional.mse_loss(values, results_t)
```

The numbers are worth sitting with. AlphaZero trained roughly **9 hours** on Chess, **12 hours** on Shogi and **13 days** on Go -- on a single machine with 4 TPUs -- and the resulting players were stronger than the best specialised engines humanity had built over _decades_. Stockfish for Chess, the dedicated Go programs, all of it, beaten by one general recipe that started from random play. The first time I read that paper I had to put it down and go for a walk ;-)

## Beyond the board: Atari and the curse of sparse reward

Board games are tidy -- perfect information, discrete moves, take-turns. Atari is messier: real-time, raw pixels, partial information. DQN (episode #107) cracked dozens of Atari games, but a handful stayed stubbornly unsolved, and the poster child for \

is **Montezuma's Revenge**.

The problem is **sparse reward**. In Montezuma's Revenge the agent must climb down ladders, jump gaps, grab a key, cross a room, unlock a door -- _hundreds_ of correct steps -- before a single point arrives. Plain epsilon-greedy DQN just rattles around randomly, never stumbling on that long lucky sequence, and so it never sees a reward to learn from. It's like trying to learn the piano when the only feedback is a standing ovation at the end of a concert you can't yet play.

The fix that stuck is giving the agent its own internal motivation -- a **curiosity** bonus for visiting states it can't yet predict:

```python
class ICMModule(nn.Module):
    \

def __init__(self, state_dim, action_dim, feature_dim=64):
        super().__init__()
        self.feature_net = nn.Sequential(      # compress states into features
            nn.Linear(state_dim, 128), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, feature_dim),
        )
        self.forward_model = nn.Sequential(    # predict next feature from this + action
            nn.Linear(feature_dim + action_dim, 128), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, feature_dim),
        )

    def compute_intrinsic_reward(self, state, action, next_state):
        phi_s = self.feature_net(state)
        phi_ns = self.feature_net(next_state)
        pred = self.forward_model(torch.cat([phi_s, action], dim=-1))
        # Big prediction error = big surprise = big intrinsic reward
        return 0.5 * (pred - phi_ns.detach()).pow(2).sum(dim=-1)
```

The trick is self-balancing. States the agent can't predict are novel, so they pay a curiosity bonus and the agent goes looking. But as it explores them the forward model _learns_ them, the prediction error shrinks, and those once-exciting states become boring -- pushing the agent toward the next unexplored frontier. It's an artificial sense of wonder that automatically fades where it's been satisfied. Count-based exploration and Random Network Distillation are cousins of this idea, and together they finally got agents through that wretched first room.

## Real-time strategy: where RL meets the meat grinder

If board games are tidy and Atari is messy, **StarCraft II** and **Dota 2** are the meat grinder. They pile on every hard thing at once: games lasting 30-45 minutes (long time horizons), a fog of war hiding the opponent (imperfect information), continuous real-time decisions, and action spaces so vast you can barely write them down.

**OpenAI Five** tackled Dota 2 by throwing PPO (episode #109) at the problem at a frankly absurd scale: 256 GPUs and 128,000 CPU cores, playing the equivalent of **180 years of Dota every single day** for ten months. A few of the tricks that made it work:

- **Patience as a hyperparameter**: a Dota game is ~20,000 decisions long, so they used a discount factor of `gamma = 0.9997` -- an agent that genuinely cares about a reward arising thousands of steps in the future.
- **Taming the action space**: the raw continuous control was discretised into roughly a thousand sensible options per step, so the policy had something finite to choose from.
- **Team reward**: all five heroes on a team shared one reward signal -- cooperative MARL straight out of episode #111, learned at industrial scale.

**AlphaStar** went at StarCraft II differently: a transformer-based policy (yes, the same attention machinery from episodes #51-53) reading the game as a set of entities, trained first on human replays and then refined with self-play inside a _league_ of deliberately diverse agents -- some aggressive, some weird, some built only to expose the main agent's blind spots. It reached Grandmaster, top 0.2% of human players, in all three races. The league is the key idea: a single self-play line can get stuck in a rut, but a whole ecosystem of rivals keeps everyone honest.

## Reward shaping: helpful nudges and how they backfire

Raw game rewards are often too sparse or too delayed to learn from quickly, so we're tempted to add intermediate signals -- a little reward for picking up the key, for moving toward the goal, for staying alive. This is **reward shaping**, and it is _gloriously_ easy to get wrong. Shape it carelessly and the agent will gleefully maximise your shaping signal in stead of the actual objective -- circling the key forever because approaching it pays, never bothering to pick it up.

There is exactly one form of shaping proven safe, and it's worth knowing by name: **potential-based shaping** (Ng et al., 1999).

```python
return -np.linalg.norm(state.position - state.goal_position)
```

The reason this particular shape is safe is subtle and lovely: because the bonus is the _difference_ of a potential across a transition, it telescopes away over any complete path and cancels out of every loop. So it can speed learning -- pointing the agent roughly toward the goal -- without ever changing _which_ policy is optimal. Any other shaping scheme risks quietly rewriting the objective. In practice plenty of successful projects use non-potential shaping anyway, carefully, accepting the theoretical risk for the practical speed-up -- but they do it with their eyes open, and so should you.

body.title: ENOUGH IS ENOUGH ___DAILY PROMPT 29 JUNE
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaHRGFonCcpx9pUPQHxXms2kTPCFCb4xHky2HE9E6zWmK/1782772893210.jpg)

Living in a university hostel has taught me many things, but one experience I will never forget was the day students almost caused a riot over electricity bills.

For weeks, we had been living in darkness. There was little or no electricity, yet every month we were expected to contribute money for electricity. At first, everyone complained quietly, hoping the situation would improve. Unfortunately, nothing changed.

One morning, a notice was posted, reminding us to pay another electricity bill. The moment students saw it, the hostel became noisy. People gathered in groups, asking the same question.

\

Someone shouted that enough was enough, and within minutes, students were pouring out of their rooms. The peaceful complaints quickly turned into heated arguments. Some students banged on doors, others demanded to see the hostel management, while a few threatened not to pay until electricity was restored.

Although it never became violent, the tension in the hostel was intense. Everyone was frustrated. It wasn't really about the money; it was about fairness. How could we keep paying for a service we were barely receiving?

Thankfully, after several discussions, the management listened to the students' complaints and promised to address the issue. The crowd gradually dispersed, and peace returned to the hostel.

That day reminded me that frustration can easily turn into a riot when people feel ignored. While anger is understandable, I also learned that dialogue often achieves more than destruction. Sometimes, the loudest protest begins with people simply wanting to be treated fairly.

body.title: Keeping images for future generations
body.body:
I see this as a very wonderful question that must of us are guilty of. Especially myself. Sometimes when I attend any function like wedding, birthday parties, burial ceremony, wedding anniversaries, house dedication, church programs and what have you. I make sure to take enough videos and pictures and without their permission I just go ahead and use them for my post here and also other social media platforms. Hmmm! I think that if someone wants to take legal action because of that I will be guilty as charged.


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUtj5EcyRxU33zjheiUFknkZLh9jQsWGiCwCPymsiAuvN/1782807558725.jpg)
This is one of the random images I took in my village when I went for my in-laws burial.


YOUR FACE ALONE 

Everyone has a right to take pictures and videos in public places. This is the truth. We all have our phones and some have very good cameras which temps to always take pictures everywhere we are. And we just go on and do it anyway. I think that my face belongs to me and people should not have access to it the way the want. I should be informed before anyone will do that. I think that sometimes I inform people before taken their images, but not all the time. You know the way you feel when you just pick up your phones and begin to take random pictures.

APPEARING IN RANDOM PICTURES OR VIDEOS 

Is not now that you can just see someone send your image online without letting you know. But for me sometimes I am grateful that people have pictures of me. One day in a WhatsApp group that I belong I just saw someone drop pictures of me and other students when we went to educational visit to Kaduna state. I was surprised and happy at the same time. I didn't know that someone took those pictures until that day and the memories just came back. I was not sad with the person rather I was so happy because of that. So, though sometimes we need to take permission before taken the pictures, it still serve as memorial of any events tomorrow. So it has two sides: the good and the bad. If I refuse permission for people to take my pictures, how will they have something to hold onto when I am not there tomorrow? Look at it from a brighter side and losen up. 

HOW WILL I FEEL IF I FIND MY IMAGE IN SOMEONE'S POST?

Well, let it just be a very good image, I will even copy it for my own use tomorrow. It should not be seen totally as something wrong. While we talk to people and ask them to be careful how to take my images without letting me know. They should also be allowed to have something to remember me tomorrow when I am gone.

My father never took a picture of himself before he died, so I never had anything to hold as long as his memory is concerned. I don't know him and he don't know me. Maybe if someone took a picture of him, it would have been of help to me too because I will know what he looks like. But is well

body.title: ‎Morocco Refused to Give Up – What a Night of World Cup Football! ‎
body.body:
‎Some football matches stay in your memory because of the quality on display, while others are unforgettable because of the emotions they bring. For me, Morocco's victory over the Netherlands falls into the second category. It had everything a football fan could ask for, such as drama, tension, heartbreak, and a finish that kept everyone guessing until the very last kick.
‎ https://img.leopedia.io/DQmNrxSR7d3CR6T4GtzdeDWNCLwMYH2eX1YrqFahNdYfRGy/uwzcpHj1HOmh_Ifk7Bb4ag13T_1440x996.jpg 

‎[Source](https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/netherlands-vs-morocco-live-updates-world-cup-2026-round-of-32-game-latest-score-and-team-news/OOFqMU4tJD47/)
‎
‎When Cody Gakpo gave the Netherlands the lead in the second half, I honestly thought the game was over. The Dutch looked composed, and with only a few minutes left, it seemed they were on their way to the next round. It was also an emotional moment for Gakpo after everything he has gone through personally in recent days, so seeing him celebrate was quite touching.
‎
‎Then came the twist nobody expected.
‎
‎Just when the Netherlands were preparing to celebrate, Morocco found one last opportunity. Issa Diop's header in stoppage time completely changed the game. I can only imagine what the Moroccan fans must have felt at that moment. One minute you're staring at elimination, and the next you are celebrating an equaliser that gives your team another chance.
‎
‎Extra time was just as exciting. Morocco looked more dangerous, and I really believed Rahimi had scored when he found himself one-on-one with the goalkeeper. Somehow, Bart Verbruggen pulled off an unbelievable save. It was one of those moments where you simply have to applaud the goalkeeper, even if you're supporting the other team.
‎
‎When the match went to penalties, it became a battle of nerves. Morocco handled the pressure much better, while the Dutch could not find the consistency they needed. Bounou came up with another important save, and Saibari calmly converted the winning penalty to send Morocco through.
‎
‎What impressed me most was not just the result but Morocco's attitude. They never looked like a team that had accepted defeat. Even after going behind, they kept pushing, kept believing, and eventually got their reward. That kind of determination is something every football fan can appreciate.
‎
‎Now they have a meeting with Canada in the round of 16, and after watching this performance, I won't be surprised if they continue their impressive run. This World Cup has already given us so many unforgettable moments, and Morocco has added another one to the list.
‎
‎Sometimes football reminds us that belief can be just as important as talent, and Morocco proved exactly that.
‎

Posted Using [INLEO](https://inleo.io/@twicejoy-sports/morocco-refused-to-give-up-what-a-night-of-world-cup-football--cjg)

body.title: A Love Song To Be Sung!
body.body:
Me:
Are we living in a simulation within a simulation within a simulation, like the movie The Thirteenth Floor?

Alan Watts:
Ah, the old dream-within-a-dream-within-a-dream! It's a marvelous game the mind plays, isn't it? But you see, whether this reality is a \

makes no difference at all. It's like asking if a wave is a simulation of the ocean. The very question presupposes a separation that isn't really there. You are the thing being simulated, and the simulator, and the experience of it all, all at once. The only real question is, are you enjoying the show?

![1000002642.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/atma.love/23xL9FknBW43T4HAMfdVF47C2J8C8TyZSW6vjc8En518LbonS1iHcVHs62tcTs8VxbT7m.jpg)

Me:
mostly, yes.

Alan Watts:
\

is the most honest answer a person can give! It means you're truly paying attention. To enjoy the show without reservation is to be a fool, but to find the joy amidst the nonsense, the beauty in the boring bits—that's the art of living. It's in that \

that the real wisdom is found.

Me:
What did Sri Ramakrishna have to say about this?

Alan Watts:
Ah, Ramakrishna! What a perfect spirit to invoke. He wouldn't get tangled in the \

question at all. For him, the world was *Lila*, the divine play of the Mother. He saw it all—every joy, every sorrow, every holy man and every sinner as Her dance. He wouldn't ask if it's real; he'd laugh and ask if you were enjoying the dance! He practiced many faiths, you see, and found they were all just different doors to the same room. **The world isn't a simulation to be figured out, but a love song to be sung.**
![1000002645.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/atma.love/23wMUEJTt17dGJz8LF6w4esB1JwtLDtFtfwTxs8Aee5VLurbqvuU9CKJhL4QHgdSGdV8n.jpg) Image of Sri Ramakrishna (public domain).

Sat Nam
Atma

Your **bearish read is the stronger case** here. The chart you posted shows HSI still trading well below that **24,550** horizontal level and under the descending dynamic resistance cluster, while the accompanying market note had Hong Kong stocks at **22,819 after a 0.9% drop** on June 30 despite policy-support hopes from Beijing ([Yahoo Finance HSI](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EHSI/), [HKEX](https://www.hkex.com.hk/?sc_lang=en)).

The key point is that **a small hourly bounce is not a trend change**. When price is stuck under a falling structure like that, rallies usually look more like relief moves than real reversals. Your **23,695 overhead resistance** framing is especially useful because it gives traders a clean line between “still weak” and “maybe this is changing.”

On the InLeo side, I’m not seeing recent HSI-specific discussion to challenge that view, so your post stands out precisely because it is **specific, chart-backed, and not pretending a green hour fixes a bad month**.

One tweak: the ending would hit harder if you define the **next downside level** explicitly. Right now the thesis is solid, but adding the likely retest zone turns it from a market take into a tradeable map.
